# Part G — Test Checklist panel (web console)

> **CURRENT AUDIT — 2026-09-22:** G.1 is delivered and exact current tool coverage is complete: the live tool catalogue and shipped checklist catalogue both contain 170 entries in the audited tree, with no missing or extra checklist names. G.2 remains open because modules can supply many tool entries but only one checklist-group entry. Human browser QA/tightening is still a closure task.
>
> **Update, 2026-09-27d — G.2 delivered.** `jarvis-multi-group-checklist.patch`
> extends `TEST_CHECKLIST_GROUP` to the multi-group shape and updates
> schema/loader/API/editor/docs/tests to match — see the "As built" note
> under G.2 below for the full breakdown. Human browser QA/tightening
> remains open, same as G.1.


**Status: Delivered.** `jarvis-test-checklist.patch`; see revision
2026-09-20l for the file list. This part didn't exist in earlier revisions of
this plan — it documents a new feature. **G.1 (below) delivered in revision
2026-09-21d; G.2 (below) delivered in rev. 2026-09-27d** — they are the two
numbered items in this part, both now closed pending only the general
real-browser human QA both note as open.

**What it is.** **Menu → Test Checklist** is a tester's workbench for every
tool Jarvis can call. Each tool has: what it does, how to test it (`ask`
prompts to type into Ask, and `run` argument sets to run from Debug without
the model), what a pass looks like (`expect`), and optional `needs` / `os` /
`care` / `watch` notes. A tester records a verdict per tool — Untested, Fully
working, Partially working, Not as intended, Bug / broken, Blocked — ticks
individual steps, and adds notes. There are keyboard shortcuts (↑/↓ to move,
0–5 to set a verdict, `/` to search), a verdict/category filter, and an
Overview pane with progress and a "needs attention" list.

**Purely front end.** The catalogue is the static file
`web/public/test-checklist-data.js`; **results live only in the browser's
localStorage** (Export/Import JSON moves them between browsers). Nothing is
written by the CLI or stored under `~/.jarvis`; there is no new server route.
The only request is the read-only `GET /api/tools` Debug already uses, to spot
tools that exist in the CLI but have no entry — those are listed by name only,
marked **NO CHECKLIST**, and named in the Overview's Coverage section. (Since
G.1 that same response also carries any entry a tool's own module supplied,
which the panel merges in.) All
catalogue text is inserted with `textContent`, never `innerHTML`.

**The rule it adds (AGENTS.md → "Test Checklist").** Whenever you add, rename,
remove or change the behaviour of a tool you **must** update its entry in
`test-checklist-data.js` in the same change — a tool change without its entry
is incomplete, like a tool with no schema. Editing a step's text un-ticks it in
testers' browsers (ticks are keyed by the text). The data must be strict JSON
between the `JSON-BEGIN`/`JSON-END` markers.

**Enforcement.** `tests/test_checklist_coverage.py` (5 checks) fails when a
tool has no entry, an entry has no tool, an entry is malformed or duplicates a
step, or a group id disagrees with `tool_registry.TOOL_GROUPS`. Run it directly:
`python3 tests/test_checklist_coverage.py`.

**State after the merge.** The patch shipped entries for the 152 tools that
existed when it was built. The merge added entries for the 16 tools the other
patches introduced (7 `browser_*`, 4 `clipboard_*`, 5 path tools) and two
groups (Clipboard, Browser control); see revision 2026-09-20m. Those 16 are
drafts and worth a human pass. The `clipboard-watch` daemon is not a tool and
has no entry; it is controlled through the existing `daemon_*` tools, whose
entries already exist.

## G.1 Let a tool module supply its own checklist entry — not just gated by whether a custom module's tools happen to be in the shipped file

**Status: Delivered — revision 2026-09-21d, `jarvis-test-checklist-supplied-entries.patch`
(see "As built" at the end of this section; the requirement text below is left
as written).** Originally: new requirement (2026-09-20 addendum).

**The gap.** Today the whole catalogue is one static file,
`test-checklist-data.js`, with every entry keyed by tool name under
`"tools"`, plus a fixed `"groups"` list of categories. Coverage checking
(above, "Purely front end") works by fetching the live catalogue from
`GET /api/tools` and diffing it against that static file's keys — a tool that
exists but has no matching key shows as a bare name, marked **NO CHECKLIST**.
That's the right behaviour for a *shipped* tool someone forgot to document,
but it's the wrong behaviour for a tool that can never have an entry in the
shipped file in the first place: anything `tool_loader.discover_actions()`
picks up from `actions/*.py`, and — more to the point — anything a specific
user wrote themselves through the Custom Tools system (`custom_tools_store.py`,
`~/.jarvis/tools/<name>.py`, editable from the web UI's Custom Tools tab). A
user's own custom tool is by definition unknown to whoever ships
`test-checklist-data.js`; today it shows **NO CHECKLIST** forever, no matter
how good the tool is, because the only place an entry can be authored is a
file that ships with the app. That's the "gated by the available tools" the
owner is pointing at — a custom module's tools are permanently locked out of
ever having a real entry, not just temporarily missing one.

**What to add.** Let a tool module supply its own checklist entry (or
entries) alongside its `TOOL_SCHEMAS`/`TOOLS`/`TOOL_GROUP`, the same way it
can already optionally supply `TOOL_KEYWORDS` and `TOOL_PACK_INSTRUCTION` —
see `actions/_template.py` and `tool_loader.py`'s extraction of those two for
the existing pattern to follow. Concretely:

- A new optional module-level `TEST_CHECKLIST` dict, in the exact same
  per-tool shape `test-checklist-data.js` already uses under `"tools"`
  (`does` / `steps` / optional `needs` / `os` / `care` / `watch`) — an entry
  authored inside a module is byte-for-byte the same shape as one authored in
  the shipped file, so the same validation
  (`tests/test_checklist_coverage.py`'s 5 checks) covers both without a
  second code path.
- **"Per type," not just per tool:** a module introducing a brand-new
  `TOOL_GROUP` — the exact case `_template.py` already calls out ("a
  brand-new group with an empty TOOL_KEYWORDS...") — currently has no way to
  give that group a label/blurb the way the shipped `"groups"` list does for
  every built-in category, so it would show up unlabeled or fall into a
  generic bucket in the panel. Add an optional
  `TEST_CHECKLIST_GROUP = {"label": ..., "blurb": ...}` (or a reserved key
  inside `TEST_CHECKLIST` itself) so a module inventing its own category gets
  a real, named section instead.
- `tool_loader.discover_actions()` extracts this the same way it already
  extracts `TOOL_KEYWORDS`/`TOOL_PACK_INSTRUCTION`: optional, validated
  against the same shape `test_checklist_coverage.py` enforces for the
  static file, and rejected-with-a-log (not a crash) if malformed — matching
  every other optional field's failure mode in that loader.
- The panel needs a way to actually see these at runtime. The static
  `test-checklist-data.js` is loaded as a plain script tag; auto-discovered
  and custom-tool entries only exist inside the running `jarvis` process.
  Extend whatever `GET /api/tools` already returns (or add a sibling route)
  to include each tool's `TEST_CHECKLIST` entry when present, and have
  `test-checklist.js` merge that into `window.JARVIS_TEST_CHECKLIST` at load
  time — shipped entries from the static file, auto-discovered/custom entries
  from the live catalogue, identical rendering either way. A tool with
  neither keeps today's bare-name **NO CHECKLIST** treatment.
- Custom Tools' own starter templates (`custom_tools_store.py`'s point 4,
  "Templates — a starter for each shape of tool") should include a
  `TEST_CHECKLIST` example in every template it hands the user, not just
  document the field in prose somewhere else — the person most likely to
  need this is exactly the person with no reason to have read
  `actions/_template.py` first.

**Documentation — do this well, not as an afterthought.** This needs the
same treatment `_template.py` already gives `TOOL_KEYWORDS`/
`TOOL_PACK_INSTRUCTION`: a clearly marked, example-carrying section in
`actions/_template.py` itself, so hand-written modules (`git_tools.py`-style)
and Custom Tools' generated files both start from the same documented
contract — not just a mention in this plan. Also update
`test-checklist-data.js`'s own header comment (the "FORMAT" section quoted
above) to say explicitly that this is now one of two ways an entry can
exist — shipped here, or supplied by the tool's own module — so someone
reading that file in isolation doesn't conclude it's still the only source
of truth.

### As built (rev. 2026-09-21d)

**Files.** New `jarvis-cli/jarvis/checklist_schema.py`, `tests/test_checklist_supplied.py`.
Changed: `tool_loader.py`, `tools.py`, `custom_tools_store.py`,
`actions/_template.py`, `web/public/test-checklist.js`, `custom-tools.js`,
`test-checklist-data.js`, `tests/test_checklist_coverage.py`, AGENTS.md,
REPO_MAP.md, `web/README.md`. No server route, CLI command or storage was added.

**Against the requirement, bullet by bullet**

| Requirement | Built |
|---|---|
| Optional module-level `TEST_CHECKLIST`, same per-tool shape | ✔ dict of tool name → entry. `group` may be left out (it *is* the module's `TOOL_GROUP`) or given, in which case it must equal `TOOL_GROUP`. |
| "Per type": label/blurb for a brand-new `TOOL_GROUP` | ✔ `TEST_CHECKLIST_GROUP = {"label", "blurb"}` — the plan offered this or a reserved key; a separate name won because it can't collide with a tool called that. Fallback when a group has no label: the panel prettifies the id (`my_group` → "My group"), so a tool is never dropped for lack of a label. |
| Loader extracts it like `TOOL_KEYWORDS`, validated, rejected-with-a-log rather than a crash | ✔ **with one deliberate difference** — see decision 1. |
| Panel sees them at runtime; merged; identical rendering; neither → bare **NO CHECKLIST** | ✔ per-tool `checklist` / `checklist_group` on `tools_list_payload()` items (the list stays a list). `mergeCatalogue()` in `test-checklist.js`. One addition to "identical rendering": a small "From the tool's own file" badge in the detail pane, so a tester knows which file to edit. |
| Custom Tools templates carry an example in **every** template | ✔ all four (`minimal`, `ui`, `ask`, `http`); `test_every_starter_template_carries_a_valid_checklist_example` fails if a new template lacks one. Their group is `custom`, which is now a shipped, labelled group ("Custom tools"). |
| Documentation "done well": `_template.py` section + the data file's FORMAT header | ✔ `_template.py` §8 (why it exists, which home to use, field-by-field, failure mode, where it surfaces) with a live example that a test validates; the data file header now opens with "one of two places an entry can live". |

**Decisions made (change any of them and say so)**

1. **A malformed entry never rejects the tool file.** `TOOL_KEYWORDS` /
   `TOOL_RESULT_SPECS` errors reject the whole module; copying that would take a
   working custom tool offline over a typo in its *test notes*. Instead the entry
   is dropped, discovery logs `[checklist] file.py: <why>`, and — since stderr is
   where nobody looks — the Custom Tools editor's **Check** and **Save** now show
   what was ignored, and which tools have no entry yet. (Persona validation
   already worked this way; it is the closer precedent.)
2. **Shipped wins if a tool is in both places** — and the coverage test *fails*
   on it, so one tool has one home. The panel's tie-break is a backstop.
3. **The payload is the transport**, not a sibling route: fewer moving parts, and
   no new CLI verb to reserve in the three diverging `RESERVED_NAMES` sets. Cost:
   `/api/tools` grows by the size of the supplied entries, bounded by the caps in
   `checklist_schema.py` (all roughly 2× or more the longest shipped field).
4. **`window.JARVIS_TEST_CHECKLIST` is not mutated.** The plan said to merge into
   it; the panel instead keeps that global as exactly the shipped file and rebuilds
   a merged view (`JarvisTestChecklist.catalogue()`) on every live read. Otherwise
   deleting a custom tool and pressing Refresh would leave its entry behind.
5. **Stricter than before, for both homes:** unknown keys (`watchs`, `need`) and
   unknown step keys are now errors, and there are length caps. All 170 shipped
   entries already conform; the point is that a typo in a custom tool's entry is
   caught instead of silently rendering nothing.
6. **Untrusted input:** an entry is plain data from a file a person wrote, but it
   is still checked to be JSON-serialisable before it can reach
   `jarvis tools-list` (one object() in a `run` block would otherwise break the
   Debug panel and the checklist for everyone), and the panel re-checks shape
   before rendering. Everything is inserted with `textContent`, as before.

**Tests.** `tests/test_checklist_supplied.py` (18 checks): extraction and
group defaulting; a matrix of 13 malformed entries all dropped-and-logged with
the tool still registering; a rejected file contributes no entry; group labels;
end-to-end from a real `~/.jarvis/tools` file to the `tools-list` payload (only
the supplying tool gains the keys; junk is dropped and the payload stays JSON);
the editor's check/write report; every template; `_template.py`'s example; and
the JS merge under node (skipped if node is absent) including "shipped data never
mutated" and "junk from the CLI can't throw". `test_checklist_coverage.py` now
counts entries from both homes, validates through `checklist_schema`, and adds
"no tool in both places" (6 checks, was 5). A mutation check confirmed the
payload test fails if the field is not emitted.

**Gotchas found**
- `discover_actions()` caches imported modules in `sys.modules` by file *stem*,
  so a test that discovers two different sources under the same filename gets the
  first module back both times (looks like "my feature does nothing"). The new
  tests use a unique filename per case.
- `custom_tools_store.validate_source()` re-implements the loader's contract
  checks by hand instead of calling `tool_loader._validate`, so any new optional
  field has to be wired into **both**. G.1 does; the next one will need to as well.

**Not done / open**
- Not opened in a real browser (see the caveat in 0.0).
- The 16 first-draft entries from rev. 2026-09-20m (7 `browser_*`, 4
  `clipboard_*`, 5 path tools) are still drafts; they need someone to run each
  test and tighten the text, which no patch can do.
- No shipped tool was migrated to its own module's `TEST_CHECKLIST`; the 170
  shipped entries stay in the data file. Migration would be optional and
  mechanical, but has no payoff until someone wants entries next to code.
- A stale entry in a *custom* tool cannot show the panel's "Not in CLI" badge
  (its entry only exists while the tool does), which is the right behaviour.

## G.2 A module — custom tools included — can already supply more than one *tool* entry; make that explicit, and give it more than one *group* entry too

**Status: ✅ DELIVERED, rev. 2026-09-27d** (`jarvis-multi-group-checklist.patch`). See "As built (rev. 2026-09-27d)" below for the full breakdown.

**What already works, and isn't the gap.** `TEST_CHECKLIST` is a dict keyed
by tool name, so nothing in G.1's schema caps a module at one entry — a
module that registers several tools can already give each of them its own
`does`/`steps`/`expect` entry. The built-in example proves it today:
`browser_tools.py` is one module that supplies **one** `TEST_CHECKLIST_GROUP`
(the "browser" category — label + blurb) and **seven** separate
`TEST_CHECKLIST` entries, one per tool (`browser_goto`, `browser_click`,
`browser_fill`, `browser_get_text`, `browser_screenshot`, `browser_wait_for`,
`browser_close`). G.1's own opening line already says a module can supply
"its own checklist entry (**or entries**)" — the *tool*-entry side of this
was never actually limited.

**The gap.** Two places this isn't explicit enough:

1. **For custom tools specifically**, nothing says so in words a
   non-implementing user would read. The Custom Tools system's own
   convention — one file per tool (`~/.jarvis/tools/<name>.py` or `jarivs-cli/jarvis/actions/<name>.py`), one
   starter template per "shape of tool" (`minimal`/`ui`/`ask`/`http`) — makes
   it easy to assume a custom module is capped at one tool and therefore one
   `TEST_CHECKLIST` entry. Nothing enforces that cap, but nothing tells the
   user it isn't there either. If a hand-written custom module legitimately
   defines more than one tool in its `TOOLS` dict, it should supply a
   `TEST_CHECKLIST` entry for each one, exactly the way `browser_tools.py`
   does — this needs to be said in prose, with the `browser_tools.py`
   precedent named, not left to be inferred from the dict's type.
2. **`TEST_CHECKLIST_GROUP` itself is still singular per module** — the
   as-built decision in G.1 requires `group` (when given) to equal the
   module's one `TOOL_GROUP`. A module whose tools genuinely split across
   more than one logical category — plausible for a larger custom module, or
   a future built-in one — has no way to give each half its own labelled
   section; everything it supplies lands under one group whether or not that
   groups them sensibly. Let a module supply more than one
   `TEST_CHECKLIST_GROUP`-shaped entry, each tagged with the subset of its
   own tool names it covers, instead of exactly one tied 1:1 to `TOOL_GROUP`.
   The single-group shape stays the default for the common case (one module,
   one category); this only removes the cap for the module that needs more.

**Documentation — do this well, same as G.1.** Whoever builds this must
update **both** of the places G.1 already treats as the documentation
contract: this section (done — this is that update) and
`actions/_template.py`'s §8 (the `TEST_CHECKLIST`/`TEST_CHECKLIST_GROUP`
section G.1 added there). Add, in `_template.py`:
- An explicit line stating a module may supply as many `TEST_CHECKLIST`
  entries as it has tools, with a two-tool example (not just one), so a
  reader never has to infer this from the schema's type.
- The multi-group shape once built, with a short example showing a module
  splitting its own tools across two labelled sections.
Also touch `test-checklist-data.js`'s own header comment again, the same way
G.1's documentation bullet did, if the multi-group shape changes anything a
reader of that file in isolation would otherwise get wrong.

**Tests, once built.** Extend `tests/test_checklist_supplied.py` (which
already covers the one-group-many-tools shape via `browser_tools.py`-style
fixtures) with: a fixture module defining 2+ tools and confirming each gets
its own entry (regression-proofing what G.2 documents, not new behaviour);
and, once the multi-group shape lands, a fixture module supplying two groups
and confirming each tool's entry resolves to the right one.

### As built (rev. 2026-09-27d)

**Files.** Changed only — no new files this time (`checklist_schema.py` and
`test_checklist_supplied.py` already existed from G.1): `checklist_schema.py`,
`tool_loader.py`, `tools.py`, `custom_tools_store.py`, `actions/_template.py`,
`test-checklist-data.js` (header comment only — see G.1's own documentation
bullet, which asked for this file to be touched again if the multi-group
shape changed anything a reader in isolation would get wrong), AGENTS.md,
`tests/test_checklist_supplied.py`. `web/public/test-checklist.js`'s merge
function was **not** touched — see decision 1 below. Patch:
`jarvis-multi-group-checklist.patch`.

**Against the requirement, bullet by bullet**

| Requirement | Built |
|---|---|
| Document explicitly that a module may supply as many `TEST_CHECKLIST` entries as it has tools (already true, just unstated) | ✔ new paragraph in `_template.py` §8 ("A MODULE WITH MORE THAN ONE TOOL SUPPLIES MORE THAN ONE ENTRY"), and `_template.py`'s own live example now genuinely does this — two tools (`example_ping`, `example_echo`), not one |
| Let `TEST_CHECKLIST_GROUP` name more than one section, each tagged with the subset of the module's own tools it covers | ✔ second shape: `{group_id: {"label","blurb"}, ...}` — the plain `{"label","blurb"}` shape stays the default and is unchanged. Told apart from the single-group shape by key set alone (`is_multi_group_shape()`): a real group id is never exactly `label`/`blurb` |
| An entry's `group` may target one of the module's own declared sections, not just `TOOL_GROUP` | ✔ `extract_supplied()`'s valid-target set is `{TOOL_GROUP} ∪ declared_ids`; `TOOL_GROUP` itself stays valid whether or not the module also gives it its own meta under the multi-group shape |
| Update schema/loader/API/custom-tools editor | ✔ schema (`checklist_schema.py`), loader (`tool_loader.py`'s `ActionModuleRecord.checklist_group` now carries a dict of dicts), API (`tools.py`'s `AUTO_TEST_CHECKLIST_GROUPS` now keys per declared group id; `tools_list_payload()` needed **no change** — see decision 2), editor (`custom_tools_store.py`'s `validate_source()` — see decision 3) |
| Update Test Checklist merge + coverage tests + templates/docs | ✔ tests below; `_template.py` §8 rewritten with a worked two-tool, two-group example; `AGENTS.md`'s Test Checklist section and `test-checklist-data.js`'s header both updated. The JS merge itself needed **no code change** — see decision 1 |

**Decisions made (change any of them and say so)**

1. **The panel's JS merge function (`test-checklist.js`'s `_mergeCatalogue`)
   was not touched.** It already merges per tool item, keyed by that item's
   own `checklist.group` / `checklist_group` fields — it has no concept of
   "one module," only "one tool." Two tools from the same multi-group module
   therefore already land in two different sections with no code change on
   that side; the only thing that had to change was making sure the Python
   payload hands each tool item its *own* correct `checklist_group`, which
   `tools_list_payload()` already did (see decision 2). A dedicated
   regression test (`test_js_merge`, case 7) was added to pin this down
   rather than leave it as an untested assumption.
2. **`tools.py`'s `tools_list_payload()` needed zero changes.** Its existing
   lookup — `AUTO_TEST_CHECKLIST_GROUPS.get(supplied.get("group"))` — was
   already per-entry, not per-module; it only needed
   `AUTO_TEST_CHECKLIST_GROUPS` itself to be populated per declared group id
   instead of once per module's `TOOL_GROUP`, which is the one-line change
   in the aggregation loop just above it.
3. **`custom_tools_store.validate_source()` needed no new logic**, only
   updated comments. It already discards `extract_supplied()`'s `group_meta`
   return value entirely (the editor's Check button only ever needed entry
   presence/absence and `checklist_problems`), so an entry naming an
   undeclared group surfaces exactly the way any other malformed entry
   already did — one more line in `checklist_problems` — with no dedicated
   multi-group branch required. This is the "any new optional field has to
   be wired into both [loader and `validate_source`]" gotcha G.1's own
   section flagged; G.2 turned out not to need a second wiring here, only a
   comment explaining why not.
4. **An unhashable `"group"` value (a list or dict a module wrote by
   mistake) is checked for before the new set-membership test, not after.**
   The old code compared `entry["group"] != group`, which never raised on
   an odd type; the new code checks membership in a `{TOOL_GROUP} ∪
   declared_ids` set, which *would* raise on an unhashable value if asked to
   test membership directly — so the check is now `isinstance(entry_group,
   str) and entry_group in valid_group_ids`, reported as an ordinary
   dropped-entry problem instead of a crash. Never raises, same guarantee
   `extract_supplied()` already made for G.1.
5. **Declaring meta for `TOOL_GROUP` itself under the multi-group shape is
   allowed, not required.** `TOOL_GROUP` is always a valid `"group"` target
   for an entry (unchanged from G.1); a module using the multi-group shape
   can optionally also give `TOOL_GROUP` its own `{"label","blurb"}` entry
   in that same dict — `_template.py`'s example does, for completeness — but
   doesn't have to.

**Tests.** `tests/test_checklist_supplied.py` grew from 18 to 30 checks:
multi-group resolution (two tools, two groups, each entry lands in its own);
an entry defaulting to `TOOL_GROUP` even under the multi-group shape;
`TOOL_GROUP` itself as an explicit, valid multi-group target; an entry
naming an undeclared group dropped and logged; one bad id/meta among several
dropped without taking the others down with it; the `TEST_CHECKLIST_GROUP =
{}` edge case (still read as the single-group shape, not a zero-group
multi-group dict); a dedicated two-tools-one-group regression test
(protecting what was already true under G.1); an end-to-end `jarvis
tools-list` payload test proving two tools from one module carry two
*different* `checklist_group` values; a `validate_source()` test covering
both a valid and an invalid multi-group reference; and the JS merge case
described in decision 1. `_template.py`'s own example is re-validated by the
existing `test_the_actions_template_example_is_valid`, updated for the new
two-tool, two-group shape.

**Not done / open**
- Not opened in a real browser (same caveat as G.1).
- No shipped or auto-discovered built-in module actually uses the
  multi-group shape yet — only `_template.py`'s worked example. `G.1`'s own
  "not done" list already noted no shipped tool has been migrated to its own
  module's `TEST_CHECKLIST` at all; that's unchanged by G.2.

# Part H — UI: Daemons/Backlog/Log search rework, a full Schedules rework, and a notification on job creation

> **CURRENT AUDIT — 2026-09-22:** This part is **partial/rework-open, not “not started.”** The repo already has daemon, backlog, log-search and schedule panels with functioning baseline behavior. For example, the backend tracks daemon restart counts and the current front end has command-step drag/reorder; however, the requested Test-Checklist-quality redesign of these panels is not complete. The remaining work is mostly UI architecture/interaction quality plus log-search behavior, not creation of brand-new backend subsystems.


**CURRENT STATUS: PARTIAL / REWORK OPEN.** A functioning first-pass implementation already exists in the current repo; the requested high-quality rework remains. Raised directly by the owner, who called out the Test Checklist panel (Part G) by name as the quality bar: "it has to be high quality just like the test checklist UI."

> **See also (2026-09-30):** new, not-yet-implemented Daemons-panel bugs and features are recorded in Part L — **L.7** (false "not running" status), **L.8** (disable-notification layout break), **L.10** (open console in cmd), **L.11** (daemon categories), **L.12** (tool-supplied daemons), **L.13** (daemon favorites — **✅ built 2026-10-04b**, see its Built block).

## H.1 Daemons / Backlog / Log search: full rework to the Test Checklist bar

**Where these live today.** All three are still built the same way every panel
before Test Checklist was: markup inline in the ~80KB `index.html`
(`daemons-overlay`, `backlog-overlay`, `logsearch-overlay`), behaviour inside
the one ~420KB `app.js`, styling inside the one ~125KB `style.css`, all reusing
the generic `.debug-overlay`/`.debug-panel`/`.skills-pane` chrome the Debug and
Skills panels also use. Test Checklist is the one panel that broke from this:
its own `test-checklist.css`, `test-checklist.js`, and a data file
(`test-checklist-data.js`), with a real information architecture on top —
verdict/category filters, `/` search, keyboard shortcuts (↑/↓, 0–5), and an
Overview pane with progress and a "needs attention" list (Part G). That
difference in investment is exactly what the owner is pointing at.

Some hover/transition polish already landed on Backlog's `.kanban__card` and
Log search's `.logsearch-hit` (see the comments already in `style.css` around
those rules — cards used to be static with no hover feedback at all). That
polish is a good sign of direction but is not the same thing as the rework
being asked for here: none of the three has Test Checklist's dashboard pane,
keyboard shortcuts, or live-filtering search, and none has its own `.css`/`.js`
file.

**Goal.** Bring Daemons, Backlog, and Log search up to the same bar as Test
Checklist — a tester who has used the Test Checklist panel should not be able
to tell, from polish alone, that these three are older. Concretely, that
means (at minimum):

- **Split each into its own files**, the way Test Checklist did — e.g.
  `daemons.css`/`daemons.js`, `backlog.css`/`backlog.js`,
  `logsearch.css`/`logsearch.js` — rather than adding more weight to the
  shared `app.js`/`style.css`. Keep the markup each panel needs in
  `index.html` (Test Checklist's own overlay markup still lives there too;
  only its behaviour and data are split out), and check how `index.html`
  currently loads `test-checklist.js`/`.css` for the loading-order convention
  to follow (see the "Scripts load LAST" comment already in `index.html`
  around line 1485) — a panel that fires its own init before the DOM/other
  panels are ready has been the actual cause of bugs before (see that same
  comment's cross-reference).
- **Daemons:** a per-row live-state indicator (colour dot: running / stopped /
  crashed) rather than only the single `daemons-status-line` summary; a
  console (`daemon-console`) that distinguishes stdout / stderr / crash
  traceback instead of one flat `<pre>`; keyboard shortcuts to move between
  services and scroll the console; and a crash-loop indicator (a service that
  has restarted N times recently) surfaced in the list itself, not something a
  tester has to find by reading the raw console. Check whether the daemon
  status route already reports a restart count before adding one.
- **Backlog:** keep the kanban board (`backlog-board`, drag-reorder already
  works per the style.css comment — audit, don't reimplement), but add the
  Overview-pane treatment Test Checklist has: counts per column, a "blocked"
  roll-up, filter by project, and a search box that filters cards live. None
  of that exists today — `backlog-board` just renders whatever `backlog_list`
  returns, unfiltered.
- **Log search:** highlight the query term inside each `.logsearch-hit`
  (today the whole line renders unhighlighted); live search-as-you-type the
  way Test Checklist's `/` search works, instead of only searching on the
  `btn-logsearch` click; and a way to jump from a hit straight into the
  relevant Daemons console or Ask conversation instead of a dead-end result.

### H.1.1 Bug (owner-reported, 2026-09-25): false crash status + empty cmd window on start

**Status:** ✅ FIXED, rev. 2026-09-27 (`jarvis-h11-daemon-panel-fix.patch`) · **Priority:** P1

Two distinct problems, confirmed by direct code reading to have two
independent root causes, exactly as this section anticipated ("likely a
different root cause from the false-crash bug above, so don't assume one
fix resolves both" — correct call):

- **False crash indicator — FIXED.** Root cause: `daemons.status()`
  compared the persisted `status` field against live PID checks, and for
  `STATUS_STARTING` specifically it had no notion of "this just started, give
  it a moment" — the instant a status check landed in the real gap between
  `start()` writing `STATUS_STARTING` (which it does immediately, per its
  own docstring: "does not wait for the child to be healthy") and the
  supervisor later writing `STATUS_RUNNING` with an actual child pid, the
  child pid was still unset, `pid_alive()` correctly said not-running, and
  the old code read "claimed to be starting, isn't running yet" as an
  immediate crash. That gap exists on every single start, so this was a
  100%-reproducible false positive — not a race that only sometimes lost,
  literally the whole window every time. Fix: a bounded grace period
  (`STARTING_GRACE_SECONDS = 10`) scoped to `STATUS_STARTING` only. Within
  that window, `status()` also checks whether the supervisor process
  itself is still alive — if it's already exited (a real, immediate
  failure, e.g. a broken interpreter path), that's still reported as
  crashed right away, no waiting; only a supervisor that's alive but simply
  hasn't reported in yet gets the benefit of the doubt, and only up to the
  grace window. A previously-`STATUS_RUNNING` daemon disappearing is
  untouched by this — still reported crashed immediately, exactly as
  before, since that path never had the "just started" ambiguity.
- **Empty cmd window on start — FIXED.** Root cause: `start()`'s Windows
  branch used `creationflags = CREATE_NO_WINDOW | DETACHED_PROCESS` when
  spawning the supervisor process. This combination is a documented Windows
  gotcha: the two flags express contradictory intent — `DETACHED_PROCESS`
  means "no console at all, don't inherit one"; `CREATE_NO_WINDOW` means
  "create a console, just keep it hidden" — and combining them is widely
  reported to produce exactly the observed symptom (a window flashing
  visible instead of staying hidden). Telling evidence once traced:
  `run_supervisor()`'s own spawn of the actual daemon child process (a
  second, separate `Popen` call, one level down) used `CREATE_NO_WINDOW`
  alone with no `DETACHED_PROCESS`, and was never reported as showing a
  window — only the supervisor-launching spawn in `start()` had the extra
  flag mixed in. Fix: `start()` now uses `CREATE_NO_WINDOW` alone, via a
  new shared `_detached_creationflags()` helper both spawn sites can use,
  so the two can't drift apart like this again. `CREATE_NO_WINDOW` alone
  already achieves full detachment (no console is created at all, so
  there's nothing to inherit from or attach to) — `DETACHED_PROCESS` was
  redundant even before it became actively harmful.

**Done:**
- [x] Reproduced the false-crash reading against a daemon that is
      verifiably running (a live PID written directly, bypassing the race
      window) and traced it to the exact `status()` branch responsible —
      confirmed the gap is deterministic (present on every start), not a
      timing-dependent flake, so no long observation window was needed to
      pin it down.
- [x] Fixed the status determination so a running daemon reads as running,
      with the grace window scoped narrowly enough that a genuine
      RUNNING→gone crash is still detected with no added delay.
- [x] Traced how the daemon child process is spawned on start (two spawn
      sites: `start()`'s supervisor launch, `run_supervisor()`'s own child
      launch) and found the flag-combination discrepancy between them;
      suppressed the visible window without touching stdout/stderr capture
      (untouched — `run_supervisor()`'s console-log redirection was already
      correct and is unrelated to this fix).
- [x] Regression coverage for both: `tests/test_h11_daemon_status.py` (13
      checks / 10 tests) — a start that succeeds shows "running," not
      "crashed"; the Windows creationflags helper is verified to never
      recombine the two flags (tested via dependency-injected sentinel
      values, since the real `CREATE_NO_WINDOW`/`DETACHED_PROCESS`
      constants are both 0 outside an actual Windows host and would make a
      naive assertion pass for the wrong reason); a supervisor that's
      already dead is still caught immediately; a clean, requested stop
      still reads "stopped," never "crashed."

**Scope guard, honored.** No server routes or `daemon_*` tool contracts
were touched — the fix is entirely inside `daemons.py`'s existing
`status()`/`start()` functions. No UI styling from the broader H.1 rework
was touched either; this stayed a correctness fix, as scoped. (The same
guard still applies going forward to H.1's own remaining rework — the
daemon restart count above is the one already-flagged candidate) — call
those out explicitly rather than quietly widening scope.

**Independently verified (audited 2026-09-27, against `jarvis-main_57_`) —
this one checked out, unlike F.8/E.3/E.5 above.** Confirmed directly in

Delivered against this section's own goal list above — **Daemons only**;
Backlog and Log search, also named in H.1's original scope, are explicitly

this section already) to do the three one at a time. Per the patch's own
notes:

- **Own files, Test Checklist convention.** `daemons.css`/`daemons.js` now
  exist as standalone modules (own `$`/`el`/`api`/`toast` helpers, no

  `classifyLine()` further splitting `crash` out of `stderr` by traceback
  shape. Verified end-to-end against a real subprocess that writes to both
  streams and then raises. Existing daemon tests unchanged and still green

  `daemons.status()` already returned the `restarts` count this section

  independent modules). An auto-scroll toggle keeps the console pinned to

  convention, same as H.1.1 above):** `run_supervisor()`'s fast-crash
  `last_error` string is computed *after* the `=== exited with code …`
  banner is already written to the console, so the "last output" it
  reports is always that banner, never the process's real last line. Predates
  this patch, is a message-quality issue rather than a UI-panel issue, and
  is left alone here — worth its own small fix later (reorder, or skip the

#### H.1.2 Bug (owner-reported, 2026-09-27): every daemon shows as "crashed"

**Status:** ✅ FIXED, rev. 2026-09-27e (`jarvis-h12-h13-h14-daemons-fixes.patch`)
· **Priority:** P1

**Root cause, confirmed by direct code reading.** `daemons.status()`'s
handling of a stale `STATUS_RUNNING` record was unconditional: any daemon
whose `status.json` still said "running" but whose recorded child pid was no
longer alive read as `crashed`, regardless of whether the *supervisor*
watching that child was also still alive. `run_supervisor()` always writes
the real final status itself (`STOPPED`/`CRASHED`, with a reason) before it
ever exits normally — a genuine in-supervision crash never reaches this
auto-detection branch at all. The only way `status()` finds
`RUNNING`-but-gone with no final status ever written is something external:
a host reboot, the supervisor being force-killed, or a jarvis upgrade
replacing the running process. In every one of those, the supervisor is gone
too, and the old code didn't check that — so it labeled every one of them
"crashed" with zero positive evidence. This was not hypothetical: an
existing test (`test_workspace.py`) asserted this was the *intended*
behavior ("not asked to stop and it isn't there -> that's a crash, not a
stop"), which is what confirms the root cause rather than just a plausible
story.

**Fix.** The branch now checks whether the supervisor itself is also gone:
supervisor gone too + no stop requested → `stopped` (no evidence of a
crash); supervisor still alive + child gone → unchanged, still an
*immediate* `crashed` (the narrower case H.1.1's own regression test already
locks in, deliberately left untouched); `stop_requested` → `stopped` either
way, unchanged.

**Test change, not swept under the rug.**
`test_stale_running_status_is_reconciled_against_the_real_os` asserted the
old, now-reversed behavior for exactly the reboot scenario. Revised to
assert `STATUS_STOPPED`, with a comment explaining why, and a new sibling
test added to keep the "supervisor alive" case pinned down as still-crashed.

**New coverage:** `tests/test_h12_daemon_fixes.py` — 8/8 checks, 6 tests.
**Full suite re-run after the fix:** `test_h11_daemon_status.py` 13/13
(unaffected), `test_workspace.py` 75/75 (74 pre-existing + 1 new),
`test_browser_daemon.py` 18/18, `test_sched_daemon.py` 10/10 — all green.

#### H.1.3 Bug (owner-reported, 2026-09-27): no way to stop a running daemon

**Status:** ✅ FIXED, rev. 2026-09-27e (same patch) · **Priority:** P1

**Two related problems, one frontend (the one reported) and one backend
(found while fixing it).** `daemons.js`'s Start/Stop toggle keyed off
`entry.running` alone — a daemon mid `STATUS_STARTING` or
`STATUS_RESTARTING` (crash-loop backoff) is not `running` yet but its
supervisor is already alive, so the row showed "Start" with no way to stop
it. Fixed with a new `isStoppable(entry)` helper
(`Boolean(entry.running) || Boolean(entry.supervisor_pid)`) driving the
button's label and action; no new backend field was needed since
`supervisor_pid` in the API response already means "alive, or null."
Separately, `start()`'s own guard only checked `running`, so clicking the
old mislabeled "Start" button on a mid-backoff daemon would have spawned a
**second** supervisor over the first — fixed by also rejecting a start when
`current["supervisor_pid"]` is truthy.

**Confidence-note follow-up.** The earlier doc-only pass flagged H.1.2 and
H.1.3 as *possibly the same root cause*. On inspection that guess was
wrong: H.1.2's fix doesn't touch `entry.running` for genuinely-running
daemons (a truly-running daemon's Stop button was never broken); H.1.3 is a
real, separate, narrower gap in the starting/restarting transition states
specifically. Recorded here rather than quietly reconciled.

**No JS test harness in this repo** (same as every other `daemons.js`
change to date), so `isStoppable()` has no automated coverage directly; the
backend guard it depends on does
(`test_start_refuses_when_a_supervisor_is_already_alive`).

#### H.1.6 Bug (owner-reported, 2026-09-29): Daemons panel never shows "running"

**Status:** ✅ FIXED in code, rev. 2026-09-29 (`jarvis-h16-h17-daemon-running-and-console.patch`) — **verified on Linux and through a simulated Windows probe; not yet run on a real Windows machine** · **Priority:** P1

**Symptom (owner).** No daemon ever shows as *running*; every one reads **crashed** or **stopped**, including ones that are alive.

**Where it was.** The owner's own triage (comparing raw `/api/daemons` with the panel) put it in the **backend**, not the front end — so this entry's earlier hypothesis 1 (front-end/mock mismatch, ranked most likely when the entry was first written without source) was **wrong**, and hypothesis 2 was right. Recorded rather than quietly rewritten.

**Root cause, from reading `daemons.py`.** `pid_alive()` was `os.kill(pid, 0)` on every platform. On POSIX that is the standard existence probe. On Windows it is not: `signal.CTRL_C_EVENT` is `0`, so CPython turns `os.kill(pid, 0)` into `GenerateConsoleCtrlEvent(CTRL_C_EVENT, pid)`, which targets a console *process group*. For an ordinary pid it raises `OSError`, which the old code read as "no such process", so **every live pid looked dead**. `status()` then did exactly what it was written to do with two dead pids: a `STARTING` daemon (supervisor "gone") → **crashed**; a `RUNNING` one (child and supervisor "gone") → **stopped** (the H.1.2 reading). That is the whole symptom, for every daemon, on every poll. It also explains why the earlier suites never caught it: they run on POSIX, where the probe is correct. (Where the call does land it delivers a real Ctrl+C to the target, which is a second reason not to use it.) A live end-to-end run on Linux confirmed the *rest* of the chain — start → supervisor → child → `status()` — reports running correctly, which is what isolates the fault to the Windows probe.

**Fix.** On Windows `pid_alive()` now uses `OpenProcess(PROCESS_QUERY_LIMITED_INFORMATION)` + `GetExitCodeProcess` and compares to `STILL_ACTIVE` (259); it never sends a signal. Merely opening a handle is not enough (an exited process stays openable while anything holds a handle), hence the exit-code check. Access-denied counts as alive; a probe that cannot run at all assumes alive (same stance as `tasks._pid_alive`), so a probe failure can never make a live daemon look dead. POSIX behaviour is byte-for-byte unchanged. `_on_windows()`, `_win_kernel32()` and `_win_last_error()` are separate functions so the Windows branch is testable on any host.

**Tests.** New `tests/test_h16_daemon_pid_alive.py` — 22/22: the Windows branch driven through a fake kernel32 (running / exited-with-open-handle / unknown pid / access denied / unreadable exit code / probe failure, handles always closed, **`os.kill` asserted never called**); `status()` end to end through that branch (live child → RUNNING; STARTING with live supervisor → not crashed; both gone → stopped, so H.1.2 is kept; supervisor alive + child gone → crashed, so H.1.1 is kept); and a **real** daemon started through the real supervisor on the host OS, polled to RUNNING, held through repeated polls, stopped. Existing `test_h11_daemon_status.py` 13/13, `test_h12_daemon_fixes.py` 8/8, `test_workspace.py` 75/75, `test_h15_daemon_editor.py` 19/19 all still pass.

**Not verified — read this.** (1) **No real Windows run.** The Windows branch is exercised through a fake `kernel32`; the real `OpenProcess`/`GetExitCodeProcess` calls have not been executed anywhere. First thing to do after applying on Windows: start a daemon and confirm the card, hero pill and Running chip all say **Running**, then Stop it and confirm **Stopped**; if it still shows crashed, run `jarvis daemon-status <id>` and read the raw `pid` / `supervisor_pid`. (2) The Windows explanation of `os.kill(pid, 0)` is from CPython's documented behaviour and source, not from a Windows repro. (3) Same-pass implementation and test, not independently re-verified.

**Found, not fixed — same bug class elsewhere.** These still probe with `os.kill(pid, 0)` and will misbehave the same way on Windows: `sched_daemon._pid_alive` (line ~55), `channels/discord_gateway._pid_alive` (~101), `doctor._pid_alive` (~641). `tasks._pid_alive` already handles Windows correctly (its comment claims to mirror `sched_daemon`'s, which it does not). Out of scope for a daemon-panel fix; worth one small follow-up that routes them all through `daemons.pid_alive`. `sched_daemon` is the one to look at first — the Jarvis scheduler daemon is a built-in that this panel shows.

**Acceptance.** A daemon that is actually running shows **Running** in the card, hero pill, Overview ring and Running chip count on the real stack. **Met on Linux; owed on Windows.**

#### H.1.7 Bug (owner-reported, 2026-09-29): Daemons console Error / System / Output detector misfiles lines

**Status:** ✅ FIXED, rev. 2026-09-29 (same patch) · **Priority:** P2

**Symptom (owner).** "The error/system/etc console detector is not working properly." No specifics were given, so the classifier (`classifyLine` / `annotateLines` in `daemons.js`) was run against realistic console text and every misfile below was **reproduced before it was fixed**.

**Defects found and fixed** (all in `web/public/daemons.js`; the backend's `E: ` stderr marker and console format are unchanged):
1. **A daemon's own timestamp made its stdout "System".** Any `[YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM:SS] ` prefix was treated as a supervisor line. Only `=== ` banners and `<<< ` stdin echoes are System now; other stamped text is Output.
2. **Routine stderr logging counted as errors.** Python `logging`, discord.py, uvicorn, Flask and similar write INFO/DEBUG to stderr, so the Errors chip and the "N error lines" counter filled with health-check noise. A stderr line that states an INFO/DEBUG/NOTICE/TRACE level (bare, in brackets, or behind a timestamp) is Output now; WARNING and unlevelled stderr stay under Errors. Blank stderr lines no longer count as errors.
3. **Errors written to stdout were invisible to the Errors filter.** A daemon logging to stdout (`print`, `console.log`, a `2>&1` shell wrapper) never showed anything under Errors, and a Python traceback on stdout was plain output. An explicit ERROR/CRITICAL/FATAL level, or a traceback, is an error wherever it was written; the traceback state machine now tracks which stream a block started on, and a stdout line interleaved mid-traceback (the two pump threads race) no longer splits the block.
4. **Warnings drawn as crashes; JS stacks ungrouped.** `…Warning:` no longer counts as the end of a crash (a `DeprecationWarning` was rendered as a crash block), and Node stack frames (`    at fn (file:line:col)`) group with their `Error: …` line. The frame pattern is deliberately strict so prose like "at 12:30 pm" is not read as a frame.
Also: `=== restart limit reached` is now flagged bad like a failing exit.

**Design note.** Severity detection is upper-case-only and anchored to the start of the line (after an optional timestamp), so prose beginning with "info" or "error" is not read as a level. Classification is by explicit markers, not guesses about wording. `origin` (the stream the line arrived on) is kept on every item even when the line is reclassified.

**Tests.** New `tests/verify_daemons_console.js` — 37/37, each fix has a `REGRESSION:` check; run against the *original* `daemons.js` it fails at the first regression, as it should. `verify_daemons_panel.js` still 111/111.

**Not verified.** Not opened in a real browser against a live daemon (same limit as H.1.5); the classifier is pure and is tested as such, but the chip counts and colours were not eyeballed. Levels in formats not covered (JSON log lines, `pino`, `level=info` key-value) are not recognised and fall back to the old stream-based reading. **Known limitation, unchanged:** a stdout line that begins with the literal text `E: ` is indistinguishable from a stderr line on disk (e.g. `apt`'s "E: Unable to locate package" when it arrives on stdout); fixing it means changing the console file format, which this patch deliberately does not.

### H.1 Backlog / Log search — rework delivered, rev. 2026-09-29 (`jarvis-h1-h2-backlog-logsearch-schedules-rework.patch`)

Delivered against this section's own goal list above — **Backlog and Log
search** (the two H.1 panels the rev. 2026-09-27c Daemons delivery left
open), plus Schedules (see H.2's own delivered note below), in one patch.
`daemons.js`/`daemons.css`/`#daemons-overlay` were deliberately **not
touched** (another agent was working on Daemons at the time; `git status` on
the patched tree shows no Daemons file changed).

**Both panels:** own `.css`/`.js` files (`backlog.css`/`backlog.js`,
`logsearch.css`/`logsearch.js`), same standalone-module shape as
`daemons.js` (own `$`/`el`/`api`/`toast` helpers, `window.JarvisBacklog` /
`window.JarvisLogSearch` = `{open, close, isOpen}`), loaded after
`daemons.js` per `index.html`'s "Scripts load LAST" convention. Their inline
blocks are gone from `app.js`; the menu items now call the modules. Both
panels' markup was rebuilt in `index.html` (toolbar row, two-column body).
Keyboard shortcuts follow the pattern the other reworked panels use.

**Backlog**
- **Live search** (title/project/note/blocked-on) and a **project filter**,
  both client-side over the already-fetched board (the board is small;
  refetching per keystroke would only be a slower version of the same filter).
- **Overview pane** built entirely from data `backlog.summary()` already
  returned but the old panel never read past a status-line count: counts per
  column (with bars), a **blocked roll-up**, a **stale-in-Doing roll-up**
  (`stale_doing`), and a **project list** with open/total/blocked per project
  that doubles as a second project picker. Clicking a blocked/stale entry
  filters the board to it.
- **Drag-and-drop between columns — newly implemented, not audited.** This
  section's own goal list said drag-reorder "already works per the style.css
  comment — audit, don't reimplement." The audit result: **it did not.**
  There was no `dragstart`/`dragover`/`drop` handler for the kanban anywhere
  in `app.js` (K.4.2's own clarification — that the only drag code belongs to
  the saved-command step editor — was correct). It now exists: dropping a card
  on another column PATCHes its `state`, and leaving the Blocked column also
  clears `blocked_on`, mirroring the Block button's own rule. The advance /
  Block / × buttons are unchanged. **Not done:** this moves cards *between*
  columns; it does not reorder within a column (not checked whether
  `backlog.py` has any persisted order to write to).
- Keyboard: `/` search, `r` refresh, Escape (clears search first). **No arrow
  navigation between cards** — not built.

**Log search** (the `#logsearch-overlay` raw-file panel)
- **Live search-as-you-type** (300 ms debounce; Enter/button still search
  immediately) and **query-term highlighting** in both the results and the
  detail pane, built from the chosen mode (words / phrase / regex).
  Highlighting is cosmetic — the backend decides what matched; a regex that
  doesn't compile as a JS regex just renders unhighlighted.
- **Two-pane layout:** results list plus a detail pane showing the hit's
  context lines (the panel already requested `context` — it just never
  displayed anything beyond the matching line; now `context=2`, limit 150,
  up from 1 / 120), with Copy line / Copy path.
- **Sets are individual checkboxes** (Conversations / Daemon consoles /
  Scheduler / Notifications) instead of one single-choice select.
  `log_files.SEARCH_ROOTS` already had a `notifications` set the old dropdown
  never offered.
- **Jump to source:** a `logs/<id>.jsonl` hit → opens that conversation
  (via a new narrow `window.JarvisAsk.openConversation(id)` hook exported from
  `app.js`); a `daemons/<id>/console.log*` hit → opens the Daemons panel
  through the already-public `JarvisDaemons.open()` and toasts which daemon to

  a `sched_ask_log.jsonl` hit → opens Schedules.
- Keyboard: `/` focuses the query, ↑/↓ moves between hits, Enter runs the
  selected hit's jump, Escape clears the query first then closes.

**Scope clarification found while writing this up:** Part 0's "log deep
search still Enter-driven" and K.4.3's "local conversation filtering plus

## H.2 Schedules panel: full rework (upgraded from "a slighter pass," 2026-09-25)

**Scope change.** Originally scoped as "a slight rework, not a rebuild" —
explicitly narrower than H.1. The owner has since escalated this to the
**same Test-Checklist-quality bar as H.1**, after flagging that the panel is
missing whole categories of interaction, not just polish: *"the schedule
page doesn't have scheduler options (aka task prompt, ask, etc.) — it's
pretty bad, it needs a full rework."* Treat H.2 as no longer scope-guarded
below H.1 — apply the same file-split, componentization, and interaction
bar.

Current state: `sched-overlay` is plain `.menu-overlay`/`.menu-panel` chrome,
`sched-list` is a bare `.skills-list`/`.skills-pane--list`, and the add row
(`sched-when`/`sched-message`) is the only interaction beyond the list
itself — no grouping by kind (reminder / notify / task / watch), nothing at
a glance distinguishing a one-shot job from a recurring one or a healthy job
from a paused/failing one without opening it, and — the newly-flagged gap —
**no way to actually configure a scheduled task's own options from this
panel**: no task-prompt field, no ask-vs-notify-vs-watch kind selector
exposed as real controls, nothing beyond the raw `sched-when`/`sched-message`
pair. Creating anything beyond the simplest reminder currently requires
going through Jarvis conversationally rather than the panel itself.

To do:

- **Split into its own files** (`schedules.css`/`schedules.js`), matching
  H.1's file-split requirement and loading-order convention, rather than
  staying inside the shared `app.js`/`style.css`.
- **Expose real scheduler options in the create/edit UI**, not just
  `when`/`message`: job kind (reminder / notify / task / watch), the task
  prompt itself when kind is `task`/`ask`, and whatever other fields
  `scheduler.create()` already accepts server-side but the panel doesn't
  surface. Audit `scheduler_tools.py`'s creation paths (L.1/H.3 already
  touch these) for the full accepted field set before designing the form —
  don't invent fields the backend can't accept, and don't leave fields the
  backend does accept unreachable from the UI.
- Group or filter `sched-list` by job kind.
- Show next-run time and recurrence directly on each row, not only in a
  detail view.
- Visually distinguish a paused/failed job from one running normally.
- **Overview-pane treatment** matching Test Checklist/H.1: counts per job
  kind, an at-a-glance paused/failed roll-up, and a search/filter box.
- Keyboard shortcuts consistent with the other reworked panels, if H.1's
  pattern is already established by the time this lands.

**Order note.** Land after L.4's repro/fix where practical — L.4 concerns
whether displayed/persisted times are even correct, and building a richer
schedules UI on top of a value that's already known to be wrong risks
polishing a bug. It's fine to build the file-split and new option fields in
parallel with L.4, but hold off on any "next-run" display polish until L.4's
root cause is understood.

### H.2 Schedules — rework delivered, rev. 2026-09-29 (`jarvis-h1-h2-backlog-logsearch-schedules-rework.patch`)

Delivered against H.2's own to-do list above, in the same patch as H.1's
Backlog / Log search note.

- **Own files:** `schedules.css`/`schedules.js` (`window.JarvisSchedules` =
  `{open, close, isOpen, refresh}`). `app.js`'s ~110-line inline block is
  gone; the `scheduled-tick` WebSocket handler now calls
  `JarvisSchedules.refresh()` (a no-op when the panel is closed or never
  built). The overlay moved from the smaller `.menu-overlay`/`.menu-panel`
  chrome to `.debug-overlay`/`.debug-panel` and a 3-pane layout (jobs |
  new-job form or job detail | Overview), collapsing to a stacked column at
  900 px.
- **The P1 gap — scheduler options in the create UI.** A real create form
  with a **kind selector** (Reminder / Notify / Task / Watch). Task offers
  Ask (prompt) / Command (saved-command name, JSON args) / Tool (tool name,
  JSON args), with name pickers fed by `/api/commands` and `/api/tools`.
  Watch is an add/remove list of `if_screen_shows` / `then` conditions plus an
  optional `otherwise`. **Advanced options:** channels (all seven from
  `notifier.CHANNELS`), importance level (1–5, labels checked against
  `notifier.LEVEL_NAMES`), repeat count, and for Task/Watch title override,
  catch-up, report-when-done, and emit-on-done. The form field set was
  derived from `scheduler_tools.py`'s real signatures, not invented.
- **How creation works — no new create route.** The form calls the existing
  `POST /api/tools/run` with `remind_me` / `notify_me` / `schedule_task` /
  `schedule_watch` (the Debug panel's direct tool path). The old panel's
  `sched-add` route is deliberately minimal (`cli.py` says so: anything that
  *runs* something goes through the panel or the AI tools). Because the
  tools call `scheduler.create()` untrusted, **the approval gate still
  applies exactly as from a conversation** — a task/command/tool job lands in
  `needs_approval` and is approved with the same Approve button; this form is
  not a way around it. Notify with a blank *When* sends immediately, matching
  the tool. `POST /api/scheduled` is no longer used by the panel; left in
  place, unchanged. **Side effect to know about:** a job created this way is
  not tied to a conversation (`conv_id` is empty), unlike one created by
  asking.
- **One new read-only route:** `GET /api/scheduled/:id` → `sched-show`, same
  id validation as the existing per-job action route. Needed because the list
  endpoint only ever returned `summarize()` shapes (action *type*, never the
  prompt/command/tool text, channels, level or repeat state), so a detail pane
  had nothing to show. Clicking a job now shows all of it.
- **Kind and status filtering, live search:** chips for kind (All / Reminder /
  Notify / Task) and status (All / Needs approval / Paused / Failed), combined
  with a search box. Each row shows a status dot, kind tag, action-type tag,
  its `when` text and "in X", and is colour-marked when paused / awaiting
  approval / errored.
- **Overview pane:** counts per kind, a needs-attention roll-up (approval /
  paused / failed), a "next up" list of the five soonest jobs, and the recent
  signal events and last-tick time — the last two were already returned by
  `scheduler.overview()` on every list call and never read.
- **Keyboard:** `/` search, `n` new job, ↑/↓ between jobs, Escape (clears
  search first).
- **Watch badge is a heuristic.** `schedule_watch` creates an ordinary task
  with an `ask` action (its own docstring says so); the list tags such a job
  "watch" only when its title starts with `Watch: ` (the tool's default). A
  custom-titled watch shows as a plain `ask`, and a hand-written ask job with
  that prefix would show as a watch. Cosmetic only — the filters use the real
  `kind`.
- **Order note satisfied:** H.2 asked to hold next-run display polish until
  L.4's root cause was understood; L.4 is fixed (2026-09-26). The panel shows
  whatever `summarize()` returns, not a client-side recomputation. Not
  re-checked visually against a live scheduler.
- **H.3 interplay:** creation now goes through the tool handlers, so a
  creation-confirmation hook implemented in `scheduler_tools.py` would cover
  panel-created jobs automatically; one implemented only in the web layer
  would not. H.3 itself was **not started at that point; built 2026-10-04d** — and because it hooks the tool handlers, panel-created jobs are covered.
- **Not done, flagged:** editing an existing job's fields — H.2 says
  "create/edit," but the scheduler has no update-fields operation (only
  cancel / pause / resume / snooze / approve), so only creation was built;
  `schedule_watch`'s optional `context` field isn't exposed; command/tool
  arguments are a raw JSON textarea, not per-field controls.
- **Verification:** same status as the H.1 note above — syntax-checked and
  applied cleanly to a fresh tree, **not opened in a browser**. One real bug
  in this delivery was found and fixed during the write-up rather than
  shipped: Notify's Advanced "Title override" duplicated its own Title field
  and was silently ignored on submit; it is now Task/Watch only.

## H.3 Every scheduled-task creation should send a confirmation notification — ✅ BUILT 2026-10-04d (`jarvis-h3-creation-confirmation.patch`; see the Built block at the end of this section)

**Current behaviour.** `tool_schedule_task`, `tool_remind_me`,
`tool_schedule_watch`, and the `when`-given branch of `tool_notify_me` (all in
`scheduler_tools.py`) create the job through `scheduler.create(...)` and
return `_ok(job)` straight to the caller — none of them calls
`notifier.notify(...)` at creation time. The only notification a job produces
today is when it actually fires, later. So confirmation that something got
scheduled exists only as text in that one chat turn's reply; nothing reaches
the user's other channels (whatever `notifier.CHANNELS` covers), and nothing
is recorded in Notifications history marking that the job was set up in the
first place — only that it later ran.

**To do.** After `scheduler.create()` succeeds in each of
`tool_schedule_task` / `tool_remind_me` / `tool_schedule_watch`, fire a
`notifier.notify(...)` confirming the job was created: title along the lines
of the job's own title, message summarizing what + when — e.g. "Reminder set
for tomorrow 9am: <message>." Reuse `_channels(args)` (already used to route
the job's own eventual notification) so the confirmation goes to the same
places. Whether `tool_notify_me`'s `when`-given branch gets the same treatment
is worth deciding explicitly — it's the same code path as the other three, so
consistency argues for it.

**One thing to get right:** `tool_notify_me`'s `when`-*omitted* branch already
calls `notifier.notify(...)` directly to deliver the message right now — that
one must NOT also get a "scheduled" confirmation layered on top, since nothing
was scheduled; it already **is** the notification.

**One thing to decide with the owner:** whether this confirmation should be
suppressible (e.g. `args.get("confirm", True)`) for a subagent or automated
flow that creates several jobs back-to-back and doesn't want a notification
per job — a burst like that could otherwise spam every channel at once.
Default to sending it; make it optional if it turns out to be noisy in
practice.

**Related work already on the list:** route this through the same "audit
every place that creates a notification" pass D.2 already calls for — check
whether these new creation-time notifications need the same
summary/raw-JSON stripping D.2 describes for fire-time notifications.

**Built 2026-10-04d — `jarvis-h3-creation-confirmation.patch` (against `jarvis-main_79_.zip`).**
Owner instruction: pick a good but not too big feature and build it, not a
daemon / front-end / conversation-or-console-storage task (another agent is
working there), then document it. H.3 fits: it lives entirely in
`scheduler_tools.py` and `notifier.py`, touches no `web/` file, no
`daemons.py` and no conversation or console store.

- **What now happens.** After `scheduler.create()` succeeds, `remind_me`,
  `schedule_task`, `schedule_watch` and `notify_me` **when `when` is given**
  each call one new helper, `_announce_created(job, args, context)`, which
  sends **one** notification of a new kind, `"scheduled"` — title "Reminder
  set" / "Task scheduled" / "Notification scheduled", message like
  `Reminder set — at today 09:47 (in 59m): call mum`. The wording of *when*
  comes from `scheduler.summarize()`, the same function the list views use,
  so the confirmation can never describe the time differently from
  `list_scheduled`. The notification carries the job id and the conversation
  id, so it is linked to the job in Notifications history.
- **Decisions the plan left open, and what was chosen** (none confirmed by
  the owner — change any of them if wrong):
  1. **`notify_me` with `when`** gets the confirmation (consistency, as the
     section argued). **`notify_me` without `when` does not** — it *is* the
     notification; a test asserts exactly one `notify()` call, of kind
     `notify`.
  2. **Suppressible: yes.** Each of the four schemas gained an optional
     boolean `confirm` (default true). `false`, and the string spellings
     `"false"`, `"no"`, `"0"`, `"off"`, turn it off — for a subagent or
     automated flow creating several jobs back to back.
  3. **Level: its own kind, default 2 (standard).** `notifier.DEFAULT_CONFIG
     ["levels"]` gained `"scheduled": 2`, so the confirmation can be turned
     down to **1 (inbox only)** in `notify_config.json` without touching the
     reminder that fires later. The job's own `level` is deliberately **not**
     passed on: a job set to level 4 broadcasts when it fires, not when it is
     merely created. An existing user config file picks the new default up
     automatically (`_load_config` merges `levels`).
  4. **Channels:** the explicit `channels` argument is passed through
     (`_channels(args)`), as the plan said; with none given the notifier
     decides from the level. Digest batching applies as to any level 1–2
     notification.
  5. **A job parked for approval** says so in the confirmation (`Waiting for
     your approval: web console → Scheduled, or jarvis sched-approve <id>`)
     — the one moment the owner most needs to be told.
  6. **Failure isolation:** `_announce_created` never raises and never
     changes the tool's result (no new keys). A notifier that throws leaves
     a successfully created job reported as created.
  7. **Nothing is sent when creation fails** (`needs_clarification`,
     `SchedulerError`).
- **Not covered, on purpose:** jobs created from the CLI (`jarvis sched-add`
  — the user typed it, the terminal already printed it), the web panel's
  create (it goes through these tool handlers via `/api/tools/run`, so it
  **is** covered and will send the confirmation too — worth knowing when
  testing the Schedules panel), the digest job `digest.py` creates for
  itself, and `daemon_schedule`. D.2's "audit every place that creates a
  notification" pass is still open; the confirmation text is short plain
  text built from the job, so it has no raw-output stripping to do.
- **Tests:** new `tests/test_h3_creation_confirmation.py`, **61/61** — one
  confirmation per tool with kind/job id/conversation id/wording checked;
  the no-`when` branch single-call check; `confirm` false and true spellings;
  nothing sent and nothing stored on a failed creation; channels honoured and
  level 4 not inherited; the real notifier with the real config (default 2,
  configured 1 honoured, job level untouched); the approval wording; a
  raising notifier; schema `confirm` on all four tools. Neighbouring suites
  (`test_scheduler`, `test_schedule_watch`, `test_notification_levels`,
  `test_sched_daemon`, `test_unattended_run`, `test_l16_*`,
  `test_tool_disable`, `test_checklist_*`) pass with the patch.
- **Build number:** `jarvis/*.py` changed, so `test_build_info.py` will report
  `build_info.py` stale until `python build_tools/bump_build_version.py` is
  run from `jarvis-cli/`. The patch does **not** include that regenerated file:
  the first L.38 patch (`jarvis-l38-raw-archive.patch`, now superseded) also edited it, so the build bump was left out to keep patches from conflicting on those lines. The current `jarvis-l38-raw-event-log.patch` does not bump it either; two patches that rewrite the same lines cannot both apply. Run the bump once after applying
  everything.
- **Not verified:** a live run through a real provider (the model has not yet
  been seen calling `remind_me` and the toast appearing), Windows toast
  delivery, the web console's rendering of a notification of an unknown kind
  (it falls back to the plain card, as `clipboard_watch` does — read, not
  seen), and the Test Checklist: **no checklist entry was added** because
  `test-checklist-data.js` is a front-end file in the other agent's area
  (acceptance row in J.3 is therefore still unticked).
