## I.6 As-built reference — the `/` command palette (rev. 2026-09-30c)

> Folded in from `SLASH_COMMANDS.md`, which describes the code in `jarvis-main_65_.zip`. The figures in sections 1, 5–7, 9 and 11 were re-checked against that archive on 2026-09-30c (35 verbs, 31 passthrough, 30 not exposed, tests passing); the behavioural descriptions were not re-exercised in a browser. Heading numbers below are the reference's own section numbers, so "section 13" means item 13 here. Where this plan's I.2 design and this reference differ, **this reference is what the code does.**

Everything about the slash commands in the Ask box: how to use them, every command,
how the engine decides what to do, how the pieces fit together, and how to extend it.

This file describes the code as it is in the repo (`web/public/slash-commands-data.js`,
`web/public/slash-palette.js`, the `JarvisHost` facade at the bottom of `web/public/app.js`,
`POST /api/slash/run` in `web/server.js`, and `jarvis skills-loaded` in the CLI).
Section 13 lists places where the registry and the CLI disagree.

Related docs, which this one does not replace:

- `DOCUMENTATION/COMMAND_PALETTE_TESTING.md` - the manual click-through checklist.
- `AGENTS.md` -> "The `/` command palette" - the rules an agent must follow when it adds a CLI subcommand or a Menu panel.
- `REPO_MAP.md` -> "The `/` command palette" - the short architectural summary.
- Master plan Part I.2 (I.2.1-I.2.11) and decisions D-I1 to D-I9 - the design history.

#### 1. What it is

Typing `/` at the very start of the Ask box opens a floating, keyboard-driven palette above
the composer. It has two levels:

- **Level 1 - verbs.** The command names, grouped Chat / Model / Skills / Run / Panels / View,
  each with a risk badge and a one-line summary.
- **Level 2 - arguments.** Once a verb is resolved and you type a space, the palette completes its
  argument from a live list (your chats, saved commands, installed or loaded skills, providers,
  services, capacity modes).

Beyond the 35 verbs, every other `jarvis-cli` subcommand is also visible. 31 of them can be run as
`/<cli-name> [args]` ("CLI passthrough"); the other 30 are shown greyed out with the reason they can't run
from a chat box.

It replaced the old `/skillload` / `/skillunload` regex and its inline suggestion box. There is now exactly
one place in the front end that parses a leading `/`.

Everything the palette does is **local**: no model call, no tokens. The footer says so ("local - no tokens").
The result of a command is shown as a **toast** (or a dialog for long CLI output); nothing is added to the
chat thread (decision D-I8).


#### 2. Using it

##### 2.1 Opening and closing

| Action | Result |
|---|---|
| Type `/` as the first character | Palette opens above the composer |
| `Esc` | Closes the palette; the Ask panel stays open. A second `Esc` closes the panel as before |
| Click elsewhere, or Tab out | Closes |
| Backspace the `/` away | Closes |
| `Shift+Enter` (makes the text multi-line) | Closes - a multi-line message is never a command |
| `hello /new` | Never opens: the slash must be at column 0 |

The popover is `position: absolute` against the composer row, so opening, filtering and closing it never
moves or resizes the thread or the input. It sits above modals' z-order baseline (`z-index: 30`, under
modals), is at most `min(56vh, 420px)` tall and scrolls inside itself. It only opens **above** the composer
(no flip-below).

##### 2.2 Keys (palette open)

| Key | Behaviour |
|---|---|
| `Down` / `Up` | Move the highlight; skips headings; wraps at the ends |
| `PageDown` / `PageUp` | Jump 6 rows |
| `Home` / `End` | First / last selectable row |
| `Shift+Tab` | Up one row |
| `Tab` | **Fills** the highlighted row into the box. **Never runs anything** |
| `Enter` | Completes *or* runs - see 2.3 |
| `Esc` | Close (see above) |
| `Shift+Enter` | Not handled by the palette; inserts a newline (and thereby closes it) |

IME: while an IME composition is in progress, `Enter` does nothing in the palette and is also not allowed to
submit the form.

With the palette closed, `Enter` sends the message and `Shift+Enter` makes a newline, exactly as before.

##### 2.3 What Enter does (the two-step rule)

`Enter` has two behaviours, chosen so that a half-typed prefix can never fire something costly.

- **Runs on the first Enter** only when the verb is all of: takes nothing required to fill in (`instant`),
  `riskTier` is `safe`, has no `confirm`, and is **not in the Chat group**. In practice: every panel opener,
  `/skills`, `/skillmake`, `/skilladd`, `/config`, `/skin`, `/help`.
- **Everything else completes on the first Enter and runs on the second.** That includes all Chat-group verbs
  (`/new /stop /clear /redo /copy`), anything with a required argument, and anything not `safe`.
  Example: type `/cl`, press `Enter` -> the box becomes `/clear` and nothing happens. A second `Enter` runs
  it (and `/clear` then asks for confirmation).
- A finished command (all required arguments present and valid against the lists the palette has cached) runs
  on `Enter`. The one exception: if a *different* first-Enter verb is highlighted, the highlight wins.

Because completeness is judged from cached lists, a stale or missing cache can only make `Enter` *complete*
instead of *run* - never run the wrong thing. On submit everything is re-resolved with fresh data.

##### 2.4 Mouse and touch

- Hover moves the highlight (a stationary pointer does not fight the keyboard after a scroll).
- **Clicking a row only fills the input**; it never runs the command, and focus stays in the box.
- Clicking a greyed-out row shows why it is greyed out as a toast.
- Rows are at least 40px tall at phone/touch width; below ~560px the description column is dropped from rows
  (the footer still describes the highlighted row).
- On touch there is no hover tooltip (see section 12).

##### 2.5 The footer

For the highlighted row the footer shows: one line saying what `Enter` will do (with the arguments typed so far
filled in), the risk badge, an example, "asks before running" where it applies, a `covers:` note (first 6
reserved names, then `+N`), the key hint (`Enter run|complete|retry|toggle - Esc close`), and
`local - no tokens` at the right.

##### 2.6 Risk badges

Every verb and CLI row carries a badge:

| Tier | Badge colour | Meaning (from AGENTS.md) |
|---|---|---|
| `safe` | quiet grey | Read-only or trivially reversible |
| `caution` | secondary accent | Changes state but scoped and recoverable |
| `dangerous` | red | Bulk-destructive, irreversible, or broad blast radius |


#### 3. Grammar - what counts as a command

`parse()` in `slash-palette.js` applies these rules to the raw textarea value:

| Input | Treated as |
|---|---|
| `/new` | Command, token `new` |
| `/chat weekend trip` | Command `chat`, rest `weekend trip` |
| `//new is just a word` | Prose. The submit handler strips **one** slash and sends `/new is just a word` (the escape hatch) |
| `/etc/hosts is odd` | Prose - a second `/` inside the first token means it is a path |
| `/ new` | Prose - a space directly after the slash |
| Any text containing a newline | Prose |
| A message with a **quote attached** (selected reply text) | Prose - never a command |
| `hello /new` | Prose |

**Exact match only.** On submit a verb or alias must match exactly (case-insensitive). A prefix never
auto-resolves; the palette list is how you complete one.

**Unknown verbs.**

- *Unknown and not close* (e.g. `/qwertyuiop`): sent as an ordinary message.
- *Unknown but within edit distance 2 of a known verb, alias or CLI name, 3+ characters* (e.g. `/nwe`, `/doctr`):
  **blocked once** with a warning toast, `No command "/nwe" - did you mean /new? Press Enter again to send it as a
  message.` Pressing `Enter` again with *identical* text sends it as a message. Changing the text, or typing
  anything, resets this.
- *A real reserved name that can't run from chat* (e.g. `/spotify-login`): blocked the same way, with its reason;
  a second identical `Enter` sends it as a message.

Near-miss detection compares against verbs, aliases and passthrough CLI names. It does **not** know saved-command
names.


#### 4. Matching and ranking

##### 4.1 Level 1 (verbs)

Score of the typed text against a verb name or alias:

| Match | Score |
|---|---|
| Exact | 100 |
| Prefix | 80 |
| Start of a word (split on space, `-`, `_`, `/`, `.`) | 60 |
| Substring | 40 |
| Subsequence (letters in order) | 20 |

- The better of the verb's own score and its aliases' scores wins (the row shows `alias /x` when an alias won).
- If nothing matched by name, the **summary** is tried, but only a real substring or word-start counts (score
  >= 40), and it is quartered. The subsequence rule is deliberately not used on descriptions: any three letters
  appear in order somewhere in a sentence, and that would also stop a typo like `/nwe` from reaching the
  "did you mean" check.
- Ties break by **most recently used** (see 4.3), then by registry order.
- Matched letters are emphasised with real DOM nodes (`.slash-hl`), never `innerHTML`.

**CLI commands** appear under a "CLI commands" heading only on a real *name* match (score >= 40), at most 8,
so a short query doesn't drown the verbs in plumbing.
**Can't run from chat** rows appear only when the query is 2+ characters and the name matches at score >= 60,
at most 6.

**With an empty query** (just `/`), the list is the six groups in order, then a **More** heading with a toggle
row "Show the other 61 commands" (`31 run from here, 30 can't`). Selecting it (Enter, or click then Enter)
expands a "CLI commands" section (31, enabled, tagged `cli`) and a "Can't run from chat" section (30, greyed).
It toggles back; closing the palette resets it.

If nothing matches: `No command "/xyz" matches` - `Enter sends it as a message`.

##### 4.2 Level 2 (arguments)

Rows are ranked by the best of: score against the label, the value, the id, and (quartered) the detail text.
A header chip shows progress, e.g. `/skillload > pick a skill - 3 of 24`. Skill and saved-command lists also use
the MRU for tie-breaking.

Arguments are split like this (`splitArgs`): every argument but the last is a single whitespace-delimited token;
the **last argument takes the rest of the line**, so a chat title or a file path can contain spaces.

##### 4.3 Recent use (MRU)

A small most-recently-used list lives in `localStorage` under **`jarvis.slash.mru`** (max 30 entries). Ids are
`v:<verb>` (also `v:<cli-name>`), `s:<skill>`, `c:<saved-command>`. **Chat titles are never stored.** If storage
is blocked, ranking just loses recency. MRU only breaks ties; it never changes which rows match.

##### 4.4 Caching

Argument lists are cached per source for **4 seconds**. A list you've opened before is painted immediately and
revalidated behind it (no blank "Loading..." flash). A failed load is **not cached**; it shows a selectable row
"Couldn't load the list" tagged `retry` (with the error text), and `Enter` retries.


#### 5. The 35 verbs

Columns: **Args** `<x>` required, `<x>?` optional. **Replying** = may run while Jarvis is still answering a previous
message. **Confirm** = asks before running. Examples are the registry's `example` field.

##### 5.1 Chat

| Verb | Args | Tier | Replying | Confirm | What it does |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `/new` | - | safe | yes | no | Starts a new conversation (`startNewConversation`) |
| `/chat` (alias `/switch`) | `<chat>` | safe | yes | no | Switches conversation |
| `/clear` | - | **dangerous** | **no** | **yes** | Clears this chat's history. Asks first; can't be undone |
| `/stop` | - | safe | yes | no | Cancels the reply in progress (sends `{type:"cancel"}` on the websocket) |
| `/redo` | - | safe | **no** | no | Re-runs your last prompt |
| `/copy` | - | safe | yes | no | Copies Jarvis's last reply as raw markdown |

Details:

- **`/chat <chat>`** - `/chat weekend trip`. Matches by exact title, exact id, or a **unique partial** title
  (prefix or word-start only; a mere substring doesn't count). Two partial matches ->
  `"x" matches N chats - pick one from the list.` (text stays). No match -> `No chat called "x".` (text stays).
  Rows show relative time (`just now`, `5m ago`, `3h ago`, `2d ago`, else a date), an origin badge (Discord /
  Instagram / Scheduled) and mark the open chat with a check and the tag `open`. When two chats share a title the
  row's inserted value is the **id** instead of the title. Covers `conv-switch`, `conv-list`, `conv-show`,
  `conv-search`.
- **`/clear`** - shares `clearAiChat()` with the toolbar Clear button; both show the same confirmation dialog
  (D-I7: the button used to clear on a single click). Covers `ai-clear`.
- **`/stop`** - with nothing running: toast `Nothing is running.`
- **`/redo`** - acts on the last element in the thread (`redoAskMessage`); with an empty thread: `No prompt to redo.`
  Refused while a reply streams. Covers `ai-drop-from`.
- **`/copy`** - copies the **whole** last Jarvis reply; empty chat -> `Nothing to copy yet.` (`/copy 2` for one code
  block waits on Part I.1, which is not built.)

##### 5.2 Model

| Verb | Args | Tier | Replying | What it does |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `/provider` | `<provider>` | safe | yes | Sets which AI provider(s) to try, in order |
| `/think` | `<level>` | safe | yes | Sets the thinking level, or shows/hides the trace |
| `/capacity` | `<mode>` | safe | yes | Switches the prompt's capacity mode |

- **`/provider`** - `/provider anthropic,openai`. Comma-separated, in try-order, or `auto` (clear the override).
  After a comma the list offers providers again. Errors (text stays): `auto` combined with names (`"auto" can't be
  combined with named providers.`); unknown names (`Unknown provider(s): x.`). Updates the picker label; the next
  ask uses it. Success toast: `Provider: auto.` or `Provider order: a -> b.` Providers reporting
  `enabled === false` or `available === false` are greyed ("not configured").
- **`/think`** - `off / low / medium / high` set the level; `show` / `hide` toggle the reasoning trace. Anything
  else: `Thinking level must be off, low, medium, high, show, or hide.` Current level (and current show/hide) is
  marked. Covers `think`.
- **`/capacity`** - modes come from the server (`/api/mode`, or the already-loaded `modeOptions`); the hint
  says "e.g. full / compact / ultra" but the real list is whatever the server returns. Unknown mode ->
  `Unknown capacity mode "x". Try: ...` with the real modes. Covers `mode`, `mode-set`.

##### 5.3 Skills

| Verb | Args | Tier | What it does |
|---|---|---|---|
| `/skillload` | `<skill>` | safe | Force a skill into context for this chat |
| `/skillunload` | `<skill>` | safe | Drop a manually-loaded skill (or `--all`) |
| `/skillmake` | - | safe | Open the skill manager on **New** |
| `/skilladd` | - | safe | Open the skill manager on **Import** |
| `/skills` | - | safe | Open the skill manager |

All are allowed while replying.

- **`/skillload pdf`** - `POST /api/skills/<name>/load` with the active conversation id. The skill's instructions
  are forced into every ask for this conversation until unloaded. Installed-skill rows mark already-loaded ones
  (check + tag `loaded`), show a `N ref` tag when the skill has references, and grey out **invalid** skills with
  their error. Unknown name -> `No installed skill called "x".`
- **`/skillunload pdf`** / **`/skillunload --all`** - `DELETE /api/skills/<name>/load`. The list offers only skills
  **currently loaded** for this chat (plus a `--all` row tagged `bulk`; if none are loaded it says "No skills are
  loaded"). A name that isn't loaded is refused: `"x" isn't loaded, so there's nothing to unload.` The list merges
  conversation-scoped and global loads; the palette can't tell you which.
- **`/skillmake`, `/skilladd`, `/skills`** - open the manager; make/add click the matching toolbar button
  (`#btn-skill-new` / `#btn-skill-import`). Covers `skills-*`, `skillmake`, `skilladd`.

All four load/unload/make/add actions run through `handleSkillSlashCommand()` in `app.js`, exposed as
`JarvisHost.skillSlash`.

##### 5.4 Run

| Verb | Args | Tier | Replying | Confirm | What it does |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `/run` | `<command>` `<vars>?` | caution | **no** | no | Runs a saved command |
| `/daemon` | `<action>` `<id>` | caution | yes | `stop`, `restart` | Start / stop / restart / check one service |
| `/organize-json` | `<path>` | safe | yes | no | Cleans up a messy JSON file |

- **`/run <name> [--var value ...]`** - `/run nightly-backup --target /mnt/data`. The name is the **longest** saved
  command name that prefixes the argument text. Variables are parsed from `--name value` or `--name=value`, with
  `"double"` or `'single'` quotes allowed. Variables the command has a default for are filled in; a variable with
  no default that you didn't supply -> `/run x needs --target.` (text stays); an option the command doesn't have
  -> `x has no --foo option.` Runs through the same `runSegments` path as the Commands panel's Run button and
  **does not ask for confirmation**, same as that button. Rows show each variable as `--x REQUIRED` or
  `--x=default`, and commands needing input carry the tag `needs args`. After the name, level 2 shows a free-text
  hint (`--var value ...`).
- **`/daemon <start|stop|restart|status> <id>`** - `/daemon restart discord`. Calls
  `POST /api/daemons/<id>/<action>`. Confirmation follows the Daemons panel's own rule: **`stop` always asks;
  `restart` asks only if the service is actually up** (`running` or has a `supervisor_pid`); restarting one that's
  down just starts it. `start` and `status` never ask. Service rows show a green (up) or grey (down) dot, and the
  `running` / status tag. Bad usage: `Usage: /daemon <start|stop|restart|status> <id>`; unknown action or id produce
  their own toasts. Covers `daemon-start/stop/restart/status`.
- **`/organize-json <path>`** - validated by the palette, then **passed through** (not handled there) to the
  `ORGANIZE_JSON_RE` branch already in the ask-form submit handler in `app.js`, which strips the leading slash.
  The bare form `organize-json <path>` keeps working. The chat bubble shows what you typed. Path is free text, so
  it can contain spaces.

##### 5.5 Panels

Each opens the matching panel. All are `safe`, take no arguments, run on the first Enter, and work while replying.
`menu` is the Menu item the verb is the typed twin of (tests enforce that every `menu-item-*` in `index.html` is
claimed by exactly one verb).

| Verb | Alias | Opens | Menu id |
|---|---|---|---|
| `/guides` | | Guides | `menu-item-guides` |
| `/debug` | `/tools` | Debug dashboard | `menu-item-debug` |
| `/checklist` | `/tests` | Test Checklist | `menu-item-testchecklist` |
| `/schedule` | `/sched` | Scheduled tasks & reminders | `menu-item-scheduled` |
| `/mcp` | | MCP servers & tools | `menu-item-mcp` |
| `/ctools` | | Custom Tools | `menu-item-ctools` |
| `/channels` | | Channels | `menu-item-channels` |
| `/daemons` | | Daemons | `menu-item-daemons` |
| `/backlog` | | Backlog | `menu-item-backlog` |
| `/logsearch` | | Log Search | `menu-item-logsearch` |
| `/setup` | | Setup | `menu-item-setup` |
| `/subagents` | | Subagents | *(none)* |
| `/notifications` | | Notifications | *(none)* |
| `/logs` | | This conversation's raw Logs | *(none)* |

(`/skills`, in 5.3, is also a panel opener with `menu-item-skills`.)

##### 5.6 View

| Verb | Args | What it does |
|---|---|---|
| `/config` | - | Opens Config (`openSettings`) |
| `/skin` | - | Opens Skin / persona settings (`openSkinModal`) |
| `/layout` | `<mode>` | `classic` (full multi-panel) or `focus` (just the chat); applies immediately and persists via `POST /api/ui-mode` |
| `/help` | `<verb>?` | Lists every command, or explains one |

- **`/help`** with no argument puts `/` in the box (which shows the full list). **`/help run`** shows a small
  card for that verb: summary, example, and its arguments. `/help nope` -> `No command called "nope".` The optional
  argument is why `/help` still runs on the first Enter (nothing is *required*), while `Tab` leaves room to type it.
  Its handler returns `"keep-open"` so the palette stays up.
- **`/layout`** rows mark the current layout.

##### 5.7 Which reserved names each verb "covers"

A verb's `covers` list names the `reserved_names.py` subcommands it is the reachable surface for (mostly plumbing
a panel already drives). Notable ones: `/config` covers `config`, `ai-config`, `playnite-config`, `spotify-config`,
`memory-config`, `everything-config`, `voice-config`; `/channels` covers 12 `channels-*` names; `/ctools` covers
8 `ctools-*` names; `/schedule` covers 8 `sched-*` names. The exact list per verb is in
`slash-commands-data.js`. Verbs with an empty `covers`: `/stop /copy /provider /run /guides /checklist /help`.


#### 6. CLI passthrough: `/<cli-name> [args]`

31 one-shot, headless subcommands run directly: `/doctor`, `/memory-recall foo`, `/logs-clear`, and so on.

**How it runs.**

1. Text after the name is split with a small shell-like splitter (whitespace, with `"..."` and `'...'` kept
   together) into an **argv array**.
2. `dangerous`-tier commands first open a confirmation modal showing the **exact command line**
   (`jarvis <name> <args>`), with the Cancel button focused so a stray Enter doesn't confirm. Cancel sends nothing
   to the server.
3. The client posts `POST /api/slash/run {name, args}`.
4. The server checks the name against the allowlist (see section 8.3) and runs `jarvis <name> <args...>` with
   `spawn()` - **no shell**. Shell metacharacters in what you typed are inert:
   `/memory-recall $(whoami) ; echo hi` searches for that literal text and executes nothing.
5. The result is shown (section 6.2).

Also: `/conv-delete <id>` for the conversation you currently have open is refused client-side
(`That's the chat you have open. Switch to another one first.`); after any `conv-*` command the sidebar refreshes.
Passthrough commands work while Jarvis is replying.

##### 6.1 The 31 commands

The **Usage** column is the registry's `usage` string, as shown in the footer. **Corrected 2026-09-30f** (`jarvis-slash-registry-fixes.patch`): every usage and summary below was re-read against its CLI handler; section 13 keeps the original findings. Tiers changed in that patch: `/memory-ns` safe→caution, `/console-clear` dangerous→caution. Two entries carry `maxArgs: 0` and take no arguments from the palette: `/subagent-keys` (also `secret`) and `/sched-clear`.

**Safe (13)**

| Command | Registry usage | Summary |
|---|---|---|
| `/doctor` | `[--deep] [--json] [--verbose] [group ...]` | Check the install for problems. Exit 1 means warnings, 2 means something is broken. |
| `/version` |  | Print the jarvis version. |
| `/memory-list` | `[--auto]` | List stored memories. --auto shows only the ones saved automatically. |
| `/memory-recall` | `<what you remember>` | Search stored memories. |
| `/memory-stats` |  | Show memory store statistics. |
| `/calendar-list` |  | List calendar entries. |
| `/calendar-events` |  | Show upcoming calendar events. |
| `/digest-status` |  | Show whether the daily digest is on. |
| `/digest-preview` |  | Preview the next digest without sending it. |
| `/policy` |  | Show the active permission policy. |
| `/policy-check` | `<tool> [--args JSON] [--context CTX]` | Check whether a tool call would be allowed. |
| `/policy-dry-run` | `<tool> [--args JSON] [--context CTX]` | Dry-run the policy against a tool call. |
| `/console-read` | `<conversation-id> [--since N] [--kinds a,b] [--turn T] [--limit N] [--surface S] [--after-last-clear]` | Read one conversation's stored console output. |

| Command | Registry usage | Summary |
|---|---|---|
| `/memory-ns` | `[namespace]` | List memory namespaces, or switch the active one. |

| `/memory-reindex` | `[--embeddings]` | Rebuild the memory search index. --embeddings also rebuilds the embeddings. |
| `/calendar-add` | `<name> <ics-url>` | Add an ICS calendar feed and check that it can be reached. |
| `/calendar-remove` | `<name>` | Remove a calendar feed by name. |

**Dangerous (6)** - confirm modal first

| Command | Registry usage | Summary |
|---|---|---|
| `/conv-delete` | `<conversation-id>` | Delete an entire conversation. Irreversible. |
| `/logs-clear` | `<conversation-id>` | Delete one conversation's stored log file. Irreversible. |
| `/sched-clear` |  | Remove every finished scheduled job (done, cancelled, error). Active jobs are kept. Irreversible. |
| `/notify-clear` | `[consumer]` | Empty the notification inbox. With a consumer name, only marks everything seen for that consumer. |
| `/notify-send` | `<message> [title] [channels,csv]` | Send a message to every configured channel. |
| `/mcp-call` | `<server> <tool> [json-arguments]` | Run an arbitrary MCP tool by name. |

##### 6.2 How the output is shown

- Output is stdout + stderr + any error text, joined and trimmed.
- **Success, a single line of 120 characters or fewer** -> a toast.
- **Anything longer or multi-line** -> a dialog with the text in a monospace block, truncated at 20,000
  characters (`... (truncated)`).
- **Named exit codes (since 2026-09-30f)** -> an entry's `exitCodes` can give a non-zero exit a meaning: `/doctor` exit 1 is shown at `warn` level titled `/doctor - warnings (exit 1)` and is not a failure; exit 2 is an error titled `/doctor - problems found (exit 2)`.
- **Failure** (any other non-zero exit, a spawn error, or a timeout) -> an error-styled dialog titled
  `/<name> - failed (exit N)` with the output. With no output at all: `/<name> failed (exit N).` or `/<name> done.`
- If the dialog helper is missing it falls back to a toast of the first 300 characters.
- Timeout is **60 seconds** (server side); a timeout reports as failed with the error text `timed out` and no exit
  code.
- "Failed" means an exit code that is not 0 **and** not named in the entry's `exitCodes`. (Before 2026-09-30f `/doctor` exit 1, warnings, was displayed as a failure: I-B13.)

##### 6.3 Where the typed text goes

`/doctor` (no space) on Enter runs it directly. With a space, level 2 shows a single non-fillable row with the
summary and `args: <usage>`; there is nothing to pick, so you type the arguments free-form.


#### 7. Commands that can't run from chat (30)

Shown greyed, tagged with their tier, each with its reason. They surface under "Can't run from chat" in the expanded
More list, or when you type a matching name. Selecting one just explains why. Submitting one is blocked once
(section 3).

This list is **not a policy list**. A command being destructive does not put it here - it goes in `passthrough` as
`dangerous`. Everything here is here for a *technical* reason.

| Reason | Commands |
|---|---|
| Needs the microphone/speaker (behind the mic and Speak buttons) | `speak`, `listen`, `transcribe` |
| Interactive flow that needs a terminal | `spotify-login`, `browser-setup` |
| Long-running supervisor - start it with `/daemon` or `/daemons` | `browser-daemon`, `discord-daemon`, `instagram-serve`, `clipboard-watch`, `ambient` |
| Runs in the foreground until it exits / a loop, not a one-shot | `daemon-run`, `sched-daemon` |
| Internal hook that runs on a timer | `ambient-tick`, `daemons-tick`, `sched-tick` |
| Internal scheduler / server / plumbing hook | `sched-signal`, `sched-ask-log`, `logs-append-run`, `console-append-run`, `commands-check-name`, `_internal_retitle` |
| Internal read behind `/skillunload`'s own argument list | `skills-loaded` |
| The model's own subagent-dispatch mechanism | `subagent-spawn`, `subagent-run` |
| Chain separator between saved-command names (syntax, not a command) | `then`, `and` |
| argparse flags | `-h`, `--help`, `-v`, `--version` |

Tiers recorded for these entries: `caution` for the supervisors, terminal flows, daemon/tick hooks and subagent
mechanisms; `safe` for the rest.


#### 8. Architecture

##### 8.1 Files

| File | Role |
|---|---|
| `web/public/slash-commands-data.js` | **The registry.** Strict JSON between `JSON-BEGIN` / `JSON-END` markers, assigned to `window.JARVIS_SLASH_COMMANDS`. Parsed by the browser, by `server.js`, and by `tests/test_slash_coverage.py` |
| `web/public/slash-palette.js` | The engine and popover UI. Pure over the registry: it hardcodes no verb names, aliases or argument sources, apart from the `HANDLERS` table (verb -> what it does). Loaded right after the data file |
| `web/public/app.js` | Calls into the palette from two places and exposes `window.JarvisHost` (bottom of file). Also holds `clearAiChat()` and `handleSkillSlashCommand()` |
| `web/public/index.html` | `<div class="slash-palette" id="slash-palette" hidden>` inside `.ask-input-row`, next to `#ask-input` (textarea, `maxlength="4000"`); placeholder text; the `menu-item-*` ids |
| `web/public/style.css` | `.slash-*` rules (around line 2606 onward); `.ask-input-row` is `position: relative` to anchor the popover |
| `web/server.js` | `POST /api/slash/run` and `GET /api/skills/loaded` |
| `jarvis-cli/jarvis/cli.py` | `jarvis skills-loaded [conversation-id]` |
| `jarvis-cli/jarvis/reserved_names.py` | The source of truth for which names exist (159 of them) |
| `tests/test_slash_coverage.py`, `tests/verify_slash_palette.js` | Automated guards (section 11) |

`jarvis-cli/jarvis/palette.py` is unrelated: it is the ANSI colour helper for terminal output.

##### 8.2 Wiring into the composer

- **Submit.** The `#ask-form` submit handler in `app.js` calls `JarvisSlash.handleSubmit(input, quotes)` first. It
  returns `{status: "handled" | "blocked" | "passthrough"}`. Anything other than `passthrough` stops the normal send
  (and re-grows the textarea). `passthrough` falls through to the normal message path unchanged.
- **Keydown.** The `#ask-input` keydown handler calls `JarvisSlash.handleComposerKeydown(e)` first; if it returns
  `true` the key was fully handled. `Escape` calls `stopPropagation()` so app.js's document-level Escape handler
  doesn't close the whole Ask panel.
- **Events.** On `input` it re-renders; on `blur` it closes after 120 ms (rows use `pointerdown` +
  `preventDefault` so picking a row doesn't blur the box); on `focus` it reopens if the text parses as a command; a
  document `pointerdown` outside closes it.
- **Public surface:** `window.JarvisSlash = { handleSubmit, handleComposerKeydown, parse, score, editDistance,
  isComplete }`.
- If `slash-commands-data.js` fails to load, the palette logs a warning and disables itself. If `slash-palette.js` is
  blocked, the composer still sends messages. A missing handler for a verb logs
  `slash-palette.js: no handler for /x` at load.

##### 8.3 Server: `POST /api/slash/run`

```
POST /api/slash/run
{ "name": "memory-recall", "args": ["two words", "x"] }
-> { "ok": true, "code": 0, "stdout": "...", "stderr": "", "error": "" }
```

- **Allowlist = the registry.** `SLASH_PASSTHROUGH` is built at startup by reading `slash-commands-data.js` and
  taking the keys of `passthrough`. If that fails it fails **closed** (empty map: nothing runs). Adding a name to
  `passthrough` is therefore what makes it runnable; nothing else does.
- **Validation (HTTP 400):** name not a string or not in the allowlist (`"x" isn't a command the palette can run.`);
  `args` not an array, more than **24** items, any item not a string, longer than **2000** characters, or containing
  a NUL byte. **Since 2026-09-30f:** also more arguments than the entry's `maxArgs` (`/subagent-keys` and `/sched-clear` take none). The client checks the same cap first, but the server is the boundary.
- **Execution:** `runJarvisOnce([name, ...args], 60000)` - `spawn()` with an argv array, no shell. `ok` is
  `exit code === 0`.
- Protected by the same `requireJarvis` middleware as the other routes.
- So it is allowlisted twice: the client only offers/runs names in `passthrough`, and the server re-checks. The
  client-side confirm for `dangerous` tier is a UX gate only; the server does not know about tiers.

Other routes the palette reads (read-only, fetched by `slash-palette.js` itself): `/api/ai/providers`, `/api/skills`,
`/api/skills/loaded`, `/api/daemons`, `/api/mode`. It writes via `/api/skills/:name/load` (POST/DELETE),
`/api/daemons/:id/:action`, `/api/mode`, `/api/ui-mode`.

**`GET /api/skills/loaded?conversationId=<id>`** runs `jarvis skills-loaded <id>` and returns `{"loaded": [...]}`:
conversation-scoped loads first, then global ones. It exists only so `/skillunload` can offer names that are really
loaded.

##### 8.4 `window.JarvisHost` (the bridge into app.js)

Everything stateful goes through this facade defined at the bottom of `app.js`; the palette does its own small
fetches for read-only lists.

| Member | Purpose |
|---|---|
| `toast(msg, kind)` | Feedback (`"error"`, `"info"`, `"warn"`) |
| `confirm(opts)` / `dialog(opts)` | `JarvisUI.confirm` / `JarvisUI.dialog` (`title`, `body`, `pre`, `confirmLabel`, `level`, `focusCancel`) |
| `state()` | Snapshot: active conversation id, `running`, conversations, saved commands, provider override, providers, think level/show, capacity mode and options, layout |
| `refreshChats()`, `loadConversations()`, `originLabel()` | Sidebar/chat list helpers |
| `newChat()`, `selectChat(id)`, `clearChat()`, `stop()`, `redo()`, `copyLastReply()`, `lastReplyRaw()` | Chat actions |
| `setProvider()`, `setThink()`, `setCapacity()`, `setLayout()` | Model/view settings |
| `runSegments(segments)` | Run a saved command |
| `skillSlash(verb, arg)` | Load / unload / make / add skills |
| `openPanel(id)` | Map of 16 panel ids to openers (`openGuides`, `openDebug`, `JarvisTestChecklist`, `openSkills`, `JarvisSchedules`, `openMcp`, `JarvisCustomTools`, `openChannels`, `JarvisDaemons`, `JarvisBacklog`, `JarvisLogSearch`, `openSetup`, `openSubagents`, `openNotifications`, `openLogs`, `openSettings`, `openSkinModal`) |
| `openSkillsToPane(pane)` | Open the skill manager on New/Import |

##### 8.5 Accessibility

- `#ask-input` gets `role="combobox"`, `aria-autocomplete="list"`, `aria-controls="slash-palette-list"`, and
  `aria-expanded` flips as the palette opens/closes; `aria-activedescendant` follows the highlighted row's id.
- The list is `role="listbox"`; rows are `role="option"` with `aria-selected`; greyed rows have `aria-disabled`.
- Two polite live regions: the footer (describes the highlighted row) and `.slash-sr` (announces "35 commands", then
  counts or "No matching commands" / "No matches").


#### 9. Registry format

`window.JARVIS_SLASH_COMMANDS` has four keys.

**`groups`** - `[{id, label}]`, Level 1's section order: `chat`, `model`, `skills`, `run`, `panels`, `view`.

**`verbs`** - one per typeable command:

| Field | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `verb` | Canonical typed name, no leading `/` |
| `aliases` | Other names resolving to the same entry |
| `group` | A `groups[].id` |
| `menu` | (panel openers only) the `menu-item-*` id this verb is the typed twin of |
| `summary` | One line; shown in rows and as the hover title |
| `riskTier` | `"safe"`, `"caution"`, `"dangerous"` |
| `instant` | `true` = takes nothing to fill in. `false` = first Enter/Tab completes the argument, second runs |
| `whileReplying` | May it run while Jarvis is replying? |
| `confirm` | `false` never, `true` always, or an array of first-argument values that trigger it (e.g. `["stop","restart"]`, case-insensitive) |
| `args` | `[{name, source, required, hint}]`; `source` is a key of `ARG_SOURCES` (a live list) or `"freeText"` |
| `covers` | Reserved names this verb is the reachable surface for |
| `example` | One realistic full example (shown in the footer and in `/help <verb>`) |
| `preview` | What the footer says Enter will do; `{0}`, `{1}` are filled from the typed arguments, or `<argname>` if not yet typed |

**`passthrough`** - `{ name: {summary, riskTier, usage, maxArgs?, noArgsHint?, secret?, exitCodes?} }`. Optional since 2026-09-30f: `maxArgs` (integer cap on arguments, enforced client and server; `0` = none, and `usage` must then be empty), `noArgsHint` (the refusal text; required with `maxArgs`), `secret` (true = the arguments would be secrets: a near-miss typo never offers Send anyway and the typed arguments are wiped; requires `maxArgs: 0`), `exitCodes` (`{"1": {label, level}}`, level `info|success|warn|error`). Runnable as `/<name> [args]`; this is also the server
allowlist.

**`notExposed`** - `{ name: {reason, riskTier} }`. Listed but not runnable.

**Argument sources** (`slash-palette.js`): `chats`, `commands`, `providers`, `installedSkills`, `loadedSkills`,
`daemonIds`, `capacityModes`, `helpVerbs` (live or derived), and static lists `thinkLevels`, `layouts`,
`daemonActions`, plus `freeText`.

**Invariant:** every name in `reserved_names.py` (159) appears in exactly one of: some verb's `covers` (98 names),
`passthrough` (31), or `notExposed` (30). 98 + 31 + 30 = 159.


#### 10. Extending it

Use `AGENTS.md` for the authoritative checklist. Summary:

**Adding or renaming a `jarvis-cli` subcommand**

1. Add/remove the name in `jarvis-cli/jarvis/reserved_names.py`.
2. Put it in `slash-commands-data.js` in **exactly one** place: a verb's `covers`; `passthrough` (one-shot, headless;
   give `summary`, `usage`, `riskTier`); or `notExposed` (technical reasons only, never "it's destructive").
3. Tier honestly (section 2.6). `dangerous` passthrough commands get the client-side confirm automatically.
4. Run `python3 tests/test_slash_coverage.py`.

**Adding a verb** - register it in `verbs` and add a handler to `HANDLERS` in `slash-palette.js`. Pick `riskTier` by
what a typo would cost; set `confirm` if destructive or it interrupts something running; set
`whileReplying: false` if it mustn't fire mid-reply; write a `preview`. Keep the two-step Enter for anything that
isn't a plain `safe` non-Chat verb. If the handler needs app state, add it to `JarvisHost`. Add cases to
`tests/verify_slash_palette.js` and the manual steps to `COMMAND_PALETTE_TESTING.md`.

**Adding a Menu panel** - give the verb that opens it a `menu` field naming the new `menu-item-*` id and add an
opener to `JarvisHost.openPanel()`. `test_slash_coverage.py` fails until every `menu-item-*` is claimed by exactly one
verb.

**Rules**

- Do not add another `/`-prefix regex to the ask-form submit handler; register a verb.
- Passthrough arguments are an argv array. Never build a command line by string concatenation on this path.
- Changes ship as scoped `diff -u` patches; a patch touching `cli.py` also needs
  `python build_tools/bump_build_version.py`.


#### 11. Tests

| Test | What it covers |
|---|---|
| `python3 tests/test_slash_coverage.py` | Registry invariants: every reserved name is in exactly one place, valid tiers, every `menu-item-*` claimed once, each verb has a summary/preview/known arg source, `clear` and `daemon` are confirm-gated and not `safe`. **543 checks pass** with `jarvis-slash-registry-fixes.patch` applied (495 before) |
| `python3 tests/test_reserved_names.py` | The computed-vs-hand-maintained reserved names set |
| `node tests/verify_slash_palette.js` | The real engine against a fake DOM and fake `JarvisHost`: parsing, submit routing, near-miss, every verb's handler, passthrough argv handling, confirm gates, keyboard model, MRU, caching, ARIA. No `npm install`. **181 checks pass** with the patch (158 before) |
| `node tests/verify_slash_route.js` | *(new 2026-09-30f)* `POST /api/slash/run` itself: the route's real source is sliced out of `server.js` and run with `app`/`runJarvisOnce` stubbed, against the real registry: allowlist, argument validation, the `maxArgs` cap, fails closed. **16 checks**; it never starts Express or runs `jarvis` |
| `DOCUMENTATION/COMMAND_PALETTE_TESTING.md` | The manual half a fake DOM can't tell you: look, floating, real focus/keys, each verb end to end in the real UI, both layouts, phone width, accessibility |

Since 2026-09-30f `test_slash_coverage.py` compares a passthrough entry's `usage` to the CLI's own `usage: jarvis <name> …` line where cli.py has one (calendar-add, mcp-call, memory-recall, notify-send) and checks that every `--flag` it names exists somewhere in the CLI. **It cannot check positionals for commands that have no such line, nor that a flag belongs to that command;** those were verified by hand on 2026-09-30f and will drift again unless re-checked when a command's arguments change.


#### 12. Not built / known limits

- **Commands contributed by custom tools (I.2.11 / K.6.7)** - not built. The plan says its contract is still TBD and
  it needs its own tracking id. The registry format leaves room for it.
- **Touch long-press for the hover tooltip (D-I4)** - on a touchscreen a tap fills the row and there is no hover to
  move the footer.
- **`/copy`** copies the whole last reply only; `/copy 2` (one code block) waits on Part I.1 (code blocks with
  one-click copy), which is a separate, unbuilt feature.
- **No inline backlog quick-add** (D-I5 deferred) - `/backlog` just opens the panel. Also deferred, not rejected:
  `/remind`, `/persona`, `/search`, `/export`.
- **`/skillunload`** doesn't distinguish "this chat" from "all chats"; it shows the merged set. The CLI's own habit of
  reporting success for a name that isn't loaded (I-B3) is unchanged; the palette just never offers or accepts one.
- **The popover only opens above** the composer.
- **Near-miss detection** compares verbs, aliases and CLI names, not saved-command names.
- Native `confirm()` used for chat deletion and daemon *remove* was left alone.
- **Panel openers that depend on a separate script** (`JarvisTestChecklist`, `JarvisSchedules`, `JarvisCustomTools`,
  `JarvisDaemons`, `JarvisBacklog`, `JarvisLogSearch`) are called with optional chaining, so if that script failed to
  load the command silently does nothing - no toast.
- `/help` for an unknown verb rewrites the box to `/` rather than keeping what you typed.


#### 13. Registry vs. CLI: mismatches found while documenting

> **Status, 2026-09-30f:** everything in this section is **fixed in `jarvis-slash-registry-fixes.patch`** (I-B13–I-B17) except I-B18. The tables below record what was found and are kept as the record; the current registry text is in §6.1. The eleven "not checked" commands were checked on 2026-09-30f; the extra mismatches that turned up are in the second table.

I compared each passthrough entry's `usage` and summary against its handler in `jarvis-cli/jarvis/cli.py` (and
`clipboard_cli.py`). The entries below don't match. The footer and hover text will show the registry's version.
Entries not listed either matched or were not checked (`/version`, `/memory-stats`, `/memory-reindex`,
`/digest-*`, `/notify-clear`, `/logs-clear`, `/console-clear`, `/conv-delete`, `/policy`, `/calendar-list`,
`/calendar-events`).

| Command | Registry says | The CLI actually does |
|---|---|---|
| `/conv-export` | `<conversation-id> [path]` | `[conversation-id] [--format F] [--out DIR] [--tools] [--thinking] [--trace]`. The id is optional (falls back to the current conversation). There is no positional path; a second positional argument is ignored |
| `/subagent-keys` | `[provider]`, "Show or change" | No args lists the key pools (redacted). `<role> <provider> <key> [key2 ...]` sets a pool; `<role> --clear` removes one. Setting keys means typing API keys into the chat box, at `caution` tier with no confirmation |
| `/calendar-add` | `<when> <title>`, "Add a calendar entry" | `<name> <ics-url>` - it adds an **ICS feed** and tests reachability |
| `/calendar-remove` | `<id>` | `<name>` - removes the feed with that name |
| `/notify-send` | `<message>` | `<message> [title] [channels,csv]` |
| `/sched-clear` | `[--all]`, "Remove scheduled jobs in bulk" | No flags are parsed. It calls `scheduler.clear_finished()`, which keeps jobs in an active status and removes the rest. The `dangerous` tier and "bulk" wording may overstate it |
| `/memory-consolidate` | `[namespace]` | `[--days N] [--review | --dry-run] [--no-model]` (default 7 days) |
| `/memory-ns` | (no args), "List memory namespaces", `safe` | With no argument it lists; **with an argument it switches the active namespace** - a state change on a `safe` command |
| `/memory-list` | `[namespace]` | The handler checks for `--auto`; I did not confirm a namespace argument |
| `/policy-check`, `/policy-dry-run` | `<tool> [args]` | `<tool> [--args JSON] [--context CTX]` |
| `/console-read` | `[run-id]` | The first argument is a **conversation id**, required and validated; flags `--since N`, `--kinds a,b`, `--turn T`, `--limit N`, `--after-last-clear` |
| `/clipboard-watch-config` | `[key value]` | `[--pattern REGEX | --clear-pattern] [--poll-seconds N]` |
| `/doctor` | `[--deep]` | Also accepts group names, `--json`, `--verbose`. Exits 0 healthy, **1 on warnings, 2 on failures** |

**Also found 2026-09-30f, while fixing I-B14 (commands section 13 had marked "not checked"):**

| Command | Registry said | The CLI actually does |
|---|---|---|
| `/logs-clear` | (no args), "Wipe the stored logs. Irreversible" | Requires a **conversation id** (`invalid conversation id`, exit 1 without one) and deletes **that conversation's** log file. Run bare it just failed |
| `/console-clear` | (no args), "Wipe the stored console output. Irreversible", `dangerous` | Requires a conversation id. **Deletes nothing**: it appends a clear marker so the Live Feed reloads as cleared (`console_store.clear_marker`). Now `caution` |
| `/memory-list` | `[namespace]` | Only `--auto` is parsed; there is no namespace argument |
| `/memory-reindex` | (no args) | `[--embeddings]` also rebuilds embeddings |
| `/digest-on` | (no args) | `[schedule] [time]` (defaults: daily, 9am) |
| `/notify-clear` | (no args), "Clear every notification" | `[consumer]`: with a name it only marks everything seen for that consumer; with none it empties the inbox. Kept `dangerous` |

**Practical consequence for `/doctor` (fixed 2026-09-30f):** the passthrough reported "failed" for any non-zero exit, so a warnings-only
report opens as an error-styled dialog titled `/doctor - failed (exit 1)`. The manual checklist's "`/doctor` shows its
report in a dialog" is true, but the framing will look like a failure.

**Status audit and this plan (resolved 2026-09-30c):** `jarvis-status-audit_20.md` and this plan both listed the `/` palette as "NOT STARTED"; both were updated in rev. 2026-09-30c to match the repo. Code blocks with one-click copy (Part I.1) remain unbuilt.


**Plan tracking ids for the section 13 findings (added 2026-09-30c):** I-B13 `/doctor` exit-code framing · I-B14 stale `usage`/summary strings (plus the missing test that compares `usage` to the CLI) · I-B15 `/memory-ns` state change on a `safe` command · I-B16 `/subagent-keys` accepts API keys typed into the composer · I-B17 `/sched-clear` tier/wording · I-B18 minor gaps from section 12. **Status 2026-09-30f:** I-B13–I-B17 ✅ FIXED in `jarvis-slash-registry-fixes.patch` (delivered, not yet confirmed applied); I-B18 ❌ NOT STARTED.

# Part J — Final step: a checklist entry for every tool, and a test for every feature, this plan adds

> **CURRENT AUDIT — 2026-09-22:** J remains the final QA closure pass. Tool coverage exists, but this Part should not be marked complete until the missing fixtures are restored, the P0/P1 defects are closed, open features have real acceptance runs, and the 16 plan-added tool entries have been human-tightened.


**Status: not started — this Part itself is new (revision 2026-09-21e).** It
is not a feature to build; it's the closing pass over everything Parts A–I
add or change, so nothing this plan shipped is left untested or undocumented
in Menu → Test Checklist or in this doc's own acceptance checklists.

## J.0 Why this is last, on purpose

Every item below needs the thing it's testing to actually exist and have
settled behaviour — a `does`/`steps`/`expect` entry written against a feature
still in flux just gets rewritten the moment the feature changes, which is
wasted work and (per Part G's own rule) un-ticks every tester's saved
progress since ticks are keyed by step text. So: don't start this early.
Item 12 in §0.4 points here. This also depends on **G.1** (the per-tool
`TEST_CHECKLIST` mechanism) already being delivered, which it is.

## J.1 Two kinds of coverage, two different homes

This plan adds things in two shapes, and they don't fit the same box:

- **Real tools** — something the model can call. These already have a home:
  Menu → Test Checklist, via the `does`/`steps`/`expect` shape G.1 formalized.
  §J.2 below is the inventory.
- **Everything else** — a behaviour change, a UI panel, a backend policy.
  Not a tool, so it can't get a `TEST_CHECKLIST` entry (that catalogue is
  keyed by tool name) — forcing a fake tool name onto "the router no longer
  mis-routes a pasted reply" would just be noise in a tool tester's list.
  This plan's own convention is already the right home for these: a
  per-Part **Acceptance checklist** section. §8.8, E.7, F.18 and I.5 already
  exist; §J.3 below points at those and drafts the ones that don't exist yet
  (Parts B, C, D, G, H).

## J.2 Tool checklist — the 16 tools this plan adds

All 16 already have a first-draft entry in `test-checklist-data.js` (see
Part G, "State after the merge") — this is the human pass those drafts were
always waiting on, plus the live-model prompt to run each with. Tightening
these can use either home G.1 offers (the shipped file, or moving an entry
into the tool's own module via `TEST_CHECKLIST`) — migration is optional,
per G.1's own "Not done/open" note; it only matters if someone wants the
entry to live next to the code.

| Tool | Group | Ask prompt to test with | What a pass looks like |
|---|---|---|---|
| `clipboard_get` | clipboard | "What's on my clipboard right now?" | Returns the current text (or a clear "nothing to return"); doesn't restate a copied password verbatim (Part B's safety note) |
| `clipboard_set` | clipboard | "Copy this to my clipboard: hello world" | Clipboard contains exactly `hello world`; paste manually to confirm |
| `clipboard_clear` | clipboard | "Clear my clipboard" | Clipboard is empty afterward |
| `clipboard_wait_for_change` | clipboard | "Watch my clipboard and tell me when I copy something new" — then copy something within ~20s | Returns the new text once it changes; returns `timed_out: true` if nothing changes before the cap (~120s) |
| `browser_goto` | browser | "Open example.com in the browser" | Session starts (or reuses this ask's session) and navigates; a `file://` or `javascript:` target is refused or confirmed, not followed silently |
| `browser_click` | browser | "Click the Submit button on this page" | Confirm-gated (`tool_safety.py`); resolves the element by role/label/text before falling back to a raw selector |
| `browser_fill` | browser | "Type my email into the email field" | Confirm-gated; fills the described field, not a guessed CSS target |
| `browser_get_text` | browser | "What does this page say?" | Returns visible page text, truncated the same way `web_fetch` is |
| `browser_screenshot` | browser | "Take a screenshot of this page" | Saved file path returned and displayed the same way the desktop-screenshot tool's output is |
| `browser_wait_for` | browser | Inside a multi-step flow: "Wait for the results to load, then tell me what's there" | Waits up to `timeout_seconds` for the described element/text before failing, instead of reading a half-loaded page |
| `browser_close` | browser | "Close the browser now" | Session ends before the ask itself would have closed it |
| `move_path` | files | "Move report.pdf to my Desktop" | File moved; confirm-gated; refuses drive roots / home folder / OS folders / `~/.jarvis` outright |
| `copy_path` | files | "Copy report.pdf to the Desktop, don't move it" | Original stays in place, a copy appears; won't overwrite unless told to |
| `rename_path` | files | "Rename draft.txt to final.txt" | File renamed in place |
| `make_dir` | files | "Create a folder called Invoices inside Documents" | Folder created; parent folders only created if asked |
| `delete_path` | files | "Delete old-notes.txt" | Goes to the Recycle Bin, not permanently unlinked; confirm-gated |

## J.4 Complex, multi-step scenarios

§J.2 and §J.3 are smoke tests — one prompt, one expected shape. That's
enough for most of what this plan adds, but not for the handful of tools and
fixes where the actual risk only shows up across several steps, a second
`jarvis` process, or a specific historical failure case. Run these in
addition to §J.2/§J.3, not instead of them, for the items below.

**Browser control (Part C) — the most stateful thing this plan adds**
1. Full session lifecycle in one ask: navigate, log in, navigate to a second
   page on the same site, read it. Expect one session opened lazily on the
   first `browser_*` call, reused for every later `browser_*` call in that
   same ask, and closed in a `finally` when the ask ends — test all three
   ends (success, error, timeout), not just the happy path.
2. **Persistent login across asks** — log in during ask 1, let that ask end,
   start a brand-new `jarvis ask` and open a page that requires login.
   Expect still logged in, via the on-disk profile, even though ask 1's
   browser *process* is gone. This is the one thing Part C itself flags as
   unverified without a real environment — don't skip it.
3. Selector fallback: click something described only in prose on a page
   where the accessible role/label/text differ from any CSS class name.
   Expect `get_by_role` → `get_by_label` → `get_by_text` tried in order
   before any raw-CSS fallback.
4. Safety refusals, each as its own case: a `javascript:` URL, a `file://`
   URL, a click whose accessible name matches the confirm blocklist
   (buy/purchase/pay/delete/remove/confirm/submit/transfer), and a click
   that navigates to a new origin. Expect all four to refuse or confirm; a
   same-origin, non-blocklisted click should *not* need confirmation.
5. Playwright not installed: run any `browser_*` tool. Expect the "Browser
   control isn't set up yet. Run: jarvis browser-setup" error, not an import
   crash that takes the rest of `tools.py` down.
6. **Warm daemon (v2), `browser_warm_daemon` on** — repeat scenario 2
   (persistent login across separate `jarvis ask` invocations) with the flag
   on. Expect the same login persistence, now via the daemon's one held-open
   session rather than the on-disk profile alone, and each ask after the
   first noticeably skipping the ~1-2s Chromium startup cost. Then stop the
   daemon process and repeat a `browser_*` call with the flag still on —
   expect a transparent fall-back to v1 behaviour, not an error.

**`clipboard_wait_for_change` (Part B)**
1. Copy something new partway through the ask. Expect the *tool call*
   itself blocks (not a background asyncio task), polling ~0.5s, returning
   the new text as soon as it changes.
2. Let the timeout elapse untouched. Expect `{"ok": false, "timed_out": true}`,
   not a hang.
3. Ask for a timeout above the ~120s cap. Expect it clamped, not honoured.

**100k+ token-burn containment (§1g)**
1. Replay the supplied JSONL in a redacted/stubbed harness and record the same
baseline metrics: 77 requests, 70 usage records, 123,368 input tokens, 2,027
output tokens, and the repeated `write_on_screen continue and enter` history
shape.
2. Compare the new run against the baseline. Expect input-token growth to
flatten once the same user/tool state stops changing, rather than increasing
just because the turn continues.
3. Verify that explicit cancellation/decline terminates the repeated action loop
and that a later, genuinely new request still starts cleanly.

**Notification importance + clipboard flood control (D.2.1 / Part B)**
1. Create one notification at each of the five levels (Silent, Standard,
Persistent, Broadcast, Confirm) and verify the persisted level, channel
behavior and digest behavior for each.
2. Run a clipboard watcher through a synthetic burst (for example 20 matching
changes) and then one isolated change. Expect bounded push notifications, a
coalesced count for the burst, and the isolated change delivered promptly.
3. Mark the same burst as level 4 (Broadcast) and confirm that path is not
silently suppressed by the coalescer.

**Path tools (F.3)**
1. Four separate refusal cases, not one: a drive root, the home folder, an
   OS folder, and something under `~/.jarvis`.
2. `copy_path` onto an existing destination without `overwrite`, then again
   with it — refused, then succeeds, and only ever replaces a *file*.
3. A cross-drive/cross-volume `move_path` (skip cleanly if no second volume
   is available rather than failing the run).

**Forced ending / withheld tools (F.1/F.8/F.11)**
1. Replay Case 1 and Case 2b from F.17's saved-log fixtures end to end, not
   just through the router. Case 1 should end in an edit; Case 2b is a known
   open gap — confirm it still fails, and fails the *same* way, not a new one.
2. Drive a real conversation into a tools-withheld round containing a
   correct tool call. Expect the call is kept, not discarded, and the key is
   not rotated.
3. Trigger each of F.8's four distinct failure shapes separately. Expect all
   four now produce the same harness-written degraded reply, not four
   different flavours of "empty response."
4. Run a turn all the way out of rounds. Expect a reply listing what ran and
   what's left — no key rotation, no "tool budget" wording leaking into the
   model-facing text.
5. Force a real ending that offers one call, then reply with a bare "go
   ahead" as the very next message. Expect the call runs directly with
   **zero** new provider calls, still through `tool_safety.py`'s confirm
   gate. Then check the edges: a non-confirmation reply after the offer
   (expect nothing runs), the same "go ahead" from a chat guest (expect
   ignored), waiting past 30 minutes before confirming (expect expired,
   ignored), and confirming after the offered tool has been removed from the
   session's schemas (expect ignored, not a crash).
6. Immediately after a forced ending, start a **new, unrelated** turn instead
   of confirming. Expect the stale pending action is not carried into it and
   doesn't fire on some later unrelated "yes."

**Failover (F.7)**
1. Get several tool calls into a turn, then force the active provider to
   fail. Expect the next provider's first message carries the real prior
   tool results (not a truncated recap in one fake "user" turn), and nothing
   gets called a second time just because the transcript was rebuilt.

**Key health (F.9)**
1. Trigger a real 429 on a key, then immediately start a new `jarvis`
   process. Expect that key skipped until its cooldown passes.
2. Run again after the cooldown passes. Expect the previously-bad key
   eligible again, with a never-failed key still preferred first.

**Router paste/confirmation (F.10)**
1. Paste Jarvis's own full previous reply back as the entire next message.
   Expect no change to which tool group loads.
2. After a `files`-group turn, send a bare "yes". Expect it still routes
   `files`, not a reset to some default group.
3. Highlight and send only an excerpt of a previous reply. Expect the
   excerpt doesn't vote in the router the way a fresh message would.

**Streaming, once §8 exists**
1. Run the same non-trivial multi-tool-call task on all five adapters
   (Ollama, openai_compatible, Anthropic, Gemini, Cohere) back to back.
   Expect text and thinking both streaming token-by-token on every one, with
   an identical segmented thinking → text → tool UI across adapters.
2. Kill the connection mid-stream on each adapter. Expect the same clean
   degraded behaviour everywhere, not just on whichever adapter §8 was built
   against first.

**Subagent live view (D.1)**
1. Spawn two or more subagents at once, cycle between them mid-run. Expect
   each shows its own live tool calls/console/thinking — never another
   subagent's — and cycling doesn't lose or blend state.
2. Once §8 lands, repeat, confirming the word-by-word tier now streams
   instead of updating once per completed round.

**Console persistence (Part E)**
1. Reproduce the exact scenario behind the saved conversation
   `205b1493df955d1c.json` that Part E's own evidence section is built from.
   Expect it now persists and filters correctly — this is the one area the
   plan explicitly warns has failed before, so a general "looks fine" pass
   doesn't count; re-run the specific case that broke it previously.

# Part K — Current 2026-09-22 audit: what exists, what is missing, priorities and exact next steps

> **Purpose:** This is the actionable part of the document. It reconciles the
> historical plan with the actual `jarvis-main(47).zip` archive and turns the
> remaining work into an explicit hierarchy. Use the format **big step →
> substep → smaller step → status → what it does → priority → dependency /
> acceptance** when implementing.
>
> **Source of truth:** current source tree first; current tests and executable
> build metadata second; historical revision prose only for provenance.

## K.0 Repo-wide snapshot

The audited archive contains approximately **206 Python files, 7 JavaScript
files, 3 CSS files, 25 Markdown files, and 68 standalone `tests/test_*.py`
scripts**. The current repository map describes three front ends (CLI, web UI,
Discord/Instagram gateways) feeding `ai_client.ask()`, with router, prompt
assembly, provider adapters and the shared tool executor underneath.

The current tool catalogue reports **170 tools**, and the shipped Test Checklist
catalogue also has **170 entries**, with **0 missing names and 0 extra names** in
the audit. The current static tool registry contains the expected groups for
core, commands, files/workspace, web/audio/vision, scheduling, channels,
memory, MCP, subagents, browser, clipboard and other product-specific tools.
The existing notification stack already contains a digest priority model
(`low` / `normal` / `high`), but the priority is not yet first-class on
`notifier.notify()` records; the new revision treats that as the foundation
for end-to-end importance and clipboard flood control.

Existing out-of-plan subsystems were also checked — memory/history,
conversation search and summarization, scheduler/tasks, daemons, backlog,
ambient monitoring, onboarding, Discord/Instagram, Playnite, Spotify,
Everything, yt-dlp, desktop/file/git/package/web/audio/radio tooling and the
custom-tools ecosystem. They are **existing product surface, not silently
converted into “missing” work**. This plan is specifically the backlog for the
issues/features captured in Parts A–J plus the cross-cutting defects found by
the current audit.

## K.1 P0 — release/security gates

### K.1.1 Subagent provider-pool fail-closed correctness

**Status:** DONE — fixed in rev. 2026-09-22c (`jarvis-p0-release-gates.patch`, §0.1g item 1).

**What it does:** A subagent process must be able to use only the provider/key
pool assigned to it. A malformed `JARVIS_SUBAGENT_KEYS` value must result in
**zero eligible providers**, never the parent Jarvis provider list and never an
uncaught `NoneType` iteration crash.

**Current source path:** `jarvis-cli/jarvis/subagents.py`
`providers_from_env()` + `jarvis-cli/jarvis/ai_client.py`
`_eligible_providers()`.

**Defect as found when this fix was made:** `providers_from_env()` already
returned `[]` for every malformed *structured* pool (empty keys, unknown
provider, etc.) — that part of this section's original text was stale.
It still returns `None` for unparseable JSON specifically, by design (its own
docstring calls this "indistinguishable from not a subagent"). The actual bug
was one level up: `_eligible_providers()` did `providers = pinned`
unconditionally, so that legitimate `None` overwrote the ambient provider list
and the very next line's `for p in providers:` crashed with
`TypeError: 'NoneType' object is not iterable` before any fail-closed logic
ran. `tests/test_subagents.py::test_malformed_pool_yields_nothing_not_main_key`
reproduced this directly.

#### K.1.1.1 Fix parser return contract

**Status:** DONE — see K.1.1's defect note above for what the actual one-line
fix turned out to be (guarding the assignment in `_eligible_providers()`, not
`providers_from_env()`'s return contract, which was already correct for every
case except the documented `None` fallthrough).

**Change:** `_eligible_providers()` now assigns `providers = pinned` only when
`pinned is not None`. Unparseable JSON therefore falls through to the ambient
provider list (matching `providers_from_env()`'s documented contract); every
other malformed shape still yields `[]` and a subagent gets nothing.

**Priority:** P0.

**Acceptance:** malformed pool shapes all return `[]`; a subagent never falls
through to ambient providers; the existing test passes. — **Met.**

#### K.1.1.2 Add shape matrix regression coverage

**Status:** DONE — already present in `tests/test_subagents.py` prior to this
fix (invalid JSON, empty-string provider + empty keys, valid provider name +
empty keys, unknown provider name, each asserted separately); this revision
did not need to add new cases, only make the existing ones pass.

**Change:** Cover invalid JSON, JSON scalar/list, missing provider, empty key
list, unknown provider, valid pool, and unexpected exception in lookup.

**Priority:** P0.

**Acceptance:** all cases fail closed and never include a parent/main key. —
**Met**; full file: 13/13 cases pass.

### K.1.2 Build/source-hash integrity

**Status:** PARTIALLY DONE — metadata regenerated and drift-guarded in rev.
2026-09-22c (`jarvis-p0-release-gates.patch`, §0.1g item 2); **the actual
executable rebuild (K.1.2.2) is still owner-side and open.**

**What it does:** Makes the build metadata prove which source tree produced the
current executable/package.

**Evidence (as of the original audit, now stale — see K.1.2.1):**
- `jarvis-cli/jarvis/build_info.py`: build 26, timestamp `2026-09-22 18:05:10`,
  source hash `62765d15d37183066ac4a2e35122111765d14541cfdd62a725665ffe2dee87b9`.
- The repo's own `build_tools.hash_source.hash_source_tree()` on the checked-in
  source computes `4fac34eb84638c653e3af2cde7cce8a9f786512118ad32d2ca94cc59c5b209d0`.

#### K.1.2.1 Regenerate build metadata

**Status:** DONE. Ran `python build_tools/bump_build_version.py` from
`jarvis-cli/` — the official path this section originally asked for, not a
hand-edit — against the tree with K.1.1's fix already applied (which is why
the new hash below differs from the `4fac34...` this section's evidence
originally cited: that number was correct for the tree *before* K.1.1's
one-line change, and the tree changed again). Result: build 27, timestamp
`2026-09-22 19:20:15`, `SOURCE_HASH`
`2d1030fca68215fc0570c4e294c2d6c6921165760a4ddcfe562759ed9f99925f`, which now
equals `hash_source_tree()` recomputed on the current tree — confirmed by
`tests/test_build_info.py` (K.1.2.3).

**Change:** Run the official build metadata path against the actual source tree
so `SOURCE_HASH` equals the computed tree hash.

**Priority:** P0.

#### K.1.2.2 Rebuild and verify the executable

**Status: ✅ CLOSED, owner 2026-10-01 — the owner ran `script.bat` on the real checkout and reports it worked.** (Reported by the owner; `verify_exe.py`'s output was not shown to me, so the `OK` line itself is not quoted here.) The historical text below is kept as written.

**Former status:** OPEN — owner-side. Not done in this revision: the fix was made
from a Linux sandbox with a copy of the archive, not the owner's actual
`D:\MyDigitalVault\prjects\whole jarvis\jarvis v2\jarvis` checkout, and there

#### K.1.2.3 Prevent future drift automatically

**Status:** DONE. New `tests/test_build_info.py` (2 checks): recomputes
`hash_source.hash_source_tree()` and asserts it equals `build_info.SOURCE_HASH`,

(`python build_tools/bump_build_version.py`) rather than just a bare assertion.
No CI workflow config exists anywhere in this repo, so this follows the
existing convention of a plain `tests/test_*.py` script run via `AGENTS.md`'s
test process, rather than inventing a `.github/workflows/*.yml` this repo has

**Change:** Add a release/CI/build check that recomputes the source hash and

## K.2 P1 — correctness and regression blockers

### K.2.1 Restore F.17 real-log replay fixtures

**Status:** DONE, rev. 2026-09-22g (`jarvis-f17-replay-fixtures.patch`).

**What it does:** Replays the two real failure scenarios that motivated Part F,

**What was actually restored, and how.** The person supplied the two raw

missing `.json` was reconstructable **exactly**, not approximated: the

payload (`"hey jarvis help me out here \nD:\...\ratioty\main.py\ni cant get
the token variable..."` for Case 1, `"jarvis could you move
C:/Users/assim/Downloads/20-09-2026.pdf to the documents/studying folder
instead thanks"` for Case 2b — the latter matching "the move-the-PDF turn"
name this section already used), with `exchanges` holding just that one

either file (the logger already strips those before writing, which is also
why `_load_fixture()`'s reconstructed provider config only ever gets
placeholder keys — see that function's own docstring); the real file paths
and a Windows username already appear in plaintext throughout this document
regardless.
