### K.2.2 Fix I-B1 — math extraction must skip Markdown code

**Status:** DONE — fixed in rev. 2026-09-22d (`jarvis-i-b1-i-b2-fixes.patch`, §0.1h).

**What it does:** Keeps `$`, `$$`, `\(` / `\)`, and `\[` / `\]` math parsing from
consuming fenced or inline code.

**Source before this fix:** `web/public/app.js::extractMath()` ran regex
replacement on raw reply text before Markdown parsing, with no way to know
whether a match was inside a code fence or inline-code span.

#### K.2.2.1 Build a code-aware extraction pass

**Status:** DONE. `extractMath()` now splits the raw text into segments
first — fenced code blocks (line-based; an unclosed fence runs to the end of
the text), then inline code spans within whatever's left (position-based,
CommonMark-style exact-run-length matching) — via two new helpers,
`_splitFencedCode()` and `_splitInlineCode()`. The four math patterns
(`_applyMathPatterns()`) run only on the non-code stretches
(`_extractMathFromNonFenced()`); code segments pass through completely
untouched. All four helpers live inside the same source range
`tests/verify_math_rendering.js` slices out of `app.js`
(`const MATH_PLACEHOLDER_OPEN` … `function renderMathIn`), so the test
automatically exercises the real shipped code, not a copy.

**Change:** Scan Markdown into code/non-code spans first, or otherwise protect
code fences/inline code before math extraction. Apply the minimum change that
keeps current KaTeX behavior for normal prose.

**Priority:** P1.

#### K.2.2.2 Add regression cases for fenced and inline code

**Status:** DONE. `tests/verify_math_rendering.js` grew from 9 to 24 checks:
the four exact repro cases from I.0.1 (A–D — `$$` inside a fence eating the
closing fence, two inline code spans merging into one, two js fences
merging across a `\[`/`\]`-shaped regex literal), plus `~~~` fences, a longer
closing fence than the opener, an indented (≤3-space) fence, an unclosed
fence, and math immediately adjacent to inline code — exactly the test list
I.0.1 asked for.

**Change:** Extend `tests/verify_math_rendering.js` or add a dedicated test with
`$$` inside fenced code, dollar pairs inside inline code, and `\[`/`\]` inside
code.

**Priority:** P1.

#### K.2.2.3 Run a real browser render check

**Status:** OPEN / environment dependent — unchanged by this fix. The Linux
sandbox this fix was made in has no network access to fetch KaTeX/DOMPurify
from their CDNs and no browser-test harness (Playwright, jsdom) set up, so
`tests/verify_math_rendering.js` still only verifies against the real
`marked` package, same caveat the file's own header already states. Worth a
manual pass in a real browser before this is treated as fully closed.

**Acceptance:** code fences remain byte-faithful and math still renders in a
real browser.

**Priority:** P2 after the source fix.

### K.2.3 Fix I-B2 — one canonical reserved-command-name source

**Status:** DONE — fixed in rev. 2026-09-22d (`jarvis-i-b1-i-b2-fixes.patch`, §0.1h).

**What it does:** Prevents a saved command from being created under a name that
the CLI/web later treats as a built-in, and prevents the three surfaces from
silently disagreeing about what is reserved.

**Source before this fix:**
- `jarvis-cli/jarvis/cli.py` had a 116-name CLI reserved-name set.
- `web/server.js` had a separate, smaller (59-name) web reserved-name set.
- `jarvis-cli/jarvis/commands_config.py` had a third, much smaller (20-name)
  set — the one `validate_command_name` actually checked when *saving* a
  command.

(Note: `jarvis-cli/cli.py`, referenced in this section's original text, is a
stale duplicate outside the actual installed package — the real module is
`jarvis-cli/jarvis/cli.py`; see the P0 fix's build-info investigation for how
that was confirmed.)

**Audit finding, confirmed again while fixing this:** the three sets were
materially different — `think`, `backlog`, `daemons`, `skillload`,
`organize-json`, `logs-search` and `mode` were all concrete examples of a
built-in that `commands_config.validate_command_name` accepted as a valid
saved-command name, which then got silently shadowed at dispatch with **no
warning at all**; and 30 real public subcommands (`doctor`, `version`, the
`policy-*`/`memory-*`/`calendar-*`/`digest-*`/`ctools-*` families) were absent
from every one of the three lists.

#### K.2.3.1 Create one authoritative reserved-name provider

**Status:** DONE. New `jarvis-cli/jarvis/reserved_names.py` holds the single
canonical `RESERVED_NAMES` set (plus `CHAIN_SEP`/`PARALLEL_SEP`, moved there
too so it doesn't need to import `cli.py` back). It's a plain hand-maintained
set, same as the three it replaces, rather than something computed by
importing every dispatch module at runtime — see the module's own docstring
for why (`RESERVED_NAMES` sits on the hot path of every plain
`jarvis <free text>` prompt, and two of the delegated modules are only
imported lazily elsewhere on purpose). `cli.py` and `commands_config.py` both
now import it — literally the same set object, not just equal copies
(checked by `test_reserved_names.py`).

**Change:** Put the canonical list in one importable/shared source or expose it
through a single CLI/API definition rather than maintaining three copies.

**Priority:** P1.

#### K.2.3.2 Make web validation consume the canonical list

**Status:** DONE. New `jarvis commands-check-name <name>` CLI subcommand
(JSON `{"ok": ..., "error": ...}`, via `commands_config.validate_command_name`).
`web/server.js` no longer keeps its own `RESERVED_NAMES` Set at all —
`validateName()` is now `async` and calls the CLI subcommand through the
existing `runJarvisOnce()` helper; both `POST`/`PUT /api/commands` route
handlers now `await` it. `commands-check-name` itself was added to the
canonical set (a saved command can't be named after it either).

**Priority:** P1.

#### K.2.3.3 Add exact coverage + collision tests

**Status:** DONE. New `tests/test_reserved_names.py` (12 checks):
- Regex-extracts every `argv[0] == "..."` / `argv[0] in (...)` dispatch
  literal out of `cli.py` (the same technique the original audit used to find
  the 30 missing names), adds `SCHEDULER_COMMANDS` and the three delegated
  `COMMANDS` tuples (`workspace_cli`, `channels_cli`, `clipboard_cli`), and
  fails if that computed set contains anything `reserved_names.RESERVED_NAMES`
  doesn't — this is the drift guard for *future* subcommands.
- Individually pins all 30 previously-missing names as now covered, so a
  future refactor can't silently drop one and still pass the drift check
  above by coincidence.
- Calls `commands_config.validate_command_name` directly on `think`,
  `backlog`, `daemons`, `skillload`, `organize-json`, `logs-search`, `mode`
  and `doctor` and asserts each is now rejected (previously all eight were
  silently accepted), plus one ordinary name is still accepted.
- Asserts `cli.RESERVED_NAMES is commands_config.RESERVED_NAMES` — the same
  object, not just equal sets.

**Acceptance:** `think` and every built-in are rejected for saved-command names;
no built-in is missing from the canonical set; a future built-in cannot be
added without updating the same source. — **Met**, 12/12 checks pass.

**Priority:** P1.

**Done separately (D-I9, rev. 2026-09-22h):** a `jarvis doctor` check
(`doctor.check_saved_commands()`, group `commands`) that lists existing
saved commands a built-in already shadows. Nothing is auto-renamed — still
the owner's call. See D-I9's own entry in Part I's decision log for what
this found already existed (a correct-since-I-B2, but terminal-only,
per-invocation warning in `cli.py`).

### K.2.4 Finish F.2 project-content discovery budgeting

**Status:** DECIDED AND IMPLEMENTED, rev. 2026-09-22h (`jarvis-followups-batch1.patch`) — with an important caveat found while verifying it against Case 2b (see below).

**What it does:** Stops "I need to inspect the repo to discover the right tool"
from consuming the same scarce round budget as the actual mutation once the
model already found the tool it needs.

**Current source:** `ai_providers.py` has a separate discovery budget for
catalog-style discovery (`search_tools`, `get_tool_schema`, `load_skill`, plus
unknown-name recovery). Current default is 3 and the regression suite passes.

**Previous gap:** `search_files` and similar project-content lookup were
treated as ordinary work.

#### K.2.4.1 Decide the policy boundary

**Status:** DECIDED. **Give project-content discovery its own separate
budget** (not folded into the existing catalog-discovery pool): new
`PROJECT_DISCOVERY_TOOL_NAMES = {"search_files", "list_dir"}` in
`ai_providers.py`, its own `RoundBudget.project_discovery_limit`/
`project_discovery_used` counters, checked independently of the existing
`discovery_limit` pool. Kept separate rather than merged because these tools
touch the real filesystem and can return arbitrarily large results depending
on the repo, unlike a static catalog lookup — so they get a smaller default
(2, vs. the catalog pool's 3), and a mixed round spanning both free
categories (e.g. `search_files` + `search_tools` together) is charged
normally rather than treated as free by either pool, same conservative
philosophy the existing catalog-discovery pool already uses for a
real-tool-call mix. Wired from `ai_client.ask()` via
`defaults.project_discovery_call_budget` (default 2), same pattern as
`discovery_call_budget`.

**Decision:** Should project-content discovery (`search_files`, possibly
`list_dir` and a tightly bounded subset of read-only repo-inspection tools) have
its own discovery budget, or remain billable work? — **Yes, its own budget,
scoped narrowly to exactly `search_files` and `list_dir`** (not a broader
subset — matching how `DISCOVERY_TOOL_NAMES` itself is deliberately not
exhaustive either; widen only with the same evidence-driven care F.2 used).

**Priority:** P1.

#### K.2.4.2 Implement only the chosen boundary

**Status:** DONE. New `tests/test_discovery_round_budget.py` cases (33 new,
74 total in that file): the project-discovery pool draws independently of
the catalog-discovery pool; an unknown/made-up tool name is *not*
project-discovery (it stays on the existing catalog-discovery/unknown-name
path); a mixed round across either free category or a real tool is charged
normally; pool exhaustion falls back to the main budget; the `0`-disables-it
guarantee; and that `ai_client.ask()` actually wires the new config default.

**Acceptance:** Case 2b fixture demonstrates that discovery no longer crowds
out an otherwise budgetable action. — **Not met, and it turns out this
fixture cannot demonstrate that either way.** Traced directly (temporarily
instrumenting `RoundBudget.take()` during a real replay, then reverting):
replaying Case 2b with this fix in place still only makes two `search_files`
calls, both correctly drawn from the new free pool —
`project_discovery_used` reaches 2, the **main round budget never moves off
0 for the entire turn**. The model in this specific recording simply stops
after its second search and tells the user to move the file themselves,
with room to spare in both the free pool and the main budget. Case 2b's
actual failure, as captured in this one recording, was never a
budget-crowding case the way Case 2a's six-straight-discovery-calls
evidence was — it's the model choosing not to attempt a third tool call at
all. That's a different, still-open, newly-clarified gap (something about
how the two `search_files` results or the accumulated context shapes the
model's next move, not the round-budget mechanism this item was scoped to
fix) — see `tests/test_replay_fixtures.py`'s updated `check_known_gap` note
for the full trace-based explanation. This item's own code change is real,
tested, and correct on its own terms (it does exactly what K.2.4.1 decided);
it just isn't the fix for Case 2b specifically.

**Priority:** P1.

### K.2.5 Finish Part E Ask-console persistence/replay

**Status:** PARTIAL — K.2.5.1 and K.2.5.2 DONE (rev. 2026-09-22e, 2026-09-22f);
K.2.5.3 shipped then **reopened** (rev. 2026-09-26b, reopened 2026-09-26h —
see K.2.5.3 below); K.2.5.4 still OPEN. **Sync note, 2026-09-26h: this
document had no record of K.2.5.3 shipping at all — only the status-audit
document did. Backfilled below from the audit's own account so the
reopening note that follows has something to reopen.**

**What it does:** Makes the Ask panel's right-side command/console trace survive
reload, reconnect, Stop, process interruption and conversation switching in
the same way the dedicated console store already survives for live runs.

**Current source:**
- `jarvis-cli/jarvis/console_store.py` already persists per-conversation events.
- `web/server.js` already exposes `GET /api/console/:id` and clear.
- `web/public/app.js` has `askTraceByConv` and `renderAskTraceForConv()`, and
  (as of this fix) `loadAskTraceForConv()` + `askLineFromStoredEntry()`, which
  hydrate `askTraceByConv` from the server the first time a tab sees a given
  conversation.
- `loadConsoleHistoryForConv()` still reloads only `surface: "live"` — that's
  correct, unrelated to this fix; the Ask surface is now handled by its own
  function rather than folded into that one.

#### K.2.5.1 Add Ask-surface replay

**Status:** DONE, rev. 2026-09-22e (`jarvis-ask-trace-replay.patch`).

**What was actually needed:** the server-side half of this item was already
built — `console_store.log()`/`begin_turn()`/`end_turn()` already default to
`surface="ask"`, and `GET /api/console/:id?surface=ask` already worked end to
end (confirmed directly: wrote a real turn through `console_store` and read
it back via `jarvis console-read <id> --surface ask`, byte-checked the JSON
shape). Only the UI-side wiring was missing, exactly as this item's own
`current source` note above already said.

**Change made:**
- New `askLineFromStoredEntry(line)` in `app.js` maps one stored
  `{kind, text, tool}` line to the same `{text, cls}` shape a *live* run
  already produces (`command` → `"$ jarvis"`/cmd, `provider` → sys,
  `tool-call`/`tool-result` → tool, `error` → fail, `status` → done only for
  the literal text `"answered"`, fail otherwise; `narration` and anything
  unrecognized → `null`, i.e. not shown, rather than guessed at).
- New `loadAskTraceForConv(convId)` calls
  `Api.getConsole(convId, { surface: "ask", afterLastClear: true, limit: 2000 })`
  and populates `state.askTraceByConv[convId]` — but only if that key doesn't
  already exist, so a trace already recorded (or being recorded live) in this
  browser session is never clobbered by a replay fetch.
- `selectConversation()` now `await`s `loadAskTraceForConv(id)` immediately
  before `renderAskTraceForConv(id)` — the one call site every path that
  shows an older conversation already goes through (sidebar click, and the
  reconnect-restore path), so no other call site needed touching.

**Change (as originally specced):** Persist/replay the Ask trace through the
same console store using a clear surface discriminator, then hydrate
`askTraceByConv` from the server. — done exactly as specced; the "clear
surface discriminator" was already `surface="ask"` vs `surface="live"`,
pre-existing on the server side.

**Verification:** new `tests/verify_ask_trace_replay.js` (13 checks) —
slices `askLineFromStoredEntry` straight out of `app.js` (same technique as
`verify_math_rendering.js`) and checks every kind `ai_client.py`'s
`console_store` calls actually write, plus truncation of long tool
arguments/results and forward-compatibility with an unrecognized kind. Also
manually verified the full round trip once end-to-end (write via
`console_store`, read back via `jarvis console-read --surface ask`, confirmed
the JSON shape matches what the new JS code expects field-for-field). Full
suite re-run: **70 Python `test_*.py` files + 2 Node `verify_*.js` files, all
pass, 0 fail.**

**Priority:** P1.

#### K.2.5.2 Preserve crash/Stop pointer semantics

**Status:** DONE, rev. 2026-09-22f (`jarvis-crash-reclaim-consoleref.patch`).

**What was actually needed:** exactly the gap E.8 disclosed rather than
fixed — `_reclaim_stale_pending()` (`conversations.py`) runs in a **new**
process (the next `jarvis ask` for that conversation), so it has no way to
learn which console-store turn belonged to the dead process; that
bookkeeping (`console_store._ACTIVE`) is plain in-process state that died
with it.

**Change made:**
- `console_store.begin_turn(conv_id)` in `ai_client.ask()` now runs
  **before** `conversations.begin_exchange(...)`, not after, so the turn id
  exists in time to hand over.
- `conversations.begin_exchange()` gained an optional `console_turn=`
  argument; when given, it's saved as a `consoleTurn` field on the pending
  exchange — the one thing a brand-new process couldn't otherwise recover.
- `_reclaim_stale_pending()` now reads that field (lazily importing
  `console_store` to avoid a module-load cycle — `console_store.py` already
  imports `conversations.py` for `is_valid_id`), calls a new
  `console_store.line_count_for_turn(conv_id, turn)`, and attaches a real
  `{"type": "consoleRef", "data": {"turn": ..., "lines": ...}}` extra — the
  same shape the in-process abandon path already produces — instead of
  leaving the reclaimed exchange with no pointer at all.
- **Caught and fixed while testing this, not part of the original ask:**
  the new `consoleTurn` field wasn't being cleaned up on the *normal*
  completion/abandon paths (`complete_exchange`/`abandon_exchange`, both
  routed through `_finish_pending`) — only in the reclaim path. Without
  that second fix, every single successful exchange would have carried a
  dead, unused `consoleTurn` key forever. `_finish_pending()` now pops it
  alongside `pending` whenever a turn resolves normally.

**Change (as originally specced):** Close the small recovery hole where
stale pending conversation reclamation can preserve the console file but
fail to attach the `consoleRef` extra to the recovered conversation
record. — done as specced.

**Verification:** new `tests/test_console_store.py` cases —
`test_hard_kill_reclaim_still_gets_a_consoleref` (simulates the exact
SIGKILL scenario: `begin_turn`+`begin_exchange`+two logged lines, then
*nothing* — no `end_turn`, no `abandon_pending_turn` — followed by a fresh
`begin_exchange()` standing in for the next process; asserts the reclaimed
exchange now carries `{"turn": ..., "lines": 2}`, matching only the lines
actually written before the simulated kill, not a phantom closing status
line that was never written) and
`test_reclaim_with_no_console_turn_is_unaffected` (a pending exchange with
no `consoleTurn` at all — e.g. one written before this fix, or by
`_run_pending_action`, which never calls `console_store.begin_turn()` —
still reclaims to `interrupted` with no `consoleRef`, exactly as before).
Two existing tests extended to also assert `consoleTurn` doesn't leak into
a normally-resolved exchange. Full suite: `tests/test_console_store.py`
57/57 (was 49); full `tests/test_*.py` re-run, **70/70**; `build_info.py`
regenerated again (build 29 → 30) since this changed the source tree.

**Priority:** P2.

#### K.2.5.4 Clean up legacy console extras

**Status:** INVESTIGATED, left as-is (rev. 2026-09-22h) — the change as
specced would be a regression, not a cleanup.

**What was found:** the `"console"`/`dumpLines` extra (`ai_client._split_console_dump`,
rendered by `renderThreadExtra`'s `"console"` case in `app.js`) and the
`"consoleRef"` extra this section assumed had superseded it are not the same
mechanism and are not in an old/new relationship. `dumpLines` heuristically
splits console-dump-*looking* text back out of the model's own reply prose
(so a raw shell dump the model pastes into its answer renders as a distinct
block instead of garbled markdown). `consoleRef` is a pointer into the
persistent per-conversation console store (`{"turn", "lines"}`) — entirely
different content, built and saved correctly by five call sites in
`ai_client.py`/`conversations.py`. Checked directly: **`app.js` has no
`case "consoleRef"` anywhere** — the pointer is written on every resolved
exchange but has no UI consumer at all yet. Removing or confining `dumpLines`
now, on the theory that `consoleRef` already covers its job, would delete
the only mechanism that currently renders this content and replace it with
nothing.

**Decision:** leave both as they are. This item's own precondition —
"after ... all replay paths are migrated" — doesn't hold, because the
migration target (a `consoleRef` renderer) was never built. If a future
change adds one (e.g. a compact "N console lines" link on an exchange,
distinct from K.2.5.1's full side-panel replay), *that* would be the right

### K.2.7 Notification importance levels + clipboard flood protection

**Status:** ✅ DONE — both real issues found during the 2026-09-26j
verification are now fixed, 2026-09-28, `jarvis-k27-fixes.patch` /
`jarvis-k27-fixes-patch-notes.md`. See the "✅ FIXED, 2026-09-28" notes
appended to each issue below for what changed; the original verification
writeup is kept in place above them since it's still an accurate record of
what was found and why.

**What's done, verified directly against the delivered code:**

- `notifier.py` — `normalize_level()`, `_channels_for_level()`,
  `LEVEL_NAMES`, `_LEVEL_ALIASES` (back-compat for `low`/`normal`/`high`
  and English words like `urgent`/`critical`). `_channels_for_level()`
  confirms the intended cumulative shape in code: level ≥2 adds
  `stream`/`toast`, level ≥4 adds `discord`/`instagram` — matches D.2.1's

- `digest.py` — `should_batch_level()`, the shared source of truth level

  running `tests/test_notification_levels.py`: **67/67 checks passed
  across 20/20 tests.**
- K.2.7.1a (custom tool/action access) — `normalize_level()`'s lookup order
  checks `config["levels"][source]` before `config["levels"][kind]`,
  giving a custom tool/action its own default the same way a built-in kind
  gets one. Matches spec.
- K.2.7.1b (scheduler plumbing) — **done**, contrary to the "designed but
  not written" status in the progress report this revision is merging in;
  the delivered code has moved past that report. `scheduler_tools.py` has

  `schedule_task`/`schedule_watch`, plus the `level` field in each tool's
  JSON schema. Verified via `tests/test_scheduler.py`: **95/95 passed**,
  including a captured notification record showing `"level": 2,
  "level_name": "standard"` for a task-kind job.

**One deliberate, disclosed default change, not a conflict:** `task`-kind
notifications now default to level 2 (Standard), which adds a toast where
the old `channels` config had `["inbox","stream"]` with no toast — because
the old per-kind channel dict doesn't map cleanly onto 5 discrete levels.
Confirmed in `notifier.py`'s own `DEFAULT_CONFIG` comment and reconfigurable
per-installation via `levels.task` in `notify_config.json`.

**Real issue #1 — D-N1's shipped behavior doesn't match the owner's actual
decision.** The owner decided (D-N1, 2026-09-26i): level 3 re-surfaces on
an interval, not just a non-auto-dismissing toast (Option B, chosen over
Option A). **The shipped frontend implements Option A only.**
`web/public/app.js`'s `toast()` function, verified directly:

```
// D.2.1 level 3+ (Persistent): the toast doesn't auto-dismiss — it
// stays until the user clicks it away, instead of the usual timeout.
t.onclick = sticky ? () => { t.hidden = true; t.onclick = null; } : null;
```

There is no timer or re-surfacing logic anywhere in the toast code — a
level-3 toast shows once and stays until manually dismissed, full stop.
Notably, `notifier.py`'s own comment describing level 3 is worded
ambiguously enough to read as either option ("the toast doesn't auto-
dismiss; it re-surfaces until acknowledged" — conflating both in one
sentence), which may be how this happened: whoever wrote the frontend
implemented the "doesn't auto-dismiss" half and treated it as done,
without registering that a separate re-surface-on-an-interval mechanism
was also required. **This needs a real fix, not just a doc update** — the
frontend needs an actual interval timer that re-shows a level-3
notification periodically until acknowledged, per D-N1. This wasn't a
gap the implementing agent flagged themselves; it was found by comparing
the shipped code against this document's own recorded decision.

**✅ FIXED, 2026-09-28 (`jarvis-k27-fixes.patch`).** `toast()` now
implements Option B, as decided. For a persistent (level 3+) notification
it auto-dismisses after the normal ~4.2s like any other toast, then
re-shows the same message every `RESURFACE_INTERVAL_MS` (10 minutes) until
the user clicks it away, capped at `RESURFACE_MAX` (6 reps, ~1 hour) so an
unattended machine doesn't loop forever. Both constants are named and
placed right above `toast()` since the owner hadn't specified exact
values — this document's own note above said to "default to something
conservative... pending further owner input if the first pass feels wrong
in practice," so these are open to tuning. The `toast()` options key was
renamed `sticky` → `persistent` (its one call site, in
`showNotification()`, updated to match) since "sticky" no longer describes
recurring behavior; the `.toast.is-sticky` CSS class name and pulsing-glow
visual were kept (still the right "needs your attention" cue), only its
doc comment corrected.

**Real issue #2 — K.2.7.2 (clipboard burst coalescing) broke 3 existing
tests.** `clipboard_watch.py` now calls `notifier.normalize_level(None,
kind="clipboard_watch")` unconditionally on every matched clipboard
change (to decide burst behavior). `tests/test_clipboard_watch.py`'s
`_install_fake_notifier()` helper — pre-existing, not part of this
delivery — stubs the module's `notifier` reference as
`types.SimpleNamespace(notify=fake_notify)`, which has no
`normalize_level` attribute. Result, **run directly during this
verification pass:**

```
FAIL test_run_notifies_on_change_no_pattern: AttributeError: 'types.SimpleNamespace' object has no attribute 'normalize_level'
FAIL test_run_skips_non_matching_changes: AttributeError: 'types.SimpleNamespace' object has no attribute 'normalize_level'
FAIL test_run_truncates_long_clipboard_text_in_notification: AttributeError: 'types.SimpleNamespace' object has no attribute 'normalize_level'
19/22 passed
```

This is a genuine regression, not a pre-existing failure — these three
tests worked before K.2.7.2 touched `clipboard_watch.py`, and the fake
notifier fixture was never updated to account for the new call. Fix is
small: either give the fake notifier a `normalize_level` method in the
test file, or have `clipboard_watch.py` degrade gracefully if
`normalize_level` is missing — the former is more honest, since a fake
that doesn't implement the interface it's standing in for is the actual
bug. **Also worth noting: `_burst_decision()`/`_maybe_flush()`/
`_buffer_change()` — the burst-coalescing logic itself — have zero
dedicated tests anywhere in this repo.** The only test contact with this
code is the 3 now-broken ones above, which were testing unrelated
clipboard behavior and happened to exercise the new code path as a side
effect of calling `run()`.

**✅ FIXED, 2026-09-28 (`jarvis-k27-fixes.patch`).** Fixed the actual bug,
which was in the test fixture, not production code — the more-honest fix
this document itself flagged as preferred. `_install_fake_notifier()` now
also exposes `normalize_level`, delegating straight to the real
implementation (`normalize_level()`'s own lookup logic already has
dedicated coverage elsewhere, K.2.7.1/`test_notification_levels.py`, so
this fixture's job stays limited to intercepting delivery). All 3 tests
pass again. While there, generalized the fixture to
`_install_fake_notifier(stop_after=1)` (default unchanged) so a test can
let more than one `notify()` call happen before breaking `run()`'s loop —
needed for the new burst test added below, since a burst by definition
spans several calls. Also added the dedicated burst-logic tests this
section's own "worth noting" flagged as missing — see K.2.7.3 below.

**What's genuinely done, no issues found:** the level-5 confirm modal

pattern) and D-N2 (Broadcast — `_channels_for_level()` correctly adds

### K.2.8 100k+ input-token burn containment from the supplied 2026-09-22 log

**Status:** ✅ DONE — verified 2026-09-26j, `jarvis-k28-token-burn.patch`.
Real fix, independently confirmed against actual delivered code — unlike
the 2026-09-26e "reported done" episode this document withdrew (see
revision 26f), this closure has an actual diff, an actual regression test,
and an actual test run behind it.

**What the implementing agent found:** the master plan's own framing above
(redundant per-request context, retry/cancellation loops) pointed at the
wrong mechanism. The per-request history cap and the F.7 cross-retry carry
logic were already well-engineered and not the source of the growth. The
real culprit is **cross-turn compounding**: each new `ask()` call gets a
fresh in-memory cache, so a repeated identical nudge across *separate
turns* (not retries within one turn) was never caught by anything, and the
persisted conversation history resent every prior near-duplicate exchange
verbatim on every subsequent turn.

**Baseline evidence:** 376 rows; 77 requests; 70 usage records; 123,368
reported input tokens; 2,027 output tokens; 572 appearances of the exact
unchanged user message `write_on_screen continue and enter` inside request
payloads.

#### K.2.8.1/K.2.8.2 Identify the redundant-context boundary and collapse it

**Status:** ✅ DONE, verified. `conversations.conversation_messages()` gained
`_collapse_repeated_user_turns()`: a run of 3+ consecutive identical user
turns collapses into one representative pair (the latest occurrence's
assistant reply is kept) with a repeat-count note, instead of resending
every occurrence verbatim. **Verified directly against the delivered code**
(`jarvis-cli/jarvis/conversations.py`, `_collapse_repeated_user_turns()`)
and by running `tests/test_k28_token_burn.py`: a reconstructed 4-run
identical-turn sequence collapses to 1 pair; the collapsed pair keeps the
latest assistant reply; the repeat count is annotated; an unrelated
trailing turn is left untouched; a run of only 2 is correctly left
uncollapsed (the 3+ threshold holds); a varied conversation keeps every
exchange; collapsed payload size does not grow with repeat count.

**Priority:** P1 — closed.

#### K.2.8.3 Make repeated cancellation/retry loops terminal, across turns

**Status:** ✅ DONE, verified. A new cross-turn check in `ai_client.py`
(`_declined_action_extra()`, `_load_declined_repeat()`,
`_declined_repeat_reply()`): if the current message is textually identical
(case/whitespace-insensitive) to the one that just got a tool call
declined, the turn short-circuits with a canned reply and never contacts a
provider. **Verified directly against the delivered code** and by test: an
exact repeat after a decline is caught; a case/whitespace-different repeat
is still caught; a genuinely different message ("yes go ahead", "okay do
it", "write something else instead", and an empty message) is correctly
*not* caught; the block has a TTL and expires; an unrelated intervening
exchange clears the block.

**Priority:** P1 — closed.

#### K.2.8.4 Replay the supplied log and add a permanent regression fixture

**Status:** ✅ DONE, verified — resolves this document's own earlier
caveat ("no replay numbers supplied," revision 26e). `tests/
test_k28_token_burn.py` exists. As disclosed by the implementing agent and
confirmed here: the real 123,368-token JSONL is not in this repository —
only its statistics are quoted in the master plan — so the fixture
*reconstructs* the documented pattern (a long run of an unchanging turn) at
a smaller but proportional scale, rather than replaying the original file
byte-for-byte. This mirrors how K.2.1 handled the same gap for an earlier
finding, and is disclosed in the test file's own docstring, not hidden.
**Run directly as part of this verification pass: 21/21 checks passed
across 9/9 tests.**

**Priority:** P1 — closed.

**Acceptance:** all four sub-criteria confirmed by direct test run —
collapsed payload is far smaller than the naive resend and does not grow
with repeat count; the cross-turn declined-action check fires correctly and
only on true repeats; action/cancellation semantics are preserved (a
different message still gets through normally). **Not yet independently
confirmed:** the report's claim that "the full existing 16-file test suite
still passes clean" — this verification pass spot-checked `tests/
test_scheduler.py` (95/95 passed) and `tests/test_channels.py` (137/137
passed), both unaffected, but did not re-run all 16 files the report
refers to by name, so that specific count is taken on the implementing
agent's word rather than independently reproduced here.

### K.2.9 Loosen the shipped-tool Test Checklist convention — new requirement, owner instruction 2026-09-26h; decided 2026-09-26i

**Status:** OPEN (not yet implemented) — requirement decided, reverses the
choice documented in L.1.6 above.

**Background:** while building L.1 (`recent_dms`), the agent found that
shipping the tool's Test Checklist entry as an inline `TEST_CHECKLIST` —
an option the `_template.py` custom-tool template documents but that, in
practice, no shipped/built-in tool actually uses — broke
`tests/test_checklist_supplied.py::test_payload_carries_a_custom_tools_entry_and_only_that_tools`,
which encodes "only a user-authored tool supplies its entry inline" as an
invariant. That agent fixed it by moving `recent_dms`'s entry into
`web/public/test-checklist-data.js` instead, matching every other shipped
tool, rather than loosening the test.

**Change requested:** loosen `test_checklist_supplied.py` instead, so a
built-in/shipped tool is also allowed to supply its Test Checklist entry
inline via `TEST_CHECKLIST`, the same as a custom tool can. This does not
require moving `recent_dms`'s own entry back — its current placement in
`test-checklist-data.js` stays valid either way — it only removes the
restriction that currently makes the inline path custom-tool-only.

**DECIDED, owner 2026-09-26i: restate the invariant, don't drop it.**
Loosening the test still needs a replacement guarantee — the fix should add
a check that no tool's entry appears twice (once inline, once in
`test-checklist-data.js`), regardless of which mechanism a given tool used,
rather than just removing the old custom-tool-only restriction and leaving
nothing in its place.

**Priority:** P2.

**Acceptance:** `test_checklist_supplied.py` permits a shipped tool to
supply its Test Checklist entry via inline `TEST_CHECKLIST`; a new check
catches any tool whose entry appears both inline and in
`test-checklist-data.js` at once; existing coverage for the custom-tool case
is unaffected; the full suite (76 files as of L.1's own pass) still passes;
`recent_dms`'s existing `test-checklist-data.js` entry is left as-is, not
migrated back to inline,
unless a future change explicitly asks for that too.

## K.3 P2 — major remaining product functionality

### K.3.1 Part A §8 — real-time token streaming of text and thinking

**Status:** IMPLEMENTED IN PATCH, rev. 2026-10-01f (`jarvis-web-streaming.patch`,
against `jarvis-main_67_.zip`; **not verified in a browser**, `server.js` never
run) — K.3.1.1–K.3.1.3 were DONE at rev. 2026-09-25
(`jarvis-streaming-all-adapters.patch`, following
`jarvis-streaming-foundation-ollama.patch`); K.3.1.4 (CLI marker line + web
transport) and K.3.1.5 (browser render entry point) are now implemented in the
new patch. **Streaming is on for web asks only** (`server.js` sets
`JARVIS_STREAM_MARKERS=1`; `JARVIS_WEB_STREAM=0` is the escape hatch). A plain
terminal run, the scheduler and subagent steps still use the blocking
transport. See K.3.1.4/.5 for what the patch does and does not cover, and the
"As-built, rev. 2026-10-01f" block at the end of this section.

**What it does:** Lets the user see model text and reasoning arrive while a turn
is running instead of waiting for the provider round to finish. This is the
missing complement to §5's interim-message narration.

#### K.3.1.1 Define a provider-neutral streaming callback/event shape

**Status:** DONE. New in `ai_providers.py`: `EVENT_TEXT`/`EVENT_THINKING`/
`EVENT_TOOL`/`EVENT_ROUND_END`/`EVENT_RESET`; `set_stream_sink(callback)` /
`_emit_stream(kind, **data)` (never raises, same philosophy as
`_surface_interim_text`'s hook call); `stream_enabled()` /
`set_log_context(..., stream=...)` as a SEPARATE knob from the sink (an
adapter can use the streaming transport with nobody listening — useful on
its own for between-chunks hang detection, §1b/§1d); a shared `_post_stream()`
next to `_post_json()` (same never-raises contract, `stream=True`,
`requests`' own read timeout naturally becomes a between-chunks timeout);
`_log_stream_response()` so the Logs viewer still gets one clean assembled
response entry per round, never one per raw chunk.

**Load-bearing decision made while implementing this, not in the original
spec:** every one of these defaults to **off** — `stream_enabled()`'s bare
getattr fallback, `set_log_context()`'s own function signature default, and
`clear_log_context()`'s reset all say `False`, and `ai_client.ask()`'s newly
added `stream_this_ask = bool(_defaults.get("stream", False))` also defaults
False. This is deliberately NOT what this item (and §8.2) call for on
paper (on-by-default). Reason: turning it on by default at the
`ai_providers.py` layer, before K.3.1.4/.5 exist to actually consume a
`stream_sink` callback, would have silently changed behavior for every
existing caller that monkeypatches `ai_providers._post_json` without
knowing `_post_stream` exists — confirmed directly: doing this the first
time broke 4 checks in `tests/test_finish_signal.py`. Flipping the
`ai_client.ask()`-level default to on is a one-line change (`stream_this_ask`'s
own fallback), intentionally saved for once the CLI/server/UI legs actually
exist and there's been a real audit of what else in the existing suite
would need updating — not folded silently into this patch.

**Change:** Add a shared event contract for text chunks, thinking chunks, turn
boundaries and errors without duplicating provider-specific UI logic. — done
as specced, see above.

**Priority:** P2.

#### K.3.1.2 Implement native streaming in each adapter

**Status:** DONE, rev. 2026-09-25 — all five adapters converted, in the
order this section already suggested (Ollama first, since it's local and
free to test end to end without a real network).

- **Ollama (done first):** new `_stream_ollama_chat(resp, url)` parses
  Ollama's NDJSON framing (one JSON object per line, no `data:` prefix, no
  `[DONE]` sentinel — genuinely different from the other four adapters'
  SSE). Tool calls confirmed to arrive whole in one line, never fragmented.
- **OpenAI-compatible:** SSE, `data: {...}` frames terminated by `[DONE]`.
- **Anthropic:** SSE, named events; fragmented tool-call
  `input_json_delta` chunks require the block's `signature_delta` to
  survive intact for replay.
- **Gemini:** a different endpoint entirely —
  `streamGenerateContent?alt=sse` — rather than a body flag; delta-shaped
  parts with a cumulative `usageMetadata`.
- **Cohere:** SSE, named events like Anthropic's; no thinking events, since
  this family has no reasoning-model member yet.

Every adapter reassembles its stream into the exact response shape its own
non-streamed parser already produces, so `_record_usage`, `_collect_thinking`,
`finish_signal`, etc. run completely unchanged whether streaming is on or off
for that attempt, and each reports its deltas live via `_emit_stream()` as
they're parsed. Covered by `tests/test_streaming_ollama.py` (24 checks —
text-only, thinking + text, a tool-call round followed by a final round,
usage/finish-signal parity with the non-streaming path, a malformed line
skipped rather than fatal, a mid-stream connection drop ending as a clean
`AIResult(False, ...)` rather than a raised exception) and
`tests/test_streaming_other_adapters.py` (60 checks, one file for the
remaining four adapters since they share the same shape-parity approach).

**Follow-up, rev. 2026-10-02d (`jarvis-streaming-complete.patch`):** the OpenAI-compatible adapter
always sent `stream_options: {include_usage: true}`. A strict host that answers
400/422 "unknown/unsupported field" for it would have failed the attempt and
burned keys over a request shape jarvis chose. It now drops the field and
retries once, and stops sending it for the rest of that call
(`looks_like_stream_options_rejected()`; shares the retry loop with the
thinking-keys retry, so a request carrying both bad fields is fixed in two
steps). Groq, which already streamed through this adapter, is covered by the
same path. See K.3.1.6.

**Change:** OpenAI-compatible, Anthropic, Gemini, Cohere and Ollama each need
provider-native stream parsing mapped into the shared event shape. — done,
all five.

**Priority:** P2.

#### K.3.1.3 Thread stream events through `ai_client.ask()`

**Status:** DONE, rev. 2026-09-25. `ask()`'s `on_stream=` parameter is wired
to `ai_providers.set_stream_sink()` (and `set_log_context(..., stream=...)`)
on every attempt, gated by `defaults.stream`/`stream_this_ask` the same way
`on_interim_text` is gated — mirroring that existing thread-local pattern.
This is live end to end for any caller that turns `defaults.stream` on and
passes `on_stream=`; no caller does yet (cli.py, the only current caller of
`ask()`, doesn't pass it — that's K.3.1.4's job), so it fires correctly under
direct test (as `test_streaming_ollama.py`/`test_streaming_other_adapters.py`
do) but nothing in the actual product exercises it yet.

**Priority:** P2.

#### K.3.1.4 Send stream events through the web transport

**Status:** ✅ IMPLEMENTED IN PATCH 2026-10-01f (`jarvis-web-streaming.patch`;
**`server.js` was only syntax-checked and covered by source checks — its npm
dependencies were not installed, so it was never started; nothing was run in a
browser**).

**What the original spec missed:** the CLI half was also absent — `cli.py` never
passed `on_stream=` to `ask()`, so "web transport" alone would still have
streamed nothing. The patch adds both halves.

**As built:**
- New `jarvis/stream_markers.py`: `StreamMarkerSink` is `ask(on_stream=...)`'s
  callback. It prints one `JARVIS_STREAM {json}` line per event
  (`{"k":"text"|"thinking","d":...}`, `{"k":"tool","name":...}`,
  `{"k":"round_end","finish":"tool"|"done"}`, `{"k":"reset"}`). Text/thinking
  deltas are coalesced over ~40 ms; a change of kind or any non-delta event
  flushes first, so order is preserved and thinking is never merged into text.
  Tool events carry the **name only** (arguments are partial JSON on most
  adapters, §8.3). It never raises (a dead stdout cannot break the attempt).
- `cli.py`: builds the sink only when `JARVIS_STREAM_MARKERS=1`, passes
  `on_stream=`, and closes (flushes) it in a `finally` before the reply is
  printed. The final assembled reply is still printed as ordinary stdout, so
  the exit/persist path is unchanged.
- `ai_client.ask()`: **passing `on_stream` now opts that ask into streaming.**
  `defaults.stream` stays the explicit override in both directions (true =
  stream even with no listener; an explicit false forces the blocking path
  even with `on_stream`). Unset follows whether anyone is listening. This
  changes K.3.1.1's "default off" reasoning: the global default is still off,
  but a caller that listens gets it.
- `ask()` also now **emits `EVENT_RESET`** (nothing emitted it before): when an
  attempt fails — or its finished reply is rejected by `_is_tool_trace_reply` —
  after uncommitted text/thinking already streamed, and also before a
  short-429 wait-and-retry. Text streamed before a tool call is never reset
  (§8.4); a round that ended `done` stays provisional until the attempt is
  accepted.

#### K.3.1.5 Render through one browser entry point

**Status:** ✅ IMPLEMENTED IN PATCH 2026-10-01f (`jarvis-web-streaming.patch`;
**not verified in a browser**; the DOM logic is covered only by
`tests/verify_ask_stream_render.js` against a fake DOM, 72 checks).

**Dependency, honestly:** this item was meant to wait for the render-pipeline
consolidation (I.3 step 3 / I-B10), which is still open. It was not done. The
streaming code is a single entry point of its own —
`applyAskStreamEvent()` in `app.js`, between the `§8 live streaming (K.3.1.5)
BEGIN/END` markers — that reuses the existing `renderMarkdown` /
`linkifyPaths` / `renderMathIn` helpers, so streamed and final rendering share
those, but they are **not** one consolidated path. Revisit when I-B10 lands.

**As built (§8.5):**
- Thinking: its own collapsible `.thinking-block` per segment, streaming plain
  text; header "Thinking…" with a pulsing marker, becoming "Thought for N s"
  and collapsing when the segment ends. Show/hide is the **existing "Show
  reasoning trace" toggle** (`thinkState.show`): a display switch only,
  applied instantly and mid-turn by `syncStreamThinkingVisibility()` (turning
  it on reveals everything already streamed; it sends no request).
- Text: streams into the turn's pending bubble as markdown, **at most one
  render per animation frame** (not O(n²)); an unclosed code fence is closed
  in the preview only (`balanceStreamingMarkdown`).
- A round that ends in a tool call **commits** its text as its own message
  (a real interim message, §8.4); the pending bubble starts over. A round that
  ends `done` stays provisional in the pending bubble.
- `reset` (§8.6): discards only the current round's uncommitted text and
  thinking blocks and adds a "Switching provider" note. Nothing committed by an
  earlier tool round is touched.
- Status line: `thinking…` → `writing…` → `running <tool>…`.
- Scrolling follows the stream only while the reader is near the bottom.
- Stop: `finalizeAskBubble` keeps whatever had streamed (marked "Stopped —
  this reply is incomplete") instead of "(no response)", and closes any
  thinking block still open.
- Reconcile: the finished reply (ask-stdout lines) is authoritative and
  replaces the streamed preview; a late animation frame cannot paint over it.
- Not covered: while the user is viewing another conversation nothing touches
  the thread, and what was streamed is **not** replayed on switching back
  (only the text preview is repainted); live thinking blocks and streamed
  interim bubbles are not saved as such — after a reload the saved `thinking`
  and "Said along the way" extras render instead.

**Priority:** P2.

#### K.3.1.6 Terminal (TTY) streaming and the `stream_options` retry — as-built, rev. 2026-10-02d

**Status:** ✅ IMPLEMENTED IN PATCH, rev. 2026-10-02d (`jarvis-streaming-complete.patch`, against `jarvis-main_70_.zip`;
four files: `jarvis/ai_providers.py`, `jarvis/cli.py`, `jarvis/stream_markers.py`, new
`tests/test_streaming_tty_and_options.py`). `git apply --check` is clean on a fresh `_70` unzip.
**Never run in a real terminal or against a live provider.** `jarvis/*.py` changed, so
`build_info.py` needs the usual bump (the patch does not include one).

What it does:
- **`TerminalStreamSink`** (in `stream_markers.py`) has the same `on_stream(kind, **data)`
  contract as `StreamMarkerSink`. Text deltas go straight to stdout behind the normal
  `Name:` prefix, written once per round. Thinking deltas go dimmed to stderr, and only
  when the reasoning `show` setting is on (the same setting `jarvis think` flips). Text
  streamed before a tool call stays on screen (§8.4); the line is just closed. A `reset`
  (mid-stream failover, §8.6) cannot unprint a terminal, so it ends the line and prints a
  dim "switching provider - restarting the reply" note on stderr, and only if text had
  actually been shown.
- **Reconcile at the end (§8.5).** `cli.py` skips the final `print(prefix + result.text)` only
  when the streamed text of the last round equals `result.text` (whitespace-insensitive,
  `covers()`); otherwise the authoritative reply is printed as before, so what is displayed
  and what is saved cannot silently drift. When streaming is active the duplicate stderr
  `»` interim line is suppressed, since that text is already on screen.
- **When it is on:** only when `stdout` and `stderr` are both ttys, `JARVIS_UI` is not
  `web`, `JARVIS_STREAM_MARKERS` is not `1`, and `policy.unattended_context_from_env()` is
  empty. `JARVIS_TTY_STREAM=0` is the escape hatch; `defaults.stream: false` still forces
  the blocking path, because `ask()` keeps that override in both directions.
- **`stream_options` retry** (`ai_providers.py`): see K.3.1.2's follow-up note.

Verification actually performed:
- `tests/test_streaming_tty_and_options.py` (new, 22 checks): the sink (one prefix, thinking
  hidden vs dimmed on stderr, interim text kept, last-round `final_text`, reset note only
  when something was shown, write errors swallowed, `covers()`), the rejection detector
  against real-looking error strings and the Groq tool-choice 400 (must not match), and an
  end-to-end `call_openai_compatible` run where the first request is answered 400
  "unrecognized argument: stream_options" and the retry streams normally.
- Re-run and passing: `test_streaming_ollama` 24, `test_streaming_other_adapters` (53 `ok` lines,
  0 failed), `test_stream_markers` 23, `test_ai_providers_fixes` 24, `test_ask_output` 38,
  `test_ollama_openai_compat_thinking` 20, `test_provider_failover_completed_work` 15,
  `test_provider_override` 10, `test_thinking_round_cap` 12.
- **The full suite was not run** (the run hit the sandbox's 300-second limit). `test_cli*`/web
  Node verifiers were not run against this patch either.

Known issues, not fixed:
- `cli.py` still prints the stderr token line and `JARVIS_USAGE` **twice** per ask (the duplicated
  block noted under K.3.1 as-built). On a terminal that is now visible as two identical token lines.
- The "notifications waiting" block (`notifier.render_for_terminal`) prints just above the reply
  in the non-streaming path. With streaming the reply is already on screen, so the block now
  appears **after** it. Left alone; say if you want it moved before the first token.
- The `Name:` prefix is read from `ai_config` before the ask, so a persona changed mid-ask by a
  tool would not be reflected in the streamed prefix.
- Overlap check owed: other open patches touch `cli.py` and `ai_providers.py` (the L.16
  items-7-8-10 patch edits `ai_providers.py`; several touch `cli.py`). Run `git apply --check`
  for this patch on top of whichever of them you apply.
- `AGENTS.md` and `REPO_MAP.md` were not edited (`stream_markers.py` is still not listed in
  `REPO_MAP.md`; this patch adds a class to it and a new test file).

What this does **not** cover: subagent steps (K.3.2.4), scheduled/unattended runs (by design),
the voice path (`cli.py`'s separate `ai_client.ask(heard, ...)` call does not pass `on_stream`),
and the browser pass.

### K.3.6 F.9 — true per-round pacing across adapter loops

**Status:** DONE, rev. 2026-09-27, `jarvis-k36-round-pacing.patch`.

**What it does:** Prevents a fast inner agent from burning provider capacity in
rapid consecutive requests even when keys are isolated.

**Current state:** the earlier requirement's “or use a different key” half was
already satisfied by `spread_keys()`. The pacing half is now built.

**Delivered:** `key_health.py` gained `pace_key(provider_name, key,
interval=None, now=None)`: extends the existing on-disk `key_health.json`
state with a `last_request` timestamp per key (alongside the existing
cooldown fields, same file, same pruning), and blocks until at least
`interval` seconds have passed since that key's last recorded request —
across processes, same as every other piece of key-health state, since
`jarvis` is a new process per call. Default floor is
`DEFAULT_MIN_ROUND_INTERVAL = 3.0s`; `key=None` (Ollama — no per-key quota)
and `interval<=0` are both no-ops. `ai_providers.py` gained `_pace_round(provider,
api_key, cfg_defaults)`, called once per round in all five adapters
(`call_openai_compatible`, `call_anthropic`, `call_gemini`, `call_cohere`,
`call_ollama`) right before that round's request goes out. The effective
interval resolves `provider.min_round_interval_seconds` →
`cfg_defaults.min_round_interval_seconds` → the built-in default, so a
tight free-tier key can be paced harder (or a generous paid one turned off
entirely) without touching the built-in default other providers get.
Distinct from `spread_keys()`: that only helps when a second key exists to
spread to; pacing helps a single-key provider too, and stacks with
`spread_keys()` when both apply. Tests added to `tests/test_key_health.py`:
the wait/no-wait timing itself, the keyless/disabled no-ops, and
provider→defaults→built-in precedence, mocking `key_health.time.sleep` the
same way `test_short_429_wait.py` already mocks `ai_client.time.sleep` so
nothing actually sleeps in the suite. Compiles clean; patch applies with
`-p1` against the zip baseline. Test suite not run by the agent this
revision — owner to run `tests/test_key_health.py` (and the full suite,
since `ai_providers.py` is touched across all five adapters) before
relying on this.

**Priority:** P1 (closed).

**Status:** DECIDED, owner decision 2026-09-25 — **full passthrough**,
overriding this document's own "curated subset" recommendation, **conditioned
on a mandatory mitigation**: every command surfaced in the palette must carry
an explicit **risk level** (e.g. safe / caution / dangerous), and hovering a
risk-labeled command must show a tooltip with what the command does plus its
subcommands/arguments, before the owner or anyone using the palette runs it.

This changes I.2's scope materially — see the new **I.2.10** sub-section
added below for what this requires (a risk classification table for the ~146
subcommands, a hover-info data source, and UI work). The dangerous-surface
list this document originally flagged (`logs-clear`, `sched-clear`,
`notify-clear`, `notify-send`, `tool-safety-set`, `mcp-call`, `daemon-run`,
etc.) becomes the initial "dangerous" tier seed list rather than a reason to
exclude those commands outright.

### K.6.6 Extra `/` verbs (D-I5)

**Status:** DECIDED, owner decision 2026-09-25 — **ship minimal now, add
later.** Only the already-specced `/copy` verb ships in v1; the candidate
list (`/backlog add`, `/remind`, `/persona`, `/search`, `/export`) is
deferred, not rejected — revisit post-launch rather than delaying Part I to
build them now.

### K.6.7 Custom-registered commands from `/actions` (NEW, owner request 2026-09-25)

**Build status, 2026-09-30c:** ❌ NOT BUILT. The palette shipped without it; the registry format leaves room for it, but the contract is still TBD and it needs its own tracking id (§I.6 section 12).

**Status:** DECIDED — **new scope, add as a plan step.** In addition to
deferring D-I5's extra verbs, the owner wants the `/` palette architecture
itself to support commands contributed by **custom tools/actions** (i.e.
whatever a user registers under `/actions`), not just the built-in CLI
subcommand set. A custom action must be able to register:
- its own palette verb/name,
- a risk-level label (same scheme as K.6.5's dangerous-command labeling), and
- the same hover-info payload (description, subcommands/args) shown for
  built-in commands.

This is new work, not yet scoped into a K-item or Part I sub-step — see the
new **I.2.11** sub-section added below. It should reuse the same risk-label
and hover-tooltip mechanism K.6.5 requires for built-ins, rather than building
a second, parallel system.

### K.6.8 Near-miss typo handling (D-I6)

**Status:** DECIDED, owner decision 2026-09-26 — **block with a hint.** An
unknown verb within edit distance 2 of a known verb (3+ characters) blocks
the submit and shows "Unknown command `/skilload` — did you mean
`/skillload`?" with a *Send anyway* action (a second identical Enter sends).
This matches the plan's own recommended default and the I-B5/I.2.6 behaviour
already specced — no change to the existing design, just a closed decision.
Anything outside edit distance 2, or under 3 characters, is sent as prose
(`/etc is where…` stays a normal message).

### K.6.9 Clear-button confirmation (D-I7)

**Status:** DECIDED, owner decision 2026-09-26 — **yes.** The existing
**Clear** button (`app.js:4681`) should confirm before clearing, the same way
`/clear` and `/daemon stop|restart` on a running daemon now do (D-I4/K.6.5),
and the same way deleting a chat already does (native `confirm()` in
`deleteConversationConfirm`). Route Clear through the existing
`JarvisUI.confirm` modal rather than adding a second confirmation pattern, so
all three destructive-action paths behave consistently.

### K.6.10 Command feedback (D-I8)

**Status:** DECIDED, owner decision 2026-09-26 — **toast only.** No new
persisted "command chip" in the thread for v1, matching the plan's own
recommended default. This avoids touching Part E's per-exchange bucketing
(`exchangeCountByConv`), which a persisted thread item would otherwise have
to interact with. Revisit post-launch if a visible in-thread record of
executed commands turns out to be wanted.

Part J's own burst/digest acceptance cases (K.2.6.2) remain untouched — that's still real Part J human-tightening work.

## K.9 Audit limitations

This audit is a source-and-test review of the provided archive, not a live
production certification. In particular, the sandbox does not provide the
user's Windows desktop, a real Chromium session with the user's login state,
all external model/API credentials, or every OS-native clipboard/backend. Those
limitations are called out as verification gaps rather than converted into
source-code failures.

### L.1 `recent_dms` — recent DM history tool

**Status:** ✅ DONE (rev. 2026-09-26c) — `jarvis-l1-recent-dms.patch`
(`jarvis-cli/jarvis/actions/recent_dms.py` new, `actions/channel_people.py`
one-line pack-instruction addition, `tests/test_recent_dms.py` new,
`web/public/test-checklist-data.js` new entry, `build_info.py`
regenerated). **Priority:** P1

**Against L.1's own sub-items:**
- **L.1.1 Data source** — uses `channels/transcript.list_threads()` and
  `read_thread()` exactly as specified; no second DM-history store.
- **L.1.2 Scope & security** — owner-only: reads the same
  `JARVIS_CHANNEL_SENDER` / `is_owner` flag `actions/channel_people.py`
  already uses. No chat context at all (a PC/CLI call) is always allowed,
  same reasoning `actions/notify_owner.py`'s docstring gives for taking no
  target argument; a chat message is allowed only when *that* sender is
  the owner. Only inputs accepted: `platform`, `limit`,
  `messages_per_thread` — no thread/user id, no path, nothing that could
  redirect the read.
- **L.1.3 Result shape** — matches the doc's suggested schema
  (`platform`/`thread_id`/`person`/`last_message_at`/`messages[]`), plus
  `user_id` for disambiguation. `person` prefers a saved
  `channels/people.py` name, falling back to the raw handle.
  Also DM-only: the doc's schema is silent on group/guild channels, but
  "who DMed me" plainly excludes them, so a thread is included only when
  its most recent inbound record's `context` is `permissions.CTX_DM`.
- **L.1.4 Truncation** — `MAX_THREADS=10`/`DEFAULT_THREADS=5`,
  `MAX_MESSAGES_PER_THREAD=10`/`DEFAULT=4`, `MAX_MESSAGE_CHARS=240` per
  message text, all independent of what the model asks for. A separate
  `MAX_CANDIDATES_SCANNED=60` loop guard bounds how many *candidate*
  threads get read at all (a server with many busy group channels — which
  this tool skips — could otherwise force scanning far more than it ever
  returns).
- **L.1.5 Registration & routing** — auto-discovered, joins the existing
  `channels` group (`actions/channel_people.py`, `actions/notify_owner.py`).
  Keywords tuned to avoid `actions/notify_owner.py`'s "message me"/"tell
  me when" territory (L.1.5's own "avoid hijacking ordinary
  chat-message tasks").
  One wrinkle worth recording: `TOOL_PACK_INSTRUCTION` is a no-op for a
  file joining an *existing* group (`tool_registry.TOOL_PACK_INSTRUCTIONS`
  keeps whichever file for that group is discovered first — alphabetically
  `channel_people.py`, per `tool_loader.discover_actions()`'s own sorted
  order) — so the real routing guidance for `recent_dms` was added as one
  extra sentence to `channel_people.py`'s already-winning instruction
  instead, with a comment explaining why.
- **L.1.6 Test Checklist entry** — deliberately **not** an inline
  `TEST_CHECKLIST` in the module (the sanctioned-but-unused-in-practice
  alternative _template.py documents): every other shipped tool's entry
  lives in `web/public/test-checklist-data.js`, which its own header calls
  "the source of truth" for a tool in that position, and
  `tests/test_checklist_supplied.py::test_payload_carries_a_custom_tools_entry_and_only_that_tools`
  already encodes that convention as an invariant (an inline entry on a
  *shipped* tool broke it — caught during this pass, fixed by moving the
  entry rather than loosening the test). Entry added under `"channels"`.
  **Reversed by owner instruction, 2026-09-26h — see new K.2.9 below.** The
  owner wants the test loosened instead, so a built-in/shipped tool can use
  an inline `TEST_CHECKLIST` the same way a custom tool can. This doesn't
  undo `recent_dms`'s own entry (still fine either way); it changes what's
  *allowed* going forward, and specifically reopens the choice this agent
  made not to loosen the test.
- **L.1.7 Acceptance** — all 8 checked, with automated coverage in
  `tests/test_recent_dms.py` (15 cases): empty history → `{"ok": true,
  "threads": []}` not an exception; a torn/corrupt trailing JSONL line
  doesn't crash it (`read_thread`'s own resilience); group/guild threads
  are excluded; `person` prefers a saved name over the raw handle; an
  unknown platform is rejected; both truncation limits are enforced even
  when the model asks for more; and — the one requiring the most care —
  a simulated non-owner chat sender is refused (`ok: false`, no `threads`
  key at all in the refusal) while a PC call and an owner chat sender are
  both allowed.

**Verification:** full local test suite (76 files, plain-`assert`
style, no `pytest`/network available in this sandbox) passes on the

**Original spec (kept below for reference):**

Lets Jarvis answer "who DMed me recently", "did anyone message me lately",
"what did the last few DMs say", "show me the recent Instagram/Discord
conversations" — a compact list of recent DM threads with a short
conversation snippet each.

#### L.1.1 Data source
**Status:** OPEN implementation step · **Priority:** P1

- Use the existing channel transcript storage in `channels/transcript.py`.
- Use the existing thread enumeration/read helpers rather than a second
  DM-history database: `list_threads()` (newest activity first) and
  `read_thread()` (recent records from one thread). Inbound records already
  carry sender handle/id, message text, context and timestamp; outbound
  records already carry reply text/timestamp/provider/conv id.

#### L.1.2 Tool scope and security
**Status:** REQUIRED design constraint · **Priority:** P1

Privacy-sensitive cross-person read operation. The model must not be able to
supply arbitrary `platform` + `user_id` + `thread_id` values to bypass access
rules. The tool must:

- run only in the owner/local trusted context;
- use existing transcript files as the source of truth;
- use safe high-level filters only (`platform`, recency/limit);
- not accept arbitrary filesystem paths;
- not expose raw credential/config data;
- return only the amount of history needed for the requested summary.

Reuse the existing permission/owner-context guard if one is more appropriate
than a parallel authorization system.

#### L.1.3 Suggested result shape

Compact enough for model context:

```json
{
  "ok": true,
  "threads": [
    {
      "platform": "discord",
      "thread_id": "...",
      "person": "Display name / handle",
      "last_message_at": "...",
      "messages": [
        {"dir": "in", "at": "...", "text": "..."},
        {"dir": "out", "at": "...", "text": "..."},
        {"dir": "in", "at": "...", "text": "..."}
      ]
    }
  ]
}
```

Exact schema can be smaller; required properties: newest conversations first,
person identity/handle, platform, last activity time, short bidirectional
snippet, enough context to identify the conversation without dumping the
entire transcript.

#### L.1.4 Truncation
**Status:** REQUIRED · **Priority:** P1

Bound both the number of recent threads returned and the number/length of
messages per thread. Do not return a full 200-message thread merely because
`read_thread()` supports that amount.

#### L.1.5 Tool registration and routing
**Status:** REQUIRED · **Priority:** P1

- Register through the existing auto-discovery/tool-module mechanism.
- Put it in the existing `channels` tool group unless the router audit shows
  a real conflict.
- Add targeted keywords for: recent DMs; recent messages from people; who
  contacted me; messages/conversations lately. Avoid keywords that hijack
  ordinary "message this person" / "reply to them" requests.

#### L.1.6 Test Checklist entry
**Status:** REQUIRED · **Priority:** P1

Per the repo's standing rule (new/changed tools need Test Checklist
coverage), add an entry covering: Ask prompt, Debug run arguments, expected
result, privacy/side-effect warning, and the prerequisite that transcript
data must exist to inspect.

#### L.1.7 Acceptance
- [ ] Jarvis can list recent Discord/Instagram DM threads.
- [ ] Each result includes a short recent snippet, not a raw transcript dump.
- [ ] Newest activity comes first.
- [ ] Empty history returns a useful empty result rather than an exception.
- [ ] Corrupt/torn JSONL lines do not crash the tool.
- [ ] A non-owner/public chat cannot use the tool to browse other people's
      history.

      ordinary chat-message tasks.

### L.2 Real conversation view inside Logs

**Status:** PARTIAL → NEW UI WORK · **Priority:** P1

Keep Raw JSON for debugging, but add a genuinely human-readable Conversation
view: user bubble → assistant bubble → tool-call card → tool-result card →
assistant continuation → provider/retry timeline event → final assistant
bubble. Should feel like the existing Jarvis chat UI, not formatted JSON.

#### L.2.1 View switch
**Status:** REQUIRED · **Priority:** P1

Replace the current two-state model (Organized / Raw JSON) with:
**Conversation** (primary human-readable view) and **Raw JSON** (exact
low-level log view). Reuse the existing toggle styling. Do not remove Raw
JSON.

#### L.2.2 Reuse existing speech bubbles
**Status:** REQUIRED · **Priority:** P1

Reuse the same bubble renderer/classes as the normal Chat/Ask surface
wherever practical. Do not build a second visual language for ordinary
user/assistant messages unless log-specific metadata genuinely requires it.

#### L.2.3 Tool-call timeline cards
**Status:** REQUIRED · **Priority:** P1

For every logged tool call/result, a compact expandable card with at least:
exact local display timestamp; tool name; short argument summary; result
status (ok/error/cancelled where available); duration when derivable from
timestamps; provider and round when available; task label when the entry
belongs to a task; source/origin when useful. Default compact; full
arguments/results expandable.

#### L.2.4 System timeline events
**Status:** REQUIRED · **Priority:** P1

Represent non-chat execution events as timeline rows/chips, not raw JSON:
provider attempt started; provider switched/failover; retry/cooldown; forced
ending; error; confirmation required; task execution started/finished. Only
show an event if the necessary data is actually logged — never invent
timestamps/status from inference when the source record is missing.

#### L.2.5 Log entry grouping
**Status:** REQUIRED · **Priority:** P1

Reconstruct a logical turn from the flat log stream; do not treat every
request/response as a separate bubble. Group at minimum by: conversation,
chronological order, tool call ↔ tool result pairs, model/assistant text
belonging to the same turn. If grouping is ambiguous, preserve chronology and
show an explicit execution event instead of falsely merging entries.

#### L.2.6 Details/inspection
**Status:** REQUIRED · **Priority:** P1

Every rendered event needs a path to its raw evidence without forcing the
user back to Raw JSON (e.g. Tool: `move_path` → click/expand → exact
arguments + raw result + provider/round metadata).

#### L.2.7 Filtering/search compatibility
**Status:** REQUIRED · **Priority:** P1

Keep the current log search/filter backend. The Conversation view must
respect direction filter, origin filter, source/provider filter, and text
search. Opening a search result should focus the relevant logical event and
keep enough surrounding context visible to understand the match.

#### L.2.8 Acceptance

- [ ] Raw JSON still shows the exact underlying entries.
- [ ] Tool calls/results are visible inline with the conversation timeline.
- [ ] Each tool event shows a real timestamp from the log data.

- [ ] Tool arguments/results are expandable.

### L.4 Bug — wrong "continue" / resume time

**Status:** ✅ FIXED, 2026-09-26 · **Priority:** P1

**Root cause (traced per L.4.1, below):** `timespec.describe()` — the only
function `scheduler.summarize()` (and therefore the web panel /
`list_scheduled` / `jarvis sched-list`) ever reads a job's display text
from — built its date/time from `trigger["at"]`. That field is written
once, at job creation, and is only ever updated again by `snooze()` (and
only for one-shot `"at"` triggers). `next_run` — the value `due_jobs()`/
`tick()` actually fire against, which correctly advances on `resume()`'s
roll-forward and on every ordinary fire-and-reschedule — was never read
back into the display. Confirmed directly: after `resume()` on an overdue
recurring job, `next_run` advances correctly to the real next slot while
`describe()`'s text stays frozen on the original creation-time value —
producing exactly "displayed 3:00 AM, actually fires later." No timezone/
DST assumption was needed or used.

**Fix:** `describe(trigger, next_run=None)` now takes the job's persisted
`next_run` and prefers it over the frozen `trigger["at"]` for anything
showing a concrete date/time; `summarize()` passes `job.get("next_run")`
through. This is a read-side fix only — `due_jobs()`, `tick()`,
`_advance()`, `resume()`, `snooze()`, `_apply_next_state()` are all
untouched, so no pause/resume/snooze/firing behavior changed. See
`jarvis-L4-D6-scheduler.patch` / `jarvis-L4-D6-patch-notes.md`.

#### L.4.0 Owner-reported repro (2026-09-25)

- A task was scheduled to say "continue" at **3:00 AM**; the owner approved
  it.
- The Schedules panel displayed the job's next-run as **3:00 AM** — the
  displayed value was correct at the time of scheduling.
- The job did **not** fire at 3:00 AM. It actually fired around **6:00 AM** —
  a ~3-hour discrepancy between the displayed/persisted time and the actual
  fire time, not merely a display glitch after the fact (the UI wasn't
  showing a stale value; the job itself ran late).
- This is the concrete case L.4.1's end-to-end trace should be run against
  first, and the case L.4.3's regression test should be built from once the
  root cause is found. Don't assume timezone/DST math yet — trace the actual
  value at every hop (persisted job → `summarize()` → API → UI, and
  separately whatever ultimately triggers the fire) rather than guessing.

The old plan has no sufficiently precise, trustworthy repro of the reported
"continue time" bug beyond this. The current scheduler already has: persisted `next_run`;
`summarize(job)` computing `in` from `next_run - now`; `resume()` logic that
rolls recurring jobs forward so Resume doesn't immediately fire an overdue
recurring job; `snooze()` logic that writes a new `next_run`. **Do not
blindly rewrite the scheduler based on the old narrative** — reproduce first.

#### L.4.1 Trace the value end-to-end
**Status:** ✅ DONE · **Priority:** P1

Traced: persisted job → `scheduler.get/list/summarize` → server/API response
→ web `renderSchedJob()` → displayed "in …" / next-run time. `summarize()`
is the sole job-context call site of `describe()` in the whole codebase
(the only other call site, `turn_trace.py`, describes a freshly-parsed
trigger with no stored job/next_run involved), so fixing it there closes
every transition at once: initial creation; pause; resume; snooze;
recurring `every` jobs; one-shot `at` jobs; error → resume; catch-up.
Timezone/DST was checked and ruled out — everything here is naive local
time end to end, and the divergence reproduces within a single process on
the same clock.

#### L.4.2 Define the correct contract
**Status:** ✅ DONE · **Priority:** P1

The displayed continuation/next-run time must agree with the persisted
`next_run` value — now enforced by `describe()` reading `next_run` instead
of the trigger's own frozen `at`. For recurring jobs, Resume already did
not unexpectedly execute immediately merely because `next_run` became
overdue while paused (pre-existing, tested behavior — unchanged). The UI
no longer displays a stale `in`/`when` value after an action that changed
`next_run`, since both are now read from the same persisted field.

#### L.4.3 Regression test
**Status:** ✅ DONE · **Priority:** P1

Two new tests added to `tests/test_scheduler.py`: a general pause/resume
staleness regression, and a fixture built from the actual reported
sequence (`test_L4_owner_reported_repro_3am_continue_task` — displayed
3:00 AM, real fire time drifts to 6:00 AM; asserts the display now tracks
`next_run` rather than staying frozen). Both check the backend value
(`summarize()["next_run"]`) and the user-visible formatted value
(`summarize()["when"]`) together.

#### L.4.4 Acceptance
- [x] Current reported sequence is reproduced and documented in a short test
      fixture.
- [x] Persisted `next_run` is correct after the action (unchanged — was
      already correct; the bug was in display only).
- [x] API/UI display matches it.
- [x] Refresh does not "fix" the value by accident; the first response is
      already correct, because it's now read directly from `next_run`.
- [x] Existing pause/resume/snooze behavior stays intact — all 80
      pre-existing scheduler checks still pass unmodified, plus 15 new ones
      (95 total, 0 failed).
