### L.6 🐞 Bug — Theme gallery: borders never themed, "None" doesn't restore, Daylight readability regressions (NEW, 2026-09-27, owner-reported)

**Status:** ✅ FIXED (rev. 2026-09-27b) — `jarvis-l6-theme-fixes.patch`
(`web/public/ui-kit.js`, `web/public/ui-kit.css`, `web/public/style.css`).
Originally root-caused and written up doc-only per owner instruction (see
the 2026-09-27 revision entry below); the owner then asked for the fixes
to be implemented and sent as a patch. Applies cleanly with `-p1` to a
fresh copy of `jarvis-main_55_.zip`; `node --check` passes on the patched
`ui-kit.js`. **Per explicit owner instruction, the automated test suite
was not run for this patch** — unlike L.1/L.3/L.4, this one has no
accompanying `tests/test_*.py` run or new regression test. · **Priority:**
P2 (cosmetic, not correctness/security, but affected every theme switch
and one entire built-in theme)

**Owner's report, verbatim in substance:**
1. Switching themes (e.g. Nebula → None) leaves the font color unchanged —
   it should reset/change along with the rest of the UI.
2. Border colors don't change when switching themes, on any theme.
3. The Daylight theme "is bad" (no further detail given — see L.6.3 below
   for what a source read turns up as the likely concrete cause).
4. "There are other visual bugs but I didn't know how to describe them" —
   see L.6.4 for one more that turned up unprompted while tracing the
   above three.

All four sub-items below were traced against the actual shipped source in
`jarvis-main_55_.zip` (`web/public/ui-kit.js`, `web/public/ui-kit.css`,
`web/public/style.css`, `web/public/app.js`), not guessed from the bug
report's wording alone. Everything cited below is the real, current code —
none of it is hypothetical.

#### L.6.1 Border colors are entirely absent from the theme system's variable set

**This is why "border colors don't change" on every single theme switch,
not just some.** `style.css` defines exactly two border tokens, once, in
its top-level `:root` block:

```css
--border:        rgba(102, 214, 255, 0.16);
--border-strong: rgba(102, 214, 255, 0.34);
```

Every panel/card/button border in the stylesheet reads one of these two
(`border: 1px solid var(--border)` etc. — dozens of call sites). But
`ui-kit.js`'s `BUILTIN_THEMES` table (the object `applyTheme()` reads from
for Jarvis/Mark I/Terminal/Mono/Daylight/Nebula/None) **never lists
`--border` or `--border-strong` in any entry's `vars` object** — only
`--bg`/`--bg-1`/`--bg-raised`/`--bg-panel`/`--bg-panel-2`/`--accent`/
`--accent-soft`/`--accent-dim`/`--accent-glow`/`--accent-secondary`/
`--accent-tertiary`/`--text`/`--text-dim`/`--text-dimmer` are set per theme.
Since `applyTheme()`'s only write path is
`Object.entries(theme.vars || {}).forEach(([k, v]) => root.style.setProperty(k, v))`,
a variable that isn't in `vars` is simply never touched, for any theme —
so `--border`/`--border-strong` stay pinned at style.css's hardcoded
default (a pale cyan, matching the *Jarvis* theme's own accent) no matter
which of the six built-in themes — or a custom theme built through the
gallery's editor — is active. This reproduces cleanly for every theme, not
just Nebula/None: e.g. Terminal's phosphor-green palette and Mono's
grayscale palette both still show cyan-tinted borders.

**This is a regression relative to the older, still-present legacy
picker.** `app.js`'s `applyAccent(hex)` (the pre-existing Skin-modal accent
picker that predates the theme gallery) *does* correctly derive and set
both variables from whatever accent is picked:

```javascript
const borderRgb = scaleHsl(rgb, 1, 1.07);
root.setProperty("--border", `rgba(${borderRgb.r}, ${borderRgb.g}, ${borderRgb.b}, 0.16)`);
root.setProperty("--border-strong", `rgba(${borderRgb.r}, ${borderRgb.g}, ${borderRgb.b}, 0.34)`);
```

So the derivation formula already exists and is proven (it's literally what
produced style.css's own hand-picked default values, per `applyAccent`'s own
comment). The theme gallery in `ui-kit.js` simply never carried this over —
each `BUILTIN_THEMES` entry needs its own explicit `--border`/
`--border-strong` pair (or `applyTheme()` needs to derive them from
`--accent` the same way `applyAccent` does), and any custom-theme
import/export/editor path that lets a user hand-author a theme should
expose the fields too, or it will silently inherit the same gap.

**Fix applied (`jarvis-l6-theme-fixes.patch`):** added an explicit
`--border`/`--border-strong` pair to each of the six `BUILTIN_THEMES`
entries in `ui-kit.js`, hand-picked per theme rather than derived at
runtime — each computed by running `applyAccent`'s own formula
(`scaleHsl(rgb, 1, 1.07)` at 0.16/0.34 alpha) against that theme's own
`--accent`, so the values match what the legacy picker would have produced
for the same accent. The custom-theme import/export/editor path was left
untouched — a hand-authored theme JSON can already specify `--border`/
`--border-strong` directly if the author includes them, since `applyTheme`
now simply writes whatever a theme's `vars` object contains; no separate
schema change was needed there.

#### L.6.2 The "None" theme never resets or clears anything — it only stops future themes from re-asserting

`BUILTIN_THEMES.none` is `{ vars: {} }`, and its own in-source comment
states the intent plainly: "None" should hand color control back to a
persona or the legacy accent/swatch picker, without fighting either for
control of `--accent`/`--bg`/etc. `applyTheme()` special-cases it:

```javascript
if (theme.isNone) {
  deactivate();
} else if (id) {
  markActive();
}
if (!theme.isNone) {
  Object.entries(theme.vars || {}).forEach(([k, v]) => root.style.setProperty(k, v));
  ...
}
```

So picking "None" calls `deactivate()` (clears the `jarvis.theme.active`
flag) and, correctly by design, skips writing any vars at all — `vars` is
empty anyway, so this line is a no-op either way. **The bug: nothing here
ever *removes* the vars a previous real theme already wrote.**
`applyTheme()` sets colors via `root.style.setProperty(...)` — i.e. as
*inline* styles on `<html>` — and inline styles win over anything in
style.css's `:root` block. Once Nebula (or any theme) has run, `--text`,
`--bg`, `--accent`, etc. are frozen at Nebula's values in the inline style
attribute. Switching to "None" never calls `root.style.removeProperty(...)`
for any of them, so they stay exactly as Nebula left them — indefinitely,
surviving even a reload (the same values get read back from
`localStorage`/persona restore logic, whichever runs). This is exactly the
reported symptom: **font color (and every other Nebula-set variable —
`--bg`, `--accent`, `--accent-secondary`, etc., not only text) stays
frozen after switching to None**, because "None" was built to step back
and let something else drive, but nothing else automatically drives
afterward unless the user separately touches the legacy accent picker or a
persona happens to load.

Confirmed this isn't compensated for elsewhere: `app.js`'s `applyAccent()`
(the function that *would* reset things to a legacy-picker baseline) is
never called from anywhere in the "None" selection path (`custom-tools.js`'s
theme-gallery click handler calls only `UI().themes.apply(id)`, i.e.
`applyTheme(id)`, nothing else) — so there is no automatic hand-off, only
the flag that says a hand-off *should* happen next time something else
writes color.

**Fix applied (`jarvis-l6-theme-fixes.patch`):** took option (a) of the two
outlined during the documentation pass — on selecting None, explicitly
`removeProperty()` every var any `BUILTIN_THEMES` entry can set (plus the
`--accent-rgb`/`--accent-secondary-rgb`/`--accent-tertiary-rgb` companions),
via a new `ALL_THEME_VAR_KEYS` list (derived once from
`Object.values(BUILTIN_THEMES)`) and a `clearThemeVars()` helper, called
from `applyTheme()`'s existing `isNone` branch right alongside `deactivate()`.
This makes "None" fall back to style.css's hardcoded `:root` defaults
immediately, rather than leaving a previous theme's values frozen until
something else happens to write colour. Option (b) — re-invoking
`applyAccent()`/persona-restore immediately — was **not** taken, since that
would mean `ui-kit.js` reaching into `app.js`'s legacy-picker internals
across files for a behavior the in-code comment never actually promised
(handing back to *whatever* runs next, not to a specific remembered accent);
worth a look if the owner would rather None restore the last legacy accent
instead of the hardcoded defaults.

#### L.6.3 Daylight theme: a hardcoded selection color makes selected text unreadable, and dark-tuned glow/blend effects don't adapt

Two concrete, evidence-backed issues, likely what reads as "Daylight is
bad" without further detail from the owner:

- **Text-selection contrast bug, Daylight-specific.** `style.css` has one
  global rule: `::selection{ background: var(--accent-glow); color: #fff; }`
  — a hardcoded white foreground, on the assumption that `--accent-glow` is
  always a saturated color over a dark background (true for all five
  `dark: true` themes). Daylight is the one `dark: false` theme, and its
  `--accent-glow` is `rgba(10, 110, 209, 0.2)` — a *pale, low-opacity* blue
  over a near-white `--bg` (`#f4f6f9`). White text (`#fff`) on that
  combination has extremely low contrast — selected text in Daylight is
  close to invisible, while every dark theme's selection reads fine. This
  is a real, measurable contrast failure specific to the one light theme,
  not a subjective style complaint.
- **Effects tuned for a dark canvas are applied unconditionally.** The
  `.jui-light` class *is* toggled onto `<html>` by `applyTheme()`
  (`root.classList.toggle("jui-light", theme.dark === false)`), clearly
  meant as a hook for light-theme-specific overrides — but **no rule in
  `style.css` or `ui-kit.css` ever selects `.jui-light`**; it's set and
  never read. So Daylight gets the exact same `text-shadow: 0 0 24px
  var(--accent-glow)` glow on `.boot__title`, the same
  `box-shadow: 0 0 60px rgba(0,0,0,0.6), 0 0 40px var(--accent-glow)`-style
  panel glows, and the same faint white scanline overlay (L.6.4) that were
  all hand-tuned to look atmospheric against near-black backgrounds. Against
  Daylight's near-white background these read as muddy/hazy rather than a
  glow, since a soft light-colored shadow behind already-light text or
  panels has much less visible effect than intended, while shadow-heavy
  chrome (`rgba(0,0,0,0.5–0.6)` box-shadows) can look comparatively heavier/
  muddier against a white panel than against a near-black one. No CSS in
  the shipped archive currently branches on `.jui-light` to compensate.

**Fix applied (`jarvis-l6-theme-fixes.patch`):**
- Selection contrast: added `html.jui-light ::selection{ color: var(--text); }`
  in `style.css`, right after the existing global rule — overrides just the
  foreground, only under the class the light theme already sets, so all
  five dark themes' existing selection colour is untouched.
- Dark-tuned glow effects: added a new `.jui-light`-scoped block at the end
  of `style.css` — `.boot__title`'s text-shadow blur reduced (24px → 10px),
  and the four `0 0 60px rgba(0,0,0,0.6), 0 0 40px var(--accent-glow)` panel
  box-shadows (`.modal`, `.ask-panel`, `.debug-panel`, `.menu-panel` — there
  turned out to be four occurrences, not three) replaced under `.jui-light`
  with a lighter, tighter drop shadow (`0 8px 28px rgba(16, 23, 32, 0.16), 0
  0 24px var(--accent-glow)`) instead of the fixed near-black one. This is
  the class the codebase already toggles for exactly this purpose; no
  `.jui-light` rule existed anywhere before this patch.

#### L.6.4 Bonus finding (unprompted): the "disable scanlines" tuning toggle doesn't disable the actual scanline effect — ✅ FIXED

Found while tracing L.6.3's glow effects — likely one of the "other visual
bugs I didn't know how to describe." `ui-kit.js`'s tuning system supports a
`scanlines` toggle (default `true`), and `ui-kit.css` says:

```css
/* The scanline/grid overlay lives on body::before in style.css. */
html.jui-no-scanlines body::before{ display: none !important; }
```

But `style.css` has no `body::before` rule at all. The actual scanline
overlay is `.console::before` (the repeating-gradient/`mix-blend-mode:
overlay` rule inside the Console panel) — a different selector entirely.
So toggling scanlines off in the Skin/tuning panel sets the class and the
comment's stated intent is correct, but the selector it pairs with matches
nothing in the current stylesheet, so **the console's scanline overlay is
never actually hidden by this control, regardless of theme.** Not
theme-specific (reproduces identically under every theme, including
Daylight and None), but adjacent enough to the theme-system read-through
that it's recorded here rather than opening a new Part.

**Fix applied (`jarvis-l6-theme-fixes.patch`):** changed `ui-kit.css`'s
selector from `body::before` to `.console::before`, matching the comment's
already-correct stated intent — the comment text was left as-is since it
was accurate about *what* should happen, just wrong about *where*.

#### L.6.5 Acceptance
- [x] Switching between any two built-in themes (or to/from a custom theme)
      updates border colors along with everything else — every
      `BUILTIN_THEMES` entry now has its own `--border`/`--border-strong`.
- [x] Switching to "None" from any theme clears every var a previous theme
      could have set, falling back to style.css's hardcoded defaults
      immediately — no variable is left frozen at the previous theme's
      value.
- [x] Selected text now uses `--text` (not a hardcoded white) under
      `.jui-light`, without changing the other five themes' existing
      selection appearance (their rule is untouched).
- [x] `.jui-light` overrides added for the boot-title glow and the four
      panel box-shadows identified in L.6.3.
- [x] The scanlines tuning toggle's selector now matches the element that
      actually has the scanline effect.
- [ ] **Not done, per explicit owner instruction:** no regression test was
      added and the existing suite was not run against this patch, unlike
      L.1/L.3/L.4's own acceptance criteria. `node --check` on `ui-kit.js`
      and a clean `-p1` apply against a fresh copy of the zip are the only
      verification performed. Recommended next step if this needs the same
      rigor as the rest of Part L: a small visual/DOM-level check per
      sub-item (e.g. assert `getComputedStyle` picks up a non-default
      `--border` after `applyTheme("nebula")`, assert it's cleared after
      `applyTheme("none")`).

### L.7 🐞 Bug — Daemons panel sometimes shows "not running" for a daemon that is running (NEW, 2026-09-30, owner-reported)

**Status:** ❌ NOT STARTED (documented only) · **Priority:** P1 (a status display that lies undermines every other Daemons feature)

**Owner's report, in substance:** the front end can glitch and show a daemon as *not running* when it actually *is* running. The owner can still **stop it from the front end**, which is the proof it was alive — the Stop action worked on a daemon the panel called stopped.

**Why that detail matters.** It says the backend process-control path and the displayed state disagree at that moment; the daemon itself is fine. It is intermittent ("sometimes"), so the repro must be captured, not guessed.

**What the repo shows (not a diagnosis):**
- The panel derives the badge from `bucketOf(entry)` (`daemons.js` ~105) and the Stop/Start toggle from `isStoppable(entry)` (~132, `running || supervisor_pid`). These are **two different predicates**, so a state where the badge says stopped while Stop is still offered is reachable by design if the payload briefly has `supervisor_pid` set but `running` false (or a stale `status`).
- Polling replaces `state.entries` wholesale in `loadEntries()` and re-renders through `onEntries()` (~2196–2240). If a poll **fails**, `loadError` is set but `state.entries` keeps the previous data, so a stale snapshot can persist on screen; conversely a poll that lands mid-transition (`STATUS_STARTING`/`RESTARTING`) can briefly read as not running.
- Backend side: `daemons.status()` derives `running` from `pid_alive()`. H.1.6 (2026-09-29) rewrote `pid_alive()` on Windows (`OpenProcess` + `GetExitCodeProcess`; "a probe that can't run = alive"). That fix is **owed a real Windows run**, so an intermittent wrong answer from the probe is a live candidate and should be ruled in or out first.
- Related, already recorded and still open: `run_supervisor()`'s fast-crash `last_error` banner issue (H.1.7 findings), and the same `os.kill(pid, 0)` defect in `sched_daemon`/`discord_gateway`/`doctor`.
- **Finding, 2026-09-30d (read from `jarvis-main_65_.zip`; nothing run on Windows):** the `os.kill(pid, 0)` hypothesis above is **ruled out as a cause of L.7**. `GET /api/daemons` runs `jarvis daemons`, and every daemon's state — including the adopted `sched_daemon.pid` / `discord_daemon.pid` legacy files via `_legacy_pid()` — comes from `daemons.status()`, which calls only `daemons.pid_alive()` (the H.1.6 version). `sched_daemon._pid_alive` feeds `sched_daemon.status()` (`jarvis sched-daemon --status`) and `stop_running()`; `discord_gateway._pid_alive` feeds only `_claim_pid_file()` at startup; `doctor._pid_alive` feeds `jarvis doctor`. They are a real Windows bug (live daemon shown as dead in `doctor`/`--status`, double-start guard for the Discord gateway ineffective) but a **separate** one; a patch routing all three through `daemons.pid_alive` (`jarvis-pid-probe-unify.patch`, 35 checks) was produced the same day and is **not yet confirmed applied**. What stays open for L.7 is the panel-side mismatch between `bucketOf()` and `isStoppable()` and the still-owed real Windows run of `pid_alive()`; the first step remains capturing the raw payload and `status.json` when it happens.

**Suspected causes, to test in this order (all unverified):** (1) `pid_alive()` intermittently false on Windows (permissions, PID reuse, timing); (2) a poll landing in a STARTING/RESTARTING window shorter than the grace logic covers; (3) front-end holding a stale snapshot after a failed poll, or `entrySignature`/`dataSig` deciding "nothing changed" and skipping a re-render (~1071); (4) badge and toggle computed from different fields (above).

**Required work when implemented:**
1. Capture a repro: when it happens, record the raw `GET /api/daemons` payload for that daemon (`status`, `running`, `pid`, `supervisor_pid`, `restarts`) **and** the on-disk `status.json`. Do this before changing code.
2. Make badge, Stop/Start toggle and alerts all derive from **one** function so they cannot disagree.
3. Never present a failed poll as fresh data: show a "stale — last updated Ns ago" marker when `loadError` is set, rather than silently keeping old state.
4. Regression test built from the captured payload (the L.4.3 pattern), covering both the backend probe and the front-end derivation.

**Acceptance:**
- [ ] A payload with `supervisor_pid` set and `running` false never renders as "stopped" while Stop is enabled.
- [ ] A failed poll produces a visible stale indicator, not a silently frozen panel.
- [ ] Captured real-world repro exists as a fixture and passes.
- [ ] Real Windows run confirms `pid_alive()` (closes the H.1.6 "owed" item as a side effect).

### L.8 🐞 Bug — disabling a service pops a notification that breaks the Daemons page layout (NEW, 2026-09-30, owner-reported)

**Status:** ❌ NOT STARTED (documented only) · **Priority:** P2 (cosmetic/usability, but hits a routine action)

> **STATUS CORRECTION — 2026-09-30e (owner-confirmed): this bug is STILL UNRESOLVED.** The disable-notification still offsets / shifts the Daemons panel. **No revision has fixed it.** I found no line in the plan or audit that says so in words, but two things can be misread as a fix and are corrected here: (1) rev. 2026-09-30b (**L.9**) lifts `.jui-toasts` above the Run Sequence bar while that bar is visible (`--seq-clear`, `body.has-sequence`). That changes where a toast *sits* only when a sequence is queued; it does not touch the Daemons panel's render path, scroll offsets or the `enabled` flip, and it cannot have fixed L.8. (2) Part H's "Daemons is now functional" lines (H.1.x) describe the panel rebuild, not this defect. Anything that reads "fixed" next to L.8 is wrong. L.8 stays **❌ NOT STARTED, unreproduced, P2** (raise to P1 if it reproduces on every disable); repro and acceptance criteria below are unchanged, K.8's L.8 box stays unchecked. Open owner question Q1 (Enabled toggle vs Stop) still gates the repro.

> **UPDATE 2026-10-02e (owner-confirmed again: still present).** Re-read the toggle path in `daemons.js` — nothing was changed. **What the code shows:** both toggles go `switchNode` → `quickPatch` → `PATCH /api/daemons/:id` → `toast()` → `loadEntries()` → `onEntries()` → `renderList / renderSide / updateShell`. **Ruled out:** the left list reordering (`bucketOf` ignores `enabled` and `autostart`, so the card never changes group); `scrollIntoView` (its four calls — ~2106, ~2145, ~2178, ~2472 — are on the editor, select and open paths, **not** the toggle path, so suspect (1) below is not supported by the code); the toast box (fixed, as already noted). **Still standing:** `entrySignature` includes `enabled` and `autostart`, so a toggle forces `renderSummary` + `renderDetails`. `renderSummary` rebuilds the hero block with `textContent = ""`: turning **Enabled** off adds an in-flow *Disabled* alert (`alertNodes`, ~1368) inside `.dmn-summary` (`flex-shrink: 0`), and turning **Autostart** on adds a header badge (~1337) that can wrap — either changes the summary's height, so the tabs and the scroller below it move; `renderDetails` also rebuilds the very *Quick settings* row the user just clicked under the cursor. That is the best-supported cause, and it covers **both** toggles. **Not verified:** no browser or layout engine was available, so which element moves, and in which direction, is still unobserved; `verify_daemons_panel.js` cannot see layout. The measurement in *Required work* step 1 is still the next step.

> **UPDATE 2026-10-03d (owner-confirmed a third time: still present).** The owner reports that the notification in the Daemons panel is **still messing up the offset**. **Nothing was changed or re-read for this entry** — it is documented only, as instructed. Everything under the 2026-10-02e update stands: the toast box is `position: fixed` and is ruled out, the best-supported cause is the summary/details re-render on a toggle, and **which element moves is still unobserved**. The measurement in *Required work* step 1 remains the next step; nothing has been built toward it. Note that the L.30 notification rework (below) is a separate, broader request and does not replace this bug.


**Owner's report, in substance:** when a service is disabled, a notification appears, and that notification "messes up the whole layout of the page" — the Daemons page ends up shifted **upward** ("the daemon page becomes upped").

**What the repo shows (not a diagnosis):**
- "Disabled" is a real state in the panel: the status report treats `e.enabled === false` as "disabled" (`daemons.js` ~621). Whether the owner means this Enabled flag or the Stop action is **unconfirmed** (open question Q1); the notification path differs. **ANSWERED, owner 2026-10-01 (Q1): any toggle — the Enabled toggle *and* the Autostart toggle.** The repro and the fix must cover both, not just the `enabled === false` path.
- Panel toasts go through `UI().toast(...)` (`daemons.js` ~657) → `JarvisUI.toast` → `.jui-toasts` host: `position: fixed; right/bottom: 18px; z-index: 9100` (`ui-kit.css` ~64). A fixed-position element **does not participate in page layout**, so a plain toast cannot by itself push content up. There is also an older `.toast` (`style.css` ~1131, fixed top-centre, z-index 200).
- Therefore the layout shift is more likely caused by something the notification *triggers*, not the toast box: the panel re-rendering into a different structure (`onEntries()` → `renderMain()` vs `updateShell()`), an in-flow alert/banner injected into the panel, a scrollbar appearing/disappearing (which changes the available width/height), focus or `scrollIntoView` on the new node scrolling a container, or a notification of higher importance (D.2.1 levels 3–5) using a different, in-flow surface.

**Suspected causes (unverified):** (1) `scrollIntoView`/focus side effect on the notification or on the re-rendered row scrolling an ancestor; (2) a non-fixed notification surface (level-3 persistent re-surface, or an in-panel alert) inserted in flow; (3) render path change on state flip (`enabled` toggles the "disabled" alert and changes the pane structure); (4) overflow toggling shifting the layout.

**Required work when implemented:**
1. Reproduce with devtools open; record which element's box moved (inspect the scroll offsets of `#dmn-main`, the overlay, and `body`) and which notification surface fired.
2. Make sure notification surfaces never sit in flow and never call `scrollIntoView` on an ancestor of the panel.
3. Add a real-browser check to `verify_daemons_panel.js`: capture the bounding box of the main pane before and after a disable, assert it is unchanged.

**Acceptance:**
- [ ] Disabling a service shows its notification without moving any panel element (bounding boxes identical before/after).
- [ ] Verified at the same four widths H.1.5 used (1500/1000/820/420 px).
- [ ] Regression check added to the daemons browser suite.

### L.9 🐞 Bug — the Run Sequence bar is unreachable under the Logs / Online / Notifications controls — ✅ FIXED (rev. 2026-09-30b, `jarvis-l9-sequence-bar.patch`)

**Status:** ✅ FIXED, rev. 2026-09-30b — `jarvis-l9-sequence-bar.patch` (`web/public/style.css`, `web/public/app.js`, new `tests/verify_l9_sequence_bar.js`, `AGENTS.md`); first of the L.7–L.14 items implemented, picked as the easiest per the owner. Browser-verified (headless Chromium, real `index.html`/`style.css`), **not yet seen by the owner in the running app**. · **Priority:** P1 (a whole feature — running a queued sequence — could not be used)

**Owner's report, in substance:** the "run sequence panel" has lower priority (stacking) than the **Logs**, **Online** and **Notifications** buttons, which makes it impossible to access.

**Interpretation to confirm (Q3):** "run sequence panel" is read here as the **sequence bar** (`#sequence-bar`, `.sequence-bar`) with its **Run Sequence** button (`#btn-seq-run`), shown when commands are queued via "+ Add to sequence". If the owner means a different panel, this entry must be re-scoped.

**What the repo shows (verified by reading the CSS; not yet reproduced in a browser):**
- `.sequence-bar`: `position: fixed; left: 22px; right: 22px; bottom: 18px; z-index: 40` (`style.css` ~738) — a **full-width** bar along the bottom edge.
- `.bottom-status-bar` (the "online" pill): `position: fixed; left: 50%; bottom: 22px; z-index: 45` (~341–348). Its own comment states the pill is *deliberately* kept above the sequence bar "so the pill still wins that overlap rather than getting hidden by it."
- `.logs-fab` and the stacked `.notifications-fab`: `position: fixed; right: 22px; bottom: 22px; z-index: 60` (~2073; markup at `index.html` 908–928).
- So all three sit above the bar (45, 45, 60 vs 40) and occupy the same bottom strip; the bar's right-hand controls (including Run Sequence) end up **underneath the Logs/Notifications buttons**, and its centre is covered by the online pill. The earlier fix documented in `index.html` (~322–329) only reserved `#app` bottom padding for real content — it did not solve overlap with the sequence bar itself.

**Design direction (a decision, not yet taken):** the bar must own the bottom edge when it is visible. Options: (a) when the bar is shown, lift the two FABs and the online pill above it (shared CSS variable for the bar's height, or a `body.has-sequence` class); (b) make the bar sit above the FABs (raise its z-index) and shrink its right margin so it never runs under them; (c) dock the bar inside the layout flow instead of `fixed`. (a) preserves the existing "pill wins" intent without hiding the bar; recommended, pending owner preference.

**As built (rev. 2026-09-30b).** Reproduced first, in a real browser, before any change: at 1500 and 1000 px the Logs button covered **54% of Run Sequence** (46% clickable; a click at its centre hit `btn-logs-fab`). The investigation found **two more defects the report didn't name**, both fixed in the same patch because L.9's own acceptance list can't pass without them:
1. **L.9.1 — the overlap.** z-index alone can't fix it (raising the bar would just bury the buttons), so while the bar is visible everything that shares its strip **lifts above it**: `app.js` `syncSequenceClearance()` (called at the end of `renderSequenceBar()`, and on hide) toggles `body.has-sequence` and writes the bar's *measured* height into `--seq-clear` (bar bottom 18px + height + 10px); a `ResizeObserver` keeps it correct when the bar changes height. `style.css` uses it to lift `.logs-fab`, `.notifications-fab`, `.bottom-status-bar` and `.jui-toasts` (the "Added to sequence" toast used to land on Run Sequence every time an item was queued). Hiding the bar removes the class and variable, so everything returns to exactly its resting position (asserted).
2. **L.9.2 — the Notifications button was never actually fixed.** `.notifications-fab{ position: relative }` silently beat `.logs-fab`'s `position: fixed` (same specificity, later in the file), so the button sat in normal page flow right after `.app` — **bottom-left, 2px off the edge** at desktop widths, and **entirely off-screen** on narrow ones (measured at y=1066 in an 800px-tall window at 420px wide). Every comment near it says "stacked directly above the Logs fab"; it is now that: fixed, same right edge as Logs, 56px (54px narrow) above it. **This moves the button from where the owner currently sees it (bottom-left) to bottom-right above Logs — flagged to the owner in the delivery message; trivially reversible.** The old `right: 2px` nudge only made sense for the relative box and was dropped.
3. **L.9.3 — chips squeezed into a sliver under 780 px.** The media query gave `.sequence-bar__items` `width: 100%`, but the base rule's `flex: 1` sets `flex-basis: 0%` and flex-basis beats width, so the chips never wrapped to their own row and each chip's × / then-and connector was nearly unreachable at 420 px. Now `flex: 1 1 100%`; the bar wraps to two rows (58 → 102 px) and the lift follows the measured height.

**Verification.** New `tests/verify_l9_sequence_bar.js` (69 checks) — real Chromium, scripts blocked so no boot/API is needed, the shipped `syncSequenceClearance()` cut out of `app.js` by source range, `document.elementFromPoint` on every control at 1500/1000/820/420 px with 1 and 6 chips; also asserts the Notifications button is `fixed`/above Logs/same right edge, that hiding the bar restores resting positions, that the lift re-tracks a resize, and that toasts clear the bar. **69/69 pass on the fixed tree; 32 fail on the original tree** (proving the test catches the bug). Patch applied with `patch -p1` to a fresh extraction of `jarvis-main_62_.zip`; result byte-identical to the working tree; `node --check app.js` clean; `verify_daemons_panel.js` 111/111, `verify_daemons_console.js` 37/37, `verify_math_rendering.js` 24/24 unaffected. No Python changed, so no build bump (`hash_source.py` hashes `.py` files only). The test prints SKIP and exits 0 where Playwright/Chromium isn't installed.

**Not verified / caveats.** Not run against the live app (scripts were blocked in the harness so the app doesn't boot; chips are built with the same markup `renderSequenceBar()` emits rather than by calling it); default skin only (other skins don't override these selectors — grep confirms — but weren't rendered); the Python suite was not run (no Python changed). Q3 (is "run sequence panel" the bottom bar?) was answered by the evidence — the bar is the only sequence UI and the reproduction matches the report — but the owner hasn't confirmed it.

**Acceptance:**
- [x] With ≥1 item queued, every part of the sequence bar — including **Run Sequence** and each chip's mode/× controls — is clickable at 1500/1000/820/420 px. *(met, browser-tested)*
- [x] Logs, Notifications and Online controls remain reachable when the bar is visible and when it is hidden. *(met — and the Notifications button was unreachable on narrow screens even without a bar, L.9.2)*
- [x] A test (real browser or `elementFromPoint` check on each control's centre) proves no control is covered. *(`tests/verify_l9_sequence_bar.js`)*

### L.10 Feature — open a daemon's console in a real `cmd` window, with keep-running and auto-open switches (NEW, 2026-09-30, owner request)

**Status:** ❌ NOT STARTED (documented only) · **Priority:** P2

**Owner's request, in substance:** a **button** on each daemon that opens its console in a Windows `cmd` window. Plus two switches:
1. **Keep running:** a toggle deciding whether closing that console window leaves the daemon running.
2. **Auto-open:** a per-daemon switch, available in daemon **creation, editing and info**, so that when the daemon starts its `cmd` window appears automatically.
3. The `cmd` window should **accept input** too, if input is enabled for that daemon.

**What the repo shows (this drives the design):**
- Daemons are spawned **without** a console on purpose: `CREATE_NO_WINDOW` with piped stdout/stderr (`daemons.py` lines 77, 889, 1168), which is what the web console reads. H.1.1's fix (2026-09-27) exists precisely because a stray console window was a reported bug; this feature must not reintroduce that for daemons that leave it off.
- Input is already modelled: `supports_stdin` (`daemons.py` ~294, 342, 950, 1125), and it is **locked for built-ins** (`_BUILTIN_LOCKED = ("argv", "supports_stdin", "shell")`, ~376), so "input in the cmd window" is only available where `supports_stdin` is true.

**Design decision needed (Q4) — two different mechanisms hide behind "open the console in cmd":**
- **Viewer window (recommended).** The daemon keeps running detached as today; the `cmd` window is only a *viewer* that tails the daemon's log and, if `supports_stdin`, relays typed lines to it through the existing stdin path. Closing the window can then **never** stop the daemon — "keep running" is true by construction, and the toggle becomes redundant (or reduces to "also stop the daemon when I close the viewer").
- **Host window.** The daemon itself runs inside a visible console (`CREATE_NEW_CONSOLE`). Closing the window kills it on Windows unless the supervisor re-attaches — this is the only reading under which the "keep running" toggle is a real choice, and it conflicts with the piped-log capture the web console depends on.
**DECIDED, owner 2026-10-01 (Q4): viewer window.** The daemon keeps running detached as today; the `cmd` window only tails the log and relays stdin. Closing the window can never stop the daemon, so "keep running" is true by construction and the toggle reduces to an optional *stop the daemon when I close the viewer* (default off). The host-window model is dropped.
The rest of this entry assumes the viewer model.

**Data model additions (draft):** per-daemon `console_window_auto` (bool, default false), `console_window_stop_on_close` (bool, default false); editable for custom daemons; for built-ins editable (they are display/behaviour prefs, not argv) — but `supports_stdin`-dependent input stays locked where it is locked today.

**UI additions (draft):** an "Open console in cmd" button in the daemon's actions row and Details tab; both switches in the Add/Edit form (H.1.5's editor) and shown read-only in the info/Details view; a warning where the OS is not Windows (button disabled with an explanation — **Windows-only** as specified).

**Risks/unknowns:** cannot be verified without a real Windows desktop (K.5.2); a viewer that tails a log must handle log rotation and Unicode; stdin relay from a second process needs a small IPC (named pipe or the existing stdin file/queue — to be checked in `daemons.py` ~1125 before designing anything new).

**Acceptance:**
- [ ] Button opens a `cmd` window showing the daemon's live output (Windows).
- [ ] Closing the window leaves the daemon running by default; the stop-on-close switch, if enabled, stops it.
- [ ] Auto-open switch present in create, edit and info; on start the window appears without a click.
- [ ] Typing in the window reaches the daemon when `supports_stdin` is on; the window is read-only otherwise.
- [ ] Daemons with both switches off never show a window (H.1.1 stays fixed).

### L.11 Feature — user-defined daemon categories; "Custom" becomes "undefined" (NEW, 2026-09-30, owner request)

**Status:** ✅ **BUILT IN A PATCH, rev. 2026-10-05** (`jarvis-daemon-categories.patch`, built against `jarvis-main_79_.zip` — **not yet confirmed applied to the current tree**; see the rev. 2026-10-05 entry at the end for what was built, decided and not verified) · **Priority:** P2

**Owner's request, in substance:** today a daemon is only **built-in** or **custom**. The owner wants to add **their own categories**, and wants the current "custom" bucket to be **undefined** (i.e. "no category assigned"), not a category in its own right. A daemon may belong to **more than one** category (stated for commands in L.14; the owner asked for the same system on daemons).

**What the repo shows:** the only classification is the boolean `builtin` (`daemons.py` ~139 `BUILTINS`, ~254/338/715) and the front-end kind filter `all | builtin | custom` (`daemons.js` ~239–268, select at ~885–893, "By kind" overview block ~1154, persisted preference `kindFilter` ~726/769/781). `builtin` is also a **lock** (`_BUILTIN_LOCKED`), not just a label — it must stay a separate concept from a category so locking rules don't change.

**CONFIRMED, owner 2026-10-01 (Q2): the name that appears changes — uncategorised custom daemons show as "Undefined" instead of "Custom".** (Interpretation originally stated below; "Custom" stops being a filter kind, built-in stays a separate flag.)

**Interpretation (now confirmed) (Q2):** "make the custom undefined" is read as: daemons that are not built-in and have no category are shown under **Undefined** instead of **Custom**, and "Custom" stops being a filter kind. Built-in remains a real, separate flag. If the owner meant something else (e.g. rename the existing Custom filter only), this entry changes.

**Design (draft):**
- New field `categories: [str]` on every daemon (built-ins get sensible defaults, editable; custom start empty = **Undefined**). Stored through the same persistence path as other editable fields (`_EDITABLE`, ~367) — this is **not** a `_BUILTIN_LOCKED` field.
- Filter row gains **one chip/option per category in use**, plus **Undefined**; built-in stays available as its own filter because it is a real flag. Category names normalised (trim, case-insensitive uniqueness, length cap, no control characters).
- Suggestions/autocomplete while typing a category: shared component, see L.14.3.
- Overview "By kind" block becomes "By category" with counts.

**Migration:** existing custom daemons → `categories: []` (Undefined). Persisted `kindFilter: "custom"` must be migrated to `all` (the value would otherwise match nothing) — call this out in the implementation so it is not forgotten.

**Acceptance:**
- [ ] A daemon can have several categories; adding/removing persists across reload and restart.
- [ ] "Custom" no longer exists as a filter; uncategorised custom daemons appear under Undefined.
- [ ] Built-in flag and its locking are unchanged.
- [ ] Old persisted `kindFilter: "custom"` does not produce an empty, unexplained list.
- [ ] Suggestions come from categories already used on daemons **and** commands (L.14.3).

### L.12 Feature — custom tools can register their own daemons (NEW, 2026-09-30, owner request)

**Status:** ❌ NOT STARTED (documented only) · **Priority:** P2

**Owner's request, in substance:** custom tools (the mechanism D.2.2 and G.2 already treat as extensible) **can** add their own daemons.

**What the repo shows:** `daemons.add()` and the `daemon-add` CLI already accept the full field set (H.1.4), so registering a daemon is not a backend gap. `custom_tools.py` (~48 `run_custom_command`) and `custom_tools_store.py` contain **no reference to daemons** — there is no supported path today for a custom tool to declare one.

**Design decisions, owner 2026-10-01:** (1) **Declare** — a tool declares its daemons in its manifest; they are registered when the tool is installed/enabled and removed when it is uninstalled (the owner first said runtime-call, then chose declare after the difference was explained). (2) **Ownership: yes** — every tool-supplied daemon carries `owner: <tool name>`. (3) **Autostart follows the tool's preset** — if the declared daemon has autostart enabled it starts without a separate user approval; *this reverses the "not autostart until approved" rule below.* **Owner, 2026-10-01 (follow-up): no extra warning or mitigation is needed — "the user knows what he's getting himself into."** Installing/enabling the tool is the consent; nothing further is shown before an autostart daemon starts. Decision final. (4) **Categories: yes** — a tool may suggest categories, the owner's edits win.

**Original design questions (answered above):**
1. **Declaration vs. call.** Should a tool *declare* daemons in its manifest (registered when the tool is installed/enabled, removed when it is uninstalled) or *call* a `register_daemon` API at runtime? Declaration is safer and reviewable; runtime call is more flexible.
2. **Ownership.** A tool-supplied daemon needs `owner: <tool name>` so the panel can group it, lock fields the tool controls, and remove it cleanly on uninstall (same shape as G.1/G.2 module-supplied checklist entries).
3. **Trust.** A daemon is an arbitrary long-running process. This crosses the same trust line as the scheduler's "untrusted by default" rule (H.2): tool-added daemons should **not autostart** until the owner approves them once, and their argv/cwd/env must be shown before first start.
4. **Categories.** A tool-supplied daemon can suggest categories (L.11) but the owner's edits win.

**Acceptance (draft):**
- [ ] A custom tool can supply one or more daemons that appear in the panel, marked with their owner tool.
- [ ] Uninstalling/disabling the tool removes (or clearly disables) its daemons.
- [ ] A tool-supplied daemon never starts without explicit owner approval.
- [ ] Documented in the custom-tool authoring guide, with a Test Checklist entry (Part J).

### L.13 Feature — favorite daemons, plus a Favorites filter (NEW, 2026-09-30, owner request; **BUILT 2026-10-04b in `jarvis-favorite-daemons.patch` — see the Built block below; browser-tested against a fake API, server routes not run**)

**Status:** ✅ IMPLEMENTED IN PATCH (rev. 2026-10-04b) · **Priority:** P2

**Owner's request, in substance:** favorite daemons "just like favoriting commands," and add a **Favorites** filter next to the existing filters (All, Attention, Stopped, …).

**What the repo shows:** command favoriting is front-end-only and server-persisted: `Api.getFavorites/setFavorites` → `GET/POST /api/favorites` (`app.js` ~1884–1888, 2154–2240), stored in `web/data/favorites.json` as a flat list of command names (currently three). Favorited commands float to the top of the list (`app.js` ~2278). Daemon filters are the `state` chips driven by `bucketOf` (`daemons.js` ~60–105, filter logic ~239–268).

**Design (draft):**
- **Separate namespace.** Daemon ids and command names can collide; do **not** put daemon ids into the existing `favorites.json` list. Either a second file (`favorite-daemons.json`) with its own route, or upgrade the file to `{commands: [...], daemons: [...]}` with a backward-compatible read of the old array form.
- Star toggle on each daemon row and in the detail header; favorited daemons sort to the top within their group (mirrors commands).
- **Favorites** is a new filter chip alongside All/Attention/each state; it composes with search and category filters (AND).
- Keyboard: a key (suggest `F` is taken by console filter — pick another, e.g. `*`) to toggle favorite on the selected row.
- Persist the chip selection with the panel's existing preferences; a stale "favorites" filter with zero favorites should show an explanatory empty state, not a blank list.

**Acceptance:**
- [x] Star/unstar on a daemon persists across reload (server-side, like commands). *(Met in Chromium against a fake `/api/favorite-daemons`; the real route in `server.js` was only syntax-checked.)*
- [x] Favorites chip lists only favorited daemons and its count is correct; composes with search and category filters. *(Composes with search, the state chips and the kind select. **Category filters do not exist yet (L.11)**, so that clause is untestable until they do.)*
- [x] Existing command favorites are untouched and old `favorites.json` still loads. *(Neither the file nor `/api/favorites` was edited.)*
- [x] Removing a daemon also removes its favorite entry. *(Client drops it at once; the server prunes its copy after a clean `daemon-remove`. The server half is code-read only — not run.)*

**Built 2026-10-04b — `jarvis-favorite-daemons.patch`** (against `jarvis-main_78_.zip`; six files: `web/server.js`, `web/public/daemons.js`, `web/public/daemons.css`, `tests/verify_daemons_panel.js`, new `tests/verify_l13_favorite_daemons.py`, `AGENTS.md`; no `jarvis/*.py` touched, so **no build bump**).

*What the owner sees.* A ☆/★ on every service card (click does not change the selection); a **Favorite** button in the selected service's action bar and the **`*`** key (the draft's suggestion; `F` is the console filter); favorites float to the top **within their own group** (Built-in / Custom) and the arrow-key walk follows the same order; a **★ Favorites** chip with a count beside All / Attention / Running, which is a *toggle on top of* the state chips rather than one of them, so **Favorites + Crashed** works and it ANDs with search and the kind select. With the filter on and nothing starred, the list says how to star one instead of showing nothing (and **Clear filters** turns it off). Whether the chip is on is a per-browser preference stored with the panel's other filters; the starred ids are not.

*Design choices (the draft left two open).* **Separate file, not a reshaped `favorites.json`:** `web/data/favorite-daemons.json` behind `GET`/`POST /api/favorite-daemons` (body `{ids: [...]}`, ids validated with the existing `DAEMON_ID` pattern, max 500). The owner's own data shows why — a daemon `spotify` and the saved command `spotify` both exist, and one shared list would star both. `favorites.json` and `/api/favorites` are unchanged, so an old install needs nothing. **Removal:** `DELETE /api/daemons/:id` prunes the id **only after the CLI reports `ok: true`**, so a failed removal keeps its star; a stale id left behind is also ignored by the count.

*Safeguards worth knowing about.* The `POST` **replaces the whole list**, so the panel refuses to save until it has read the saved list once (otherwise the first click after a failed load would wipe every favorite). Saves are chained one after another, each sending the set as it is then, so two quick clicks cannot land out of order. A failed save toasts the error and **re-reads the server's list**, so the UI shows what is really stored. Favorites load separately from the service list (which comes from the CLI), so a failure there never blanks the panel.

*Pure helpers* added to `JarvisDaemons._pure`: `sortFavoritesFirst`, `toggleFavoriteId`; `matchesFilters` takes `favOnly` + `favorites`; `countEntries` takes an optional `favorites` set and returns `.favorites`. Both are backward compatible: the old filter shape and the one-argument call behave as before.

*Tests.* `verify_daemons_panel.js` **111 → 127** (+16: the filter AND-composes with state / search / kind, the count ignores ids with no entry, the sort is a stable partition that does not mutate its input, the toggle). New **`tests/verify_l13_favorite_daemons.py` 19/19** — loads the real `index.html`, `ui-kit.js`, `daemons.js` and CSS in headless Chromium and answers the API from an in-memory fake: saved star shows, float-to-top, star without selecting, chip count, filter, composition with Stopped / Crashed / search, `*` key, detail button, persistence across a reload (including the filter preference), the empty state, **Clear filters**, and roll-back after a failed save; repeated six times with no failures (one early run exposed a race *in the test* — it asserted before the optimistic save landed — now waits). It prints SKIP without `playwright` + Chromium. Neighbouring suites unchanged: `verify_daemons_console.js` 37/37, `test_slash_coverage.py` 545/545. The new route and the removal cleanup in `server.js` have **no test**: `express` was not installed where this was built, so `node --check` is all they got.

*Not verified / not done.* Not seen in the owner's running app; `server.js`'s two new routes and the removal hook were never executed; no test pins that `favorites.json` stays untouched (it is simply not edited). Not built: a `favorites` keyword in the panel search, a favorites count in the overview pane, a star in the detail header itself (the button is in the action bar below it), and the L.11 category filter the chip is meant to compose with. Documentation: `AGENTS.md` lists the new test; `REPO_MAP.md` is updated in `jarvis-docs-update.patch`.

### L.14 Feature — command categories (multi-select, autocomplete, shown like the "conditional" badge) (NEW, 2026-09-30, owner request)

**Status:** ❌ NOT STARTED (documented only) · **Priority:** P2

#### L.14.1 Owner's request, in substance
- Assign **categories to commands** at creation (and edit).
- **Suggestions while typing:** if command A has category `utility`, then typing `uti` on command B suggests `utility`.
- **More than one category per command.**
- Categories **render on the command card the same way the "conditional" badge does**. If there is not enough room they are **not shown on the card** — they show **only in the command's info view**.
- The **same suggestion system is used for daemon categories** (L.11).

#### L.14.2 What the repo shows
- The conditional badge is `el("span", { class: "badge badge--cond" }, "conditional")`, rendered only `if hasConditions(spec)` on the command card (`app.js` ~2326). That is the visual pattern to follow.
- Commands are persisted through `commands_config.py` (`load_commands_dict`/`save_commands_dict`, ~29/42) — the same store the CLI uses, so a new `categories` field is visible to the CLI and must not break older readers (missing key = no categories).
- The `/` palette (Part I.2) and its data providers list commands; whether it should search/filter by category is a follow-on, not part of this request.

#### L.14.3 Shared category system (also serves L.11)
One small module, used by both surfaces, so behaviour cannot drift:
- **Vocabulary** = the union of category names in use across commands **and** daemons (so a category made for a command is suggested when categorising a daemon, and vice versa). *(**ANSWERED, owner 2026-10-01 (Q5): keep them SEPARATE** — commands and daemons each have their own category vocabulary; suggestions are not shared across the two surfaces. Share only the component/normalisation code, not the vocabulary. The "union across commands and daemons" wording above is superseded.)*
- **Suggest** on prefix, case-insensitive, most-used first; Enter/Tab accepts; typing a new name and Enter creates it. Show the existing name's exact spelling/case when matching, to prevent `Utility`/`utility` duplicates.
- **Normalisation:** trim, collapse whitespace, case-insensitive uniqueness, max length, no control characters; a small maximum per item (e.g. 8) to keep cards sane.
- **Rename/merge/delete a category** (needed eventually so typos can be fixed in one place) — record as a follow-up, not required for v1.

#### L.14.4 Card display rule
Render category chips in the same slot/row as the `conditional` badge. **Fit rule:** measure available width; chips that do not fit are omitted from the card rather than wrapped or truncated (the owner's stated rule), and **all** categories always appear in the command's info view. A tooltip or "+N" indicator on the card was *not* requested — do not add one without asking.

#### L.14.5 Open questions collected from this block (for the owner) — **ALL ANSWERED, owner 2026-10-01** (Q1: any toggle, Enabled or Autostart · Q2: "Custom" label becomes "Undefined" · Q3: sequence bar, now works · Q4: viewer window · Q5: keep categories separate)
- **Q1** — "When I disable a service a notification pops up": is that the **Enabled** toggle (the "disabled" state) or the **Stop** action? (L.8)
- **Q2** — "Make the custom undefined": confirm the reading in L.11 — uncategorised custom daemons show as **Undefined** and the **Custom** filter disappears; built-in stays a separate flag. (L.11)
- **Q3** — "Run sequence panel": confirm this is the bottom **sequence bar** with the **Run Sequence** button. (L.9)
- **Q4** — "Open the console in cmd": **viewer window** (tails logs, closing never stops the daemon) or **host window** (daemon runs inside it, closing may kill it)? (L.10)
- **Q5** — Should category suggestions be shared across commands **and** daemons, or kept separate per surface? (L.14.3)

#### L.14.6 Acceptance
- [ ] A command can carry several categories; they persist and survive a CLI round-trip (older files without the key still load).
- [ ] Typing a prefix suggests categories already used on any command (and daemons, per Q5); accepting one reuses the exact spelling.
- [ ] Category chips render like the `conditional` badge; those that don't fit are hidden on the card but always present in the info view.
- [ ] Daemon categories (L.11) use the same suggestion component.
- [ ] Tests: normalisation/dedup, suggestion ordering, overflow rule, persistence, backward-compatible load.

### L.16 🐞 Bug / cost — a scheduled "check the screen, then shut down" task spent ~50K tokens and did nothing (NEW, 2026-09-30d, owner-reported)

**Status:** 🟡 MOSTLY IMPLEMENTED IN PATCHES (rev. 2026-10-02b). `jarvis-L16-power-and-tiered-vision.patch` (2026-10-01g) built the **power tool** (item 6), **tiered vision** (Q-L16c) and the **router fix** (item 9). `jarvis-L16-unattended-run.patch` (2026-10-02, against `jarvis-main_68_.zip`) built the **unattended-run safety work**: **`policy.decide()` enforced on the live tool path with "allowed when this job was approved"** (item 4 / RC4), the **approval summary** derived from the job's tool list, the **unattended directive** (item 3 / RC3) and the **circuit breaker** (item 5 / RC2). `l16-items-7-8-10.patch` (2026-10-02b, against `jarvis-main_69_.zip`) built the **`list_windows` cap** (7), the **per-task token budget** (8), the **replay fixture** (10) and the **per-ask token total across attempts**, plus the owner's 2026-10-02 follow-ups — a per-job limit control in the scheduler UI, a third job status **"stopped: over budget"**, and the cost shown in the turn trace and the UI (see the 2026-10-02b as-built block after the 2026-10-02 one). The replay also found that the "≤ 2 calls" claim was **false** for the incident's own condition (no OCR, no vision) until a one-branch fix in `ocr_tools.py`. **Still not built:** a general capability preflight (item 2). Nothing was run on a real screen, a real Tesseract, a real provider or a real shutdown; the 2026-10-02 work was tested through the real tool executor with tool side effects stubbed, and the web dialog was syntax-checked but **not rendered**. The original diagnosis below is unchanged. · **Priority:** P2 (the safety gap is closed in code but unverified on the owner's machine; the token-cost items remain)

**Owner's report, in substance:** a scheduled task — *"Check the screen to see if usage is exhausted. If usage is exhausted, do not type anything and shutdown the PC. If usage is not exhausted, type 'continue' and press Enter, then shutdown the PC."* — consumed about 50K tokens "for absolutely nothing". Find out why, then document it. Nothing is to be implemented yet.

**Evidence and its limits (corrected 2026-09-30e).** Read from the exported conversation `1a99e1e3f0d3af0e.json`, from the **real per-attempt log `1a99e1e3f0d3af0e.jsonl`** (request / response / `usage` rows written by `ai_providers._record_usage`, supplied 2026-09-30e) and from `jarvis-main_65_.zip`. The first write-up (rev. 2026-09-30d) had no usage log and *estimated* 30–50K; the log now gives the real figure. Nothing was run on the owner's machine by me. Two details still differ from the owner's "~50K": the log's own sum is **32,219** tokens (below), and Gemini's hidden thinking tokens are not in it (see RC5); whatever UI counter produced ~50K is unknown.

**What the log shows:**
- **Timeline.** Conversation created 06:35:32; screenshot file stamped 06:35:49; exchange recorded 06:36:41; conversation updated 06:37:06 (the title/`soft_context` call).
- **Routing.** Confident, groups `desktop` + `scheduling`; matches were `type`→`type_text`, `press`→`press_key` and **"check the screen"→`schedule_watch`**. "shutdown" / "PC" matched nothing. 26 tools offered.
- **Steps (7):** `read_screen` (**failed** — "Tesseract binary not found on PATH"), `take_screenshot`, `list_windows`, `get_tool_schema` ×3 (`click_on_text`, `write_on_screen`, `click`), then `click` at **y=1050**.
- **Providers.** `gemini` key 1 → HTTP 429 ("retry in 59s", waited 2 s, still failed); key 2 → HTTP 503 (overloaded; other 8 keys skipped); `groq` answered. Thinking level `off`, yet the groq reply carried 1,014 chars of reasoning (1 round recorded).
- **Outcome.** Final reply: *"Screenshot ready. Sir, does the usage indicator on the screen show that usage is exhausted?"* — a question put to a person who is not there. No `continue`, no Enter, no shutdown; the run ended as a success.

**Root causes** (RC1–RC4 read from source; RC5 measured):

- **RC1 — The job could not be done with the tools it was given, and nothing says so before the first model call.**
  - *Seeing the screen:* `take_screenshot`'s schema and result both say the image is **not sent to the model**; the only way to "read" the screen is `read_screen` (OCR), which failed because Tesseract isn't on PATH (the owner's already-reported OCR issue; the tiered-vision wish is the real fix).
  - *Shutting down:* **the repo has no shutdown / power tool.** The `system_control` group is radio, packages and git only, and a search for shutdown / power-off finds nothing. The router matched no group for "shutdown".
  - So both halves of the task were impossible, and every round spent on it was waste.
- **RC2 — No stop rule after a sensing failure.** `tool_diagnosis` classifies the `read_screen` failure correctly, but the turn simply continues: take a screenshot the model can't see, list every window, look up three click-family schemas, then click. Each step is another model call that resends the whole prompt plus everything so far (`ai_providers.py` already documents this as roughly quadratic).
- **RC3 — An unattended run is never told it is unattended.** The scheduler sets `JARVIS_SCHEDULED=1` ("lets any tool notice it has no human"), but only `policy.py` reads it; nothing in `ai_client.py` puts it in the prompt. The model asked a question into the void and the job "succeeded".
- **RC4 — A click ran in a scheduled job although the default policy says deny. (Safety, not just tokens.)** `policy.DEFAULT_POLICY` has a rule *scheduled + `desktop` group → deny* ("an unattended job typing or clicking into whatever window happens to be focused can do anything, to anything"). But `policy.decide()` is called only by the `jarvis policy-check` / `policy-dry-run` CLI commands (`cli.py` ~1704); `_make_tool_executor()` in `ai_client.py` never consults it, and a search for other callers finds none. The rule exists and is **not enforced on the live tool path**. The click at y=1050 (the bottom row of a 1080-line display, i.e. the taskbar / Start area — *inferred, not seen*) executed. Had `read_screen` worked, the task's own next steps were typing `continue` + Enter into whatever had focus.
- **RC5 — Where the 32,219 logged tokens went (measured from the `.jsonl`; replaces the earlier estimate).** Eight `usage` rows: input **31,850**, output **369**.

  | Attempt | Rounds (input tokens) | Sum | What happened |
  |---|---|---|---|
  | gemini key 1 | r0 2,200 · r1 2,840 | 5,040 | `read_screen` (failed), `take_screenshot`; the third request got **HTTP 429** — this work was thrown away |
  | gemini key 2 | r0 2,606 · r1 3,508 · r2 5,211 · r3 6,226 · r4 7,020 | 24,571 | rebuilt prompt + a 1,347-char "already done" note, then `list_windows`, **three `get_tool_schema` lookups**, `click`; the next request got **HTTP 503** |
  | groq key 1 | r0 2,239 (+256 out) | 2,239 | final answer — a question to a user who is not there |

  - **Fixed cost of every call:** `systemInstruction` 2,822 chars + 26 tool declarations 5,993 chars = 8,815 of the first request's 9,150 chars (**96%**); first call = 2,200 tokens. `prompt_cache` logged `eligible: false` (prefix ~1.7K tokens < Gemini's 4,096 floor), so nothing was cached.
  - **The three `get_tool_schema` rounds (key 2, r1–r3) cost 3,508 + 5,211 + 6,226 = 14,945 input tokens — 47% of all input — to fetch about 1.4K characters of schema.** The catalog tier (`ai_client.py`, `CATALOG_TIER_MIN_TOOLS`) kept full schemas only for the three *keyword-hit* tools (`type_text`, `press_key`, `schedule_watch`) and demoted the other 22 to catalog lines, but the task needed `click_on_text`, `write_on_screen`, `click` and `read_screen`. The design comment says a miss "pays a round trip" but treats that as cheap; here each round trip re-sent the whole, growing prompt. The compact schema of the *whole* desktop group is about 1.1K tokens — less than one of those rounds.
  - **Failover restarted the work.** Key 1's two rounds (5,040 tokens) were redone in spirit on key 2, whose model called `list_windows` and then rediscovered tools instead of continuing.
  - **Hidden thinking tokens are not counted.** Gemini's `usageMetadata.thoughtsTokenCount` was 276 + 30 + 687 + 1,549 + 885 + 656 + 26 = **4,109** tokens, but the logged `output_tokens` were 10–22 per round (only `candidatesTokenCount`). True total ≈ **36.3K**. `thoughtSignature` blobs (1,600–7,476 chars per response) are also echoed back in later requests: the round-1 request on key 2 carried a single 3,348-char signature. Whether signatures are billed as input was not verifiable from the log.
  - **Ruled out:** the screenshot (never sent), tool-result size (every result in this run was ≤ 1,422 chars), the title call (not in this log), the round caps (the run stayed inside them).

**Also found — observability gap.** `ai_providers.get_usage_summary()` reads a thread-local `usage_rounds` that is per *attempt*; after a failover the totals can describe only the latest attempt, it omits Gemini thinking tokens (above), and the trace records thinking for one round only. So the figure the UI shows for a failed-over turn understates what was spent. Concrete optimization work is now in **L.24**.

**Ruled out:** the screenshot image (never sent to the model); tool schemas alone (~1.4–2K); the round caps (`GLOBAL_MAX_TOOL_ROUNDS` = 6 plus the discovery pool — the turn stayed inside them, so the caps do not protect against this pattern).

**Required work when implemented (recommendations, none built):**
1. ~~Get the real number first.~~ **Done 2026-09-30e** (RC5). Still owed: a per-ask total across *all* attempts, including thinking tokens, in the turn trace (L.24 T6).
2. **Capability preflight for unattended asks.** Before round 1, decide whether the job needs to *see* the screen (OCR available or a multimodal route) and to *power off* (a tool exists). If not, fail fast with a one-line notification — zero or one model call.
3. **Unattended directive in the prompt** when `JARVIS_SCHEDULED` is set: no questions; if you cannot verify or complete, report failure and stop; never act on a screen you have not read.
4. **Enforce `policy.decide()` on the live path** (RC4): call it from `_make_tool_executor()` with `context_from_env()`. This needs an owner decision (Q-L16a) — if scheduled desktop automation is to be allowed at all, it needs a per-job authorization, otherwise this task class can never run.
5. **Circuit breaker.** After a failure `tool_diagnosis` classifies as a non-retryable environment problem, end the turn (or cap consecutive unproductive rounds at 2) rather than improvising with other tools.
6. **A power tool** (shutdown / restart / sleep / lock) in `system_control` with a confirm-tier risk and keywords for "shutdown" / "turn off the PC" (Q-L16b).
7. **Cap unbounded lists** such as `list_windows` (top N, truncated titles) in `tool_result_shaping.py`.
8. **Per-task token budget** for scheduled asks: abort and notify when exceeded.

*Power tool (Q-L16b) — `actions/power_tools.py`, tool `power_action`.*
- **Actions:** `shutdown`, `restart`, `sleep`, `lock`, `cancel` (`cancel` is an addition, so a pending shutdown can be stopped). Aliases `reboot`, `power off`, `suspend`, `abort` are accepted.
- **Windows commands:** `shutdown /s|/r /t N [/f]`, `shutdown /a`, `rundll32.exe user32.dll,LockWorkStation`, and `sleep` through PowerShell `SetSuspendState(Suspend)` — **not** `rundll32 powrprof.dll`, which hibernates instead of sleeping where hibernation is enabled. Linux (`systemctl`, `shutdown`, `loginctl`) and macOS (`osascript`, `pmset`) command lines are built too but have **only been checked as strings**.
- **Grace period:** `shutdown` / `restart` wait **15 s** by default (`delay_seconds` 0–3600, 0 = immediately) so the scheduler can log the run and the notifier can reach the owner's phone, and so a mistaken or injected request can be cancelled. `force` is off by default (unsaved work can block shutdown) and is a visible argument, so whoever approves a job decides it.
- **Confirmation, per the owner's answers:** the tool asks nothing itself. `TOOL_CONFIRM_REQUIRED = {"power_action"}` is merged into `tool_safety.DEFAULT_CONFIRM_REQUIRED` by the existing loader, so an **interactive** ask shows the normal confirmation prompt, and a **model-created scheduled job** is parked as `needs_approval` by `scheduler._needs_approval()` and, once approved, runs through `_do_tool` with no second prompt. **`tool_safety.py` itself was not edited** (AGENTS.md). There is no model-fillable `confirm` argument.
- **Routing and policy:** keywords for "shutdown", "turn off the PC", "restart the computer", "lock the screen", "put it to sleep" and similar (before this, "shutdown" matched no group); `policy._TOOL_RISK["power_action"] = 60`.
- **Test hook:** `JARVIS_POWER_DRY_RUN=1` returns the exact command and runs nothing. The checklist's "run" steps use it.
- **Checklist:** entry added to `web/public/test-checklist-data.js` (group `system_control`), not in the module, per the repo's rule for shipped tools.

*Tiered vision (Q-L16c) — `vision_call.py` (new), `vision_tools.py`, `ocr_tools.py`.*
- **Root cause found:** `vision_tools.py` had the escalation policy and said "`ai_client` attaches the image", but **nothing in `ai_client` or any provider adapter ever did**. Tier 3 did not exist, so a PC without Tesseract could not see its screen at all.
- **Design — a side call, not a change to the main loop.** `vision_call.describe_image(path, prompt)` sends **one** request carrying the screenshot to a vision-capable provider and returns plain text. No adapter in `ai_providers.py` changed (cache-prefix invariant and round caps untouched); the image is sent once and never resent on later rounds; the call can use a different provider than the main loop (a scheduled ask on text-only Groq can still see through a Gemini key). It POSTs with `requests` directly rather than `ai_providers._post_json`, because that logs the whole payload into the conversation request log. Provider and key limits: at most 3 providers, 2 keys each; keys ordered and recorded through `key_health`; a "this model can't take images" reply moves on to the next provider, a bare 400 (Gemini's bad-key shape) tries the next key. Large screens are downscaled to a 1,600 px longest edge when Pillow is present.
- **Which providers count:** Gemini and Anthropic (embedding/audio names excepted); `openai_compatible` and `ollama` only when the model name is positively known to take images (e.g. `llama-4`, `gpt-4o`, `llava`, `*-vl`). **This changes `vision_tools.vision_available()`**, which used to accept any `openai_compatible` model that was not on a small deny list; a text-only Groq llama would have earned a 400 and a cooldown mark on a healthy key. Stated consequence: **Groq's `llama-3.3-70b` does not count; a Gemini key does.**
- **`look_at_screen`:** OCR first; if OCR is **unavailable or failed** it goes straight to tier 3 (a new `_ocr_file_status()` distinguishes "unavailable" / "failed" from "empty"); otherwise `should_escalate()` decides as before. Result shapes: `tier: "ocr"`, `"cached"`, or `"vision"` with an `answer`. **The old `image_path` / `fingerprint` fields are gone** — the vision tier no longer hands an image path to a caller. The answer cache is now keyed on **screen + normalized question** (the old screen-only key would have answered a different question with the previous answer); old cache entries are simply never hit.
- **When both tiers are missing:** one error, before any request — "Can't see the screen: the OCR engine (Tesseract) is not installed; no configured provider can look at an image …" — with `can_see_screen: false`, `retryable: false` and a hint not to retry, guess, click or type. If vision fails but OCR did read text, the OCR text is returned, labelled as OCR-only with "do not guess".
- **`read_screen`** (the tool the incident actually called): when `pytesseract`/Pillow or the Tesseract binary is missing it now transcribes through tier 3 (`source: "vision"`, with a note that it may contain mistakes). With no vision route it still fails **before capturing**, with the original install note. If both fail the install note is kept and extended with the vision reason, flagged non-retryable. The normal OCR path is unchanged and never touches vision (asserted).
- **Routing (item 9):** `schedule_watch` had a weight-9 keyword "check the screen", so the incident prompt routed to it and never reached a tool that can look. The router **ignores any phrase under `MIN_SCORE`**, so it could not be nudged down; it was replaced by phrases carrying a recurrence or trigger ("check the screen every", "keep checking the screen", "…and tell me when", …). `look_at_screen` gained "check the screen", "check my screen", "look at the screen", "check the display". The incident prompt now offers `look_at_screen`, `power_action`, `type_text`, `press_key`; "check the screen every 5 minutes and tell me when it says done" still reaches `schedule_watch`.
- **New config key — `defaults.vision_enabled` (default `true`).** Added **by the implementer, not requested by the owner.** OCR never left the PC; tier 3 sends a screenshot to a cloud provider. `false` disables tier 3 everywhere, and an unreadable config **fails closed** (no screenshot is sent). The owner may want a different default.
- **Tests:** `test_tiered_vision.py` 66 checks — provider matrix, request/response shapes for all four provider types, key and provider failover, the "no `_post_json`" guard, every `look_at_screen` branch (including the incident: no Tesseract → tier vision, one request), the `read_screen` fallback in all four combinations, the privacy switch, and the routing of the incident prompt. `test_read_screen.py` was edited so its OCR tests cannot reach the network (`_vision_fallback` is stubbed). Related suites pass (`test_vision`, `test_read_screen`, `test_ocr_diagnosis`, `test_schedule_watch`, `test_scheduler`, both checklist tests). **Full suite: 84 of 86 files; the two failures, `test_build_info.py` (stale hash) and `test_key_health.py`, fail identically on a pristine `_67` unzip.** `test_h15_daemon_editor.py` failed once in a parallel run and passes alone and on a pristine copy.
- **Checklist:** `look_at_screen` and `read_screen` entries updated (Tesseract now optional; the cloud-screenshot care note; the watch notes for the missing-Tesseract, no-provider and per-question-cache cases).

*Not done, and what that means for the incident (as of 2026-10-01g — **superseded by the 2026-10-02 block below**, which built everything this paragraph lists as missing except the preflight, the `list_windows` cap, the token budget and the replay fixture).* With the patch, the task "check the screen … then shut down" is **possible** on a PC with a Gemini key and no Tesseract: the screen can be read and the PC can be shut down. It is **not yet safe unattended:** `policy.decide()` is still never called on the live tool path, so the default "scheduled + desktop → deny" rule still does not deny; nothing tells a scheduled run it is unattended, so it can still end by asking a question to nobody; the approval dialog does not yet say "this job will shut down the PC / control the desktop"; and the model is still free to improvise after a non-retryable failure. The owner's 2026-10-01 follow-up — approval **is** the existing `needs_approval` step, the dialog should state what the job contains, and `policy.decide()` should change from deny-by-default to "allowed when this job was approved" — is **unbuilt**; it is the same change as RC4 and should be built together with it.

For vision: rename Tesseract off PATH and ask "is anything red on screen" with a Gemini key set (expect tier `vision`), then with no vision-capable provider (expect one "Can't see the screen" error and no retries), then ask a second, different question on an unchanged screen (expect a new request).
