**As-built, 2026-10-02 (`jarvis-L16-unattended-run.patch`, against `jarvis-main_68_.zip`).** Closes L.16 items 3, 4, 5 and the approval summary, on the owner's 2026-10-01 answer: **a scheduled job is allowed what it was approved for, and approval is the only confirmation it gets.** Eleven files: new `jarvis-cli/jarvis/job_risk.py` and `tests/test_unattended_run.py` (66 checks); edited `jarvis/ai_client.py`, `policy.py`, `scheduler.py`, `task_runner.py`, `cli.py`, `actions/scheduler_tools.py`, `build_info.py` (bumped to build 47), `web/public/schedules.js`, `web/public/schedules.css`. Applies cleanly to a fresh `_68` unzip. **No new tool was added, so no Test Checklist entry changed.** The top-level `jarvis-cli/cli.py`, `ai_client.py` and `tools.py` are older copies that already differed from the `jarvis/` modules in the supplied zip; they were **not** edited.

*Which actions are flagged — `job_risk.py`.* Derived from the job's **tool list, never from prompt text** (free text is what a model, or a page it read, controls).

| Kind | Tools | Summary sentence |
|---|---|---|
| power | `power_action` | shut down / restart / sleep / lock this PC (a `tool` job names its own action: "will restart this PC") |
| desktop | `type_text`, `write_on_screen`, `press_key`, `hotkey`, `click`, `click_on_text`, `drag`, `scroll`, `move_mouse`, `focus_window` | control the desktop (click, type and press keys in whatever window is focused) |
| files | `delete_path`, `write_file`, `edit_file`, `move_path`, `rename_path`, `copy_path` | delete or overwrite files |
| shell | `run_shell`, `run_custom_command`, `run_command`, `run_chain`, `dev_agent`, `code_agent` | run shell commands |

This is the owner's suggested list, **unconfirmed**. Read-only desktop tools (`read_screen`, `list_windows`, `take_screenshot`) are not flagged, but a *desktop approval covers them* (`covering_kind`), because the default rule denies the whole desktop group and the incident job's first step was `read_screen`. Wording: a `tool` or `command` job says **"will"**; an `ask` job says **"can"**, because the model picks its tools at run time — its list is every router group that matched, **before** the router trims to two groups, so the summary is a superset of what the live ask is offered. If the classifier throws, `assess()` returns an explicit "couldn't work out what this job can do" line rather than an empty list, because "nothing flagged" must never be the silent wrong answer.

*What changed.*
1. **`policy.decide()` is enforced** in `_make_tool_executor()` (RC4), only when the run is scheduled/unattended (`policy.unattended_context_from_env()`: `JARVIS_SCHEDULED`, or `JARVIS_CONTEXT` naming an unattended context; **`JARVIS_SCHEDULED` wins over a stray `JARVIS_CONTEXT=interactive`**; a bare non-tty `jarvis ask` is **not** enforced). `decide()` gained `approved_kinds`. A call whose kind was approved with the job is **allowed and skips the `tool_safety` confirm** — the approval stands in for it. A flagged kind the job was **not** approved for is denied (an allowlisted read-only `run_shell` is exempt). Approval never buys: a **sensitive path** (e.g. `~/.ssh`, Jarvis's own safety files) or a **destructive argument pattern** (e.g. `rm -rf`, disk format), or a **deny rule the owner wrote** in `policy.json` — only the *built-in* default rules yield, since `policy.json` is seeded with the defaults and "built-in" therefore means "equal to a default rule". Only `deny` is acted on in the executor; `confirm`/`review` verdicts fall through to the existing gate. If `decide()` itself raises, the call is denied for flagged tools and allowed for the rest (fail closed where it matters, not everywhere). The edit sits next to the confirm gate (an AGENTS.md explicit-review area): **the gate is untouched; one `elif job_approved: pass` branch was added in front of it.**
2. **Approval summary.** `scheduler.create` stores `risk` (`job_risk.assess`); `approve()` freezes `approved_kinds`; `_do_ask` always sets `JARVIS_JOB_APPROVED_KINDS` (empty included, so a value inherited from an outer run cannot leak in); `summarize()` and `sched-show` expose `risk` (derived on demand for jobs created earlier); `sched-list --text` prints `!` lines; `sched-approve` prints "approving: …" to stderr (stdout JSON unchanged); `schedule_task` results carry `approval_covers`. In the web Scheduled panel the detail pane shows "Approving this allows: …" and **Approve opens a `JarvisUI.confirm`** (level warn, focus on Cancel, the job's prompt as the preformatted block) whenever anything is flagged — a job with nothing flagged is still one click. **The dialog was syntax-checked (`node --check`) but never rendered.**
3. **Unattended directive (RC3).** `ai_client.UNATTENDED_DIRECTIVE` is the first line of the per-request prompt **tail** when `JARVIS_SCHEDULED` is set: no questions, no waiting, report one plain line and stop, never click/type on a screen it has not read, stop on `retryable false` or a blocked call. Absent for every interactive ask; the cached static prefix is byte-identical (asserted).
4. **Circuit breaker (RC2).** In an unattended run, a result with `retryable: false` (checked on the raw and the shaped result) or a policy denial **trips** it: every later call — including the rest of a parallel batch — returns the same stop result **without running** (not cached, so a failover cannot replay it as real), and `RoundBudget` is emptied (rounds, both discovery pools, grace) so the adapters stop offering tools and run their existing forced-ending path: the model gets **one** final call to report in a line. **Interactive asks never trip it** (a person is there to fix the cause).

*Behaviour to know about.*
- **Task steps** (`task_runner`) set `JARVIS_SCHEDULED` but have **no approval step**. They pop `JARVIS_JOB_APPROVED_KINDS`, so the "unlisted flagged kind → deny" rule does **not** apply to them: they keep the policy rules and the existing confirm path as before, and the built-in desktop rule still denies desktop tools in them. If the owner wants task steps held to the same rule they need an approval step first.
- **Jobs approved before this change** carry `approved_at` but no `approved_kinds`; their kinds are derived on each run, so they do not silently lose desktop or power access.
- **A job's approval is frozen.** `scheduler` has no way to edit a job's action after creation (only snooze / pause / cancel), so approval cannot be widened by editing the prompt. **A future edit feature must re-park the job.**
- **Approval can under-promise for an `ask` job:** a tool the router did not predict is **denied at run time**, not allowed — the safe direction.
- **L.20 `send_dm` item 8** ("refuse when `JARVIS_SCHEDULED` unless the job carries an explicit authorization") now has a mechanism to hang on, but it needs a new kind in `job_risk`; none was added. *(2026-10-02c: `send_dm` shipped with a flat refusal in unattended runs instead; a `message` kind would be the way to relax it.)*

*Tests.* `tests/test_unattended_run.py`, 66 checks, drives the real executor with `execute_tool` stubbed: default deny of a scheduled `click` / `read_screen`; desktop approval allows `click` and read probes and asks no confirm; `power_action` runs only under a power approval and then asks no confirm; a desktop approval does not cover `run_shell` or `delete_path`; the sensitive-path and `rm -rf` floors; an owner-written rule outranks approval; an interactive ask is unchanged; the context rules; the summary from the tool list for `tool` / `command` / `notify` / `ask` jobs, including the incident prompt (power listed before desktop, "can" wording) and a throwing classifier; `create` → `approve` → env at run, including a leaked outer value; the directive and the byte-identical prefix; the breaker (only the failing call runs, later calls stop, budget and grace emptied, interactive unaffected, an ordinary failure does not trip, stopped calls not cached). **Full suite: 86 of 88 test files before the build bump; after `bump_build_version.py` (build 47) `test_build_info.py` passes, leaving `test_key_health.py`, which fails identically (two timing-jitter checks) on a pristine `_68` unzip.** The full suite was not re-run after the bump; the new, scheduler, policy and build-info files were re-run on a freshly patched `_68` copy and pass.

*Not verified.* No live model, real screen, real Tesseract, real provider or real shutdown. The web approval dialog was not rendered. The ≤ 2-model-calls figure is by construction (breaker + budget), not measured through a provider loop. Whether the directive actually stops the model asking a question is untested.

*Verify first, on the owner's machine.* (1) Create an `ask` job mentioning shutdown and the screen and check that Approve shows the dialog with the right lines. (2) Replay the incident with Tesseract missing and no vision provider: expect one failed `read_screen`, later calls stopped, a one-line report, no click. (3) Approve a `power_action` job and run it once with `JARVIS_POWER_DRY_RUN=1` before trusting it on a real schedule. (4) Confirm a job approved for the desktop only is denied when it reaches for `run_shell`.

*Still open.* The flagged-action list (confirm or change); whether task steps should be held to approved kinds (needs an approval step); whether the circuit breaker should also apply to interactive asks (currently no); the capability preflight (item 2), `list_windows` cap (7), per-task token budget (8), replay fixture (10) and the per-ask token total (L.24 T6); `AGENTS.md` and `REPO_MAP.md` (`job_risk.py`, `power_tools.py` and `vision_call.py` are not listed) were **not** edited.

**As-built, 2026-10-02b (`l16-items-7-8-10.patch`, against `jarvis-main_69_.zip`).** Closes L.16 items 7, 8 and 10, the per-ask token total (L.24 T6) and, from L.24, T7, T8 and the `1a99e1e3f0d3af0e` half of T9. Twenty files: **new** `tests/test_l16_caps_and_budget.py` (40 checks), `tests/test_l16_scheduler_budget.py` (33), `tests/test_l16_replay.py` (22) and `tests/fixtures/1a99e1e3f0d3af0e.jsonl`; **edited** `jarvis/ai_client.py`, `ai_providers.py`, `token_usage.py`, `desktop_tools.py`, `ocr_tools.py`, `scheduler.py`, `turn_trace.py`, `cli.py`, `reserved_names.py`, `build_info.py` (bumped to **build 50**), `web/server.js`, `web/public/schedules.js`, `schedules.css`, `app.js`, `test-checklist-data.js` (the `list_windows` entry) and `REPO_MAP.md` (one row). Applies cleanly to a fresh `_69` unzip. No new tool.

*ANSWERED, owner 2026-10-02.* (1) **30,000 tokens is the default limit.** (2) A switch in the **scheduler front end** that overrides that limit **or prevents the run being killed** — built per job. (3) A **third status, "stopped: over budget"**. (4) The cost is **shown in the turn trace and the UI**.

*Item 7 — the `list_windows` cap.* In `desktop_tools.tool_list_windows`: at most **15** windows (`LIST_WINDOWS_MAX`), the active one first, then visible, then minimized (stable inside each group); each title cut to **80** characters (`LIST_WINDOW_TITLE_MAX`) **with no ellipsis**, because `focus_window` / `get_window_info` match by partial title and a pasted "…" would stop matching. `count` is still the true total; when the cap bites the result also carries `truncated`, `not_shown` and a hint to pass part of a title to `focus_window`, and `titles_cut` when a title was cut. **The cap is in the tool, not in `tool_result_shaping.py`:** that module is verbosity-gated ("full" bypasses it), and its own docstring leaves item counts to the tool, so a cap there would bound the result at some capacity modes and not others. The Test Checklist entry for `list_windows` was updated.

*Item 8 — the token ledger and budget.* `ai_providers.TokenBudget` is **one ledger per `ask()`**, summing input + output + hidden thinking tokens across **every provider and key attempt** (the old per-attempt `get_usage_summary()` reset on each failover). It is fed by `_record_usage`, the one place every adapter reports a round, and lives in a thread-local that `set_log_context()` does not reset. It always counts; it **enforces only when it has a limit, and only unattended runs get one** (`policy.unattended_context_from_env()`). Enforcement is not an exception thrown from `_record_usage` (the adapters' own `try/except` would turn it into a retry or failover): once the ledger is over its limit `RoundBudget.take()` refuses every kind of round, `_forced_ending()` makes no closing call, and `ask()` does not start another provider/key attempt and writes the reply itself. A response that already carries a final answer is never discarded. `ask()` is now a thin wrapper around `_ask_impl()` that restores the previous ledger on return or raise.
- **Limit sources, in order:** `JARVIS_TOKEN_BUDGET` (set per run by the scheduler from the job's own limit), then `defaults.scheduled_token_budget`, then **30,000**. `0` means no limit. An unreadable value falls back to the **default, not to "no limit"** — a typo must not switch the protection off. An interactive ask is never limited.
- **`token_usage.extract_usage`** now reports Gemini's `thoughtsTokenCount` as `thinking_tokens` (only when present, so existing entries keep their shape). **Not done:** `reasoning_tokens` for OpenAI-compatible providers, so the ledger understates for those.
- **The check runs after each response**, so a run can overshoot by up to one round: in the replay the response that crossed the limit brought the total to 33,833 against 30,000.

*Per-job limit (the scheduler front-end control).* Each job may carry `token_budget`: absent = the default, a number ≥ 1,000 = that limit, `0` = **no limit — never stopped for cost**. Set with `scheduler.set_token_budget()`, `jarvis sched-budget <id> <default|off|N>`, and `POST /api/scheduled/:id/budget` (`limit` = `"default"`, `"off"` or a number, validated in `server.js`). The detail pane shows a **"Token limit per run"** control for `ask` jobs (Default / Custom / No limit, Save). `_do_ask` always sets or clears `JARVIS_TOKEN_BUDGET` so a value inherited from an outer run cannot leak in. It takes effect on the job's next run. `sched-budget` was added to `reserved_names.py` (`test_reserved_names` caught it missing).

*The third status — "stopped: over budget".* `scheduler.STATUS_OVER_BUDGET = "over_budget"`. `_do_ask` reads the ask's own `JARVIS_USAGE` marker line (`ending: "token_budget"` plus the whole-ask ledger, which `ai_client` now puts on `result.usage`) — never the reply text — and returns `ok: False, over_budget: True`. **Every trigger type is parked** (one-shot, recurring and event): a run that blew its budget will do it again tomorrow, so unlike a transient failure it is not re-fired daily until the owner resumes it. **A cost stop is always notified, even for a job that normally stays quiet**, with the title prefixed "Stopped: over budget —". `resume()` accepts the status. UI: its own chip ("Over budget"), sidebar count, orange dot and row edge, a "stopped: over budget" tag, a detail-pane explanation, and a Resume button.

*Trace and UI.* `TurnTrace.tokens` (stored and reloaded with the trace extra): the one-line summary ends "N tokens" or "stopped: over budget", the expanded narrative says what the turn used against its limit (thinking shown separately), and `token_budget` is a recognised ending with its own sentence. The CLI's ending note explains it, and the web debug panel shows a **"Whole ask"** / **"Stopped: over budget"** block above the per-round numbers. The stop branch stores a `trace` extra, which it did not before.

*Item 10 — the replay, and what it measured.* `tests/test_l16_replay.py` drives the **real** `ask()` loop, offline, from `tests/fixtures/1a99e1e3f0d3af0e.jsonl`. **Real:** `ask()`, the adapters, round budget, policy gate, circuit breaker, ledger, result shaping, and (scenario B) the real `ocr_tools.tool_read_screen`. **Recorded:** every model reply, served per URL in order, usage included. **Synthetic:** the one request the original run never made — the closing "stop and report" call — answered with one canned line, its input tokens **estimated** from request size at the recording's own 4.16 chars/token. **Stubbed:** every tool except `read_screen` (`system_tools.execute_tool` is replaced, so the test can never click, type or shut anything down). The fixture has no `.json` conversation record, so the user text comes from the first logged request.

| Scenario | Model calls | Click | Ledger tokens |
|---|---|---|---|
| C — control: interactive, no guards | **11** | **yes** | 36,328 (4,109 of them thinking) |
| A — unattended, desktop not approved | **2** | no | ~3,392 (closing call ~906, estimated) |
| B — unattended, desktop approved, no OCR, no vision | **2** | no | ~3,602 (closing call ~1,116, estimated) |
| D — unattended, 30,000 limit, tools as recorded | 9 | no | 33,833 (stopped over budget) |
| D — 12,000 limit | 6 | no | 13,748 (stopped over budget) |
| D — limit off (`JARVIS_TOKEN_BUDGET=0`) | 11 | **yes** | 36,328 |

The control reproduces the incident (11 calls, 7 steps ending in the click, 32,219 logged + 4,109 thinking = 36,328), so the guards are measured against the real thing.

*What the replay found.* (1) **The "≤ 2 calls" claim was false for the incident's own condition.** With no OCR **and** no vision route, `read_screen` returned the plain install note without `retryable: false`, so the circuit breaker never tripped and the run went on for **9 calls** (`take_screenshot`, `list_windows`, three `get_tool_schema` lookups). The earlier text said both screen tools fail "non-retryable"; that was true only of the branch where vision was tried and failed. Fixed in `ocr_tools.py` (the no-vision branch now goes through `_with_vision_failure`: `can_see_screen: false`, `retryable: false`). (2) **The budget is a backstop, not the fix.** At the incident's own profile the 30,000 default stops the run only after round 7 and saves the last two calls (about 2,500 tokens, 7%) — it does stop the click. What makes the incident cheap is the breaker plus policy enforcement (A and B). (3) The fixture contained the owner's Windows user name and a browser window title; both were replaced with same-length placeholders (replay results identical). Generic window titles (Settings, Steam, KDE Connect, "Friends - Discord") remain.

*Behaviour to know about.*
- **Recurring jobs are parked, not retried**, after a cost stop (see above). This was my choice, not the owner's — **please confirm**.
- A stopped run returns `ok=True` from `ask()` and the CLI exits 0; the *scheduler* is what records it as over budget. A caller other than the scheduler that runs an unattended ask sees a normal reply.
- **Task steps (`task_runner`)** set `JARVIS_SCHEDULED`, so by the same environment logic an ask run inside a task step gets the 30,000 default, has **no** per-job override, and is **not** given the over-budget status. **Not examined or tested.**
- Only Gemini's thinking tokens are counted; the ledger understates for providers that report reasoning tokens another way.
- A `JARVIS_CONTEXT` naming an unattended context (daemons etc.) is also limited, for the same reason.

*Tests.* New: `test_l16_caps_and_budget.py` 40, `test_l16_scheduler_budget.py` 33, `test_l16_replay.py` 22. After the final fix, on a fresh `_69` unzip with the patch applied: those three, `test_reserved_names.py` (12/12) and `test_build_info.py` pass. **One full-suite run on the patched tree, before the `reserved_names` fix and the fixture scrub, gave 89 of 91 files; one failure was `test_reserved_names.py` (caused by this patch, since fixed) and the second non-pass was not identified (likely `test_key_health.py`, which fails on pristine trees, but not confirmed).** The full suite was not re-run on the final patch.

*Not verified.* Nothing ran on a live model, a real screen, real `pygetwindow`, a real Tesseract or a real shutdown. The scheduler and debug-panel JavaScript passed `node --check` only; **nothing was rendered in a browser and `server.js` was never started**, so the limit control, the chip, the new route and the debug block are untested as UI. The effect of the limit on a long legitimate job is a judgement (30,000 is below the incident's 36.3K and above the ~10K a simple ask costs), not a measurement of the owner's jobs.

*Verify first, on the owner's machine.* (1) Scheduler → an `ask` job → Token limit: save a custom value, "No limit" and back to Default, and check each persists. (2) Create a job with a very low limit (1,000) and run it: expect a "Stopped: over budget" notification, the status chip, and the debug panel's "Stopped: over budget" block. (3) Resume it. (4) With more than 15 windows open, call `list_windows` and check the result says it was truncated and `focus_window` still works from a shortened title.

*Still open.* Confirm that recurring jobs should be parked after a cost stop; whether task steps need the same limit control; `reasoning_tokens` for OpenAI-compatible providers; whether the stop should be recorded as a failure for non-scheduler callers; the capability preflight (item 2); `AGENTS.md` (not edited); L.24 T4 (cap input across attempts) is now partly covered by the ledger for scheduled runs only.


### L.17 🐞 Bug — opening one command from the `/` palette leaves the other commands unresponsive (NEW, 2026-09-30e, owner-reported)

**Status:** ❌ NOT STARTED (documented only) · **Priority:** P1 — switching between commands is the palette's whole job · **Purpose:** any command must open, and the next command must work right after it, without closing the first by hand.
**Report:** opening one command makes "other XY commands" stop responding. *Which* pairs is not recorded; the first task is to find out (Q-L17).

**What the code shows (read in `jarvis-main_65_.zip`; nothing run in a browser):**
- `JarvisHost.openPanel(id)` (`app.js` ~9749) looks the id up in a 16-entry `openers` map and calls it. Nothing closes the panel that is already open, checks whether one is, or hands the keyboard back.
- Seven modules each add an always-on `document` `keydown` handler that only checks its **own** overlay (`daemons.js:2449`, `test-checklist.js:1121`, `schedules.js:724`, `backlog.js:404`, `logsearch.js:353`, `custom-tools.js:381`, plus ~12 in `app.js`). Two panels open at once means two handlers reacting to one key (Esc closes both; `app.js` ~9840 documents exactly this "each module no-ops when hidden" convention).
- Daemons' `onKey` takes an unmodified `/` (focus its search, `preventDefault`) and single letters `s n e p r a f 1 2` whenever focus is not in an input → with Daemons open, `/` cannot open the palette.
- The composer — and with it the palette input — lives in the Ask surface (z 90), below `.menu-overlay` (92) and `.debug-overlay` (95). While any panel is open the palette is unreachable; it only comes back after that panel closes. (Same family as **I-B19 / I-B20**.)
- Panel handlers return early when `document.querySelector(".jui-backdrop")` exists (`daemons.js` ~2379). `ui-kit.js` `closeModal()` removes the node **160 ms after** closing, so keys are swallowed in that window; if a modal is ever replaced or throws before that timeout runs, the guard stays true and every panel shortcut is dead. Not seen, but the DOM query is fragile.

**Likely root cause (hypothesis, unverified):** there is no single owner of "which panel is open and who gets the keyboard". Panels are independent overlays with independent global key handlers, and the palette that opens them sits underneath them.

**Required fix (when implemented):**
1. Reproduce first: matrix A→B over all 16 panel verbs, in Classic and Focus; log `document.activeElement`, `elementFromPoint` at the composer, the count of visible overlays, and which `keydown` handlers fire. Record which pairs fail (closes Q-L17).
2. Reuse `JarvisHost.openPanel`'s map as the **one** panel registry (no second list): add `isOpen/close` per panel; `openPanel(id)` first awaits the current panel's `close()` (honouring its dirty-confirm), then opens, then sets `JarvisPanels.top = id`.
3. Every panel `onKey` also requires `JarvisPanels.top === its id`, so only the topmost reacts; Esc closes only the topmost.
4. Keep the palette reachable while a panel is open: a global open shortcut that works when focus is not typing, rendering the popover above panels (z between 95 and ui-kit's 9000); picking a panel verb swaps panels (step 2). Decide with I-B19 whether outside clicks close it.
5. Replace the `.jui-backdrop` DOM query with `JarvisUI.isModalOpen()` backed by `openModal`.
6. On panel close, return focus to the composer.
**Dependencies:** I-B19, I-B20 (fix together), L.19 (checklist entries). **Owner question Q-L17:** which two commands failed, and in which layout? **Owner answer 2026-10-01:** the owner described a different, more specific symptom — *open the `/` palette, scroll down to the "More" section, press "Show the other N commands", and the palette disappears.* That is **I-B19** (§I.0.3), not the panel-switching pair L.17 asks about; the A→B pair matrix for L.17 is therefore **still unanswered**, though the two may share a root cause (see I-B19's 2026-10-01 note). **Second owner answer, 2026-10-01 (this one *is* an L.17/I-B20 pair): switching from the Ask Jarvis panel to Skins through a command — the Skins panel does appear, but the Ask Jarvis panel stays on top of it, and the owner must close Ask manually to reach Skins.** Root cause found by code reading — see the 2026-10-01 note at I-B20 (§I.0.3). **Update 2026-10-01e:** I-B19, and I-B20's `.modal-backdrop` cause (Skin, Settings, command builder), are fixed in `fix-I-B19-I-B20.patch` (not browser-verified). L.17's own scope — the full ordered-pair matrix, and the palette being unreachable while a panel is open — is **unchanged and still not started**.

**Regression tests required:** new `tests/verify_panel_switching.js` in the `verify_l9_sequence_bar.js` style (real Chromium, shipped `index.html`/CSS): for every ordered pair (A,B) of the panel verbs, open A then B through `JarvisSlash.handleSubmit`, assert A hidden, B topmost (`elementFromPoint`), B's own shortcut works, exactly one handler acted, Esc closes only B, focus is back in the composer, the palette opens again, A reopens. Plus: `/` while Daemons is open opens the palette; a confirm dialog closed then a panel shortcut within 160 ms still works after the fix; dirty Daemons editor → switching prompts once and cancel keeps A open. Add the pair cases to `verify_slash_palette.js`; keep `test_slash_coverage.py` green.

### L.18 Feature — Debug panel: filter tools by the module / provider they are loaded from (NEW, 2026-09-30e, owner request)

**Status:** ❌ NOT STARTED · **Priority:** P2 · **Purpose:** answer "which tools came from *this* file / *this* MCP server / *my* custom tool file?" inside the Debug panel.
**What already exists (do not rebuild):** `tools._tool_source()` gives each tool one of four **origin buckets** — `builtin`, `auto` (shipped `jarvis/actions/*.py`), `user` (`~/.jarvis/tools`), `mcp` — exposed as `source` in `/api/tools` (`tools_list_payload()`), with the button row `#debug-source-filter` (`index.html` ~826) and `debugFilteredTools()` (`app.js` ~5781). That is the §3 feature and stays as the coarse first level.
**What is missing:** a tool's actual **source = the place it is loaded from**: the Python module for built-in / shipped tools (`screenshot_tools`, `actions/notify_owner.py`), the file in `~/.jarvis/tools/` for user tools, the **MCP server name** for MCP tools. The loader already knows it (`[tools] Auto-discovered [...] from notify_owner.py`).
**Source ≠ category (keep these apart in code, labels and tests):**
- *group / category* is how the router bundles tools (`tool_registry.TOOL_GROUPS`: `desktop`, `channels`, `scheduling`…). `recent_dms.py` and `channel_people.py` are two sources in one group; `notify_owner.py` is group `channels`.
- *name / name prefix*, *Test Checklist section* (`checklist_group`), *safety flags* and *tags* are also not sources.
- Not the existing four buckets either: they say where a tool *class* comes from, not which file.
**Analogy to follow:** the Test Checklist organises by where an entry lives (shipped data file vs a tool's own module, merged per tool) and filters by section chips / a select with counts (`state.group`, `dom.groupSel`, `test-checklist.js` ~806, ~1116). The Debug filter gets the same interaction.
**Implementation:**
1. `tools.py`: add **additive** `source_detail: {kind, module, label, path?, server?}` to each `tools_list_payload()` item. `module`: the discovered record's file for auto/user tools; `TOOLS[name].__module__` for built-ins; `server` parsed from the record (not the name prefix) for MCP. Leave `source` unchanged.
2. `app.js`: second filter row built from the distinct `source_detail.label` values with counts (chips, or a select when > ~8), AND-combined with bucket + search; state `debugModuleFilter`; persisted like other Debug prefs; card badge shows the module label; empty state "No tools from this source".
3. `index.html`/CSS: reuse `.debug-toggle-btn`; no new design language.
4. Docs: update the §3 row and AGENTS.md's Debug notes; note in `_template.py` that a tool's source is derived, never declared.
**Dependencies:** none; touches the same payload as the Test Checklist merge (`checklist`, `checklist_group`) — additive keys only. **Tests:** every tool has exactly one `source_detail`; per-module counts sum to the catalogue total and to each bucket; filtering by a module never returns another module's tool; two tools of one group but different modules are separable (source ≠ group regression); user tool in a temp dir; MCP tools carry their server; old payload without `source_detail` degrades to the four buckets; Chromium check of chips + counts + combined filters.

### L.20 Feature — Jarvis DMs a specific person (NEW, 2026-09-30e, owner request; already scoped as planned in D-I10)

**Checked: is there already a way to DM a specific person? Partly — the plumbing exists, the tool does not.**
- `channels/outbound.py` `dm_owner()` / `notify_owner()` and the tool `notify_owner` (`actions/notify_owner.py`) send to **the owner only**.
- `channels/discord_gateway.send_dm(discord, token, user_id, text)` is already **generic** — it fetches any numeric user id, chunks and sends via a short-lived client. A bot can only DM a user who shares a server with it and allows server-member DMs (the function already names this error).
- `channels/directory.resolve()` maps `@handle → id` (only for people who have messaged the bot); `channels/people.py` holds identity / notes / follow state; `channels/transcript.py` logs outbound (`log_outbound`).
- Instagram: only an owner-directed send (`dm_owner_instagram`) exists; a per-person Instagram send was **not verified**.
- `recent_dms` (read-only, owner-only) and `remember_sender` exist; **there is no send-to-person tool** (D-I10 already says so).
**Status:** ✅ BUILT 2026-10-02c (`jarvis-send-dm.patch`; **not yet tried against a real Discord/Instagram account**) · **Priority:** P2 · **Purpose:** "DM Maryem that I'll be late" from chat or the UI, and the building block for L.23.
**Steps:** (1) new tool `send_dm` in `actions/` (group `channels`, next to `recent_dms`): args `person` (name, `@handle` or `platform:id`), optional `platform`, `message`; (2) resolve through `people.all_people()` + `directory.resolve()`; ambiguous or unknown → error with candidates, never guess; only known contacts unless the owner passes a numeric id; (3) **owner-only** with the same `_current_sender()` guard `recent_dms` uses; (4) `confirm_required` true in `tool_safety` and a `policy.py` tier above read-only, plus `/api/tools/preview` showing the exact recipient and text; (5) call `discord_gateway.send_dm` through a new `outbound.dm_person(platform, person_id, text)` beside `dm_owner`, so callers share one path; (6) log every send with `transcript.log_outbound` and the scheduled-ask log; (7) rate limit per recipient; (8) refuse when `JARVIS_SCHEDULED`/unattended unless the job carries an explicit authorization (ties to L.16 RC4); (9) add keywords to `tool_registry` ("dm", "message <name>", "tell <name>") and a Test Checklist entry.
**Dependencies:** D-I10 (owner-only decision), L.16 RC4 (policy enforcement), L.21 (person resolution). **Tests:** unknown/ambiguous person; non-owner sender refused; preview shows recipient; send failure (no shared server) names the cause; transcript line written; scheduled-context refusal; router fixture.

**As built (2026-10-02c).** New `actions/send_dm.py` (group `channels`) and `channels/outbound.dm_person(platform, person_id, text)` beside `dm_owner`, with per-platform `dm_person_discord` / `dm_person_instagram`. Args: `person` (saved name, `@handle` or `platform:id`), `message` (≤ 1500 chars), optional `platform`, optional `dry_run`.
- **Resolution (step 2), never guesses.** Tiers, first one that finds anyone wins: whole text equals a saved name / handle / id in `people.json`; one whole *word* of a saved name (`Maryem` finds `Maryem Ben Ali`, `mar` does not); `directory.json` `@handle`; a bare numeric id with an explicit platform (flagged `known_contact: false`). Two matches → error with a `candidates` list; none → error with `known_contacts`. The owner's own account and anyone whose follow state is `blocked` are refused.
- **Owner-only (3)**: the same `JARVIS_CHANNEL_SENDER` / `is_owner` check `recent_dms` uses; no chat context (the PC) is allowed.
- **Confirm + policy (4)**: `TOOL_CONFIRM_REQUIRED = {"send_dm"}`; `policy._TOOL_RISK["send_dm"] = 50` (confirm band at the PC, `review` from chat or when scheduled); `policy.dry_run()` describes the exact recipient and text. `dry_run=true` on the tool itself resolves the person and returns who/what **without sending**.
- **Rate limit (7)**: 5 per recipient and 20 overall per hour, persisted in `~/.jarvis/channels/dm_sends.json` (a fresh process per call means an in-memory counter limits nothing). Only *delivered* sends count; a failed one does not use up the quota.
- **Unattended (8)**: refuses outright under `JARVIS_SCHEDULED` or `JARVIS_CONTEXT` = scheduled/unattended. The plan's "unless the job carries an explicit authorization" is **not built**: it needs a new kind in `job_risk.py`'s approval summary (see the 2026-10-02 as-built block at L.16). Until that exists the safe floor is a flat refusal.
- **Logging (6)**: every attempt, delivered or not, is appended to the person's `transcript.py` thread as an outbound record `kind: "owner_dm"` (their existing DM thread when the inbound log knows it, else `dm-<id>`), so `recent_dms` and the audit log show it. **The scheduled-ask log is not written** — send_dm cannot run in a scheduled job, so there is nothing to log there.
- **Failure** names the cause: Discord's "shares a server / allows server-member DMs" (from `discord_gateway.send_dm`), Instagram's closed 24-hour window.

Also `turn_trace`, `tool_diagnosis` entries and the `channels` pack instruction (added to `channel_people.py`'s, the one that actually reaches the model).
- **Test Checklist (9)**: `send_dm` entry in `web/public/test-checklist-data.js`.

Instagram per-person send relies on the 24-hour window recorded by `instagram_gateway`; not tried. The "find this user's thread" lookup scans at most 60 threads and falls back to `dm-<id>`.

### L.21 Feature — person + conversation memory (NEW, 2026-09-30e, owner request)

**Status:** ⏳ PLANNED · **Priority:** P1 (foundation for L.22 and L.23) · **Purpose:** Jarvis remembers what matters about specific people and retrieves only the relevant slice of past conversations — dynamically, for any person and topic, without inventing history and without mixing people.
**What exists (reuse):** `channels/people.py` — identity keyed by platform id, name, follow state, **≤ 6 notes × 160 chars**, `prompt_block()` injected by `base._ask_jarvis()`; `channels/transcript.py` — durable per-thread audit log with `conv_id`; `memory.py` (+ `memory_semantic.rank()`) — relevance-scored facts with **soft** namespaces ("a soft filter, not a wall"); `conversation_search` (owner-only); `remember_sender` (name only, D-I10 relevance gate still undesigned). **Gaps:** notes are a tiny free-text list; no per-person facts with provenance; no per-person instructions; namespaces are not a hard boundary; nothing summarises a past thread.
**Design (additive; no second identity table):**
- **Identity** — the person id *is* `people.key(platform, user_id)`; optional owner-confirmed `links` to join the same human across platforms; never auto-merged by name.
- **Store** — one JSONL per person under `~/.jarvis/channels/people/<key>/memory.jsonl` (isolation by file, lazy loading). Record: `{id, kind: fact|instruction|episode, text, provenance: owner_stated|person_stated|observed|inferred, source: {conv_id, thread, ts, line_range}, confidence, tags, created, expires?, status: active|proposed|retired}`. `inferred` is never stated as fact.
- **Episodes** — short summaries of past threads written from `transcript.py`, each storing a pointer to the transcript lines it summarises; the transcript stays the source of truth.
- **Write paths** — owner tools `person_remember` / `person_forget` (owner-only, resolve person as in L.20); automatic candidates enter as `proposed` behind the D-I10 relevance gate and the owner's approval; per-person export and delete.
- **Retrieval** — `person_context(person_key, message, budget)`: load **only that person's file**, rank with `memory_semantic`, return ≤ a fixed budget (default ~500 tokens) plus matched instructions (L.22); injected through the existing `prompt_block()` slot — one injection point, nothing per-turn for people who aren't speaking.
- **No made-up history** — the block lists each item with date + provenance + id; an empty result injects "No earlier conversation or saved facts about this person"; system-prompt rule: anything not in the block is "I don't recall"; recalled statements must carry an id (checked in tests).
- **Separation** — the wall is in the loader keyed by person, not in the prompt; any cross-person search is owner-only; a non-owner turn cannot read another person's file, the owner's global memory (beyond explicitly shared facts) or other threads.
**Steps:** P1 data model + loader + isolation tests → P2 owner write/forget tools → P3 retrieval + injection + token budget → P4 episode summaries → P5 proposed-fact gate (D-I10) → P6 a People view in the Channels panel.
**Dependencies:** D-I10, L.20, L.24 (token budget). **Tests:** per-person isolation (A's turn never contains B's text, including after renames); empty-history sentinel; provenance shown; budget cap respected on 1,000 records; retrieval relevance on paraphrases; stale/expired items skipped; forget removes every trace; golden "no hallucinated history" fixtures.

### L.22 Feature — contextual instructions about people (NEW, 2026-09-30e, owner request)

**Status:** ⏳ PLANNED · **Priority:** P1 after L.21 · **Purpose:** "Don't discuss T with X" works later, when X brings T up — as a general mechanism, with no X or T in the code.
**Model:** an instruction is an L.21 record `kind: instruction` with `{subjects: [person keys] | "anyone", topic: free text + derived keywords, directive: don_t_discuss | only_discuss | ask_owner_first | notify_owner | tone | custom, scope: {from, until?}, created_by: owner, visibility: never_reveal}`. The directive is a small enum plus free text, so new kinds need no code.
**Flow:** (1) inbound from person P → identify P (`people.key`); (2) load P's and "anyone" instructions (cheap, file-local); (3) match the message to each instruction's topic — lexical + `memory_semantic` similarity first; only an ambiguous score triggers one cheap classifier call (same pattern as `_quick_title_completion`); (4) inject **only matched** instructions as a high-priority block; (5) reply per directive, **without revealing** the instruction, its owner or the withheld content; (6) log "instruction applied" for the owner (optionally a notification via L.23).
**Hard cases to specify and test:** rephrased/indirect asks; P claiming the owner allowed it; prompt-injection text from P; instruction added mid-conversation; conflicting instructions (most specific + most recent wins, owner can list them); expiry; an optional post-check that scans the draft for the topic on `hard` instructions and rewrites.
**Dependencies:** L.21 (store + identity), L.24 (only matched instructions cost tokens). **Tests:** property-style with randomly generated person/topic strings (proves nothing is hard-coded); paraphrase recall; other people unaffected; the reply never quotes the instruction; non-owner cannot create, edit or read instructions; owner listing; expiry.

### L.23 Feature — notify the owner only when a reply is genuinely important (NEW, 2026-09-30e, owner request)

**Status:** ⏳ PLANNED · **Priority:** P2 · **Purpose:** DM/notify the owner when someone's reply matters, never for routine chatter.
**Reuse, don't duplicate:** `outbound.notify_owner()`; `notifier.py` levels (Silent / Standard / Persistent / Broadcast / Confirm, D.2.1); `people.needs_owner_notice` / `mark_notified` (already tell the owner once about a new person); `channels/permissions.decide()` and `policy.decide()` as the model for a **staged, stop-at-first-deny pipeline**; `schedule_watch`/`signal_event` for "tell me when X replies".
**Design:** a notification is considered only for a thread marked **awaiting** (created when the owner or Jarvis sent a DM via L.20, or the owner said "tell me if X answers about T") — any other message costs nothing. Pipeline: (1) deterministic gates: awaiting/watched, quiet hours, per-thread cooldown, dedupe, daily cap; (2) one cheap structured classifier call `{important, urgency 0–2, reason}` given the reply, the owner's original ask and the matched L.21 facts; (3) urgency → notifier level; (4) deliver a summary through `notify_owner`, not the raw thread; (5) write every decision, including "not important", to the audit log; (6) owner feedback (`useful / too noisy`) adjusts the threshold. Default on classifier failure: quiet digest, never a flood.
**Dependencies:** L.20, L.21, L.22, L.24. **Tests:** message table (thanks/ok → quiet; a direct answer to the ask, a deadline, an emergency → notify); no classifier call outside awaiting threads; cooldown/dedupe/cap; classifier outage; decision log entries; owner feedback changes the threshold.

### L.24 Token cost — measured findings and optimization work (NEW, 2026-09-30e; covers the owner's "~10K for a simple task" and L.16)

**Status:** ❌ NOT STARTED (investigated and documented only) · **Priority:** P1 · **Purpose:** simple requests should cost one or two model calls.
**Evidence (real usage logs, supplied 2026-09-30e).** Figures are the `usage` rows of each log; output excludes Gemini thinking tokens. **The logs contain the Windows user name and open-window titles — scrub them before using them as test fixtures.**

| Log | Task | Rounds | Input | Output | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `5267d91a8b996d48.jsonl` | interactive: "hey jarvis has anyone texted you on discord" | 5 (gemini key 1) | **10,649** | 79 | the owner's ~10K case |
| `1a99e1e3f0d3af0e.jsonl` | scheduler: "Check usage and shutdown PC" | 5 + 2 + 1 over 3 attempts | **31,850** | 369 (+4,109 thinking) | see L.16 RC5 |

**Why the 10K turn (5267) cost what it did:**
- **Wrong tool group — the real cause.** The router matched the word "discord" to the desktop tool `click` (`('desktop','click','discord')`), 18 tools offered; "texted you" is **not** a keyword of `recent_dms` (which has "who dmed me", "did anyone message me"…; checked with `tool_router.route`). The question is answered by one call to `recent_dms` (which exists) — about 1 round.
- **Fixed cost × rounds:** system 1,811 + 19 declarations 4,034 chars ≈ 1.4K tokens on every call; 5 calls ≈ 7.2K of the 10.6K input (68%).
- **Two wasted rounds:** `read_screen` failed (Tesseract missing) and `take_screenshot` (image never reaches the model) ≈ 4.2K input.
- **Side effects:** it changed the user's focused window (`focus_window` on Discord) and answered from a window title — "You appear to have direct messages open with @Bac2027" — which does not answer the question and was never read from the screen.
- **Uncapped output:** `list_windows` returned 22 windows (1,877 chars) and the same result is re-sent unchanged in every later request; prior-result compaction (`ai_providers.py`, "O(N²) round-loop leak") did **not** visibly apply in the Gemini path — to verify.

**Work items (each with a test):**
| # | Change | Expected effect | Test |
|---|---|---|---|
| T1 | Router: add `texted`, `anyone texted`, `dm'd` etc. to `recent_dms`; stop a bare platform word ("discord") from being a *confident* `desktop` trigger (require an action verb such as open/click/focus) | 5267: 10.6K → ~2K | router fixtures for both prompts; existing `test_tool_router*` stay green |
| T2 | Catalog tier: when a matched group's **full compact schemas ≤ ~1.2K tokens** (desktop ≈ 1.1K), offer the whole group; let `get_tool_schema` take a list and allow parallel lookups; log discovery rounds as a metric | 1a99: −~15K | replay: no more than one discovery round; size test on each group |
| T3 | Circuit breaker on non-retryable sensing failures (OCR/binary missing): stop, report, do not fall back to `take_screenshot`/`list_windows` for "reading"; do not offer `take_screenshot` where the model can't see images and the user isn't present | both logs: −2 to −3 rounds | replay of both logs ends in ≤ 2 calls |
| T4 | Failover: keep the prior attempt's tool results **and a "do not redo" line**, honour the provider's retry hint, and cap **total input tokens across attempts** per ask | 1a99: −~5K | fake-provider test: 429 on round 3 doesn't restart exploration |
| T5 | Trim per-call static text: the skills line (two skills listed on every call), desktop workflow notes only when the desktop group is active, tools blurb | −0.2–0.4K per call | prompt-size snapshot test per capacity mode |
| T6 | Count **thinking tokens** (`thoughtsTokenCount`, `reasoning_tokens`) in `token_usage.extract_usage`; one per-ask total across **all** attempts in the turn trace and UI | makes savings measurable | extraction unit test on both logs' response bodies |
| T7 | Cap `list_windows` (top N + truncated titles + active window first); verify old tool results are compacted in the Gemini adapter | −0.3K per later round | result-size test; round-N request shows the compacted form |
| T8 | Per-task token budget for scheduled asks: abort and notify when exceeded | bounds worst case | budget test with a fake provider |
| T9 | Replay fixtures from both logs (scrubbed), asserting call counts and token ceilings (5267 ≤ 2.5K, 1a99 ≤ 2 calls) in the F.17 style | prevents regressions | the fixtures themselves |
**Order:** T6 (measure) → T1 (biggest win, smallest change) → T3 → T2 → T4 → T7 → T5 → T8/T9. **Dependencies:** L.16 items 2–5 (capability preflight, unattended prompt, policy enforcement). **Open question Q-L24 — ANSWERED, owner 2026-10-01: per capacity mode** (not a blanket default for small groups): the catalog tier is switched on/off according to the active capacity mode.

**Update 2026-10-02b (`l16-items-7-8-10.patch`):** **T6** partly built — `thinking_tokens` for Gemini, one ledger per ask across all attempts, in the trace and debug panel (`reasoning_tokens` for other providers **not** done). **T7** built — the `list_windows` cap, in the tool; the "verify old tool results are compacted in the Gemini adapter" half was **not** examined. **T8** built — default 30,000, per-job override, third status. **T9** — only the `1a99e1e3f0d3af0e` half (scrubbed fixture, `tests/test_l16_replay.py`; ≤ 2 calls **measured**); the `5267d91a8b996d48` fixture and its ≤ 2.5K ceiling are **not** built. **T4** — the ledger caps total tokens across attempts for scheduled runs only; keeping the prior attempt's tool results and a "do not redo" line is **not** built.


### L.25 Feature — Tool Manager tab (NEW, 2026-10-01, owner request; **BUILT 2026-10-03 in `jarvis-tool-manager.patch` — see the Built block below for what is and is not done**; design questions Q-L25a–d ANSWERED 2026-10-01b; owner addition 2026-10-01h: individual tools and commands can be disabled — **Q-L25e–g ANSWERED 2026-10-03**; protected-tool list **BUILT 2026-10-03**)

**Status:** ✅ IMPLEMENTED IN PATCH (2026-10-03; **not run against the real `server.js` or a live model — see Not verified**) · **Priority:** P2

**Built 2026-10-03 — `jarvis-tool-manager.patch`, against `jarvis-main_72_.zip` (build 52 → 53; 27 files, +3,419/−438).** Two rounds of work are in this one patch, because `jarvis-main_72_.zip` does **not** contain the first round (an earlier delivery was made against `_70_`): **(1)** the Tool Manager itself and **(2)** switching tools and saved commands off. Read the "What the repo shows" bullets below as the *pre-build* state.

*Round 1 — the Tool Manager (`web/public/tool-manager.js` + `.css`, panel markup in `index.html`):*
- **Replaces the Custom Tools tab** (Menu → Tool Manager; the `ctools` palette verb is kept and `/toolmanager` added as an alias; **`/tools` was not taken — it is already Debug's alias**). `custom-tools.js` is cut down to the theme gallery the Skin modal shares, plus forwarders so any old `JarvisCustomTools.open()` call still lands in the new panel. Same chrome as the Test Checklist (`.debug-overlay`/`.debug-panel`), text-never-markup (a test fails on any `innerHTML`), keyboard, focus trap, offline/error/empty states, three panes.
- **Loaded-tools list** with search, source chips (Shipped / Yours / MCP / Commands / Off / Attention), category and safeguard filters, grouped catalogue, per-tool detail with parameters, the file each tool came from, and **rejected files shown with the loader's reason** at the top of the list.
- **Per-tool safeguards, three switches:** *Ask before running* (`confirm_required`), *AI overview* (`ai_review`) and a new **`approval_summary`**. Hotkeys `1`/`2`/`3`; "edited" tag and "Reset to defaults" against the built-in defaults carried in the payload. **`approval_summary` changes what an approval covers** (`job_risk.py`): switched off for a tool `job_risk` normally flags, the approval no longer names it **and no longer authorises it**, so an approved scheduled job can't run it unattended; switched on for any other tool it joins the approval under a new `marked` kind. **AI overview alone still produces a confirmation** (`ai_client` asks when *either* flag is on) — the panel says so instead of implying the switches are independent.
- **User tools:** per-file on/off, create, edit, delete, run-a-test, import. The editor is rebuilt: file-name validation as you type, templates, a gutter that **marks the failing line and scrolls it into view**, a Syntax → Imports → Contract stage tracker, Ctrl+S / Ctrl+Enter. **Import** shows the source, then asks (`JarvisUI.confirm`) **before any server call**, because checking a file executes it; a file whose name exists is blocked; a file the validator rejects writes nothing. Creating/saving in the editor still does **not** ask (Q-L25d).

*Round 2 — switching off (`jarvis/tool_disable.py`, new):*
- **What "disabled" means (owner, 2026-10-03): the model cannot see the tool and cannot use it.** The owner still can (Debug panel, Test Checklist, `jarvis <saved-command>` typed at a terminal).
- Every tool — **shipped, yours or MCP** (an MCP server's tools are ordinary `mcp_<server>_<tool>` entries, so no special case) — and every **saved command** gets an *Available to Jarvis* switch (hotkey `4`). **Per-tool, independent of the per-file switch** (one tool in a multi-tool file can be off alone). Protected tools show it locked, with the reason.
- **Hidden from the model:** `tool_schemas_for_session`, `schemas_for_tools`, `search_tools` (matches, and a group whose every tool is off is not listed), `get_tool_schema` (refused), the "did you mean" hint; for commands `search_commands`, the name resolver (a disabled name is refused, partial names never guess into it, "available" never lists it) and **both prompt blocks** that list commands (filtered once at the top of `_ask_impl`).
- **Refused if called anyway:** `execute_tool` is now **default-deny** for a disabled tool (`owner=True`, passed only by the Debug panel's direct run, opts out); the model's executor refuses **before the cache lookup and before the confirm gate** (a disabled tool never even asks the owner to confirm it), and an **unattended run is stopped** by the circuit breaker so it can't improvise around the switch; `run_command`, `run_chain` (before running any segment) and `update_command` refuse a disabled command.
- **Scheduled jobs (Q-L25g):** a job whose action names a disabled **tool** fails clearly through `execute_tool`; one that names a disabled **saved command** is not spawned — `scheduler._do_command` records `last_error`, writes the run log and sends a failed notification. **Before** switching off, the panel asks the server which jobs name the item (`scheduler.jobs_using`) and confirms, listing them; if that lookup itself fails it still asks. A job that asks the model to decide for itself (`ask`) cannot be checked, and the confirmation says so.
- **Where it lives (Q-L25a):** `~/.jarvis/disabled.json` (`{"tools": [...], "commands": [...]}`) — **not** in a command's spec (the model could flip that back with `update_command`) and not under `actions/`. Written through `atomic_io` with `.bak` fallback; **a failed save is an error, never a silent "it worked"** (`atomic_io.write_json` returns `False` rather than raising). Re-read on every call, like `tool_safety.json`.
- **Protected tools (Q-L25b), built from what the code hard-wires, not guessed:** `search_tools`, `search_commands`, `get_tool_schema`, `load_skill`. The prompt tells the model to call the first two; the catalog tier keeps `get_tool_schema` callable; `ai_providers.DISCOVERY_TOOL_NAMES` is the discovery set. **Nothing else is protected on purpose: the confirm gate, `risk_review()` and the AI-review gating live in code (`_make_tool_executor`, `tool_safety.py`), not in a model tool, so no tool is a "confirm-gate dependency".** Enforced on **read** as well as on write, so a hand-edited file can't disable one.
- **Holes found and closed while building:** `update_command` by exact name skipped the resolver's check (the model could rewrite a switched-off command); **renaming a disabled command in the commands panel re-enabled it** (the switch now follows the rename); deleting a tool file or a command left its switch behind for the next tool or command with that name (both now clear it); the editor's validator accepted files the loader rejects (see below).
- **CLI/server:** `jarvis tool-disable-set`, `command-disable-set` (`true|false|forget`, `<old> rename <new>`), `disabled-list`, `disabled-dependents`; `POST /api/tools/disabled`, `POST /api/commands/:name/disabled`, `GET /api/disabled`, `GET /api/disabled/dependents`. The four CLI names are in `reserved_names.py` and covered by the `ctools` palette entry.

*A bug in the existing editor, fixed:* `custom_tools_store.validate_source` did **not** run three checks the loader runs (`TOOL_KEYWORDS` not a dict; keywords naming a tool not in `TOOLS`; `TOOL_RESULT_SPECS` not a dict). The editor said "valid", Save wrote the file, and the tool silently never loaded — the failure the editor exists to prevent. It now rejects them with the loader's wording; `test_tool_manager_flags.py` runs both validators on the same sources so they can't drift apart again.

**Tests:** `tests/test_tool_disable.py` **98**, `tests/test_tool_manager_flags.py` **50**, `tests/verify_tool_manager.js` **100** (all new). Full suite on a **fresh `_72_` + the patch: 95 of 96 files** — the one failure is `test_key_health.py` (two timing assertions, e.g. a measured `1.9998` against `2`), which fails identically on the unpatched `_72_` and `_70_`. Also driven in headless Chromium against the real CLI through a stand-in server (58 asserted interaction checks over both rounds: 30 + 28): switches, the dependent-jobs confirmation, locks, filters, commands, file on/off, editor errors, import accept/decline/refuse, delete, reload persistence.

**Not verified / not built:**
- **Not run against the real `server.js`** (Express is not installed here); the browser pass used a stand-in server that mirrors the routes over the real CLI. `server.js`'s new routes were `node --check`ed only. **No live model:** "the model is never offered it" is shown at the schema/search/executor level, not with a real provider call.
- **Tool-owned daemons, tabs and palette commands (L.12) are not switched off together with their tool** — not built. Skills that reference a disabled tool are not handled. Palette verbs and CLI commands are untouched (Q-L25e, below).
- **No Test Checklist entry for the Tool Manager itself** (Part J / L.19 style) and no manual pass on a real install.
- The Debug panel does not mark a disabled tool (it still lists it and still runs it for the owner).
- **A confirm-gated shell tool (`run_shell`, `run_custom_command`) could edit `~/.jarvis/disabled.json`** exactly as it could edit `tool_safety.json` today; the guarantee is "no model-facing *tool* writes it" (a test scans every tool module), not "no file access".
- **`AGENTS.md`'s invariant is NOT amended** (owner: "don't update the docs yet"). It still says tools stay "fully loaded and locally executable… never gate real tool execution behind [the router]". The behaviour above keeps the first half (a disabled tool stays in `TOOLS` and runs for the owner) and does not put the gate in the router, but `execute_tool` now refuses by default. Proposed wording for later: *"`TOOLS`/`CORE_TOOL_SCHEMAS` stay fully loaded and executable by the owner. A tool the owner switched off (`tool_disable.py`) is hidden from the model and refused to the model and to scheduled jobs at `execute_tool` and `_make_tool_executor` — never in the router."* Also: `AGENTS.md` says not to touch `tool_safety.py` or the gating in `_make_tool_executor()` during router/discovery work — this *is* safety work, but a reviewer should look at the new `approval_summary` flag and at the refusal block added **ahead of** (not inside) the confirm gate.
- Small doc edits went into the patch for the Custom Tools → Tool Manager rename: `AGENTS.md` (one word), `web/README.md`, `DOCUMENTATION/COMMAND_PALETTE_TESTING.md` (the `/toolmanager` alias) and `REPO_MAP.md` (renamed entries plus a row for the new files). No behavioural text was changed and the invariant above was left alone.
- Observation, not touched: **`jarvis-cli/cli.py` (2,716 lines) is dead code** — the entry point is `jarvis.cli:entry`, nothing imports it, and its `RESERVED_NAMES` is stale.


**Owner's request, in substance:** a new **top-level tab in the web UI** that shows the **tools currently loaded**, lets the owner **load / unload** them, **import** tools, "etc etc" (the owner did not list the rest; the suggested extras below are marked as suggestions, not requirements).

**Owner addition, 2026-10-01h (documented only):** the Tool Manager must also let the owner **disable certain tools and commands** — selectively, one at a time, not only a whole tool file. The owner's wording was one line ("say that you can disable certain tools/commands"); how far it reaches is read below and the unclear parts are recorded as questions **Q-L25e–g**, not decided. Read as: (1) **individual tools** — including a single tool inside a file that exposes several, and shipped tools as well as user and MCP tools — and (2) **commands** — taken to mean the owner's **saved commands** (`~/.jarvis/commands.json`, the ones `run_command` / `run_chain` run); whether it also means slash-palette verbs is Q-L25e. A disabled item is **kept, not deleted**, stays visible in the manager marked disabled, and can be switched back on.

**What the repo shows (read in `jarvis-main_66_.zip`; nothing run):**
- **Shipped tools** (`jarvis/actions/*.py`, discovered by `tool_loader.discover_actions()`) have **no enable/disable switch**; they are always loaded. Anything the owner edits there is wiped by `script.bat`'s reinstall (the reason `custom_tools_store.py` exists).
- **User tools** live in `~/.jarvis/tools/<name>.py`. `custom_tools_store.py` already has `list_tools()`, `set_enabled()` (a `.disabled` filename suffix), write/validate/delete/test, and templates. The **Custom Tools** panel (`custom-tools.js`, `/api/ctools`, CLI `ctools-list|show|write|check|run|toggle|delete|templates`) drives it. So *load/unload for user tools largely exists*; there is **no import-from-file** flow and **no view that mixes shipped, user and MCP tools**.
- **The Debug panel** lists every tool read-only, bucketed by origin; L.18 already asks to filter it by module/provider. **MCP tools** are managed in the MCP panel. `jarvis tools-list` prints the catalog as JSON. **Skills** are a separate concept (`/skillload`, `/skillunload`) and are *not* tools.
- A rejected tool file is **silent** today (see `custom_tools_store.py`'s docstring and `actions/_template.py`'s warning) — a manager is the natural place to show load errors.
- **Disable granularity today (read in `jarvis-main_67_.zip`; nothing run):** user tools can be disabled only **per file** (`custom_tools_store.py`, a `.disabled` filename suffix), so one tool in a multi-tool file cannot be switched off alone — and there is **no disable of any kind for shipped tools or MCP tools**. **Saved commands have no enabled/disabled state at all:** `commands_config.validate_command_spec()` knows `run`, `vars`, `confirm_required` and `ai_review` only (an unknown key such as `enabled` would pass validation and be ignored by everything that reads the spec). The only per-tool switches that exist are `tool_safety.json`'s `confirm_required` / `ai_review`, which are *gates*, not an off switch.

**Proposed scope (draft):**
1. **Loaded-tools list** — every tool the router can currently offer: name, group, **source** (shipped / user / MCP / module-supplied), enabled state, risk (confirm-required, ai-review from `tool_safety`), and the file or server it came from.
2. **Load / unload** — toggle per tool and per source file. For user tools this reuses `set_enabled()`. For shipped tools it needs a **new persistent disabled-list stored under `~/.jarvis/`** (not in `actions/`, so reinstalls keep it). Protected tools (the ones `AGENTS.md` treats as core, e.g. the confirm gate's dependencies) must be marked non-unloadable.
   - **2a. Disable individual tools and commands (owner addition, 2026-10-01h).** A per-tool switch independent of the per-file one (so one tool in `scheduler_tools.py`, which exposes seven, can be off while the rest stay on), and a per-command switch for saved commands. Both are persistent, survive a restart and a `script.bat` reinstall, and keep the item's definition intact. The list shows **disabled** as a state distinct from *rejected/failed*, and offers a filter for it. Disable and unload overlap — whether they are one switch or two is part of Q-L25f. *(Suggested, not decided:)* reuse the one persistent disabled-list under `~/.jarvis/` that Q-L25a already requires, with entries keyed by tool name, and key command entries by command name.
3. **Import** — bring a tool file in (upload `.py`, or drop into `~/.jarvis/tools/`), validated by the same `discover_actions()` path before it is written, with the editor's existing "tell me why it's broken" error surface.
4. *(suggestions, not requested)* export a tool, reload/refresh the catalog, search/filter, delete, show rejected/failed files with their error, open a tool in the existing Custom Tools editor, link to its Test Checklist entry.

**Interactions with other decided items:**
- **L.12 / D.2.2 / K.6.7:** a tool can own daemons (`owner: <tool>`), a UI tab (`render: inline|sandboxed`), palette commands and a notification source. **Unloading or disabling a tool should remove/disable all of those together**, and the manager should show what each tool contributes. (Consistent with L.12's "uninstall removes its daemons".)
- **L.18:** the Debug panel's module filter and this tab overlap; decide whether the manager replaces the Debug tool list or both stay.
- **Tab registration:** the manager is itself a top-level tab, so it should use the same tab mechanism D.2.2 describes rather than a one-off.
- **Palette:** a `/tools` verb must be added with a risk tier (I.2.10) and a `COMMAND_PALETTE_TESTING.md` entry (L.19 style); the coverage test will fail until it has one.
- **AGENTS.md invariant — needs an explicit decision (Q-L25f).** `AGENTS.md` says `TOOLS` / `CORE_TOOL_SCHEMAS` "stay fully loaded and locally executable at all times; only what's **sent to the model** gets filtered … never gate real tool execution behind it". A disable that also *refuses to run* a tool is in tension with that sentence, so building it means either keeping disabled tools callable locally (hidden from the model only) or amending the invariant on purpose. This is the same question Q-L25b's "unload" already raised and did not settle.
- **The model must not be able to switch anything back on.** The model can already create and edit saved commands (`create_command`, `update_command`) and is the component most exposed to text from other people. So the disabled state **must not live where those tools can write it** — a plain `enabled` field inside a command's spec in `commands.json` would let `update_command` re-enable it. Same reasoning as the existing rule that there is no `daemon_add` tool and that `notify_owner` takes no recipient. Whatever the storage, the manager (and the CLI) set it, and no model-facing tool does.
- **Things that reference a disabled item:** scheduled jobs (`scheduler._do_tool` checks only that the tool name exists), saved-command chains (`run_chain` steps), skills and L.12 tool-owned daemons/tabs. A disabled tool or command that a job depends on must **fail clearly when it fires**, never be skipped silently or run anyway. Showing "N scheduled jobs use this" before disabling is a suggestion, not a requirement.
- **Commands the model is told about:** saved commands are listed to the model in the prompt's commands block (`_commands_context`). A disabled command must drop out of that list, so it also stops costing prompt tokens.

**Design questions — ANSWERED, owner 2026-10-01 (second follow-up):**
- **Q-L25a — unload persists across restarts: YES.** Unloading is a persistent disable (stored under `~/.jarvis/`, not in `actions/`, so `script.bat` reinstalls keep it).
- **Q-L25b — shipped tools may be unloaded: YES** (the owner answered "hmm yes"). **Which tools are protected: DEFERRED, owner 2026-10-01 ("we'll figure that out later")** — not decided, not blocking the rest of the design. Suggestion on record only: the things the safety model and the UI itself depend on must stay non-unloadable (the confirm-gate dependencies and discovery tools such as `search_tools`/`get_tool_schema` — the exact list to be built from `AGENTS.md`'s protected areas and confirmed). Everything else is unloadable. **PROTECTED LIST BUILT, 2026-10-03 (on the owner's "build those"):** `search_tools`, `search_commands`, `get_tool_schema`, `load_skill` — taken from what the prompt, the catalog tier and `ai_providers.DISCOVERY_TOOL_NAMES` hard-wire. **No tool is a "confirm-gate dependency"** (that gate is code in `_make_tool_executor`/`tool_safety.py`, not a tool), so the suggestion's first half yields an empty set. The owner has not confirmed this exact list; it is trivial to extend (`tool_disable.PROTECTED_TOOLS`) and a test pins it.
- **Q-L25c — the Tool Manager REPLACES the Custom Tools tab.** It is a superset: it keeps everything Custom Tools does today (list, edit, validate, enable/disable, run/test, delete, templates) and adds the loaded-tools view, shipped-tool load/unload and import. It also gets a **"Create a tool" button that opens a reworked, better version of the current create-a-tool editor** (**owner clarification, 2026-10-01: "reworked" means the UI needs a rework — the current editor's interface is "really bad."** This is a UI/UX redesign, held to the same Test Checklist quality bar as the rest of the tab. The current editor's *behaviour* — validate before save, say immediately why a file is broken — is worth keeping; the specific UX problems were not itemised, so the first design task is to review the current editor with the owner and list them).
- **Quality bar (owner requirement): the whole Tools tab must be high quality, at the same standard as the Test Checklist** (`test-checklist.js` — the "tester's workbench": same `.debug-overlay`/`.debug-panel` chrome as Daemons/Backlog/Debug, grouped catalogue, per-item detail, verdict/notes state, export/import, text-never-markup rendering, graceful offline behaviour, its own test suite). Treat that panel as the reference for polish, structure, empty/error states and accessibility, not just for looks.
- **Q-L25d — import requires confirmation: YES.** Importing a tool file must ask for confirmation before it is first loaded (show the source / what it contributes, then the existing `JarvisUI.confirm` modal). An imported file is arbitrary Python in the Jarvis process, so confirmation applies to **import**; **DECIDED, owner 2026-10-01: confirmation applies only when importing** — creating or saving a tool in the editor does **not** ask for confirmation (as today; it still validates before saving).

**Design questions raised by the 2026-10-01h addition — ANSWERED 2026-10-03:**
- **Q-L25e — what counts as a "command"?** Taken to mean **saved commands** (`commands.json`, run through `run_command` / `run_chain`; managed in the commands panel). Not decided: **slash-palette verbs** (the registry in `slash-commands-data.js`, 35 verbs) and **CLI commands**. Suggested: saved commands only for now; palette verbs and CLI commands are fixed built-ins with their own risk tiers and a coverage test, and are left alone unless the owner says otherwise. **BUILT AS SUGGESTED, 2026-10-03: saved commands only.** Palette verbs and CLI commands are untouched and are **not** covered; say so if you want them in scope.
- **Q-L25f — what does "disabled" mean for execution, and is it the same as "unloaded" (Q-L25a/b)?** Options: (A) **hidden from the model only** — still callable by the owner from the CLI / Debug / a direct run, which keeps the `AGENTS.md` invariant intact; (B) **refused everywhere**, including scheduled jobs and direct runs — a stronger switch that needs the invariant amended on purpose. Suggested: one persistent switch whose meaning is (A) plus "scheduled jobs and chains fail clearly", with (B) only if the owner wants a hard off. **Unconfirmed.** **ANSWERED, owner 2026-10-03: "disabled means that the model cannot see that tool nor can he use it."** Built as (A) hidden from the model **plus** a refusal for anything automatic (the model's executor, scheduled jobs); the owner's own runs (Debug, Test Checklist, `jarvis <command>`) still work. This is a reading of the answer, not a quotation: the owner did not say whether scheduled jobs count as "the model" — they are refused because nobody is at the keyboard. **The `AGENTS.md` invariant has not been amended** (see Not verified).
- **Q-L25g — scheduled jobs and chains that use a disabled item:** warn before disabling, fail clearly when they fire, or both? Suggested: both; never silent. **BUILT AS SUGGESTED (both), 2026-10-03** — the owner did not answer this one, so it is my reading and open to change: the panel warns before switching off (listing the jobs that name the item) and the job fails clearly when it fires. A chain naming a disabled command is refused before any segment runs. `ask` jobs (the model chooses its own tools) cannot be checked.

**Consequences of replacing Custom Tools (to handle when built):**
- The `ctools` palette verb (registry entry `ctools`, menu item `menu-item-ctools`) must be re-pointed to the new tab (or renamed, with the old name kept as an alias) and keep its risk tier; `tests/test_slash_coverage.py` and `tests/test_reserved_names.py` will need updating.
- The backend stays: `custom_tools_store.py`, `/api/ctools` and the `ctools-*` CLI commands are reused, not rewritten. Only the front end (`custom-tools.js`, its Menu entry) is replaced. Keep the theme-gallery code that `custom-tools.js` shares with the Skin modal working (its header says the two share it).
- Existing user tools, their `.disabled` state and their Test Checklist entries must survive the swap unchanged (no data migration should be needed).
- Menu entry, docs (`README.md`, `REPO_MAP.md`, `AGENTS.md` mentions of the Custom Tools tab) and `COMMAND_PALETTE_TESTING.md` need updating when this is implemented.
- **Done 2026-10-03:** the `ctools` verb is re-pointed at the Tool Manager (kept, plus alias `/toolmanager`; risk tier unchanged; `test_slash_coverage` 545/545 and `test_reserved_names` 12/12 pass, with the four new CLI names added); the theme gallery survives in `custom-tools.js`; existing user tools and their `.disabled` state need no migration (the manager reads the same `ctools-*` backend). Docs: the Custom Tools mentions were renamed in `AGENTS.md`, `REPO_MAP.md`, `web/README.md` and `COMMAND_PALETTE_TESTING.md`; nothing else in them was edited.

**Acceptance (draft):**

- [x] Unloading a user tool stops it being offered to the model; reloading restores it; the state survives restart. *(Per-file switch as before, plus a per-tool switch. Persistence is a file on disk, checked by reloading the page; a real process restart was not exercised.)*

The confirmation comes before any server call because checking a file executes it.)*
