### L.26 🐞 Bug — the Daemons "Restart" button (and `daemon-restart`, and the `daemon_restart` tool) refuses with "already has a supervisor running" (NEW, 2026-10-02e, owner-reported; **FIXED 2026-10-03b in `jarvis-l26-l28-patch.zip` — see the Built block; tested on Linux with real supervisor processes, not yet checked on a real install**)

**Status:** ✅ IMPLEMENTED IN PATCH (2026-10-03b; **Linux only, real supervisor processes — not run on Windows or from the real web Restart button, see Not verified**) · **Priority:** P1 (a core control on the panel never works as labelled; on a running daemon it leaves the daemon **stopped**).

**Built 2026-10-03b — `jarvis-l26-l28-patch.zip` (same change as `l26-l28.diff`), against `jarvis-main_72_.zip` (build 52 → 54; 13 files — 3 new test files, 10 edited; +1,201/−21 counting the new tests).** One patch carries L.26, L.28 and the L.28 follow-ups. *(An earlier cut of this patch carried build 53 and lacked the follow-ups; it is superseded.)*
- **The fix (`jarvis/daemons.py`):** `stop()` now returns only when the **child and its supervisor** are both gone — the gap `restart()` lost its race in. `restart()` stops whenever the child is running **or** a supervisor is alive (so a `starting`, `restarting` or crash-looping daemon is covered), then waits (bounded by `RESTART_SUPERVISOR_WAIT` = 5 s) for the old supervisor to be gone before `start()`. **The H.1.3 "a supervisor is already alive" guard is unchanged**, so a genuine second supervisor is still refused. A failure now says what state the daemon was left in (`could not stop before restart: … ('x' is <state>)`, `stopped 'x' but could not start it again: …`).
- **Two defects in my own first cut, found by the existing suite and fixed before shipping:** (1) a supervisor that runs as a **thread of the calling process** (as `tests/test_workspace.py` does) records the caller's own pid; waiting for it never ends, and the force-kill fallback then SIGTERMed the caller itself (the suite run died with exit 143). `stop()` now never waits on or signals its own pid (`_is_other_process`). (2) A long-lived caller that `start()`ed the daemon in-process (the Discord gateway, the web tool runner) owns the supervisor as a child; once it exits it stays a **zombie that `pid_alive` counts as alive**, and `stop()` would sit out its whole timeout. `_reap()` collects it (POSIX `waitpid(WNOHANG)`; a no-op on Windows).
- **Tests — `tests/test_l26_daemon_restart.py`, 9:** a **real supervisor and a real child, each operation its own `python -m jarvis` process** (as the web server does it, so the zombie artifact described above does not colour them). Covers restart on a running daemon (new child pid, new supervisor, old supervisor gone), twice in a row, on a crash-looping daemon, on a stopped daemon, `stop()` returning only after the supervisor is gone, a second supervisor still refused, a failed start after the stop saying so, the in-process zombie case, and the self-pid case. **Against the unpatched `daemons.py` 5 of the first 7 fail** — with the owner's exact message, `already has a supervisor running`. (The two tests added later were not run against the unpatched file.)

**Acceptance criteria above — all five met in the sandbox:** (a) running daemon ends running under a new pid ✅ · (b) crash-looping daemon is unstuck ✅ · (c) a failed restart names the state ✅ · (d) a second supervisor is still refused ✅ · (e) real-supervisor tests ✅.

**Not verified (L.26):** **Windows** (there `stop` is `taskkill /T /F` and `_reap` does nothing); the **web Restart button end to end** (no browser or real `server.js` here); a daemon whose **grandchild holds the pipe open** (the supervisor's 2 s join — the wait is bounded, but the case was not exercised). **Owner check:** press Restart on a running daemon and on a crash-looping one on the real install.


**Owner's report:** the restart button doesn't work; it always says it can't start because a supervisor is already running.

**Reproduced (2026-10-02e), not just read.** In a scratch `HOME` on Linux, with each operation as its own `python -m jarvis` process (as the web server does it), using a daemon that just sleeps:
- `daemon-restart` on a **running** daemon → after ~2.8 s: `ok: false`, `'repro' already has a supervisor running (pid N) — stop it first`. The daemon is **now stopped** (the child was killed; nothing started it again).
- `daemon-restart` again (daemon stopped) → `ok: true`, starts it. The third call fails again. So Restart behaves as *Stop with an error toast* every other click.
- `daemon-restart` on a **crash-looping** daemon (`restart=always`, status `restarting`, supervisor alive, child not running) → the same refusal every time; `daemon-stop` on it works.
- A first attempt that called `daemons.restart()` in-process looked even worse (the supervisor never "exited") — that was a harness artifact (an unreaped zombie child still counts as alive to `pid_alive`), so it is **not** evidence; the per-process runs above are.

**Root cause (from `jarvis/daemons.py`, confirmed by the runs):** two correct pieces of logic disagree about "stopped".
1. `restart()` calls `stop()` only when `status()["running"]` is true. `stop()` declares success the moment the **child** is gone (`not status(did)["running"]`).
2. `restart()` then calls `start()` immediately. `start()` refuses when `status()["supervisor_pid"]` is alive (the H.1.3 guard, which is correct — two supervisors race for `console.log` / `status.json` / `stdin.queue`).
3. The **supervisor outlives its child**: `run_supervisor()` still has to join both pump threads (up to 2 s each if a grandchild holds the pipe), write the exit line, close the console, unlink the flag, write the final status and let the interpreter exit. `start()` runs microseconds after `stop()` returns, so it loses that race essentially every time.
4. Separately, if the daemon is not `running` but its supervisor is alive (`starting`, `restarting` backoff, a crash loop), `restart()` skips `stop()` entirely and `start()` refuses — so Restart can never un-stick the daemons that most need it.

**Where it shows up:** the web Restart button (`POST /api/daemons/:id/restart` → `daemon-restart` → `daemons.restart`), the CLI, and the AI tool `daemon_restart` (`actions/workspace_tools.py:94`) — all one function. Scheduled starts (`tick()`) and any future autostart (L.27) go through the same `start()` guard.

**Why it was missed:** no test in `tests/` calls `daemons.restart()`; the H.1.x tests exercise `start`/`stop`/`status` separately.

**Not verified:** Windows. The sandbox is Linux; the ~2.8 s figure includes Linux's wait for a zombie child and will differ on Windows (where `stop` is `taskkill /T /F`). The *logic* gap does not depend on the platform; the owner's "always" on Windows is consistent with it.

**Draft acceptance criteria (when implemented):** (a) Restart on a running daemon ends **running** under a new pid, with no error; (b) Restart on a `restarting` / crash-looping / `starting` daemon ends running; (c) a failed restart never silently leaves the daemon stopped — the message says what state it is in; (d) a genuine second supervisor is still refused (H.1.3 stays); (e) a test that uses a **real** supervisor process (not a mock) for (a) and (b).

**Design questions for the owner (Q-L26):** none blocking; the obvious shape is "stop must wait for the supervisor, not just the child, and restart must stop a live supervisor even when the child is down" — recorded as a direction, not decided.

### L.27 🐞 Bug — daemons never auto-start: `autostart_all()` exists and nothing calls it (NEW, 2026-10-02e, owner-reported; **FIXED 2026-10-04 in `jarvis-l27-autostart.patch` — see the Built block; not run on Windows, in a browser, or with the real web server**)

**Status:** ✅ FIXED in code (2026-10-04) · **Priority:** P1 (the Autostart switch was stored and shown, and did nothing).

**Built 2026-10-04 — `jarvis-l27-autostart.patch` (against `jarvis-main_77_.zip`; 4 files, +350/−4, most of it the test; no build bump — `build_info.py` still says build 54 until `script.bat` rebuilds).**
- **Where the call went (Q-L27, answered by assumption, NOT owner-confirmed).** `scheduler.tick(startup=True)` now calls `daemons.autostart_all()`, after the existing `daemons.tick()` rider and individually wrapped so it can never cost a reminder. The startup tick is the one moment all three long-lived drivers already treat as "Jarvis just started": the web server's boot tick (`sched-tick --startup`), `jarvis sched-daemon`, and a Task Scheduler / cron `sched-tick --startup` at login. So candidates (1) web-server start and (2) PC login (once Task Scheduler is pointed at `sched-tick --startup`) are both covered; candidate (3) "first command after boot" is not. **Deliberately not on the 30 s tick:** a daemon the owner stopped by hand stays stopped until the next startup (pinned by a test). **If the owner meant something else by "start with Jarvis", this is the decision to revisit.**
- **`autostart_all()` hardened (`daemons.py`).** It now skips a daemon whose *supervisor* is alive (STARTING, or RESTARTING in crash-loop backoff), not only one whose child is running — `start()` would refuse those with the H.1.3 guard and they would have been reported as failures (and it must not fight L.26's restart logic). A genuine failure is written to the daemon's own status as `last_error: "autostart failed: …"`, so the Daemons panel can show why it stayed down; one bad daemon does not stop the others.
- **Tick result.** `sched-tick` / `scheduler.tick()` now returns `daemons_autostarted` (a list; always present, empty off the startup tick). Nothing in `server.js` reads it yet and nothing raises a notification for a failed autostart.
- **Panel text (`web/public/daemons.js`).** The Autostart tooltip (two places) no longer says "nothing in the current build launches autostart daemons yet"; it now says it starts each time Jarvis starts and that a service stopped by hand stays stopped until then.
- **Tests:** new `tests/test_l27_daemon_autostart.py`, **10 checks, every one through the real start path** — `python -m jarvis sched-tick --startup` / `sched-daemon --once` as their own processes, real supervisors and children, status read from a fresh process (the L.26 harness lesson: no in-process `start()`). They cover: an autostart daemon comes up; `sched-daemon --once` also starts it; non-autostart and disabled ones stay down; a plain tick never autostarts; a hand-stopped daemon stays stopped across plain ticks; a second startup tick leaves a running daemon (same pid, same supervisor) alone; a crash-looping supervisor is left alone with no "autostart failed"; a failed autostart is reported and recorded; one bad daemon does not block another; the tick result keeps its existing keys. **9 of the 10 fail on the unpatched `_77_` tree** (the tenth, "stay down", should pass either way); **10/10 with the patch**.
- **Neighbouring suites with the patch:** `test_scheduler`, `test_sched_daemon`, `test_workspace`, `test_l26_daemon_restart` (9/9), `test_l16_*`, `test_h11`, `test_h16`, `test_schedule_watch`, `test_browser_daemon`, `verify_daemons_panel.js` 111/111 and `verify_daemons_console.js` 37/37 all pass. **`test_h12_daemon_fixes` and `test_h15_daemon_editor` fail under `run_tests.py --jobs 4` — identically on the untouched `_77_` tree (they share the real registry) — and pass serially with and without the patch; run daemon tests serially.** The full suite was **not** run.
- **Not verified / not done:** Windows; a browser; the real web server's boot tick; the Task Scheduler / login path (needs `sched-tick --startup` wired there by the owner). A startup tick that finds the scheduler lock held (a slow scheduled ask running) is skipped for that boot, so autostart waits for the next startup — judged rare, not handled. A failed autostart is visible on the daemon's status and in the tick result but raises no notification.

**Evidence:** `daemons.autostart_all()` (`daemons.py:1026`) is defined and honours `autostart` and `enabled`, but a search of the whole tree finds **no caller** — not in `cli.py` / `workspace_cli.py` (no `daemon-autostart` verb), not in `web/server.js`, not in `scheduler.py` or `sched_daemon.py`, not in `script.bat` or `launch-web.ps1`. By contrast scheduled daemon starts *are* wired (`scheduler.py:882` → `daemons.tick()`). The panel's own help text under the switch says as much: *"nothing in the current build launches autostart daemons yet"* (`daemons.js` ~1777, ~2068). `autostart` is only ever read in `autostart_all()` and written by the add/edit paths.

**Consequence for other plans:** L.12's decision "autostart follows the tool's preset, no extra warning" assumes autostart works; today it would register a daemon that never starts. K.4.1 / H.1.5 describe the Autostart toggle as a feature; it is a stored flag only.

**Open owner question Q-L27:** what does "start with Jarvis" mean here? Candidates: (1) when the **web server** starts (the one long-lived Jarvis process); (2) when the **PC logs in** (needs `script.bat` / `launch-web.ps1` or a scheduled task); (3) the first Jarvis command after boot. This decides where the single call goes. Whatever is chosen must be safe to call twice (it must not spawn a second supervisor) and must not be defeated by L.26's refusal after an unclean shutdown.

**Draft acceptance criteria:** an enabled daemon with `autostart` set is running within N seconds of the chosen trigger; a disabled one is not started; one already running is left alone; a failure is logged and shown, never silent; a test with a real start path, not only `autostart_all()` called by hand.

### L.28 Token findings from the two newest Discord conversations (NEW, 2026-10-02e; measured from the logs, **PARTLY IMPLEMENTED 2026-10-03b in `jarvis-l26-l28-patch.zip` — see the Built block; not run against a live model or the real Discord gateway**)

**Status:** ◐ PARTLY IMPLEMENTED (2026-10-03b) — findings 1, 2 and 4 addressed in code, finding 5 made **diagnosable** (not diagnosed), finding 3 only **softened**. **Priority:** P2.

**Built 2026-10-03b — `jarvis-l26-l28-patch.zip` (see L.26 for the patch facts).** Two rounds in one patch: the first round did findings 1, 2 and 4; at the owner's request ("do these too") the second did the four items the first round had left alone.
- **Finding 2 — tools-off guests: fixed (`ai_client.py`).** An **explicitly empty** `JARVIS_ALLOWED_TOOLS` (what `channels/base.py` sets for a sender with no tool permission) now runs the ask as a plain **no-tools** ask: no schemas, no tool executor, and the prompt no longer says "call `search_tools` first". Unset still means unrestricted; a non-empty allowlist is untouched. It uses `JARVIS_ALLOWED_TOOLS`, not the Tool Manager's switch (see the cross-check in Revision 2026-10-03b). *Plausibly also explains the three Groq 400s — the prompt named a tool the request did not offer — but that is a hypothesis; there was no live reproduction.*
- **Finding 1 — the 27,631-token greeting: addressed at the router (`actions/notify_owner.py`).** Guest phrasings — "tell ur owner hi", "let the owner know", "dm your owner", "notify the owner" and variants, 20 phrases at weights 8–10 — now route confidently to `notify_owner`. Always a messaging verb plus *your/ur/the/my* owner, so "who is the owner of this repo" and "my owner told me to say hi" do not route there (tested). **The token saving was not measured.**
- **Finding 4 — failover churn (`key_health.py`, `ai_client.py`, `ai_providers.py`):** (a) a **loopback** endpoint that refused a connection (Ollama not running) is skipped for 60 s **across asks** (`key_health.json` gains a `hosts` section; old files still load). Never skipped when it is the only provider, never applied to a remote host, and a success clears it. (b) **Groq's `tool_use_failed` is now a request-shape failure**, so the provider's other keys are skipped and the next provider is tried. *Added at the owner's request after being tried and reverted once: the logged message was already covered by the existing markers and there was no evidence the broader rule helps. **Trade-off:** a garbled generation is nondeterministic, so another key might have worked.* (c) **Not addressed:** Gemini 503s and Groq's 8,000 tokens-per-minute limit.
- **Finding 3 — the 10,296-token `send_dm` ask: softened, not solved (`actions/send_dm.py`, `actions/channel_people.py`).** The root is that "maryem" is a word *inside* the saved handle `maryem.not.maryam11_16812`, and a word of a handle has never been a match (only a word of a saved **name** is, tier 2). **That was not loosened** — `send_dm` still never guesses a recipient. Instead an unknown-name error now carries `did_you_mean` (close spellings of known contacts, ratio ≥ 0.75, at most 3, only for names of three or more letters), lists the nearest contacts first, and says to **confirm with the owner, never pick**; the channels instruction now says to call `send_dm` straight away and not `recent_dms` first. A saved name for her (`remember_sender`) would still save the most.
- **Finding 5 — the unanswered owner message: diagnosable, still not diagnosed (`channels/base.py`).** While an ask runs, a watchdog writes an `error` row (provider `watchdog`) plus a stderr line every **90 s** (`STALL_LOG_SECONDS`) naming the last provider attempt and last tool, and a row when an ask **waited more than 5 s** behind another on `_ASK_LOCK`. It **kills nothing and times nothing out**; the cause is still unknown.
- **Guests who are allowed tools (what finding 1/2 left over):** `send_dm` and `recent_dms` — the only tools whose handlers refuse a non-owner — are no longer **offered** to a non-owner chat sender: dropped in `schemas_for_tools`, `search_tools` and `get_tool_schema` (`tools.OWNER_ONLY_TOOLS`, driven by `JARVIS_CHANNEL_SENDER`; an unparseable value is not treated as a guest). **Execution is untouched** — the handlers' own owner check is still the gate, and a test re-asserts it. **This is a token and misuse saving, not a security boundary** (see L.29).
- **Tests:** `tests/test_l28_token_waste.py` **58** checks (**23 fail on the unpatched files**) and `tests/test_l28b_followups.py` **49** (**16 fail against the first round's code**). Still passing: `test_send_dm` 22/22, `test_discovery_round_budget` 74, `test_l16_caps_and_budget` 40, `test_request_shape_failover` 24. **Full suite on a fresh `_72_` + the patch: 96 of 97 files** — the one failure is `test_key_health.py` (two timing assertions, identical on the unpatched tree).
- **A mistake of mine, caught by the suite:** the first cut inserted a helper between `@functools.wraps(_ask_impl)` and `def ask`, so the decorator bound to the helper and `ask()` lost its signature (`test_discovery_round_budget`, `test_l16_caps_and_budget`). Fixed before shipping.

**Not verified / not done (L.28):** no **live model** and no real **Discord gateway** (the watchdog row has never been seen in a real stall); the **Groq marker's effect** (no live 400); whether `did_you_mean` actually removes a round; **token savings are not measured anywhere in this patch**; Groq's 8,000 TPM limit and a smaller guest `history_window` are untouched; **no hard wall-clock deadline for asks** was added (wait for the watchdog to show where a stall sits).


**Sources:** `7b971647284ec43f.jsonl` (owner thread, 206 rows) and `7cca05eac02bea61.jsonl` (the guest Maryem's thread, 769 rows), both Discord, 2026-09-17 → 2026-10-02; "newest" = 2026-10-02 20:29–20:44 UTC (the owner's transcript shows local time, UTC+1). Only builds with L.24 T6 log an `ask total` row, so the per-ask table below covers today's asks; the older history is aggregate only, and **thinking tokens were not logged before 2026-10-02** (older totals understate).

**Shape of the cost.** Input is ~89% of today's tokens in the guest thread (42,444 in / 2,022 out / 3,365 thinking over 25 rounds) and ~97% across its whole history (174.7K in / 5.4K out). A round costs ~1.4–2.4K input before anything useful happens (system prompt ~2.7K characters, a 22-message rolling history, the tool list), so **cost ≈ rounds × ~1.8K**; the lever is rounds, not reply length. Prompt caching never applies (prefixes of 481–926 tokens against floors of 4,096 for Gemini and 1,024 for Groq) — which is fine at this size, not a defect.

**Today's asks, guest thread (ask-total tokens):** 2,031 · 6,909 (`😢😢`) · 1,728 · 1,557 · 4,841 (`its urgent, text assim`) · 4,629 · 2,332 · 3,861 · 8,533 · 8,276 · 1,938 = **46,635**. Owner thread: 1,650 (`yo jarvis`) and 10,296 (the `send_dm` ask). Plain chat asks (`meow`) cost 1.5–1.9K and are fine.

**Findings (ordered by waste):**
1. **A greeting cost 27,631 tokens.** Getting "Tell ur owner hi" delivered through `notify_owner` took five asks (4,629 + 2,332 + 3,861 + 8,533 + 8,276): the model asked for the wording three times, then needed `search_tools` → `get_tool_schema` → `notify_owner` (three more full-history rounds), with two Groq failures and a failover in the middle. A guest is offered only `search_tools`, `get_tool_schema` and `search_commands`; the router did not pre-select `notify_owner` for "tell ur owner". This is the same discovery tax L.24 T1 targets, now measured on a chat path.
2. **Tools-off guests are still offered discovery tools, and every use is guaranteed to fail — 11,750 tokens today.** `channels/base.py` sets `JARVIS_ALLOWED_TOOLS=""` when the sender has no tool permission, so `execute_tool` answers `tool not permitted` to everything; but `search_tools` / `get_tool_schema` / `search_commands` are still in the request and the system prompt still says "call search_tools first". Seen at 20:29:55 (`😢😢`: 4 Groq rounds, 6,909 tokens, a search for the previous topic, then `get_tool_schema("search_tools")`, both refused) and 20:35:15 (`text assim`: 3 rounds, 4,841). The tools worked for her from 20:37 on, i.e. the owner changed her permission mid-session; that is a config change, not a bug.
3. **`send_dm` ask: 10,296 tokens in three rounds** (2,157 / 3,575 / 3,745). The model called `recent_dms` (limit 10) only to learn the handle behind "mariem" (the spoken name does not match `maryem.not.maryam11_16812`); the result carried five threads, including two Instagram fixture threads and a 2026-09-17 thread, and rode along in the next two rounds. Probably unavoidable while the person has no saved name (`remember_sender` was refused for her on 2026-09-24), but a saved name would let `send_dm` resolve it alone in one round.
4. **Failover churn.** Today, guest thread: Gemini 503 "high demand" ×4; Groq 400 ×3 (`tool_use_failed`: the model called `search_commands`, which was not in that request's tool list) and Groq 429 ×2. Groq's on-demand limit on `openai/gpt-oss-120b` is **8,000 tokens per minute** ("Used 6217, Requested 2051"), i.e. about four ~2K requests a minute, so one five-round ask (8.5K) can exceed it by itself. Ollama sits in the chain but is not running: each time it is reached it costs a ~4 s connect failure (20:41:57 → 20:42:01) and gives nothing. All-time in the guest log: Gemini 429 ×32 and 503 ×9, concentrated on 2026-09-24 and 09-30.
5. **An owner message was never answered, and the cause is not in the logs.** "has anyone dmed you recently?" was sent at 21:37:47 local (20:37:47 UTC); its ask did not start until 20:39:57, made one Groq call and a `recent_dms` call, sent a second Groq request at 20:40:00.580, and then **nothing** — no response row, no error row, no `ask total` — until the next ask at 20:44:22. The owner's transcript shows no outbound reply to that message. Possible causes: a hung HTTP call with no timeout row, or the process killed; and `channels/base.py` serializes asks under `_ASK_LOCK`, so a hung ask would block every other chat. **Unverified.**

**Not examined:** per-provider billing (the logs count tokens, not money); whether a smaller `history_window` for guests would pay for itself; thinking-token cost on Gemini beyond today's 3,365 (7%).

**Draft directions (not decided; for L.24 T1/T3 and L.16):** do not offer discovery tools to a sender whose tool permission is off, and say so in that turn's system prompt; pre-select `notify_owner` for guest "tell the owner …" phrasing; skip a provider after a `tool_use_failed` 400 for the rest of the ask; skip Ollama when it has failed to connect recently; log a timeout row so finding 5 is diagnosable.

**Direction → outcome (2026-10-03b):** *no discovery tools for a tools-off sender* — done · *pre-select `notify_owner` for guest "tell the owner …"* — done · *skip a provider after `tool_use_failed` for the rest of the ask* — done (other keys skipped, next provider tried) · *skip Ollama when it failed recently* — done (60 s, loopback only) · *log a timeout row so finding 5 is diagnosable* — done as a stall watchdog, not a timeout.

### L.29 `send_dm` cannot run from chat — there is no confirmation channel — and what that implies for fixing it (NEW, 2026-10-02e; first real use of L.20; **documented only**)

**Status:** ❌ L.20's "from chat" purpose is **not met**; the safe failure worked. **Priority:** P1 for the owner's stated use ("DM Maryem that I'll be late" from Discord); the security notes below are P1 for whoever designs the fix.

**What happened (owner thread, 20:44 UTC).** The owner (`delpion`) asked on Discord: "yo jarvis tell mariem that youre never meowing". Round 0 → `recent_dms`; round 1 → `send_dm {person: "maryem.not.maryam11_16812", platform: "discord", message: …}`; result `{ok: false, cancelled: true, "'send_dm' requires user confirmation, but no confirmation channel is available here — not run."}`; round 2 → an honest reply ("the system refused to transmit it without a manual confirmation prompt — which isn't available in this channel"). **No message was sent.** Credit where due: the failure was reported truthfully and nothing leaked.

**Cause.** `TOOL_CONFIRM_REQUIRED = {"send_dm"}`; `ai_client`'s confirm gate cancels a confirm-required tool whenever `on_confirm_request is None`; `channels/base.py` calls `ai_client.ask(...)` **without** one. So *every* confirm-gated tool is permanently cancelled in chat — `send_dm` was never going to work there. L.20 already lists "not verified against a real account", but it described chat as supported ("`review` from chat", "from chat or the UI").

**What this run did and did not exercise.** The gate cancelled the call *before* the tool body ran, so none of the L.20 controls were exercised for real: owner-only check, contact resolution, rate limit, transcript logging, `dm_person` delivery and its failure messages. The 22 tests cover those by simulation; the live path is still untested. At the PC / web UI, where a confirm prompt exists, the tool may well work — **also untested**.

**Security notes the fix must respect (read from the code and the logs):**
1. **The missing confirm channel is currently the only thing stopping guest-triggered shell and agent tools.** The guest thread shows the model trying `run_shell` (2026-09-30 21:45, a Python urllib one-liner) and `code_agent` (2026-10-02 20:29) — both ended "requires user confirmation, no channel". The allowlist did not stop them: the confirm gate runs *before* `execute_tool`'s allowlist check.
2. **A sender with tool permission gets everything.** `base.py` sets `JARVIS_ALLOWED_TOOLS=""` for tools-off senders and leaves it **unset** (= unrestricted, per its own comment) for tools-on senders. After the owner enabled tools for Maryem, her offered set grew to include `send_dm`, `recent_dms`, `remember_sender` and `who_am_i_talking_to` — owner-only tools declared to a guest, protected only by each tool's own `is_owner` check. (`run_shell` has a read-only allow-list exemption from confirmation, so a tools-on guest could run those commands today; not examined further.)
3. **Therefore adding a generic confirm channel to chat would remove the only guard in point 1.** The fix must not make `run_shell` / `code_agent` / `edit_file` confirmable from a guest's turn.

**Options to weigh (Q-L29, owner decision needed; none chosen):**
- **A. Owner-sender is the confirmation.** In chat, treat a `send_dm` call from the *verified owner id* as already confirmed (the message "tell mariem …" is the instruction), still previewed in the reply, still rate limited and logged; every other confirm-gated tool stays cancelled in chat. Smallest change; leaves the confirm gate intact for guests.
- **B. Out-of-band approve/deny.** The bot DMs the owner the exact recipient and text and waits for "yes"/"no" (needs a pending-approval store and a timeout; a good fit with L.16's approval summary and `job_risk`). Safest, most work; also the natural base for L.23.
- **C. PC/UI only.** Keep chat refused and say so in the tool's description so the model stops trying (cheap, but drops the stated chat use).
Whatever is chosen, add a per-sender tool allowlist so a guest is offered `notify_owner` and not the owner tools (also saves the schema tokens in L.28).

**Cross-check, 2026-10-03b:** L.28's guest-tool work does **not** touch this gap. `send_dm` and `recent_dms` are now simply **not offered** to a non-owner chat sender (`tools.OWNER_ONLY_TOOLS`); their handlers still refuse a non-owner and remain the gate. That is a token and misuse saving — **not** a security boundary and **not** the per-sender allowlist this section asks for: a guest who is allowed tools is still offered everything else, confirm-gated tools included. How a chat sender approves a gated action (**Q-L29**) is still open.

**Update 2026-10-03f:** the owner asked for Discord/Instagram "ask prompt capabilities" (**L.42.1**). Under reading A (prompts Jarvis puts to the sender) that is the route to answering Q-L29; the security notes above bind it unchanged. Nothing decided or built.

**Update 2026-10-03f (second round):** the owner chose the approval surface — **Discord native buttons, Instagram a Y/N text reply** (see L.42.1). That is a variant of option **B** (an explicit approve/deny, not "the owner's message is the confirmation"), delivered *in the chat* rather than as a separate DM. Details and the security rules are under L.42.1. Option A and C are not chosen. Still unbuilt.

**Draft acceptance criteria:** the owner asks on Discord and the DM is delivered (or refused with a cause), once, with a transcript record; a guest asking for the same is refused before the model sees the tool; `run_shell` / `code_agent` from a guest turn remain impossible, with a test that pins it; a real send is observed on both Discord and (24 h window) Instagram, which closes L.20.

### L.30 Feature — full notification rework (NEW, 2026-10-03c, owner request; **BUILT 2026-10-04h in `l30-notification-rework.patch` — see the Built block below; not yet run on the owner's machine**)

**Owner's request, in substance:** "full notification rework". No further detail was given.

**What exists today (read from the source in `jarvis-main_74_`; nothing run):** `jarvis/notifier.py` (659 lines); the web **Notifications** panel (`notifications-overlay`, subtitle "everything ever sent, persisted on disk") fed by `/api/notifications` and a full-history route in `server.js`; the importance levels and the summary-not-raw-output rule (**D.2**, **D.2.1**), clipboard flood protection (**K.2.7**), notify-the-owner-only-when-important (**L.23**), the notification layout bug on the Daemons panel (**L.8**, still unresolved) and the scheduler's failed-job notifications (**L.25**, Q-L25g).

**Not decided (scope unstated):** whether "full" means the panel only, the delivery pipeline (levels, channels, flood control), the sources that feed it (jobs, daemons, clipboard, tools — see **D.2.2**), or all three. Until that is answered, none of the existing notification items above should be treated as superseded.

**2026-10-04h — owner detail and decision.** The owner said the notifications are "really really bad" **both UI-wise and functionality-wise** and confirmed the full scope: the panel, the toasts and the behaviour behind them. The delivery channels (Discord, Instagram, voice, Playnite, OS toast) and the L.8 Daemons-panel offset bug were left out on purpose.

**What was wrong (read from `jarvis-main_82_`, then confirmed in a browser — see the revision):**
1. **One shared toast.** Notifications were shown through the single `#toast` element that every error and "Copied" message also uses. Two notifications in the same tick overwrote each other, and any error toast wiped a reminder off the screen.
2. **The D-N1 re-surfacing was real but fragile.** (An earlier message in this conversation wrongly said level 3 only made the toast sticky; the code did implement D-N1.) It used **one timer for the whole page**, so a second persistent notification cancelled the first one's re-surfacing; it lived only in the tab, so a reload lost it; and it ended silently after six tries.
3. **Level 5 threw its answer away.** The Acknowledge dialog's result was never read, so "Acknowledge" acknowledged nothing — and `JarvisUI.confirm` closes whatever modal is already open, so a level-5 notification could silently dismiss a pending tool approval.
4. **The badge was a counter in the tab.** It reset to zero on every page load and had no relation to what was actually unread.
5. **The panel was a flat, read-only list** of the last 200: no read state, filters, search, dismiss or clear.
6. **The inbox could lose data.** Every writer did load → modify → save of the whole file with no lock, and a flat "newest 200" cut dropped an unread reminder as soon as a burst pushed it out.

**Built (`l30-notification-rework.patch`, against `jarvis-main_82_`; 16 files, +2,792/−316):**
- **Two kinds of "seen", kept apart.** `seen_by` (delivery to a consumer, `notify-ack`) is unchanged. New per-record `read_at` and `acked_at` are the **owner's** state; only they drive the badge, the Unread filter and the re-surfacing. A persistent (3) or confirm (5) item *needs acknowledgment* until `acked_at` is set; reading it acknowledges it.
- **`notifier.py`:** `mark_read`, `mark_all_read`, `dismiss`, `clear_read`, `summary()` (total, unread, failed-unread, per-kind counts, the awaiting-acknowledgment list), `history()` filters (unread, failed, needs-ack, kind, source, multi-word query), an `O_EXCL` lockfile around every inbox write (same approach as `subagents.py`; best effort — it never blocks delivery for more than ~3 s), and **state-aware pruning**: the cap is now **500** (was 200); read items go first, then plain unread, and an item still awaiting acknowledgment goes last.
- **CLI:** `notify-summary`, `notify-read <ids|all>`, `notify-dismiss <ids|read|all>`, and `notify-history [N] [--unread --failed --needs-ack --kind= --source= --q=]` (the plain form is unchanged; the reply gained `total`, `unread`, `kinds`, `needs_ack`). Registered in `reserved_names.py` and the slash registry (`/notifications` covers the two safe ones; `notify-dismiss` is a `dangerous` passthrough like `notify-clear`).
- **`server.js`:** `GET /api/notifications/summary`, `POST /api/notifications/read`, `POST /api/notifications/dismiss`, and filters on `/history`. Ids are pattern-checked and every value is its own argv entry (no shell).
- **New `web/public/notifications.js` + `.css`:**
  - **Toast stack** (top centre): one card per notification with source, time, a title, a short body, a ×N count when the same notification repeats, **Acknowledge** where one is needed, and **Open chat / Open schedule** when the record has a `conv_id` / `job_id`. At most four cards; click opens the panel at that item. It steps below a visible error toast instead of hiding behind it.
  - **Inbox panel:** unread dots, All / Unread / Failed / Needs-ack chips, a kind dropdown, search, day sections, a pinned **"Needs your acknowledgment"** section, runs of the same notification collapsed into one ×N row (click to expand), Show more, per-row Mark read / Acknowledge / Dismiss, **Mark all read**, **Clear read** (asks first), an empty state per case, and keys `/` `j` `k` `r` `x` `Esc`.
  - **Honest acknowledgment:** D-N1 is kept (every 10 minutes, at most six times) but **per notification, re-checked against the durable state each time**, so acknowledging in the panel or another tab stops it; anything still unacknowledged **comes back on screen after a reload**. Level 5 dialogs queue, wait for any open dialog to finish, and **record** the answer ("Later" leaves it pending).
- **`app.js`:** `showNotification()` now delegates to `JarvisNotifications.show()` (with a last-resort fallback to the old one-line toast if the module failed to load); the old panel code, the persistent-toast machinery and the dead `.notif-card` / `.is-sticky` CSS were removed. The generic `toast()` for errors is unchanged.
- **`doctor.py`:** the inbox check now counts unread by the owner's read state and reports items awaiting acknowledgment.

**Behaviour the owner may want changed (decisions I made, not asked):** clicking a row marks it read (except one awaiting acknowledgment, which needs the button); **Mark all read also acknowledges** everything waiting; **Dismiss deletes for good, with no undo**; level 2 cards hide after 8 s (12 s when they need acknowledgment) and level 1 raises no card; the panel no longer closes on the document-level Escape handler of other panels because it has its own.

**Not changed:** the delivery channels and their rules, the level meanings (D.2.1), digest batching, flood control (K.2.7), `notify_owner`, `tool_safety.py`, any confirmation gate, and **AGENTS.md** (no invariant is touched). **L.8 is not addressed** — the new stack is `position: fixed` like the old toast, and which element moves in the Daemons panel is still unobserved.

**Status: ✅ BUILT in a patch (2026-10-04h); not verified on the owner's machine — see Revision 2026-10-04h.**

### L.31 Feature — MCP servers rework (NEW, 2026-10-03c, owner request; **✅ BUILT IN A PATCH — `jarvis-l31-mcp-servers-ui.patch`; applied with the other pending patches to `jarvis-main_85_.zip` on 2026-10-05g; not run on the owner's machine**)

**Owner's request, in substance:** "mcp servers rework". No further detail was given.

**What exists today (read, not run):** `jarvis/mcp_client.py` (696 lines); the `jarvis mcp-*` CLI commands (status, refresh, call, config); the **MCP** menu panel (`mcp-overlay`) over `/api/mcp` and `/api/mcp/refresh` in `server.js`; a `jarvis doctor` check for configured vs enabled servers; MCP tools shown as their own Debug source (**K.3.4**); and, since **L.25**, every MCP tool is an ordinary `mcp_<server>_<tool>` entry that the Tool Manager can switch off (there is no per-*server* switch there).

**Scope as built (my reading — the owner never narrowed it):** the **panel and its write path**, plus per-server enable and trust. The client / transports (`mcp_client.py`'s stdio and HTTP code) and the Tool Manager were **not** reworked. The original "Not decided" question is therefore still partly open: nothing here changes how servers appear in the Tool Manager (there is still no per-*server* switch there; the panel marks tools the Tool Manager switched off instead).

**What was built:**
- **Panel (`web/public/mcp-servers.js` + `mcp-servers.css`, new; the old MCP block left `app.js`, which now only opens it).** One card per server: a status word (Ready / Off / Error / Needs fixing / Not connected yet / Tool list is old), the transport, whether its tools ask first or are **Trusted**, when the tool list was last read, and the reason in plain words when something is wrong. Every card has an on/off switch, a per-server **Refresh**, **Edit**, **Remove**, and a **Trusted** switch (turning it on asks first). Tools are expandable and each is marked when the Tool Manager (L.25) has switched it off, so "plugged in but the model can't use 3 of 9" is visible here. **Add / Edit form** in the panel (arguments one per line, environment variables as rows). Search by server or tool name, a "Needs attention" filter, keyboard keys, phone width. All server-supplied text goes in as text nodes, never markup. Pure helpers are exposed as `JarvisMcp._pure`.
- **Write path (`mcp_client.py`, `cli.py`, `server.js`).** New `save_server(name, spec, replace=None)` (add / edit / rename), `set_server_flag(name, "enabled"|"trusted", value)`, `remove_server(name)`, and `validate_server_spec()` — shared by the editor (refuses to save) and `status()` (shows the problem on the card). A new server **starts switched off and confirm-gated**; an edit keeps the existing switches and any hand-added keys; turning a server off drops its cached tools at once; a malformed `mcp_config.json` is never overwritten; two names that would share the `mcp_<name>_` tool prefix are refused. Reached only through the new **`jarvis mcp-edit <enable|disable|trust|untrust|remove> <name>`** and **`jarvis mcp-edit save <name> <json> [--replace <current-name>]`** verbs and three routes — `POST /api/mcp/server`, `POST /api/mcp/server/:name/:action`, `DELETE /api/mcp/server/:name` — alongside the existing `GET /api/mcp` and `POST /api/mcp/refresh`.
- **`status()` additions (old fields unchanged):** per server `state` (`disabled` / `misconfigured` / `error` / `not_refreshed` / `stale` / `ok`, decided in one place), `problems`, `description`, `command`, `args`, `cwd`, `url`, `url_redacted`, `env_keys`, `tools`, `disabled_tool_count`.
- **Secrets never reach the browser.** Environment **values** are never returned (only the variable names), and a URL is shown as `scheme://host[:port]/path` with `?…` for a query and userinfo dropped; an edit that leaves a secret box untouched sends `null`, which `save_server` reads as "keep it".
- **Housekeeping:** `mcp-edit` added to `reserved_names.py`; `REPO_MAP.md` (panel row, test rows; the `mcp-edit` CLI lines were added 2026-10-05g) and `AGENTS.md` (test commands and a new invariant, 2026-10-05g) amended.

**Invariants kept:** the security rule at the top of `mcp_client.py` is unchanged — **servers are added or changed only by a human** (the panel's buttons, `jarvis mcp-edit`, or the file), never by a model tool; `actions/mcp_tools.py` imports none of the edit functions and `tests/test_mcp_edit.py` pins that. MCP tools are still confirm-gated by default; Trusted is an explicit per-server human choice. Nothing in `tool_safety.py`, confirmation prompts, `risk_review()` or the AI-review gating was touched; `MAX_TOOL_ROUNDS` untouched.

**Verified (2026-10-05g, in the combined tree):** `tests/test_mcp_edit.py` 120/120, `tests/test_mcp_client.py` 55/55, `tests/test_reserved_names.py` 12/12, `node tests/verify_mcp_servers.js` 74/74. **Not re-run here:** `tests/verify_mcp_servers_ui.py` (the real page in headless Chromium against a real stdio MCP server) — no Chromium in this sandbox; its result belongs to whoever built the patch and is not independently confirmed.

**Not verified / limits:**
- **Never run on the owner's machine**, with a real MCP server of the owner's choosing, on Windows, or against a remote (HTTP) server with a real token.
- The three new `server.js` routes were **syntax-checked only** (Express is not installed in the sandbox); the browser test answers `/api/mcp*` by calling the same CLI verbs, so it proves page + module + CLI agree, not `server.js` itself.

### L.32 Feature — full Focus mode rework (NEW, 2026-10-03c, owner request; **BUILT IN A PATCH 2026-10-05d — `l32-focus-stage.patch`; not run**)

**Owner's request, in substance:** "full focus mode rework". **Assumption recorded, not confirmed:** this means the **Focus layout** (the Classic ↔ Focus switch, `btn-layout-switch`, `applyLayout()` in `app.js`, `body.layout--focus`, the persisted `ui_mode`); no other "focus mode" was found in the source.

**What exists today (read, not run):** Focus is "chat first, the rest one click away" — the Ask panel is `position: static` and inline, the grid panels are hidden and Menu is the way to reach them; the **D.1** subagent live pane docks beside Ask only in Focus at ≥1000px; and several open or fixed items depend on it: **I-B12** (Commands panel hidden in Focus; mitigated by `/run`), **I-B20** (panel stacking over Ask), the onboarding wizard's layout choice, and the Focus-layout CSS comments in `index.html`.

**Not decided (scope unstated):** what is wrong with Focus today, and whether the rework is visual, structural (which panels belong in it) or behavioural. **Interacts with L.34:** if the commands section is removed, I-B12 stops being a Focus problem.

**Built 2026-10-05d — `l32-focus-stage.patch` (against `jarvis-main_84_.zip`; 3 files, +173/−1; not run on the owner's machine).** Owner: "i want you to rework everything by focused i mean make a whole new idea for the focused look etc etc", then "document your changes". The assumption above was kept, **not confirmed**: "Focus mode" is still read as the Focus *layout*, and the owner never said what was wrong with it. The new design is called **"Stage"**.

**The idea.** The old Focus was the Classic Ask panel stretched to full size (boxed panel, three permanent columns). Stage treats the conversation as a page: no panel chrome, one centred reading column, and everything that used to be a permanent column becomes a drawer.
- **Top bar:** frameless strip; the clock and the "Command Interface" subtitle are hidden in Focus; the Skin button and the capacity switch stay but sit at 50% until hovered or focused.
- **Ask panel:** border, background, shadow and corner marks removed; a soft accent glow at the top of the screen; a one-line header (brand, title, **Chats**, **Activity**, then provider / thinking / Clear / Menu at 50% until hover or focus).
- **Thread:** a single centred column, 860 px wide. Your messages are rounded pills tinted with the accent; Jarvis's replies are unboxed text with the accent hairline on the left (media bubbles keep their box). The empty state is a large centred greeting.
- **Composer:** a floating rounded pill (the `.ask-input-row` itself, so the `/` palette still anchors to it) that glows on focus.
- **Drawers:** the **Chats** list slides in from the left and the live **Prompt** column from the right (labelled **Activity** on the button). One drawer at a time; a scrim click, Escape, or choosing a conversation closes it. The **Activity** button pulses while the prompt's state says `live` (a `MutationObserver` on `#ask-prompt-state`); the drawer never opens by itself.
- **D.1 dock:** when `#subagents-overlay` is docked, visible and not collapsed, the stage gets right padding (`:has()`, no JS) and the Activity drawer opens beside the dock instead of under it.

**What changed in the files.** `index.html`: a `#focus-scrim` and a `.focus-only` nav group (`#btn-focus-chats`, `#btn-focus-activity`) inside the Ask panel head. `style.css`: one block after `.panel-menu--focus-only`, scoped to `body.layout--focus` except the generic `.focus-only` (hidden outside Focus), `.focus-scrim`, `.btn--focus-nav.is-live` and the `focus-live` keyframes; it also honours `prefers-reduced-motion` and has a ≤ 780 px tier. `app.js`: `applyLayout()` removes any open drawer when leaving Focus; the Escape handler for the Ask panel no longer closes it in Focus; a new `initFocusStage()` wires the buttons, scrim, a capture-phase Escape that closes a drawer first, chat-pick-to-close and the Activity glow.

**Left as it was.** Classic; `applyLayout()`'s open/close of the Ask panel; the persisted `ui_mode` and `/api/ui-mode`; the setup wizard's `ui_mode` step; Menu's reparenting between its two triggers; `updateSubagentsDockMode()` and `SUBAGENTS_DOCK_MIN_WIDTH`; the server (no `server.js` change). **The Commands panel is still hidden in Focus**, so **I-B12 is unchanged**, and so is the L.43 finding that the Config button is unreachable in Focus.

**Effect on the related items.** **I-B12:** unchanged. **I-B20:** a behaviour change — in Focus, **Escape no longer closes the Ask panel** (it is the page, not something opened); general panel stacking over Ask was **not re-examined**. **D.1:** coexists via the `:has()` rule above (untested). **Onboarding layout choice:** untouched.

**Behaviour I decided (change any on request):** the 860 px column; one drawer at a time; Activity glows but never auto-opens; choosing a chat closes the drawer; Escape closes an open drawer before anything else; the clock and subtitle are hidden in Focus; the 50% dimming of the secondary controls; the button names "Chats" and "Activity"; Jarvis replies lose their box.

**Verified:** `node --check app.js` passes; `patch -p1 --dry-run` is clean on a fresh `_84_` extract of `web/public` (`git apply --check` was **not** run); the real `index.html` and `style.css` were rendered in headless Chromium from `file://` with hand-built message markup and `body.layout--focus` set by a script, and two screenshots (the stage, and the Chats drawer open) were looked at.

**Not verified:** the app with the server running; the `applyLayout()` / `toggleLayout()` path and every new JS handler (button clicks, the scrim, Escape, chat-pick-to-close, the Activity glow observer) — **none was executed**; the Activity drawer; the dock together with a drawer; widths ≤ 780 px; the setup wizard; real reply content (code blocks, JSON trees, media, the quote popup, where the `/` palette lands over the new composer). **No test suite was run and no test was added** (no existing test references `layout--focus`, by grep); no Test Checklist entry; build number not bumped; `REPO_MAP.md` and `AGENTS.md` not amended. The CSS uses `color-mix()` and `:has()` (current browsers); an older browser ignores those rules (tinted bubbles fall back to the plain look, the dock spacing to overlap). **Cosmetic, not fixed:** in the preview the mic button sits slightly lower than Send.

**Owner questions opened:** **Q-L32a** — is "Focus mode" the layout (so this patch is the right target)? **Q-L32b** — keep the clock and subtitle hidden in Focus? **Q-L32c** — should Activity open by itself when Jarvis starts running something, instead of only glowing?

### L.33 Feature — custom tools rework, again (NEW, 2026-10-03c, owner request; **✅ BUILT IN A PATCH 2026-10-05f — `l33-code-editor.patch` against `jarvis-main_84_.zip`; not run on the owner's machine**)

**Owner's request, in substance:** "custom tools rework too", later narrowed to three things: **syntax highlighting**, **Jarvis inline suggestions "just like VS Code"**, and **an overall much better UI** ("and etc etc"). That settles the scope question this entry used to carry: it is the **editor inside the Tool Manager (L.25)** — not the file format, the loader, or the tool-owned extras.

**What was built (all in `web/public` unless noted):**
- `code-editor.js` + `code-editor.css` (new): a textarea with a painted layer behind it, so caret, selection, IME, undo and scrolling stay native. Own Python tokenizer (strings incl. triple-quoted and f-strings, comments, numbers, keywords, builtins, `def`/`class` names, decorators, calls, CONSTANTS, `self`). Colours are mixes of the existing theme tokens, so every skin applies.
- VS Code-style editing: smart Enter (indent after `:` or an open bracket, dedent after `return`/`pass`/…), Tab / Shift+Tab, soft-tab Backspace, auto-closing brackets and quotes with type-over, Ctrl+/ comment toggle, Alt+↑/↓ move line, Shift+Alt+↑/↓ copy line, bracket-pair highlight, current-line band, error-line band and gutter marker, line/column status bar. Edits go through `execCommand`, so **Ctrl+Z undoes them** (checked in a browser).
- Completion popup (Ctrl+Space, or after two characters): Jarvis snippets (`jtool`, `jschema`, `jparam`, `jchecklist`, `jerr`, `try`, …), Python keywords and builtins, words from the file.
- **Inline suggestions:** after a 1 s pause at the end of a line (a blank line counts), a dimmed suggestion appears after the caret; **Tab** accepts, **Ctrl+→** takes one word, **Esc** dismisses, **Alt+\** asks right now; typing the suggested letters keeps the rest on screen. Path: editor → `POST /api/ctools/:name/suggest` (`web/server.js`) → `jarvis ctools-suggest` (`cli.py`, source on stdin) → `custom_tools_suggest.py` → one provider call. Provider choice: first enabled, keyed provider flagged `"completion": true` in `ai_config.json`, else one flagged `"summarizer"`, else the first eligible one. Limits: ~200 output tokens, 15 s, ≤ 12 lines, **40 suggestions per editing session** (then it pauses and says so), results cached per spot.
- Tool Manager (`tool-manager.js` / `.css`): Save / Validate / Back moved to the top bar (they used to sit under the code); the side panel gained **Outline** (click to jump), **Insert** snippets, the **suggestions switch** (remembered in the manager's prefs) and **keyboard shortcuts**; a failed check now offers **Go to line N**. If `code-editor.js` fails to load, the manager falls back to a plain text box and says so.
- `ctools-suggest` added to `reserved_names.py` and `tests/test_reserved_names.py`; `REPO_MAP.md` and `AGENTS.md` (test commands) amended.

**Invariants kept:** the model still cannot create or change custom tools — a suggestion is text on screen until the owner accepts it, and **Save still runs `validate_source`**; nothing in `tool_safety.py`, confirmation prompts, `risk_review()` or the AI-review gating was touched; `MAX_TOOL_ROUNDS` untouched; the suggestion call is not an `ask()` (no tools, no conversation, no memory, no thinking).

**Verified (here, headless Chromium + Node + Python; no real provider key):** `tests/verify_code_editor.js` (109 helper checks); `tests/verify_l33_code_editor.py` (63 real-browser checks: colours, painted layer vs caret width, smart Enter / Tab / auto-close / comment / move line, undo, completions, ghost text show / accept / dismiss / type-along / word-accept, no request mid-line or when switched off, scroll sync, error marker, outline, Ctrl+S saves exactly the editor text); `tests/test_custom_tools_suggest.py` (42 backend checks with a fake provider). `verify_tool_manager.js` (100), `test_tool_manager_flags.py` (50) and `test_reserved_names.py` (12) still pass. Two screenshots were viewed. `git apply --check` and the tests were re-run on a fresh `_84_` extract. One bug was found and fixed by the browser run (every auto-close and smart Enter was applied twice).

**Not verified / limits:**
- **Never run against a real provider.** The prompt and the reply cleaning are tested with fakes only; how good the suggestions are depends on the model.
- **Each suggestion sends the code around the caret (≤ ~5 KB) to the AI provider**, and the switch is **on by default** (my choice; one click to turn off, remembered). **Q-L33a: default on or default off?**
- The tokenizer is a fast lexer, not a parser: odd corners (nested same-type quotes inside f-string braces, backslash line continuations) can mis-colour. A typical tool file (≈ 300 lines) re-highlights in about 9 ms per keystroke; 3,000 lines about 60 ms; 15,000 lines about 165 ms.
- Not tested on a phone or in Firefox / Safari. `execCommand` is deprecated but keeps native undo working; if it fails the editor sets the text directly (correct result, no undo step).
- The real `server.js` route was syntax-checked only (Express not run); the Python run-full test suite was not run — only the related files.
- **Not tested together with the other pending `_84_` patches** (L.32 also edits `index.html`; L.30 edits `cli.py` and `REPO_MAP.md`; L.38 edits `cli.py`). Different hunks, but nobody has applied them in one tree. **Update 2026-10-05g:** this patch, the L.38 replay patch, the L.31 MCP patch and the L.36 Channels patch were applied together to `jarvis-main_85_.zip` — see Revision 2026-10-05g; L.30 and L.32 were not part of that tree. **That run found a gap in this patch:** `ctools-suggest` was added to `reserved_names.py` but not to `slash-commands-data.js`, so `test_slash_coverage.py` failed; fixed 2026-10-05g by adding it to the `ctools` verb's `covers`.
- **Update 2026-10-05s:** the Focus layout now has an **Agent side panel** for `dev_agent` / `code_agent` — see **L.47**. It adds a body class `focus-agent-open`, which `applyLayout` clears when leaving Focus, and it shares the right-hand side with the Activity drawer (opening Activity closes it).
- Not built: find/replace, multi-cursor, code folding, minimap, a diff against the saved file; no Test Checklist entry for the manager (unchanged gap); build number not bumped.
- **Correction to the earlier note:** `custom-tools.js` is **not** the old panel — it is the theme gallery for the Skin modal (its own header says so) and was left alone. Deleting it would break the Skin modal.
- Still open and untouched: **D.2.2** (custom tool/action UI tabs), **L.12** (tool-owned daemons, tabs and palette commands are not switched off with their tool), **L.18**.

**Status: ✅ BUILT IN A PATCH — not run on the owner's machine.**

### L.36 Feature — Channels menu rework (NEW, 2026-10-03d, owner request; **✅ BUILT IN A PATCH — `jarvis-channels-people-permissions.patch`; applied with the other pending patches to `jarvis-main_85_.zip` on 2026-10-05g; not run on the owner's machine**)

**Owner's request, in substance:** "channels menu rework". No further detail was given, so it is unclear whether "menu" means the **Channels menu item** in the top Menu dropdown or the **Channels panel** it opens (assumed the panel; unconfirmed).

**What exists today (read, not run):** the **Channels** panel (`channels-overlay`, `menu-item-channels`; code in `app.js` ~8505 onward) — a status line plus a list of per-platform allow-list "chips" (Discord and Instagram) that add and remove entries through `GET /api/channels` and `POST /api/channels/:platform/:set`. It deliberately shows permission posture only: **bot tokens, enabled flags and owner setup are not editable there** and still point at the Guides panel and `jarvis channels-set …`, because a token must never pass through the browser. Behind it: `channels_cli.py` (`channels-config/status/set/allow/deny/test/whoami/log/directory/people/follow/block`, `discord-daemon`, `instagram-serve`), `jarvis/channels/` (`permissions`, `people`, `directory`, `outbound`, `transcript`, `dedupe`, `discord_gateway`, `instagram_gateway`), and the open items that depend on it: **L.20–L.22** (DMs, person memory, per-person instructions), **L.23**, **L.28** (guest token cost) and **L.29** (`send_dm` has no confirmation channel from chat; Q-L29 open).

**Not decided (scope unstated):** what is wrong with the panel today, whether people/contacts and the transcript log belong in it, and whether the token-never-in-the-browser rule stays. That rule is an existing design decision recorded in the code, not something this entry changes.

**Status (as of 2026-10-03d): ❌ NOT STARTED — documented only. Superseded by the built block at the end of this entry (2026-10-05g).**

**Update 2026-10-03f:** **L.42** (ask prompts, thinking view and image sending for Discord/Instagram) would need per-platform switches; if the owner wants them in the Channels panel they belong to this rework. Not decided.

**Update 2026-10-03f (second/third round) — what the rework is meant to be (owner, in substance):** the Channels panel becomes **per-user instead of global**: laid out like the **Test Checklist** UI, but where the Test Checklist has tools, this has **people** — each with a profile picture, name, user id and so on — and it **shows registered users only**. Per-user settings replace the single global switches (the allow-list chips are the global thing today).
- **What the source shows today (read, not run):** `channels/people.py` already keeps one record per person, keyed by platform and user id, with `handle`, `name`, `first_seen`, `follow` status, notes and an owner flag (`touch`, `set_name`, `set_follow`, `all_people`); `channels/directory.py` maps handles to ids; `channels/permissions.py` holds the global allow-lists. **No avatar or profile-picture field exists anywhere in `channels/`** (a grep for avatar/pfp/picture found nothing), and neither gateway stores one. So the pictures are a **new data source**: Discord exposes an avatar for a user it has seen; Instagram's messaging API may or may not return one for a sender — **not examined**, so a placeholder avatar may be needed on Instagram. "Registered" is read as "has a record in `people.py`" (anyone who got past the gate); the owner did not define it.
- **First per-user settings already decided elsewhere:** the **inbound-images grant** (L.42, Q-L42g — owner by default, others only when the owner switches it on for that person; stored as an `image_allowlist` and shown per user, per the fourth-round decision under L.42), and, as candidates, the thinking trace (L.42.2 — currently per *thread* by owner answer, not per user) and the tools-on / tools-off flag that is today a global list. Any other setting is **not yet specified**.
- **Rules that carry over unchanged:** bot tokens never pass through the browser; guest data stays in `people.py`, never `memory.py` (`AGENTS.md`); the per-user switch must not create a path for a guest to approve a gated action (L.29, L.42.1).
- **Not decided:** which settings appear per user, how the panel is reached from the Test-Checklist-style layout (list of people, detail pane, filters), whether the allow-list chips survive as a fallback, and whether an unregistered sender can be pre-registered from the panel.

**Built 2026-10-05g — `jarvis-channels-people-permissions.patch` (code; the docs are this block, `REPO_MAP.md`, `AGENTS.md` and `README.md`).** The Channels panel is now **per person**, and the "Not decided" items above were settled in the patch as follows (my reading of the owner's description; the owner has not seen it run):
- **Panel (`web/public/channels-panel.js` + `channels.css`, new; the old chip UI left `app.js`, which only calls `JarvisChannels.open()`).** Laid out like the Test Checklist: **left** the people (avatar, name, handle, what each can do at a glance, search and filters); **middle** one person, with a **Profile** tab and a **Permissions** tab; **right** one card per platform (enabled, token *set or not*, owner, master tools switch) and, collapsed, the **old global allow-lists as a fallback** (so the chips survive). **Registered people only** — "registered" is read as "has a record in `people.json`", which nobody denied at the gate ever gets. Unregistered senders **cannot** be pre-registered from the panel. Names, handles, notes and tool descriptions go in as text, never markup.
- **Per-person switches** (each flips the same thing the CLI does): **dm**, **reply** and **tool** are the existing allow-lists (the call `channels-allow` already makes); **owner** moves the single `owner` string in `channels.json` (switching it on for someone moves it off whoever had it); **send_dm** is new (may Jarvis DM this person for the owner); **blocked** records the block *and* removes the person from all three lists (the older `channels-block` only recorded "stop asking me", which would have left a blocked person in `reply_allowlist`). A person covered by a `"*"` entry **cannot** be switched off individually — the switch refuses and says why (there is no deny-list in the gate).
- **Which tools — new.** A person who may use tools can be limited to a **custom list** (`inherit` = no per-person limit). It is an **allow-list, never a deny-list**, so a tool added later is not silently open to a limited person. Stored in new `~/.jarvis/channels/user_perms.json` (only non-default values). The machinery's own plumbing tools (`search_tools`, `get_tool_schema`, `search_commands`, `remember_sender`, `who_am_i_talking_to`) are added at run time and never stored, so the panel shows exactly what the owner ticked. Enforced in `channels/base._ask_jarvis` through the **same `JARVIS_ALLOWED_TOOLS` variable and lock as the existing tools-off case** — `tools.run_tool` is still the single enforcement point; it can only shrink what `may_use_tools` allows (tools off always wins; an empty custom list = no tools).
- **Fails closed.** `user_perms._load()` tells "no file" from "unreadable file"; an unreadable `user_perms.json` raises `PermsUnreadable`, and that one message is answered **with tools off** (and `send_dm` refuses), instead of reading as "no limits". The gateway log line now shows `tools=custom (N)` / `off (limits unreadable)` / `off (person's list is empty)`.
- **`send_dm`:** one extra refusal — "DMs to X are switched off" with a hint pointing at Menu > Channels > Permissions. It only ever adds a reason to say no; owner-only, known-contacts-only, confirm-gated, rate limit and the unattended refusal are unchanged. The Test Checklist entry for `send_dm` gained the matching test and note.
- **Profile pictures (answers the L.36 "no avatar anywhere" finding).** `people.json` records gain an `avatar` URL. **Discord** supplies one on every event (`discord_gateway._avatar_url`, never raises); **Instagram's webhook does not carry one**, so Instagram people show an initials placeholder (coloured by a stable hue) and a later message with no picture never wipes a stored one. A stored URL must be **https on an allow-listed image CDN** (`discordapp.com/.net`, `discord.com`, `cdninstagram.com`, `fbcdn.net`), ≤ 300 characters, no quotes or angle brackets — it is the one stored value the owner's browser would load. `IncomingMessage` gained an `avatar` field that no stage of `decide()` reads.
- **CLI and routes.** `jarvis channels-users [platform]` (every registered person with every switch, JSON), `jarvis channels-user <platform> <id|@handle> <dm|reply|tool|owner|send_dm|blocked> <on|off>` (an `@handle` is resolved only against people who have actually messaged in — never a guess, never `directory.py`), `jarvis channels-user-tools <platform> <id> inherit | custom [tool …]`; all three added to `reserved_names.py` and the slash-command registry. `server.js`: `GET /api/channels/people`, `POST /api/channels/people/:platform/:id/flag`, `POST /api/channels/people/:platform/:id/tools` — argv arrays only, ids and tool names regex-validated, and they proxy the CLI so the panel and the terminal run one implementation (`channels/user_admin.py`). The original `GET /api/channels` and `POST /api/channels/:platform/:set` are unchanged.

**Invariants kept:** bot tokens never pass through the browser (the platform cards say only whether one is set and print the terminal command); guest details stay in `people.py`, never `memory.py`; no switch can create a path for a guest to approve a gated action; nothing in `tool_safety.py`, confirmation prompts, `risk_review()` or the AI-review gating was touched; `MAX_TOOL_ROUNDS` untouched. `AGENTS.md` now states the "can only take access away, fails closed" rule as an invariant.
