### L.37 🐞 Bug — on Groq every tool round came back 400 "property 'reasoning_content' is unsupported", burning all four keys (NEW, 2026-10-03e, owner-reported with log `7b5013b522d1fe40`; **FIXED IN A PATCH 2026-10-03e — `l37-groq-reasoning-echo.patch`, against `jarvis-main_74_`; not run against Groq**)

**What the log shows (57 rows, `openai/gpt-oss-120b`, `reasoning_effort: low`, `stream: true`):**
1. A one-round ask works ("hi" answered on key 1).
2. A tool-using ask ("spin up a subagent for testing") succeeds on round 1 — Groq returns reasoning plus a `search_tools` call — and the **second request of the same ask is rejected with HTTP 400** on `messages.N`: for `role:assistant`, property `reasoning_content` is unsupported. Both retries on that key carry it again (the second drops `reasoning_effort`, which was never the cause), so the ask moves to the next key.
3. On the next key the transcript is the flattened failover hand-over (earlier calls appear as `[called search_tools with {...}]`, reasoning gone), so round 1 there works — until that key makes its own tool call and hits the same 400. The first conversation turn ended on key 3 (answered by asking for a role and goal); the second ran out of keys.

**Cause (read from `ai_providers.py`, matches the log):** `_stream_openai_compatible_chat` builds the assistant message with a `reasoning_content` key so the trace can be shown and logged, and `call_openai_compatible` appended that message **whole** to the transcript for the next round. The corrective retry treated any 400 as a possible rejected thinking knob (`looks_like_thinking_rejected` → `strip_from_payload`), which removed `reasoning_effort` and left the real offender in place.

**Fix, in `l37-groq-reasoning-echo.patch` (2 files, +218/−3):**
- `_history_message()` appends a copy of the assistant message **without** `reasoning_content` / `reasoning`; the original dict is untouched, so the trace, usage and log still read it. **DeepSeek keeps it** (it wants reasoning handed back during a tool loop) — chosen by matching "deepseek" in the provider name, URL or model; other hosts are not examined.
- A second line of defence: when a 400 names `reasoning_content`, the retry strips it from the transcript on the **same key** (`_strip_reasoning_from_messages`) instead of misattributing it to the thinking knob.
- `tests/test_l37_reasoning_echo.py` — **15 checks**; four fail on the unpatched file. Related suites on the patched tree all pass: `test_l28_token_waste` 58, `test_l28b_followups` 49, `test_tool_disable` 98, `test_discovery_round_budget` 74, `test_l16_caps_and_budget` 40, `test_ai_providers_fixes` 24, `test_streaming_other_adapters` 60, `test_provider_failover_completed_work` 15, `test_streaming_ollama` 24, `test_provider_override` 10, `test_stream_markers` 23, `test_streaming_tty_and_options` 22.

**Not fixed, not understood:** in the second turn, keys 3 and 4 each returned **only reasoning, no content, no tool call, `finish_reason` null and no usage row**, reported as "empty response content". Earlier streamed tool calls in the same log were assembled correctly, so this is a different failure; whether the stream was cut or the host ended without a call is **unknown**, and nothing in the patch addresses it. It needs a fresh log taken **after** this fix, since the earlier cascade may have been feeding it.

**Not verified:** a live Groq request (the tests use a fake `_post_json`); other OpenAI-compatible hosts that might also reject the field (the fix removes it for every host except DeepSeek, which is the safe direction for the hosts seen so far); the web and terminal rendering of the trace after the change (the trace is still collected; only the copy sent back changed).

### L.38 Feature — save everything raw: conversation saving and console saving rework (NEW, 2026-10-03e, owner request; **BUILT IN A PATCH 2026-10-05b as a raw event log — `jarvis-l38-raw-event-log.patch`; replaces the first, side-archive version of 2026-10-04c; 2026-10-05e: the web UI now replays from it and the tool-driven extras are rebuilt from it — `jarvis-l38-replay-from-log.patch`**)

**Owner's request, in substance:** rework conversation saving (and console saving) so that, "instead of paraphrasing the things it saved," it saves **everything** — "the raw input and all."

**What exists today (read from `jarvis-main_74_`; nothing run):**
- `conversations.py` stores one record per exchange — the user's text, Jarvis's final reply, provider, and `extras` — capped at `MAX_STORED_EXCHANGES = 60` per conversation. Tool calls, their results, reasoning and the system prompt are **not** in it.
- What the model is given of older turns is **not raw**: the current conversation sends the last few exchanges truncated (`MAX_USER_CHARS` 500, `MAX_ASSISTANT_CHARS` 700) plus a recap, and the recap is written by a model (`history_summarizer.py`, cached in `history_summary_cache.json`) with a mechanical-truncation fallback; other conversations contribute only a title and a one-line gist.
- `console_store.py` is append-only per conversation but caps each line at `MAX_LINE_CHARS = 4000` with an "(N chars omitted)" marker, and records tool results "capped".
- `logs.py` already writes the **raw** request/response/tool traffic per conversation (it is the file in L.37) and is separate from both stores; clearing it must not clear the console store (E.3/E.4).

**Open question (Q-L38):** is the goal (a) a **complete stored record** — every request, tool call and result and reasoning, no per-line caps, no 60-exchange limit — or also (b) giving the **model** the raw history instead of the recap? (b) multiplies the tokens of every ask and interacts with L.24 and L.28; (a) does not. ~~Not answered.~~ **Answered 2026-10-05b** — see the owner's clarification below.

**Owner's clarification (2026-10-05b) — what "raw" means.** After the first build the owner wrote: *what I meant by raw data is that instead of the conversation FILE storing paraphrased console output and paraphrased conversations, it stores the actual raw data from the actual conversation to show it again later correctly — and that also adds support for future UI additions without having to change the system again.* So the request is about **what is stored and whether a view can be rebuilt from it**, not about overflow. **Q-L38 is answered:** the stored record, with replay and future UI features as the purpose. Giving the *model* raw history instead of the recap (b) was not asked for and is **not built**. The first build (2026-10-04c) misread this: it added a side file holding only what the existing stores drop (exchanges past 60, clipped and rotated console lines, tool results), so the conversation file and console store stayed the derived, paraphrased record. That version is **superseded** and not to be applied.

**What the stores keep today, as the owner's complaint is about (read from `jarvis-main_79_`):** the saved reply is the model's text *after* `_split_console_dump` has pulled lines out of it; the saved thinking is clipped by `reasoning.clip_trace`; screenshots, downloads and the like are saved as small `extras` (a filename; at most the first five downloads); console lines are cut at 4,000 characters and the file is trimmed at 2 MB; only the newest 60 exchanges are kept.

**Status: 🟡 BUILT IN A PATCH, 2026-10-05b (`jarvis-l38-raw-event-log.patch`, against `jarvis-main_79_.zip`; 8 files, +829/−2; build number NOT bumped — run `python build_tools/bump_build_version.py` from `jarvis-cli/` after applying).** The raw event log is written and can rebuild the conversation file's exchanges and the console store's lines; **the web UI still replays from the old stores**, deliberately (see Not done). (b) is not built. **Update 2026-10-05e: the web replay and the extras rebuild are now built — see the "Built 2026-10-05e" block below; (b) is still not built.**

**The model.** `jarvis/raw_archive.py` — one append-only JSON-Lines file per conversation, `~/.jarvis/events/<conv_id>.jsonl`, **no cap, no rotation, no clipping, no splitting, no summarising**. Each line has a format version `v`, a UTC `ts`, a `kind` and open-schema fields, so a later UI feature is a new *view over the same events* and the storage does not change again. Every other store is a view of it. Event kinds:
- `user` — exactly what was typed or sent, byte for byte.
- `model_reply` — the model's text **before** the console-dump split (and any cut note), the provider, the **full** thinking text (the saved extra is clipped), every interim narration item, the turn trace.
- `console` — every console line at **full length**, with `seq`, turn, surface, console kind, tool, provider, stream.
- `tool_run` — tool name, arguments, the **full pre-shaping result**, the confirmation record.
- `reply` — what the conversation file was handed: text, provider, `status` (`answered` / `interrupted`), `reason`, the saved `extras`; carries `user` only when no `user` event preceded it.
- `exchange_removed` — exactly the exchanges a redo took out.

**Derived views (the proof it is sufficient).** `rebuild_exchanges()` reproduces the conversation file's exchanges from the events alone — **every** exchange, past the 60-cap — including a redo, an interrupted turn, a stale turn reclaimed by the next `begin_exchange`, and a turn that never resolved (kept as `pending`). `rebuild_console()` returns every console line, including the ones the console store's 2 MB cap rotated out. `export_records()` is the whole stream with a `meta` line of per-kind counts.

**Hooks (small; each swallows errors — logging never breaks an ask).** `conversations.py`: a `_raw()` helper; `begin_exchange` → `user`; `complete_exchange`, `abandon_exchange`, `append_exchange` → `reply`; `drop_from_user` → `exchange_removed`; **Clear and delete remove the log**. `console_store.append()` → `console`, written before the clip; `console_store.read(..., full=False)` gained an **opt-in** `full=True` that restores a clipped line from the log by `seq`. `ai_client.py`: `tool_run` next to `runs.append(run_entry)`, and `model_reply` at the single success site. `conv_export.export_raw()`. `cli.py`: **`conv-export <id> --raw`** writes `jarvis-<title>-<stamp>-raw.jsonl` (a `meta` line, then every event; `-f` and the include flags are ignored) and **`console-read <id> --full`** restores clipped lines. Both are flags on existing commands, so `reserved_names.py` and the palette registry are untouched. `REPO_MAP.md` gets a module row and an `events/` state row.

**What did NOT change.** The conversation file and the console store keep their shape, caps (60 exchanges, 4,000-char clip, 2 MB trim) and bytes — `console-read` without `--full` is identical to before, which is why restoring is opt-in; the prompt truncation (`MAX_USER_CHARS` 500, `MAX_ASSISTANT_CHARS` 700) and the model-written recap, so **the model sees exactly what it saw**; `logs.py`. No `web/`, `server.js`, daemon or palette file is touched.

**Decisions taken without the owner (say if wrong).** Clear and delete **remove** the event log (no hidden copy survives the owner asking for a conversation to go away; clearing the Logs viewer or the Live Feed does not touch it). `JARVIS_RAW_ARCHIVE=0` stops writing (reading, export and delete keep working). The log is **unbounded**. Restoring clipped lines is **opt-in** (`--full`). The directory is `events/`, not `archive/`.

**Not done / limits.**
- *(Done 2026-10-05e — see the block below.)* **The web UI is not switched to replay from the log.** That is a `server.js` / `web/` change in the other agent's area; until it is made, the UI shows what it showed before. This is the step that delivers "show it again correctly" in the browser, and it is open.
- *(Done for the tool-driven extras 2026-10-05e — see the block below.)* **`extras` are still derived at write time** (`_extras_from_runs` and friends). Their raw material — the `tool_run` events — is in the log, but nothing yet rebuilds extras from it, so a new kind of card would still need a derivation written.
- **No backfill:** a conversation that existed before the patch has no events; its log starts at its next turn.
- Turns that end through the forced-ending, cutoff or token-budget paths write `reply` and `console` but no `model_reply` (the text is Jarvis's own, not the model's).
- `logs.py` still truncates at 20,000 chars per entry and is not merged in; the assembled provider request is not captured beyond what `logs.py` keeps; no size warning, prune command or doctor line; the stale top-level `jarvis-cli/cli.py` copy was not touched.

**Mistakes made and fixed on the way (recorded because they were mine).** The first design restored clipped console lines by default, which changed `console_store.read()` and broke the existing `test_console_store` contract — now opt-in. My first `console-read` flag edit put the `--full` branch between `after_last_clear = True` and its `i += 1`, so `--after-last-clear` never advanced the argument loop and the command hung (found by `test_console_store`'s 30 s timeout; there is now a regression test for `--after-last-clear --full`). The first restore loop was quadratic.

**Tests (run before the owner asked for testing to stop; none run since).** New `tests/test_l38_raw_archive.py` **59/59**: a **real `ask()`** through a fake HTTP provider and the real tool executor writes `user`, `console`, `tool_run`, `model_reply` and `reply`, stores the typed text byte-for-byte and the model text unsplit, and `rebuild_exchanges()` equals the live file; full thinking stored while the saved copy is clipped; rebuild equals the live file past the 60-cap, after a redo, an interrupt, a hard-killed turn and an unresolved turn; `read(full=True)` restores a clipped line and the default read is unchanged; `rebuild_console()` returns all 80 of 80 lines after the console cap rotated some out; Clear and delete remove the log; the off switch, a bad id, an unwritable directory and a torn last line never raise; a real `python -m jarvis` process for `conv-export --raw`, `console-read --full` and the flag-loop regression. `test_console_store.py` **57/57**. Full suite **101/103**: `test_build_info.py` (stale until the bump) and `test_key_health.py` (listed as failing on the pristine `_79_`; fixed in the tests by rev. 2026-10-04g). In one earlier parallel run `test_h15_daemon_editor.py` failed under load and passed alone, on both the patched and the pristine tree. The new file cannot run unpatched (the module does not exist there).

**Not verified.** `git apply --check` was run only against a pristine `_79_` extract — **not against `_80_`–`_82_` or the other pending patches** (the L.30 patch also edits `cli.py` and `REPO_MAP.md`, so textual conflicts there are possible); a live ask through a real provider and network (only the fake-HTTP path ran); the web server's `/api/console` replay; Windows (the test sets `HOME` and `USERPROFILE` and forces UTF-8 output but was not run there); disk growth over a long-lived conversation.

**Open owner questions** (as of 2026-10-05b; **(2) and (3) were built in 2026-10-05e**, see the block below). (1) Should Clear / delete remove the log (built: yes)? (2) Switch the web replay to derive from the event log (needs `server.js` / `web/` work — when the other agent is done)? (3) Rebuild the saved extras from `tool_run` events, so new cards need no new write-time code? (4) Backfill old conversations (impossible for what was never stored), a size warning or a prune command? (5) Lift `logs.py`'s 20,000-char cap too? (6) Do you ever want (b), raw history for the model?


**Built 2026-10-05e — the web UI replays from the log, and the tool-driven extras are rebuilt from it (code + docs; `jarvis-l38-replay-from-log.patch`, against `jarvis-main_84_.zip`; 10 files, +1,106/−127).** These were the two items the 2026-10-05b build left open. The owner asked for both and for a `.patch`, then for the docs.

*What changed.*
- **`jarvis/thread_extras.py` (new).** The derivation of the saved cards — `screenshot`, `download` (first five files), `presentFile`, `organizeJson`, `devAgent`, `confirm`, `declinedAction` — moved out of `ai_client.py` into one pure module. `ai_client._extras_from_runs` and `_declined_action_extra` are now thin wrappers over it, so **write time and rebuild time run the same code**. `TOOL_DERIVED_TYPES` names the extras that are a function of the tool runs alone; `rebuild_turn_extras(runs, stored)` re-derives those and keeps every other saved extra, in saved order, after them. With no logged runs it returns the saved extras untouched, so a log that begins mid-turn never costs a card.
- **`raw_archive.rebuild_exchanges(conv, derive_extras=False)`.** The default is exactly what it was. With `derive_extras=True` each exchange's tool-driven extras are re-derived from the `tool_run` events logged since its `user` event. An **interrupted** turn gets the cards for what it did before it stopped (the conversation file never had them).
- **`raw_archive.replay_record(conv)` → `(record, info)`.** The conversation file's record with `exchanges` replaced by the rebuilt ones — **every** exchange, past the 60-cap. `info.source` is `events` or `conversation-file`. **The log is only trusted if it agrees with the file** on the turns they share (same user and reply text, newest first); otherwise the file is returned untouched and `info.reason` says why. A log that begins after the conversation did keeps the older file exchanges in front (`from_file`). No log, or an unknown conversation, behaves as before.
- **`jarvis conv-show <id> --replay`** returns that record plus a `replay` field. Without the flag it is unchanged.
- **`console_store.read(..., full=True)`** now takes the **union** of the store and the log by `seq`: a clipped line gets its full text back (`restored`), a line the 2 MB cap rotated out comes back (`recovered`), and the store's own "earlier output trimmed" marker is dropped once the lines it apologises for are back. Before this it only restored clipped lines. Nothing is lost when there is no log, and the default read is byte-for-byte unchanged.
- **`raw_archive.read(kinds=...)`** skips lines that cannot contain a wanted kind before parsing them (a plain substring test on the `"kind": "<k>"` text `record()` writes; a line that merely contains that text is still parsed and then filtered as before). On a 9 MB test log a two-kind read took 9 ms against 25 ms for a full read — a small gain at that size; nothing larger was tried.
- **`web/server.js`.** `GET /api/conversations/:id` asks for `--replay` unless `?source=file` is given, with a 20 s timeout (was 10 s). `GET /api/console/:id` adds `--full` only for `full=1` / `full=true` (anything else is ignored, so nothing from the query string reaches argv). A `jarvis` build that predates `--replay` ignores the flag and returns the file, so the server degrades the same way.
- **`web/public/app.js`.** `Api.getConsole` sends `full=1` when asked, and the two **history loads** (the Ask trace in `loadAskTraceForConv`, the Live output in `loadConsoleHistoryForConv`) ask for it. The ~1 s subagent poll does not. The thread itself needed **no** change: `loadConversationIntoThread` and `seedThreadExtrasFromRecord` already render whatever `exchanges` and `extras` the endpoint returns.

*What did not change.* The conversation file, the console store, their caps (60 exchanges, 4,000-char clip, 2 MB trim), the prompt truncation and the model-written recap — **the model sees exactly what it saw**. `logs.py`. Every extra that is **not** a function of the tool runs — `thinking`, `interimText`, `trace`, `console`, `consoleRef`, and the F.11 offered-action extra — is still produced at write time and replayed from the saved copy; only the tool-driven set is re-derived. **A new card kind that comes from tool runs must be added to `thread_extras` and to `TOOL_DERIVED_TYPES`**, or a rebuild will drop the saved card of that kind.

*Decisions taken without the owner (say if wrong).* (1) **The log must agree with the file before it replaces anything**, so a stale or mismatched log can add history and cards but never swap in a different conversation; the cost is that any disagreement (for example a hand-edited file) silently falls back to the file. If the owner would rather the log always win, it is one condition in `replay_record`. (2) `?source=file` exists as an escape hatch. (3) The `declinedAction` extra's `ts` is the time the declined call ran (from the event timestamp, millisecond precision), not the moment of rebuild, so the "is this still fresh" check on a repeated message keeps its meaning; it differs from the originally saved value by milliseconds. (4) Full console history is requested only on history loads, never on the poll.

*Tests.* New `tests/test_l38b_replay_from_log.py` **67/67**: a **real `ask()`** (fake HTTP, real executor, one canned tool) whose rebuilt extras **equal** the saved ones; every card kind written through the write functions and rebuilt equal to what was saved (the declined action's `ts` aside, checked to be within 0.5 s); a test that **changes the derivation and shows old history follow it** (a card the file lost comes back from the logged run); `replay_record` past the 60-cap, with a log that begins late, with a log that disagrees, with no log, with a pending turn, after a redo, and for an interrupted turn; `read(full=True)` recovering rotated-out and clipped lines and dropping the trim marker, with `since` / `kinds` / `surface` / `turn` / `limit` / `after_last_clear` still working, and a default read unchanged afterwards; real `python -m jarvis` processes for `conv-show` (with and without `--replay`, an unknown id) and `console-read --full`; and static checks of the web wiring. New `tests/verify_replay_from_log.js` **18/18**: the **real** route handlers sliced out of `server.js` and run against stubs (argv, the `?source=file` and `full` rules, the 400 / 404 / 500 mapping, the invalid-id guard, the query-string injection case), and the real `Api.getConsole` and `loadAskTraceForConv` sliced out of `app.js`. Re-run and passing: `test_l38_raw_archive` 59, `test_console_store` 57, `test_conversation_persistence` 34, `test_k28_token_burn` 18, `verify_ask_trace_replay` 13, `verify_ask_stream_render` 72, `verify_slash_route` 16. **Full Python suite on a fresh `_84_` + the patch: 110 of 111 files**; the one failure is `test_build_info.py`, which **also fails on the untouched `_84_`** (stale `SOURCE_HASH`), so it is the owed build bump and not this patch. `git apply --check` and `patch -p1` are clean on a fresh `_84_` extract. The build number is not bumped.

*Mistakes of mine, fixed.* My first test compared the whole extras list for equality and failed on the declined action's timestamp, which is what led to decision (3) and a test that states the tolerance. A first benchmark wrote 4,000 console lines through the console store, which trims on every append, and ran past the tool time limit; it was redone against the event log directly.

*Not verified.* The real `server.js` was never started (Express is not installed in the sandbox) — only its two route handlers were run against stubs. **Nothing was run in a browser**, so the replay of a long conversation, the full Ask trace and the Live output were not seen on screen. No live provider; no Windows. Replay time on a very large log (hundreds of MB) was not measured. **`app.js`, `cli.py`, `ai_client.py` and `REPO_MAP.md` are also edited by other pending patches** — the L.32 Focus patch touches `app.js`, the L.30 patch `cli.py` and `REPO_MAP.md` — in different regions, but the patches were **not tested together**.

*Not done.* No backfill: a conversation that predates the event log still replays from its file. Turns that end through the forced-ending, cutoff or token-budget paths still have no `model_reply`. `logs.py`'s 20,000-char cap and the assembled provider request are still not merged in. No size warning, prune command or doctor line for the log. No Test Checklist entry and no `AGENTS.md` change (its invariants are untouched; the "add a card kind to `thread_extras`" rule above is **not** written there — say if it should be). `REPO_MAP.md` got a `thread_extras.py` row and a `replay_record` note in the patch, but no rows for the two new test files.

*Open owner questions.* (1) Should a disagreement between the log and the file fall back to the file (built) or let the log win? (2) Should the F.11 offered-action extra and the other non-tool extras also be rebuilt (they are not functions of the tool runs alone)? (3) Should `AGENTS.md` carry the `thread_extras` rule? (4) Size warning / prune for the log, and lifting `logs.py`'s cap — unchanged from 2026-10-05b. (5) (b), raw history for the model — unchanged, not asked for.


### L.39 Observation — "thinking is always on with Groq" (NEW, 2026-10-03e, owner-reported; **documented only, not changed**)

The log shows `reasoning_effort: low` on every request and a trace even for "hi". `reasoning.py` sends **no** thinking knob when the level is `off`; whether the level was off in this session is unknown. **Unchecked and unverified:** my belief that `openai/gpt-oss-*` on Groq cannot be switched off at the API (only low/medium/high) — if true, "off" can only mean "send low and hide the trace", which is a design decision for the owner. **Q-L39:** what should "off" do for Groq?

Only Groq appears in the supplied log, so it neither confirms nor refutes this. The other adapters have streaming code (K.3.1) and passing tests (`test_streaming_other_adapters` 60, `test_streaming_ollama` 24, `test_streaming_tty_and_options` 22), but those tests use fake HTTP and K.3.1 was never run against a real provider. **Q-L40:** on a non-Groq provider, what does the web UI do — nothing streams, an error, or the whole answer arrives at the end?

### L.41 Removal — the commands section of the system prompt, and the other "junk" in it (NEW, 2026-10-03f, owner request; **✅ FOUND ALREADY BUILT in `jarvis-main_79_` — status corrected 2026-10-04e; see the note at the end of this section**)

**Owner's request, in substance:** "the system prompt has lots of junk that needs to be deleted", followed by the compact system prompt of one ask pasted in full, and then: "the whole commands section should be deleted." Only the commands section was named; "lots of junk" was not itemised.

**Reading, unconfirmed — and it bears on L.34.** L.34 recorded the identical sentence ("the whole commands section should be deleted") with no context, and its open question was whether that meant the Commands panel, the saved-commands feature, or both. This time the sentence came with the system prompt, which makes it likely that the owner means **at least the commands section of the prompt**. That is a reading of the message, not an answer: it says nothing about the panel (L.34 layer 1) or the feature behind it (layer 2), so **Q-L34a/b stay open** for those. Until the owner says otherwise, L.41 is the prompt-only slice and L.34 is everything else.

**Where each piece of the pasted prompt comes from** (read from `jarvis-main_75_`; nothing run):

| Text in the pasted prompt | Built by | Position |
|---|---|---|
| "You are J.A.R.V.I.S, a local AI butler…" | `_system_prompt_parts` (compact persona) | static prefix |
| "Tools are listed by name only…" | `_tools_blurb(compact=True)` | static prefix |
| "Skills available…" and the two skill lines | `skills.catalog_text()`; each description is cut at `DESC_MAX = 160` characters with "…" | static prefix |
| "COMMANDS: only some are listed above — …search_commands…" | first entry of `_TOOL_WORKFLOW_CLAUSES` (compact text), emitted by `_tool_workflow_notes` whenever `search_commands`, `run_command` or `run_chain` is offered | per-request tail |
| "Before telling the user you don't have a tool… try search_commands instead" | `pack_instructions_ctx` in `_build_messages` (`ai_client.py` ≈1336). **Two sentences about two things:** the first is about `search_tools`, the second is about saved commands | per-request tail |
| "Commands:" list and "…and 22 more not shown here…" | `_commands_context(compact=True)`, fed by `commands_config.load_commands_dict()` and capped by `profile["max_commands"]` | per-request tail, last |

**Same family, not in the pasted prompt:** the full-mode and ultra-mode variants of the COMMANDS clause; `freq_ctx` (`stats.frequent_commands_context`, only when a capacity mode has `include_freq`, i.e. the 400 % mode); and the router's per-group pack line for the commands group, "Prefer search_commands over guessing a saved command's exact name" (`tool_registry.py` ≈480), which is added when that group is offered.

**How much it is.** By my count of the pasted text, the commands-related text is about **764 of ~1,980 characters (≈39 %)**: the "Commands:" block 333, the COMMANDS clause 209, and the commands sentence of the discovery nudge 222. The skills block is another 506 (≈26 %). The tool schemas are sent separately and are not in that count.

**Two things in the paste that are not in the source.** The `\n` and `\"` escapes are JSON escaping from wherever the prompt was copied (a log); `_system_prompt_parts` joins parts with real newlines. And lines such as "open (app*): opens shit" and "_testAiCmd" are descriptions of the owner's own saved commands, not prompt text; they disappear with the block.

**What removing the prompt section would touch (read, not tried):**
- **Three edit sites:** the `_commands_context` call in `_build_messages` (and the `skip_commands_listing` logic that only exists to trim it); the COMMANDS entry in `_TOOL_WORKFLOW_CLAUSES`; the commands sentence in the `pack_instructions_ctx` nudge (plus, if wanted, the `tool_registry.py` pack line and `freq_ctx`).
- **The model stops knowing saved commands exist.** With no listing and no clause, "run my spotify command" works only if the router offers the commands group and the model calls `search_commands` unprompted. That is a real behaviour change unless L.34 layer 2 removes the feature anyway. Worth saying to the owner before building.
- **Cache invariant (`AGENTS.md`):** all three blocks are in the per-request tail, so removing them cannot disturb the cached static prefix. `tests/test_prompt_cache.py` guards that; not run.
- **Tests and knobs:** `tests/test_tool_disable.py` (≈ lines 264–265) calls `ai_client._commands_context(...)` and asserts that a switched-off command is absent from the block, so it needs rewriting if the function goes. `max_commands`, `include_freq`, `MAX_COMMANDS_LISTED`, `COMPACT_MAX_COMMANDS` and the legacy override keys (`compact_max_commands`, `ultra_max_commands`) become dead; no reference to them was found in `web/public`.
- **L.25 / `PROTECTED_TOOLS`:** `tool_disable.py` protects `search_commands` because "the system prompt tells the model to call" it (its own comment, and the entry text near its top). If the prompt stops saying so, that stated reason is gone; L.34 already notes the protected list and its test change with it.

**Other candidates for "junk" — listed so the owner can strike them, none decided:**
1. The **Skills block**: two skills are listed, the descriptions are truncated mid-sentence at 160 characters ("…", so the model reads half a sentence), and one of them (`jjs-movesets`, a Roblox-game kit author) is unrelated to anything else in the prompt. It sits in the cached prefix, so it costs little per ask but is always there.
2. The **first sentence of the discovery nudge** (about `search_tools`) — kept or dropped independently of the commands sentence.
3. The **tools blurb** — it carries the confirm-before-destructive rule, so deleting it is a safety decision, not a tidy-up.

**Owner questions:** ~~Q-L41a~~ answered (prompt section only), ~~Q-L41b~~ answered (nothing else), ~~Q-L41c~~ answered (`search_commands` stays offered) — see *Owner answers* below. ~~Q-L41d~~ answered: delete the COMMANDS clause (second round, below).

**Owner answers, 2026-10-03f (to Q-L41a–c):**
- **Q-L41a — answered: yes, the prompt section; the owner calls it "the frequent commands section" and says it should be removed.** Recorded in the owner's words. **Which code that is needs a sentence:** the pasted block headed `Commands:` (the first N saved commands in file order, `_commands_context`) is what the owner is looking at; the source also has a separate "frequently used commands" block (`stats.frequent_commands_context`, `freq_ctx`) that appears only in the 400 % mode and was **not** in the paste. The owner's label fits `freq_ctx` by name and the `Commands:` block by what was pasted. **Both are listed in the plan as in scope** (they are the same kind of text, and leaving one behind would defeat the request); the owner can narrow that. The panel (L.34 layer 1) and the saved-commands feature (layer 2) are **not** covered by this answer.
- **Q-L41b — answered: nothing else.** The skills block, the `search_tools` sentence and the tools blurb **stay**. The owner repeated that the target is the frequent-commands section.
- **Q-L41c — answered: yes, `search_commands` stays offered to the model.** So `PROTECTED_TOOLS` and its test are unaffected by L.41, and saved commands remain reachable by search.

The COMMANDS clause says "only some are listed above" and the full-mode variant says "the 'Saved commands' list above is only a partial preview"; the discovery nudge's second sentence points the model at `search_commands` for "a saved routine/command". With the list gone, "listed above" is false. Options: reword the clause to "call search_commands to find a saved command's exact name" (keeps the behaviour, drops the false claim), or delete it as part of the removal. **Not decided; my recommendation is to reword**, because Q-L41c keeps `search_commands` offered and the model still needs to be told to use it instead of guessing a name.
- **Effect of the answers on the edit list above:** it shrinks to the `_commands_context` call (and `skip_commands_listing`), `freq_ctx`, and — per Q-L41d — the wording of the COMMANDS clause. The discovery-nudge paragraph, the skills block, the tools blurb and the `tool_registry.py` pack line are not part of the request.

(2) After this, the prompt still names `search_commands` in exactly one place — the second sentence of the discovery nudge (`pack_instructions_ctx`), which the owner chose to keep (Q-L41b) — plus the router's per-group line in `tool_registry.py` when the commands group is offered. ### L.42 Feature — Discord and Instagram get ask-prompt, thinking-view and image-sending capabilities (NEW, 2026-10-03f, owner request; **documented only, nothing built**)

**Owner's request, in substance:** "also give instagram/discord ask prompt capabilities / seeing thinking capabilities / and image sending capabilities", with the instruction "what you need to do isn't to implement things, it's to document in the plan." Nothing was implemented.

**Reading, unconfirmed:** three things the web Ask panel already does and the two chat gateways do not. Each has an ambiguity, recorded under its own heading.

**What the three share (read from source).** Both gateways normalise a platform event into an `IncomingMessage` and call `channels/base.handle_message`, which calls `_ask_jarvis` → `ai_client.ask(text, commands=…, conversation_id=…, on_attempt=…, on_tool_call=…, sender_context=…)` and sends back **only `result.text`**, chunked to `max_reply_chars` (1900 on Discord, 900 on Instagram, per `channels/config.py`). `ask()` also accepts `on_confirm_request`, `on_trace`, `on_stream`, `on_interim_text`, `think_override` and `provider_override`; **chat passes none of them.** That one place is also where owner-versus-guest is known (`decision.may_use_tools`, `permissions.is_owner`), so every constraint below has one natural home. Asks are serialised behind `_ASK_LOCK`.

#### L.42.1 Ask-prompt capabilities

- **Two readings, owner to pick.** **(A) Prompts Jarvis puts to the sender — confirmation / approval.** Today a confirm-required tool is cancelled in chat because `on_confirm_request is None`; that is exactly **L.29 / Q-L29**, and this reading makes L.42.1 the route to answering it. **(B) The Ask panel's prompt-side controls** — the `/` palette verbs (Part I), a per-message think level (`think_override`, `--think`), a provider override, `/skillload`. In chat these arrive as plain text; whether a message starting with `/` should be interpreted at all was **not examined**. (Discord's native application slash-commands are a different mechanism and also not examined.)
- **Constraints (from L.29's security notes, which stand):** a generic confirm channel in chat would remove the only thing currently stopping guest-triggered `run_shell` / `code_agent` / `edit_file`, so approval must be accepted **only from the verified owner id**, never from whoever triggered the ask unless that person is the owner; a guest turn must stay unable to approve a shell, agent or file-edit tool; an out-of-band approve/deny needs a pending-approval store with a timeout; and a prompt DM to the owner on Instagram can fail once the 24-hour window is closed (L.20). Discord components (buttons) and Instagram quick replies / templates are possible approve/deny surfaces — named as options only, not looked at in the code.
- **Q-L42a:** reading A, B, or both? *(Answered 2026-10-03f: A — see the owner answers below. Q-L29's A/B/C is still open.)*

#### L.42.2 Seeing thinking

- **What exists.** `reasoning.py` requests thinking per provider. `ai_client.ask` collects it (`ai_providers.get_thinking_trace()`), saves it as a `thinking` extra on the conversation when `reasoning.save` is on (default true), and calls `on_trace(trace, thinking)`. The web UI shows the saved extra as a collapsible "Thinking (N rounds, level)" block (`app.js` ≈3970) and handles live `thinking` stream deltas (≈3229). **`AskResult` has no thinking field and chat passes no `on_trace` / `on_stream`**, so the gateway cannot see the trace today. Whether the chat conversation's saved extra can be read back by the gateway was **not checked**.
- **Constraints and risks.** (1) **Owner only.** A trace can quote the memory block, other people's records (`people.prompt_block`), tool results and the sender block; showing it to a guest could leak the owner's private context. Gate it like `send_dm` (`is_owner`). (2) **Transcript:** `transcript.log_outbound` would store whatever is sent, thinking included — decide whether it should. (3) **Fit:** Discord's 2000-character cap (spoiler tags `||…||`, a separate message, or the full trace as an attachment); Instagram DMs have no formatting and this code caps replies at 900. (4) **Cost:** the thinking tokens are already paid; extra sends cost messages, not tokens. (5) **Dependencies:** **L.39** (what "off" means on Groq), the unexplained reasoning-only responses under **L.37**, and **L.40** (streaming only proven on Groq) — watching it think *live* needs `on_stream` and edits to a sent message, and Discord rate-limits edits (not examined). (6) Show nothing when the level is off.
- **Q-L42b:** owner only, always on or a toggle (per platform, per chat, or a chat command)? The final trace after the reply, or live? Inline, spoiler or attachment? *(Partly answered 2026-10-03f: off by default, toggle on.)*

#### L.42.3 Image sending

- **What exists.** No image code in either gateway or in `channels/outbound.py`: Discord's `send(text)` (`discord_gateway.py` ≈262) and `send_dm` send text only; Instagram's `send_message` POSTs a text message to Graph `/{ig_user_id}/messages`; an inbound Instagram message with no text is dropped (`instagram_gateway.py` ≈238, "an image/sticker with no caption — nothing to answer"). Tools that produce images (`take_screenshot` → `~/.jarvis/screenshots/ss_*.png`, `present_file`, `look_at_screen`) announce them to the web UI with a `JARVIS_MEDIA\t<kind>\t<file>` line on stderr (`screenshot_tools._emit_media`, `present_tools`), which `server.js` reads. **In a gateway process nothing reads that line, so the image is made and nobody receives it.** The model gets only an ok/path back by design; vision is a side call (`vision_call.py`).
- **Platform facts — from a web search on 2026-10-03, not tried against a live account.** Instagram DMs accept `image` attachments (png or jpeg, 8 MB) given either as a **URL** or as an **attachment ID** from the Attachment Upload API (whose docs describe uploading from a URL or from a server-side file), up to ten per message; the 24-hour window still applies (L.20). Discord bots can attach files; the **free upload limit is reported as 10 MB by some pages and 20 MB by others — only third-party pages were found, nothing authoritative** — so check Discord's own documentation. A multi-monitor PNG screenshot can exceed either, so downscaling or converting to JPEG is likely needed (not measured).
- **Security — the load-bearing part.** Sending a file from the PC to a chat is exfiltration if the wrong person can trigger it: a screenshot shows the owner's desktop and `present_file` takes an arbitrary path. So: owner-only (or confirm per send); an allow-list of what can be sent (the screenshots folder and files the model itself produced), never arbitrary paths; guests never offered `take_screenshot` / `present_file`; a rate limit and a transcript record, as `send_dm` has; and the recipient is the asking thread only, never a named third party. Today the missing confirm channel blocks all this by accident (L.29) — **fixing L.42.1 must not unblock it for guests.**
- **Mechanism options, none chosen:** (a) a new owner-only tool that sends to the current thread; (b) extend `AskResult` with a media list that `handle_message` attaches; (c) consume the `JARVIS_MEDIA` lines in-process. Whichever is picked should keep the `JARVIS_ALLOWED_TOOLS` model rather than add a second gate.
- **Receiving images** (a user sending Jarvis a screenshot) — dropped on Instagram, ignored on Discord. *(Was "adjacent, not requested"; the owner then asked for it — see the owner answers below.)* **Q-L42c:** is "image sending" outbound only, or inbound too? *(Answered: inbound too.)* **Q-L42d:** screenshots only, or any file `present_file` can present? *(Answered: screenshots and files, if possible.)*

#### L.42 — owner answers, 2026-10-03f (to Q-L42a–d)
- **Q-L42a — answered: confirmation prompts, not `/` commands.** L.42.1 is therefore reading **A**: Jarvis puts an approve/deny prompt to the sender. Palette verbs in chat (reading B) are out of scope. **This does not yet answer Q-L29's A/B/C** (owner-sender-is-the-confirmation, out-of-band approve/deny, or PC-only): *how* the prompt works is still open. The L.29 security notes bind it unchanged — the approver must be the verified owner id, and a guest turn must not be able to approve `run_shell`, `code_agent` or `edit_file`.
- **Q-L42b — partly answered: thinking is always off, and can be toggled on.** Recorded as the default (**off in chat**) plus a switch. **Still open:** where the switch lives (per platform, per chat, a chat command, the Channels panel — L.36), whether it is owner-only (my recommendation, unconfirmed: a trace can quote the memory block and other people's records), final trace after the reply or live, and the format (spoiler, separate message, attachment). "Always off" is also a different thing from L.39's "off" for Groq, where the model may think regardless; here it means *the gateway does not send it*.
- **Q-L42c — answered: yes, inbound images too.** L.42.3 now covers **receiving** images. What the source shows (read, not run): Discord's `on_message` builds an `IncomingMessage` from `message.content` only (no `attachments` are read); `IncomingMessage` has no media field; Instagram drops a message with no text. The main tool loop is text-only by design and `vision_call.describe_image(image_path, prompt)` is the existing one-image side call (tiered vision, L.16) that returns text. **Constraints to settle before building:** who may send an image (a guest's image costs the owner's vision-provider tokens and is an injection channel — text inside an image reaches the model as instructions), size and count caps, downloading from the platform CDN (Instagram media URLs are described as short-lived; Discord attachment URLs — not examined), where the file lands and when it is pruned, a prompt note that the description came from an image sent by *that sender*, and what happens when no vision provider is configured (`vision_enabled`). The conversation record would hold the description, not pixels, unless **L.38** says otherwise.
- **Q-L42d — answered: screenshots and files, "if possible".** Outbound scope is widened from screenshots to files `present_file` can present, **subject to the allow-list rule above** — "any file" is the exfiltration case, so "if possible" is read as: files Jarvis itself produced or the owner names, within size limits, owner-only, never a path a guest or a fetched page supplied. The owner can overrule that reading. Platform ceilings differ (Instagram: png/jpeg images and, per Meta's changelog, PDFs; other file types **not verified**; Discord: free limit reported inconsistently), so some files will not be sendable on some platform and the tool should say so rather than fail silently.
- **Open after the first round of answers:** Q-L42e, Q-L42f, Q-L42g — **answered in the second round, below.**

#### L.42 — owner answers, second round, 2026-10-03f
- **Q-L42e — thinking switch: a chat command, "for example `/thinking on` or something like that."** Recorded as: an owner-typed command in the chat thread turns the trace on or off; default off (first round). **Tension to note, not a contradiction:** the first round said *not* `/` commands for ask prompts (Q-L42a); this is one specific toggle command, so the gateway needs a small command parser that runs **before** the ask — a message that is a recognised toggle is handled and never sent to the model (no tokens, no transcript confusion). Unrecognised `/…` text still goes to the model unchanged. **Not decided:** the exact word (`/thinking` was given as an example), the scope of the setting (that thread, that platform, or everywhere — a persisted per-thread flag is my default suggestion, unconfirmed), whether it replies "thinking on", and how the trace is shown (spoiler, separate message, attachment) and final-versus-live — **those formatting questions from Q-L42b remain open.** Discord also has *native* application commands (`/thinking` typed into the slash menu) which are a different mechanism from a typed message; which one is meant was not said. Owner-only stays the assumption.
- **Q-L42f — approval mechanism: Discord native buttons; Instagram a Y/N system.**
  - **Discord:** the bot sends the exact action (tool, recipient, text, path) with Approve and Deny buttons (discord.py components). Rules that must hold: only the verified owner id can press (check the interaction's user, not the thread); one press resolves it and the buttons then disable; a timeout expires it as denied; a button press after a gateway restart must fail closed. Whether buttons survive a restart (persistent views) was **not examined**.
  - **Instagram:** the bot sends the exact action and asks for Y or N as a text reply. Rules: only the owner's thread and id; the reply must be matched to one pending request, so a stray "y" in ordinary conversation never approves anything (suggest: accept only while a request is pending, only within the timeout, and show a short code or require "Y"/"N" as the whole message); anything else cancels or is treated as a normal message, owner's choice; a timeout means denied; the 24-hour messaging window applies, so a prompt cannot be sent after it closes (L.20) — in that case the action is refused with a stated cause. Instagram has quick replies and templates, but the owner asked for plain Y/N.
  - **Shared:** a pending-approval store on disk (so a restart cannot leave an approvable ghost), the action shown to the owner **is the action that runs** (no re-generation between prompt and execution), every decision logged to the transcript, and the approval prompt is only ever raised for an ask the **owner** started. A guest-triggered ask still gets no confirm channel, so `run_shell`, `code_agent` and `edit_file` stay impossible from a guest turn (L.29 note 1) — recorded as my reading of "only owner", not stated by the owner. **Not decided:** the timeout length, and whether an owner ask that is gated *and* running unattended (a scheduled job) may ever prompt — `send_dm` refuses unattended runs today and that should not change.
- **Q-L42g — images: owner only, with per-person access the owner can grant.** Recorded as: inbound images are accepted from the owner by default; any other person is accepted only if the owner has switched images on for that person. The grant is per person, not global, so it belongs with the other per-person records (`channels/people.py`, capped, keyed by platform id — and, per `AGENTS.md`, a guest's details never go in `memory.py`) or `permissions.py`'s allow-lists; which one was **not decided**. Default for everyone else is **off**. The L.42.3 constraints still apply to a granted person (size and count caps, injection risk, token cost on the owner's vision providers, a prompt note saying the description came from an image by that sender). Whether the grant should also cover *outbound* images to that person was not asked; assumed **no** — outbound stays owner-only (L.42.3). A natural place to set the grant is the Channels panel (L.36) and/or `jarvis channels-set …`; not decided. Related: **L.22** (per-person instructions).
- **Still open after both rounds:** the thinking command's word, scope and the trace format (**Q-L42e′**); the approval timeout and restart behaviour (**Q-L42h**); where the per-person image grant is stored and set (**Q-L42i**); whether a grant covers outbound (assumed no). Nothing built.

#### L.42 — owner answers, third round, 2026-10-03f
- **Q-L42e′ (scope only) — per thread.** The thinking setting is remembered **per conversation thread** (a Discord channel/DM, an Instagram thread), not globally and not per platform. **Still open:** the command word (`/thinking on` was only an example) and the trace format (spoiler, separate message, attachment; final versus live). Note the interaction with the Channels rework (L.36): that panel is moving to **per-user** settings, whereas this one is per **thread**; a user's DM thread and their setting coincide, a group channel does not — flagged, not resolved.
- **Q-L42h — approval timeout: 60 seconds.** An unanswered Approve/Deny (Discord) or Y/N (Instagram) request counts as **denied** after 60 s. **Not answered:** what a gateway restart does to pending requests; the default reading stays **fail closed** (a pending request does not survive a restart and cannot be approved afterwards), recorded as my reading.
- **Q-L42i — the per-person image grant is set in both places: the Channels panel and the CLI.** *(Wording corrected in the fourth round: the CLI verb is `channels-allow … image …`, not `channels-set`; storage is an `image_allowlist`, not `people.py` — see below.)* Stored with the per-person records. The panel side is the per-user rework described under **L.36**; the CLI side extends `channels_cli.py`'s `channels-set`/`allow`/`deny` family. **Still open:** the storage file (`people.py` record versus `permissions.py`), and the exact CLI spelling.
- **Still open now:** the thinking command word and trace format; restart behaviour of pending approvals (assumed fail closed); the storage location and CLI spelling of the grant. Nothing built. *(All four settled in the fourth round, below.)*

#### L.42 — owner answers, fourth round, 2026-10-03f
- **Q-L42e′ — answered.** The command is **`/thinking`** (`on` / `off`, per thread). The trace is sent **as a spoiler, in a separate message**, after the reply. On **Discord** that is the `||…||` spoiler syntax; a trace longer than one message (2,000 characters) is split across several spoiler messages or sent as an attachment — **not decided, my suggestion is split, capped at a few messages with a "trace truncated" note**. **Instagram has no spoiler syntax, to my knowledge — not verified.** So on Instagram the trace goes as a separate message with a plain "Thinking:" label (no way to hide it); the owner may prefer to leave Instagram without the feature. Not asked; recorded as the fallback. Final-after-reply (not live), per the "separate message" wording — my reading.
- **Q-L42h restart question — answered: yes, a restart cancels every pending approval.** Fail closed, as assumed; the pending-approval store is cleared at gateway start, and a late Approve press or "Y" fails with a stated reason.
- **Q-L42i storage and CLI — owner: "idk, you decide the best approach." My decision, as the plan's recommendation (reversible, none of it built):**
  - **Store the image grant as a fourth allow-list, `image_allowlist`, in the channel permissions config — not in `people.py`.** Reasons: (1) it is a *permission*, and the closest existing analogue, `tool_allowlist`, already lives there; (2) it can be granted **before** the person has ever written to the bot, which a `people.py` record (created only after the gate) cannot; (3) the CLI, the `@handle`→id resolution and the panel's `POST /api/channels/:platform/:set` route already handle named sets, so the change is mostly "add a set"; (4) `people.py` stays what `AGENTS.md` says it is — a capped record of guest facts that is surfaced into that person's own conversation — and a permission flag does not belong in it. The owner is always allowed regardless of the list.
  - **CLI spelling — no new verb:** `jarvis channels-allow discord image @name` / `channels-deny … image …`, with `image` added to the short aliases next to `tool`. This corrects my earlier line: **`channels-set` writes a *global* config key (`channels-set <platform> <key> <value>`), so it is the wrong tool for a per-person grant**; the per-person pattern in `channels_cli.py` is `channels-allow/-deny/-follow/-block`. The set will also need declaring wherever `config.py` lists the allow-lists and validates their names — **not examined**.
  - **Panel (L.36):** the per-user view is built from `people.py` (identity, picture, who is registered) joined with the allow-lists (the settings); each per-user toggle reads and writes the same list the CLI does, so the two can never disagree. A future per-user setting that is *not* a permission would be a `people.py` field; that split is the rule.
  - **What this does not change:** default for everyone else is off; a granted person's image goes through the L.42.3 limits; the grant covers inbound only (outbound stays owner-only); thinking stays per thread.
- **Nothing is open for Q-L42e–i now.** What remains of L.42 is the part never asked: Discord button persistence, Instagram's 24-hour window handling in the approval prompt, the inbound-image limits (size, count, retention) and the exact files for outbound.

**Interactions:** **L.29 / Q-L29** (L.42.1 reading A answers it); **L.36** (Channels panel — any per-platform toggle for these would live there; tokens still never go through the browser); **L.28** (guest token cost); **L.20 / L.22** (DM window, per-person rules); **L.38** (raw saving would store thinking); **L.39 / L.40** (thinking and streaming). Not related to L.41.

**Draft acceptance criteria (extended 2026-10-03f):** *inbound images* — an image sent by an allowed sender is described and answered, a denied sender's image is ignored, an oversize or unsupported image gets a clear refusal, and no pixels are stored unless L.38 says so; *thinking* — default off, switch on, owner-only unless told otherwise; *ask prompts* — the owner can approve or deny a gated action from chat, a guest turn cannot approve anything, with a test that pins it; *thinking* — the owner sees it where chosen, a guest never does, with a test; *images* — the owner receives a screenshot in a real Discord and a real Instagram thread, a guest asking for the same is refused before the model sees the tool, nothing outside the allow-list can be sent, and the oversize case is handled.

**Status: ❌ NOT STARTED — documented only. Nothing was built or changed.**

That adds the possibility that people other than the owner use `/thinking`, which the "owner-only stays the assumption" lines above did not allow for. **Nothing here is changed or answered by it yet** — Q-L44h asks the owner to confirm.
