### L.43 Feature — a Settings button replaces the Skin button; Settings keeps the Skin section, gets many more sections, and an Advanced tab that edits any value in the project (NEW, 2026-10-05c, owner request; **documented only, nothing built**)

**Owner's request, in substance (2026-10-05c):** add to the docs a **Settings button that replaces the Skin button**; the Settings window **still has the Skin section**; it also has **lots of other features**; and an **Advanced tab that lets you change *any* value in the whole project** (the AI-configuration ones and so on). Instruction: **only document, do not implement.** The owner gave no list of the "other features" and no definition of "any value" — both are open (Q-L43a, Q-L43b); everything below that is not in this paragraph is my reading of the source or a proposal, and is labelled.

**What exists today (read from `jarvis-main_84_`, not run):**
- **The Skin button.** `#btn-skin` in the top bar (`index.html`, `topbar__titles`), wired by `qs("#btn-skin")` → `openSkinModal` in `app.js`; the `/skin` palette verb opens the same modal. The modal (`#skin-backdrop`, class `modal-backdrop`) has: persona presets (name + palette in one click), assistant name, "address me as", attitude; a theme gallery (the code it shares with `custom-tools.js`); corner rounding / glow / text size; accent swatches and a custom colour; a saturation slider (disabled for the "Classic (hardcoded)" preset); Reset Defaults / Cancel / Save. **Where each part is stored differs:** name, address-as and attitude are written **server-side** into `ai_config.json` (`persona.assistant_name` etc., by read-modify-write of the raw file); the theme, shape, accent and saturation are **per-browser** (`localStorage`, key `jarvis.skin.v1`).
- **A "Settings" modal already exists, under another name.** The **Config** button (`#btn-settings`, in the **Commands** panel header) and the `/config` verb open `#settings-backdrop`, whose title is literally **"Settings"**. Its tabs are **auto-discovered**: `GET /api/config/list` returns every `*.json` sitting **directly** in `~/.jarvis`; each tab is an editable JSON tree plus a Raw toggle, saved with `PUT /api/config/file/:name/raw`. `server.js`'s `KNOWN_CONFIGS` gives friendly labels and hints to `commands.json`, `ai_config.json`, `playnite.json`, `spotify.json`, `memory.json` and `tool_safety.json`, and a **validator only for `commands.json`, `ai_config.json` and `memory.json`**; every other file gets the generic "is it valid JSON" check. `resolveConfigFile` refuses anything that is not a plain `<name>.json` in that one directory, so **subdirectories (`channels/`, `daemons/`, `conversations/`) and the repo's own `web/data/*.json` are not reachable.** The new button's ids must not collide with the existing `btn-settings` / `settings-*` ids (see Q-L43e).
- **Other places that already hold "settings", scattered:** the top-bar capacity switch (`#btn-mode-switch`; `mode-set`), the Logs panel's own "Settings" pane (per-API-key capacity mode), the layout switch (`/layout`), Notifications levels (`notify-config`, L.30), the Tool Manager's switches (L.25), per-feature CLIs (`ai-config`, `playnite-config`, `spotify-config`, `memory-config`, `everything-config`, `voice-config`, `mcp-config`, `channels-config`, `clipboard-watch-config`, `tool-safety-set`).
- **In Focus layout the Config button is not reachable.** It lives inside `<main class="grid">`, and `body.layout--focus .grid { display: none }` (`style.css`) hides that whole grid; the top bar is not hidden by that rule. So the Skin button works in both layouts and the Config button only in Classic (Focus users have `/config`). A Settings button in the top bar would fix that as a side effect. This is from markup and CSS, **not seen in a browser**; it is the same family as **I-B12**.

**What "any value in the whole project" can mean — an inventory (counted by grep over the source, not exhaustive, not classified one by one):**
| Layer | Where it lives | Reachable from the web UI today? |
|---|---|---|
| JSON config files | top level of `~/.jarvis` (`ai_config.json`, `commands.json`, `tool_safety.json`, `policy.json`, `channels.json`, `spotify.json`, `playnite.json`, `everything.json`, `voice_config.json`, `mcp_config.json`, `memory.json`, `notify_config.json`, `disabled.json`, … — names the code references) | **Yes**, through the Config/Settings modal (generic tree/raw editor) |
| JSON in subdirectories and in the repo | `~/.jarvis/channels/*.json` (people, directory, dedupe), `web/data/*.json` (favorites, reboot) | **No** (by design of `resolveConfigFile`), except through each feature's own panel |
| Environment variables | **37** distinct `JARVIS_*` names across `jarvis-cli/`, `web/server.js` and `web/public/`. A mix: per-process plumbing Jarvis sets itself (`JARVIS_CONVERSATION_ID`, `JARVIS_SCHEDULED`, `JARVIS_CHANNEL_SENDER`, …) and real knobs (`JARVIS_RAW_ARCHIVE`, `JARVIS_TOKEN_BUDGET`, `JARVIS_PROVIDER_OVERRIDE`, `JARVIS_THINK_OVERRIDE`, `JARVIS_WEB_STREAM`, `JARVIS_TTY_STREAM`, `JARVIS_DIR`, …) | **No** |
| Constants in code | **≈258** module-level numeric constants in `jarvis-cli/jarvis/*.py` by a simple pattern (more, if strings and lists are counted) — e.g. `MAX_TOOL_ROUNDS = 5` in `ai_providers.py`, `DEFAULT_MIN_ROUND_INTERVAL = 3.0` in `key_health.py` | **No**, and **not a setting at all today**: changing one means editing source |
| Per-browser state | `localStorage` (`jarvis.skin.v1`, saved UI choices) | Partly, through the Skin modal and a few panels |
| Text, not values | the system prompt's wording, personas, skills | Out of scope unless the owner says otherwise |

**Findings that bear on the design (read, not run):**
1. **The Config modal can already show secrets in the browser.** It lists every top-level `*.json`, so `ai_config.json` (provider `api_keys`) and `channels.json` (`bot_token`, `access_token`, `app_secret`, `verify_token`, per `channels/config.py`) appear as plain editable text; a grep of `app.js` for masking/redaction around those fields found none. That **sits uneasily with the rule recorded under L.36** ("bot tokens never pass through the browser"), which describes the Channels *panel* only. An Advanced tab that reaches every value makes the question unavoidable (Q-L43d).
2. **Saves apply at once and are barely validated.** `ai_config.json` is re-read fresh on every ask ("nothing to restart after saving"), and only three files have a validator, so one typo in an Advanced edit breaks every ask until it is fixed by hand.
3. **A stale save can clobber a newer file.** Only `commands.json` is refreshed in place when it changes underneath an open modal (`syncCommandsIntoSettingsTab`); the other tabs have no such guard, and the CLI and other tabs write the same files.
4. **`AGENTS.md` invariants collide with "any value".** `MAX_TOOL_ROUNDS` "stays at 5. Never lower it", and the confirmation prompts, `tool_safety.py` and `risk_review()` are not to be touched "as a drive-by". Those rules are written for **agents changing code**, not for the owner changing a setting, but a literal "any value" screen would let the owner (and nothing else) change them, so the rule needs an explicit owner ruling rather than silence (Q-L43d). `tool_safety.json` is already editable in the Config modal today.
5. **The server has no per-request authentication** beyond binding to `127.0.0.1` (the header comment in `server.js`; `requireJarvis` only checks that the CLI is installed). Anyone who can reach the loopback port — a local browser tab, a local program — could call the file-write route. That is already true of the Config modal; an Advanced tab widens what it can reach, so it should not be built on the same route unchanged.

**Proposal (mine, not the owner's — change any of it):**
- **The button.** A **Settings** button in the **top bar** takes the Skin button's place (visible in both layouts). It opens **one** modal (same `.modal-backdrop` class, so I-B20's z-index fix of 96 carries over and it sits above Ask, the menu panels and the debug-style panels). The Skin modal's content moves in as a **Skin section, unchanged in behaviour**: same controls, same split of server-side persona vs per-browser theme, same Save / Reset Defaults.
- **Layout.** A left rail of sections and a right pane, in the manner of the Test Checklist rather than the current row of file tabs, with a search box that filters sections and, in Advanced, individual values. Keyboard, focus trap, text-never-markup and offline/error/empty states as in the H.1 reworks. (The owner stated no quality bar for this item; H.1's is the precedent.)
- **Sections — candidates only, the owner named none (Q-L43b):** *Skin* (as above); *AI* (provider priority, providers and keys, prompt/capacity mode, thinking, streaming — today the "AI" tab of the Config modal, the capacity switch and the Logs per-key pane); *Layout* (Classic / Focus); *Notifications* (levels, per-kind switches, L.30); *Tools & safety* (confirm / AI-review flags, the Tool Manager's switches — subject to Q-L43d); *Integrations* (Playnite, Spotify, Everything, Voice, MCP; Channels settings stay in the Channels panel, L.36); *Memory & storage* (memory, the raw event log's on/off, L.38); *About / build info*.
- **Advanced tab.** The one place where "any value" lives. Three layers, so the literal request is met without turning the project into a code editor: **(1)** every JSON file the current Config modal reaches, generalised (and extended, by an explicit allow-list, to the subdirectory files and `web/data`), as a searchable key/value list with a "changed from default" filter, a per-value reset, and the existing tree / Raw views; **(2)** an **override store** for environment variables and code constants — a small registry the code reads through one helper (`tunable("MAX_TOOL_ROUNDS", default)`), so a value can be changed without editing source and the default is always known; the ≈258 constants are **not** all exposed at once, someone has to decide which are tunables; **(3)** read-only display of per-process plumbing (`JARVIS_CONVERSATION_ID`, …) that must not be edited.
- **Guardrails the tab needs (each is a recorded requirement, not a nice-to-have):** per-file **schema validation** (today three of the files listed above); **atomic writes** (`atomic_io.py` exists) with a **timestamped backup and one-click undo**; a **diff before save**; a **version/mtime check** so a stale save is refused rather than overwriting; **secrets masked by default** with an explicit reveal; each value tagged **applies immediately / next ask / needs a restart of X**; **owner-only and UI-only** — no model tool and no chat path can reach it (same reasoning as there being no `daemon_add`).
- **Palette and docs when built.** `/skin` and `/config` stay as shortcuts that open Settings on the Skin section and on Advanced; `slash-commands-data.js` (the `config` and `skin` entries — their `covers`/summary text changes), `tests/verify_slash_palette.js`, `test_slash_coverage.py`, `DOCUMENTATION/COMMAND_PALETTE_TESTING.md`, `REPO_MAP.md` §6 and, if the owner rules on Q-L43d, `AGENTS.md`'s invariants. A new modal is not a `menu-item-*`, so the Menu-panel rule does not apply; the **verb** rules do.

**Not decided (owner questions):**
- **Q-L43a — what does "any value" cover?** (1) every value in the JSON config files plus environment variables; (2) that **plus** a registry that exposes chosen code constants; (3) literally any value in the source (a code editor). Recommended: **(2)** — (3) is a different and much riskier feature.
- **Q-L43b — which "other features" belong in Settings?** The candidate list above is mine. Say which to keep, drop, or add.
- **Q-L43c — "an advanced tabs":** one **Advanced** tab (read so), or a group of advanced tabs?
- **Q-L43d — safety and secrets.** May Advanced edit the safety-critical values (`tool_safety.json`, `policy.json`, allow-lists, `MAX_TOOL_ROUNDS`)? If yes, `AGENTS.md`'s invariant needs amending to say "the owner may change it from Advanced; no agent or model may". And may API keys / bot tokens be shown and edited in the browser (they already can be, by the Config modal), masked-with-reveal, or never?
- **Q-L43e — what happens to the existing Config button** (Commands panel header): removed (folded into Advanced), or kept? The owner said the Skin button is replaced; they did not say that about Config. And, because "Settings" is already the title of the Config modal, which name wins?
- **Q-L43f — `/skin` and `/config`:** keep as deep links to the new sections (proposed), or fold into one `/settings`?
- **Q-L43g — when does a change take effect,** and may Advanced edit per-process variables that need a restart of the web server, the Discord daemon or the scheduler (and who restarts them)?

**Interactions:** **L.30** (notification levels and the new panel), **L.31** (MCP rework — its configuration), **L.32** (Focus rework — the Config button is unreachable in Focus today; the top-bar Settings button fixes it), **L.25 / L.33** (Tool Manager switches), **L.34** (if the commands feature is deleted, the Commands tab and the Config button's home change), **L.36** (the tokens-never-in-the-browser rule, and per-user channel settings that stay in the Channels panel), **L.38** (`JARVIS_RAW_ARCHIVE`), **I-B12** (features that exist in one layout only), **I-B20** (modal stacking), and `AGENTS.md`'s invariants (Q-L43d).

**Draft acceptance criteria:** in **Classic and Focus** the top bar shows **Settings** and no Skin button; it opens one modal above Ask, the menu panels and the debug-style panels; the **Skin section** does everything the Skin modal does today, with the same storage split (persona server-side, theme per-browser) and a Save that does not lose either; **`/skin`** and **`/config`** still work and land on the right section; **Advanced** can find a value by name, change it, see a diff, save it atomically, undo it, and reset it to default, for every file and every registered tunable; an invalid value is **refused with a reason** and nothing is written; a stale save is refused; secrets are masked until revealed; no model tool, chat path or guest can reach the tab or its routes (with a test that pins it); and the new modal, the palette change and the invariants ruling are covered by tests and the docs listed above.

**Not verified:** every "what exists today" line was read from the source, not run; the 37 and ≈258 figures are grep counts (a simple pattern for the constants; the variable list was not split into knobs and plumbing); the Focus-layout claim comes from markup and CSS, not a browser.

**Status: ❌ NOT STARTED — documented only. Nothing was built or changed.**


### L.44 Feature — a per-person thinking switch (on / off / override) in the Channels panel (NEW, 2026-10-05k, owner request; **documented only, nothing built**)

**Owner's request, in substance:** "also add a thinking switch (on and off and an override option — meaning even if they use `/thinking level` they can't do anything)", with the instruction "document the change, don't implement." It was given right after the Channels feature ideas (L.36-P1…P16), so it is read as **one more per-person setting in the Channels panel (L.36)**. Nothing was implemented.

**Reading, unconfirmed.** For each person the owner can set (1) whether thinking is **on or off** for them, and (2) an **override**: when it is set, nothing that person types in chat (`/thinking …`, with or without a level) changes anything — the owner's setting wins. Without the override, the person's own `/thinking` command works as L.42 describes. The owner's own account is assumed to be unaffected (the owner's `/thinking` always works).

**What exists today (read from the `_88_` source; nothing run).**
- **The web UI already has a thinking command with a level:** `/think <level>` in `web/public/slash-commands-data.js`, summary "Set the thinking level, or show/hide its trace", values `off / low / medium / high / show / hide`. So in the web UI "thinking" is **two things in one verb** — an effort level and a visible trace. The owner's wording "`/thinking level`" most plausibly points at this.
- **Chat has none of it yet.** `ai_client.ask()` accepts `think_override` and `on_trace`, but the chat path (`channels/base._ask_jarvis`) passes neither (consistent with L.42's finding), and no `/thinking` handling exists in the gateways. L.42 (documented only) decided the chat command is **`/thinking` with `on` / `off`, per thread**, the trace sent as a **spoiler in a separate message** after the reply (Q-L42e′), and recorded **owner-only as an assumption** (Q-L42b, "a trace can quote the memory block and other people's records").

**The model I would build, if the owner agrees (my reading — owner may overrule):**

| Owner sets for a person | Person types `/thinking …` | Effective result |
|---|---|---|
| **Off**, no override | allowed — changes that thread's setting | follows the person's last command in that thread, else off |
| **On**, no override | allowed | follows the person's last command in that thread, else on |
| **Off + override** | does nothing | always off |
| **On + override** | does nothing | always on |

So *override is a lock on whichever value the owner chose*, not a third value. This is the reading that makes "on, off **and** an override" coherent; the alternative (a single three-position control where the third position means "locked off") is Q-L44b.

**Where it would live and what it must respect (all unbuilt).**
- **Panel (L.36):** a **Thinking** row in the person's Permissions tab: an on/off switch plus an **Override** switch with a one-line explanation ("their own /thinking is ignored"). Written through the same `channels-user*` CLI path and `/api/channels/people/...` routes so the panel and the terminal run one implementation (`channels/user_admin.py`).
- **Storage:** by L.42's own rule (Q-L42i) a **permission** belongs with the other per-person permissions, not in `people.py`; the person's own per-thread toggle is a separate, non-permission, per-thread flag (L.42, Q-L42e′). Which file holds the owner's value and lock (the existing `user_perms.json` or the channel config) is **not decided** (Q-L44g).
- **Invariants:** **fails closed** — an unreadable store means **off and locked**, never on; the gateway enforces the lock **before** the ask (the `/thinking` parser from L.42 runs ahead of the model and a locked person's command is handled there, never sent to the model); the owner's switch only ever *adds* a capability that is off by default, so — unlike the other L.36 switches — it is a **grant**, like the L.42 image grant, and needs the same care; tokens still never pass through the browser; guest details stay in `people.py`, never `memory.py`.
- **Not the same as L.39:** on Groq the model may think regardless of any setting (L.39/L.40), so this switch controls what the **gateway asks for and sends**, not whether a provider thinks internally. The panel text should not promise more than that.

**Interactions.** **L.42.2 / Q-L42b / Q-L42e′** (the thinking trace and its `/thinking` command; this entry turns "owner-only" from an assumption into an owner-set switch — **it does not by itself override Q-L42b**, see Q-L44h); **L.36** (the panel; **L.36-P4 presets** could carry a thinking value, **P3 test-as-this-person** could show the effective thinking state); **L.28 / L.24** (token cost — a higher thinking level for a guest is likely to cost more, not measured, and is one reason an owner would want the lock); **L.39 / L.40** (Groq thinking).

**Owner questions opened:**
- **Q-L44a — level, trace, or both?** In the web UI `/think` carries both a level (`off/low/medium/high`) and show/hide of the trace. Does this switch control the **level**, the **trace shown to the person**, or both? (My reading: both under one setting is confusing; the trace is the L.42 feature and the level is new for chat.)
- **Q-L44b — what is "override"?** A lock on the chosen on/off value (my reading, above), or a third value meaning "locked off"?
- **Q-L44c — what does a locked person see?** Silence ("can't do anything" read literally) or a short fixed notice such as "thinking is set by the owner"? (My suggestion: a notice, because a silent failure looks like a bug. Not asked.)
- **Q-L44d — default for a new person.** I recommend **off + override**, so nobody but the owner gets a trace until the owner decides. Q-L42b's default is "off with a toggle", which for a guest would let them turn it on themselves.
- **Q-L44e — owner exempt?** Assumed yes: the owner's own `/thinking` is never locked.
- **Q-L44f — group channels.** The setting is per **person** here but per **thread** in L.42 (flagged under Q-L42e′, never resolved): in a group channel the trace is visible to **everyone in the channel**. Whose setting applies to a turn (the person who triggered it, my assumption), and should a guest's "on" ever send a trace into a shared channel?
- **Q-L44g — storage** (above).
- **Q-L44h — guests seeing traces at all.** Q-L42b recommended owner-only because a trace can quote the memory block and other people's records. Turning "on" for a guest accepts that risk deliberately. Confirm that is intended, and whether the trace shown to a guest should be reduced (for example the final reasoning only, without tool-call arguments).

**Not checked / limits.** Only source reading on `_88_`; nothing run. The claim that higher levels cost more tokens is a general expectation, not measured here. How the web `/think` levels map onto each provider's setting (and which providers ignore them) was **not examined**. Discord native application commands versus a typed `/thinking` message is still undecided (Q-L42e).


### L.45 Feature — Tool Manager: editor tabs, an "Ask Jarvis" agent that writes the tool with you, and closable side panes (NEW, 2026-10-05m, owner request; **✅ BUILT IN A PATCH 2026-10-05m — `jarvis-tool-tabs-ask-agent.patch` against `jarvis-main_86_.zip`; not run against a real model or on the owner's machine**)

**Owner's request, in substance (four items).** (1) *Add an "ask agent" place in tool making — pick a good place — so Jarvis helps you make the tool and you can see him write the tokens / edit the things in real time.* (2) *When you are editing a tool, closing the menu should not make it GONE — it stays in a tab, and "make a new tool" opens a new tab, like any IDE.* (3) *Make it possible to close the Overview tab and the Tools tab so the UI is not cluttered.* (4) Generate the patch and update the docs. Read (3) as the Tool Manager's **left Tools list** and **right Overview pane**; there were no other "tabs" before this change.

**What was built.**
- **Editor tabs (the middle pane).** Every tool opened with Edit / Open in editor, or made with Create a tool, is a **tab** above the code, with a "tool details" tab first (the selected tool's safeguards, as before) and a **+** at the end. Create a tool opens a **new** tab each time (`untitled 1`, `untitled 2` …; the number is kept even after the file is named). Opening a file that is already open just focuses its tab. A dot marks unsaved changes, a pulsing dot marks "Jarvis is writing"; the x, middle-click and Delete close a tab; closing a tab with unsaved text (or one Jarvis is still writing into) asks first. Each tab keeps its own editor — caret, scroll and undo history survive switching. Picking a different tool in the list no longer throws the editor away (it used to ask "discard?"); it shows that tool's details and the editor waits in its tab.
- **Closing the Tool Manager keeps everything.** `close()` now only hides the panel — no "discard and close?" prompt — and reopening lands on the same tab. Tabs and unsaved text are also kept in this browser (`localStorage`, key `jarvis-tool-manager-tabs`, up to 12 tabs; clean saved files are re-read from disk instead of copied), so a **page reload** restores them; a file deleted in the meantime is dropped. If storage is blocked or too large, the page warns before unloading with unsaved tabs. Escape closes the panel, not a tab.
- **Ask Jarvis (the agent dock).** A dock **under the code of every editor tab** — beside the text it changes, never covering the Outline / Check / Insert pane on the right — with a chat log, a text box (Enter sends, Shift+Enter adds a line), **Send / Stop**, and **Undo AI edit**. The model gets the file **as it is right now** (including anything typed since the last turn), the request, and the last few turns of the chat (notes only, never old code). It answers with a short note and the **complete** new file in one ```python fence; that file **streams into the editor as it is produced** (the textarea is read-only while it types, the view follows the newest line, the tab pulses). A reply without a fence is a question or a refusal and leaves the editor untouched; a reply cut off before the closing fence is **never applied**; Stop keeps what has been written so far; Undo AI edit puts back the text from before the last edit (Ctrl+Z also works). A failed attempt restores the old text. Save and Validate are blocked while it is writing.
- **Plumbing.** `POST /api/ctools/:name/agent` (`web/server.js`) → `jarvis ctools-agent <name>` (`cli.py`) → new `jarvis/custom_tools_agent.py`. The web server answers with newline-delimited JSON (`{"type":"stream","k":"text"|"reset","d":…}` then one `{"type":"done",…}`); the CLI reuses the existing `StreamMarkerSink` / `JARVIS_STREAM` marker protocol (K.3.1.4) and ends with exactly one `JARVIS_AGENT_DONE {json}` line, which is authoritative (a provider that cannot stream still works — the editor just fills at once). The Stop button aborts the fetch; the route then kills the child process so tokens stop being paid for. Limits: 4,000 characters of request, 120,000 of file (`MAX_SOURCE_CHARS`), 8,000 output tokens, 150 s per attempt, 200 s hard stop. If a key fails mid-reply the next key starts over (a `reset` clears the half-typed text).
- **Provider choice differs from suggestions on purpose.** Ghost-text suggestions use the cheap `"completion"` / `"summarizer"` provider; writing a whole tool uses the first enabled, keyed provider that is **not** flagged `completion` or `summarizer`, and falls back to the suggestion provider only if that is all there is.
- **Closable side panes.** An **x** on the Tools and Overview pane headers, plus **Tools** / **Overview** toggle buttons in the panel header (dashed = hidden). The middle pane takes the freed width; the choice is remembered (`jarvis-tool-manager-ui`) and beats the narrow-viewport rules. Pressing `/` brings a hidden Tools list back to focus the search. The Ask Jarvis dock can also be collapsed (remembered).
- **Smaller changes.** `code-editor.js` gained `setReadOnly()` and `scrollToEnd()` (additive). `ctools-agent` is reserved (`reserved_names.py`) and covered by the slash registry (`slash-commands-data.js` — the same gap that `ctools-suggest` hit in rev. 2026-10-05g). The editor's "Back" button became "Close" (it closes the tab). The "Good to know" text no longer says the model can't write tool files — it now says Jarvis can draft into the editor but only your Save writes a file.

**Invariants kept.** The model still **cannot create, change, save or run a custom tool.** `custom_tools_agent.py` returns text only: it passes the model **no tools**, never calls `ctools-write`, and touches no file (a test pins that nothing is left on disk). What streams into the editor is an **unsaved buffer**; saving is still the owner's Save, which still runs `validate_source`. Everything shown is inserted with `textContent` (the existing "no innerHTML" check in `verify_tool_manager.js` still passes). **Worth knowing:** Validate and Save execute the file's top level (that is how `TOOL_SCHEMAS` is read), so **AI-written code runs the moment you press Validate**; the reply and the Overview note both say "read it first". There is no sandbox.

**Verified here.** `tests/test_custom_tools_agent.py` (new, 29): reply splitting (note + fence, no fence, open fence, fence without newline), prompt contents and clipping, exactly one DONE line, tokens reach stdout as markers, no tools offered, streaming on during the attempt and off afterwards, cut-off reply not applied, empty / oversized / no-provider refusals, key fall-through with a `reset`, provider choice, nothing written to disk, `ctools-agent` reserved. `tests/verify_tool_manager.js` 108 (8 new: the same splitter in JS, tab numbering). **`tests/verify_tool_manager_ui.py` (new, real headless Chromium, `/api/*` mocked, skips if Playwright is missing), 24 checks:** x and toggles hide / restore both panes and the middle pane widens; Create opens separate tabs; switching tabs keeps each tab's text; closing the panel shows no prompt and reopening keeps the tabs; an agent reply lands in the editor, shows its note and offers Undo, which restores the template; a question leaves the editor alone; an error is shown; the dock collapses; tabs survive a **page reload**; closing a dirty tab asks; no page errors. Two screenshots were looked at. `ctools-agent` run for real from the CLI with no provider reached the "couldn't connect" path and still printed one DONE line. Every changed JS file passes `node --check`, `cli.py` and the new module compile. The patch passes `patch --dry-run` on both a pristine `_86_` extract and `_86_` with the Focus / people patch applied (the two touch different files).

**Not verified — please test these.** **A real model** (fakes only): how well each provider follows the "whole file in one fence" instruction, and whether the output is any good, are unknown; a model that ignores the fence leaves the editor untouched and shows its text as the note. **Live streaming** was not seen: the browser test's mock delivers the stream in one piece, so the type-as-it-arrives path (animation-frame batching, read-only toggling, scroll-follow) is covered by code reading and the Python / JS splitters only; the real `web/server.js` route was syntax-checked and **never run** (Express is not installed here), including client-disconnect-kills-child and proxy buffering (the route sends `X-Accel-Buffering: no`). Firefox, Safari, a phone, Windows. **The full Python suite was not run** (owner's instruction); `test_slash_coverage` and `test_reserved_names` were not re-run after the `ctools-agent` additions. **Not applied on top of the `_87_` / `_88_` Channels patches** (`index.html` is edited by this patch and by `channels-add-person-panel.patch`, in different places; unchecked). No Test Checklist entry for the new agent route or tabs (the manager still has none). Build number not bumped.

**Decisions I took (owner may overrule).** (a) The agent lives **under the code, inside each tab**, not in the right pane (that stays for Check / Outline / Insert) and not a floating window. (b) **Whole-file replies only**, no diffs or partial edits — simplest protocol, always a loadable file, but long files cost more tokens per turn. (c) The chat is **not** saved: it lives with the tab for the session and is lost on reload (the tab text is kept; the chat is not). (d) Chat history sent to the model is notes only, last 6 turns, 600 characters each. (e) Tab persistence is **on by default** and local to this browser, not on the server. (f) A saved file's tab keeps its name locked, as before. (g) The model is told to avoid deleting / overwriting / sending data unless asked and to say so — a prompt, not an enforced rule.

**Open.** **Q-L45a** — should Jarvis be able to **Validate for you** and fix its own errors in a loop (it would execute AI-written code without you pressing the button — I did **not** build it, deliberately)? **Q-L45b** — which provider should the agent use (today: first non-helper keyed provider; a `"agent": true` flag like `"completion"` is the obvious knob)? **Q-L45c** — save the chat per tool across reloads? **Q-L45d** — partial edits / a diff view instead of whole-file replacement; "review before apply" instead of typing straight into the editor. **Q-L45e** — tabs for the *other* panels (Import review, Debug) — not asked, not done. Relates to **L.33** (the editor, suggestions), **L.25** (the manager), **L.12**, **D.2.2** (untouched).

**Update 2026-10-05p — Markdown in the Ask Jarvis dock, and the live-typing fix (`jarvis-markdown-and-live-editor.patch` against `jarvis-main_91_.zip`; code, not run).** Owner report: the editor "gets reloaded each time" Jarvis edits, so the edit can't be watched in real time. **Cause (read in code, not reproduced):** the streaming path *did* deliver tokens, but every animation frame the dock called `setValue()` on the editor, which is the "open a new file" reset — it snaps the view to line 1, moves the caret to 0, clears suggestions and repaints, and then `scrollToEnd()` dragged the view back down. Worse for an *edit* of an existing file: the model sends the whole new file, so the editor showed only what had arrived — a 300-line tool collapsed to a few lines and grew back. **Fix:** `code-editor.js` gets `stream(text, head)` (replace the text without the reset; mark the line being written; follow it only when it leaves the view) and the dock now shows the arrived lines **over** the old file with the old lines not yet reached still underneath, dimmed (`overwriteView()` in `tool-manager.js`). Applying the final file, Undo and a failed edit's restore also go through `stream()` now, so they no longer snap to line 1. A provider that **doesn't stream** (the DONE line carries the whole file) is now **typed in by lines over at most ~1.5 s** instead of swapping silently; Stop ends it. If the edit is interrupted (Stop, dropped connection) the editor keeps the new text written so far and drops the old text that was only showing underneath. **Markdown:** Jarvis's notes in the dock are rendered as Markdown through one shared renderer; the owner's own text and error messages stay plain text. The same renderer serves the Channels conversation view (see L.36 below).

**Shared renderer — `window.JarvisMarkdown.renderInto(el, text, {streaming, balance})` in `app.js`.** Same pipeline as the main chat bubble (marked → DOMPurify → KaTeX) so there is one renderer, with three differences because the text may have been steered by a stranger: **images are never loaded** (replaced by `[image: alt]` — an `<img>` to someone's server would tell them the owner opened the log), links open in a new tab with `rel="noopener noreferrer"` and only `http(s)` / `mailto` survive, and `streaming` closes an unfinished code fence so text still to come isn't swallowed into one code block. Styled by a new `.jv-md` block at the end of `style.css`. If `app.js` failed to load, both surfaces fall back to plain text, never raw HTML.

**Not changed:** the server route, the CLI side, the `JARVIS_STREAM` protocol and the provider choice — **this is entirely front-end**. The invariant stands: the model still cannot create, change, save or run a custom tool; the typed text is still an unsaved buffer. **Not verified (owner is testing):** everything — no browser, no live model, no real `server.js` run; only `node --check` on the five changed scripts and `patch --dry-run` on a pristine `_91_` (applied result identical to the working tree). **Known test risk:** `tests/verify_tool_manager_ui.py` mocks the agent reply as one `done` event with no streamed text, so with the new typed-in reveal the code now appears over ~1–1.5 s rather than instantly — a check that reads the editor straight after the reply may need a short wait. `verify_tool_manager.js` and `verify_channels_panel.js` pin "no innerHTML in this file"; the patch adds none to either (the one `innerHTML` is in `app.js`). **Decisions I took (owner may overrule):** (a) old text stays visible, dimmed, until overwritten (rather than blanking the editor); (b) the typed-in reveal for non-streaming providers; (c) Markdown only for Jarvis's words, never for what a person wrote; (d) no tests added (owner's instruction) — the helper `overwriteView` and the renderer have **no permanent test** yet, which `AGENTS.md` asks for once a change has regression risk. **Open:** whether the dimmed-old-text view is wanted or a plain blank-then-type is preferred; whether the Channels view should also render Markdown for *inbound* messages (left as plain text — they are strangers' words, and Discord already formatted them); the other L.45 questions (Q-L45a–e) are unchanged.

**Status: ✅ BUILT IN A PATCH — not run against a real model or on the owner's machine.**

**Correction 2026-10-05v (L.45 follow-up — see Revision 2026-10-05v).** Two statements above are no longer the whole story. (1) *"a reply cut off before the closing fence is **never applied**"* — still true, but a cut caused by the provider's **output limit** is now **continued** (up to 3 follow-up calls) before giving up, so a long tool usually completes instead of being discarded. (2) *"Whole-file replies only … long files cost more tokens per turn"* — that cost is exactly what produced the owner's repeated cut-off message; the prompt now also asks for compact files, and the provider's own `max_tokens` is honoured (see the revision). The "never applied" rule, the no-tools boundary and the owner-presses-Save rule are unchanged.

### L.46 Feature — Tool Manager: draft backups, switches for daemons / personas / UI elements, tool-shipped web files (`tool.js` / `tool.html` / `tool.css`), and new template examples (NEW, 2026-10-05n, owner request; **documented only, nothing built**)

**Owner's request, in substance (four items), with the instruction "add these in the docs, don't implement anything yet."** (1) *Unfinished tools should be backed up even if the user didn't save them.* (2) *Add entries in the Tool Manager for daemons, personas and UI elements, so they can be toggled off.* (3) *Tools can ship their own `tool.js`, `tool.html` and `tool.css` and choose how to present them — either a **button that opens that page**, or a **menu entry like Test Checklist** that opens the panel in a div. The files may sit in folders; the tool must **declare the path**.* (4) *Add examples to the templates, and **keep the old UI-element way** (do not remove it).* Nothing was implemented, no code or test was changed; source was read in the `_86_` tree only (not `_87_` / `_88_`).

**What exists today (read in source, nothing run).**
- **Backups.** The server keeps **one** `.bak` of the *previous saved* version, written by `custom_tools_store.write_tool` when a save overwrites a file. Text that was never saved reaches **no disk anywhere on the server.** L.45 keeps open tabs and their unsaved text in this browser's `localStorage` (`jarvis-tool-manager-tabs`, up to 12 tabs, size-capped; it is skipped silently if storage is blocked or too large), and the pre-AI text for "Undo AI edit" lives only in memory for the session. So today a cleared browser profile, another browser or another device, or a storage-quota failure loses unsaved work.
- **Switches.** `tool_disable.py` records only **tools and saved commands** in `~/.jarvis/disabled.json` (no model-facing writer — a test asserts it — and a `PROTECTED_TOOLS` list that cannot be switched off). "Off" there means *the model cannot see or use it*; the owner still can. Daemons, personas and UI elements have **no off switch**. This is the already-recorded gap: *"a switched-off tool does not remove the daemons, tabs or palette commands it owns (L.12)"* (Revisions 2026-10-03 and 2026-10-03b, "Not built").
- **Personas.** A tool file may export `PERSONAS` (validated by `persona_registry.py`, reaches the Skin modal). **Daemons.** `daemons.add()` / `daemon-add` exist, but **no tool can declare one** (L.12 — decided, not built). **UI elements, today = two different things:** (a) the **UI bridge** (`ui_bridge.py`: `ui.toast / bubble / dialog / confirm / choose / prompt`) called from a tool's Python — fire-and-forget over stderr, blocking prompts over stdin, **text only, no HTML**, with a default and timeout so unattended runs never hang; the `ui` template in `custom_tools_store.TEMPLATES` shows it; (b) a tool's `TEST_CHECKLIST` entries in Menu → Test Checklist.
- **Web files.** None. A custom tool is **one flat `.py` file** in `~/.jarvis/tools/` (`list_tools` globs `*.py`; the check / write / run / enable routes all take a single file name). **D.2.2** already records the requirement for tool-supplied tabs (`render: "inline" | "sandboxed"`, sandboxed recommended; a read-only-by-default message API with **declared** actions and `JarvisUI.confirm` for dangerous ones) and says the **wire format "still needs writing before implementation"**.
- **Templates.** `TEMPLATES` holds Python-source-only entries (`minimal`, `ui`, a `cleanup_temp` example, and others); a template is one string.

**L.46.1 — Draft backups (proposed design, nothing built).**
- **What.** Autosave every open editor tab's text **to the server** while it is unsaved — shortly after typing stops, when a tab is switched or closed, when the panel is closed, and on `visibilitychange` / `beforeunload` — so unfinished work survives a cleared browser, another browser or a crash. Applies to **new (never-saved) tabs and edited-but-unsaved tabs**, and should also snapshot the text **just before an Ask Jarvis edit** (today that backup is memory-only).
- **Where (proposal).** A hidden drafts area under `~/.jarvis/tools/` (for example `~/.jarvis/tools/.drafts/<tab-or-name>.py` plus a small index). `custom_tools_store.list_tools` globs `*.py` in the top folder, so a subfolder would **not** be listed or loaded as a tool — **to be confirmed for `tool_loader.py` before relying on it.** A draft must **never** be loaded, run, validated or counted as a tool.
- **Behaviour (proposal).** Reopening the Tool Manager (or a new browser) offers **"Restore N unsaved drafts"** as tabs; saving a file deletes its draft; closing a tab with **Discard** deletes it; an untitled draft keeps its `untitled N` number; keep the last few versions per draft rather than one (so a bad AI edit can be stepped back past); a visible "Drafts" note somewhere in the Overview pane so the owner knows backups exist. The localStorage copy stays as the fast path; the server copy is the durable one.
- **Needs deciding.** **Q-L46a** — retention (how many versions, how long) and a size cap. **Q-L46b** — **secrets:** a draft can hold pasted API keys or tokens and would now sit on disk, in the same folder as saved tools (saved tools already can); acceptable? **Q-L46c** — a new route and CLI verb (names TBD, e.g. `ctools-draft-save` / `-list` / `-delete`) means reserved names, slash-registry coverage and a Test Checklist entry (see AGENTS.md); **Q-L46d** — drafts per browser or one shared set for the owner (the app is single-owner, so shared is the simpler reading).
- **Invariant to keep.** Backups are written by the **owner's editor only**; the model gets no path to read or write them (same rule as `ctools-write`).

**L.46.2 — Switches for daemons, personas and UI elements (proposed design, nothing built).**
- **What.** New kinds of row in the Tool Manager (the list already has `tool`, `command` and `broken` kinds, with source chips and groups) — **Daemons**, **Personas**, **UI elements** — each with an **Available** switch like the existing one, a lock-with-reason for anything that cannot be switched off, and the dependents warning the panel already shows for scheduled jobs.
- **"Off" must be defined per kind — the L.25 meaning ("the model can't see it") does not fit.** *Proposed:* **daemon — off = it will not start and is shown as off (a running one is stopped after asking); persona — off = hidden from the Skin picker and ignored as an auto-applied preset (if it is the active persona, fall back to the previous or default one and say so); UI element — off = the button / menu entry / panel is not shown, and its files are not loaded.** In every case the owner can switch it back on, and **nothing the owner built by hand is deleted.**
- **Storage (proposal).** Extend `~/.jarvis/disabled.json` with new keys (for example `daemons`, `personas`, `ui`) rather than a new file, **keeping its rule that no model-facing writer exists** and that a stored name that no longer exists is forgotten (`forget_*`). Old files with only `tools` / `commands` keep working (additive).
- **Scope problem to settle first.** Most of this can only apply to things that **have an owner tool**: **tool-supplied daemons are not built (L.12)** and **tool-supplied tabs are not built (D.2.2)**; personas are the only one already supplied by tools. So a daemon or UI-element row would initially list **user-created daemons** (which have no owning tool) and **built-in UI** — or wait for L.12 / L.46.3. **Q-L46e** — does the owner mean *all* daemons / personas / UI, or only those a **tool** brought? **Q-L46f** — **what is a "UI element"** here: a tool's page / button / menu entry (L.46.3), a UI-bridge call, a `TEST_CHECKLIST` entry, a palette command, or built-in menu items? My reading is the first, plus palette commands and checklist entries a tool owns. **Q-L46g** — which ones are **protected** (cannot be switched off): the active persona, the Tool Manager's own menu entry?
- **This closes the long-standing gap** recorded after L.25 ("a switched-off tool does not remove the daemons, tabs or palette commands it owns"): switching a *tool* off should offer to switch off what it owns, with the list shown first.

**L.46.3 — Tools that ship their own `tool.js` / `tool.html` / `tool.css` (proposed design, nothing built).**
- **Layout.** A tool may live in a **folder** (for example `~/.jarvis/tools/my_tool/` holding `my_tool.py`, `tool.html`, `tool.js`, `tool.css`, plus images). The Python file **declares the path** to its web files; the loader must refuse anything that does not resolve inside that tool's own folder.
- **Declaration (illustrative shape only — names are not decided):** a module-level `TOOL_UI = {"path": "my_tool/", "html": "tool.html", "js": "tool.js", "css": "tool.css", "title": "…", "icon": "…", "presentation": "button" | "menu", "render": "sandboxed" | "inline", "actions": […]}`. `render` and the **declared-actions message API** are the **already-decided D.2.2 choices** (sandboxed recommended; inline is an explicit opt-in; read-only by default, declared actions only, dangerous ones through `JarvisUI.confirm`). The **wire format is still unwritten** and has to be written first.
- **Two presentation modes the tool chooses between.** (a) **Button** — a button (placed on the tool's own row / details in the Tool Manager, and optionally on the main screen) that **opens the tool's page** in an overlay. (b) **Menu** — an entry in the main **Menu** next to Test Checklist, Debug and the others, which opens the tool's panel **in a div** using the same overlay chrome. The owner's UI-element switch (L.46.2) hides either one.
- **What it takes.** (1) The loader and `custom_tools_store` must learn **folder tools** — today they glob `*.py` and the check / write / run / enable routes take one file name; (2) a new **read-only route that serves only declared files from a declared folder** (extension allow-list, size caps, no `..`, no absolute paths, no symlink escape, `Content-Type` set, a strict `Content-Security-Policy`); (3) the front end builds the button or menu entry from the declared metadata (with `textContent`, never `innerHTML`, for everything except the tool's own sandboxed page); (4) the editor needs **more than one file per tool** — the L.45 tabs fit this (`tool.py`, `tool.html`, `tool.js`, `tool.css` as tabs of one tool, with a check that the declared paths exist); (5) import of a folder tool (a zip, or a drop of several files) with the same **"this runs as you" confirmation** as `.py` import; (6) **uninstall / disable** removes the entries (ties to L.46.2).
- **Trust — say it plainly.** A custom tool's Python already runs **as the owner** with no sandbox. An **inline** `tool.js` runs inside the owner's page with access to **every `/api/*` route the page can call**, so it is *at least* as powerful as the tool's Python and can bypass the UI's confirm prompts unless the message API forces them. **Sandboxed** (an iframe with no page access, talking only through the declared-actions message API) is the right default and the only mode that adds containment. Per D.2.2 the owner has already accepted offering both; a warning when importing an inline tool is the minimum.
- **Needs deciding.** **Q-L46h** — the `TOOL_UI` field names and where the declaration lives (a Python dict, or a `tool.json` manifest next to the files); **Q-L46i** — may one tool declare **several** buttons / menu entries; **Q-L46j** — are tool pages allowed to call the owner's chat (`ask`) or only their own tool's actions; **Q-L46k** — one menu entry per tool or a single "Tools" submenu so the Menu does not fill up; **Q-L46l** — can the **model** open or read a tool's page (my default: no — humans only, like the Tool Manager itself).

**L.46.4 — Template examples (proposed design, nothing built).**
- **Keep the old way.** The existing **`ui` template (UI bridge: toast / bubble / dialog / confirm) is not changed or removed**, and the UI bridge remains the way for a tool to talk back from Python. New examples are **added alongside it**.
- **New examples to add (proposal):** a **folder tool with a button page** (`tool.html` + `tool.js` + `tool.css`, sandboxed, one declared read-only data request and one declared action), a **folder tool with a Menu panel** (same, with `presentation: "menu"`), an **inline** example with the warning spelled out in its comments, a **tool-supplied daemon** and a **persona** example (once L.12 exists; the persona one can ship now), and a short comparison in the template picker's hint ("UI bridge: messages and prompts from Python · Page: your own screen").
- **Shape.** A template is one string today. Multi-file examples need an **additive, opt-in** richer shape (a template may carry a `files` map; a plain-string template keeps working exactly as now — the AGENTS.md "additive data-shape changes" rule), the Create-a-tool flow must be able to open **several tabs** from one template, and the picker must say which examples create a folder.
- **Also required when built (AGENTS.md):** a **Test Checklist entry** for each new tool-facing behavior, reserved names and slash coverage for any new CLI verb (the `ctools-suggest` and `ctools-agent` slips), and tests for path validation that try `..`, absolute paths, symlinks and oversized files.

**Order I would suggest (opinion, not a decision).** **L.46.1 drafts first** — self-contained, no new trust questions, and it fixes real data loss now; then **L.46.2 for personas and user daemons** (small, uses existing pieces) with the rest of the row kinds arriving as L.12 / L.46.3 land; then **L.46.3 + L.46.4 together** (large: new folder-tool concept, a serving route, a sandbox and a message API that has to be specified first). Rough sizes: 46.1 small–medium, 46.2 medium, 46.3 large, 46.4 small–medium after 46.3. **These sizes are guesses, not measured.**

**Interactions.** **D.2.2** (this is its "complete customization" requirement made concrete — the two should be built as one design), **L.12** (tool-declared daemons — L.46.2 and L.46.3 depend on it for daemon / tab rows), **L.25** (the switches and the "off" meaning), **L.33 / L.45** (the editor and tabs that would carry multi-file tools and show draft restore), **L.34** (the commands-section removal would change which row kinds exist), **L.36** (the tokens-never-in-the-browser rule applies to anything a tool page can reach), **L.42** (chat-channel capabilities), **I-B20** (modal stacking for tool pages), `AGENTS.md` invariants (a tool page must not widen what the model can do).

**Not checked / limits.** Source reading only, on `_86_`; **nothing was run.** `tool_loader.py`'s handling of subfolders of `~/.jarvis/tools/`, how Menu entries are registered and whether they can be added from data rather than markup, and the `_87_` / `_88_` changes were **not examined.** The sandbox and message-API design is not specified here beyond what D.2.2 already decided.

**Status: ❌ NOT STARTED — documented only. Four owner decisions needed before building: Q-L46e / Q-L46f (what "daemons, personas, UI elements" covers), Q-L46b (secrets in drafts), Q-L46h (manifest shape).**

### L.47 Feature — the Focus layout's Agent side panel (NEW, 2026-10-05s, owner request; **✅ BUILT IN A PATCH 2026-10-05s — `jarvis-agent-focus-panel.patch` against `jarvis-main_92_.zip`; nothing was run**; **update 2026-10-05t: `code_agent` runs are now saved for replay — `jarvis-code-agent-replay.patch` against `jarvis-main_95_.zip` (which already contains the Agent panel); nothing was run**)

**Owner's words:** in Focus mode, whenever agent mode is running it opens a side panel that shows the codebase Jarvis is currently working on, the files it is working on, and so on.

**How it was read.** "Focus mode" = the L.32 Focus layout (the "Stage"). The repo has no feature called "agent mode", so it was read as the two agent tools, `dev_agent` (builds a new project) and `code_agent` (works inside an existing codebase), which already stream progress events. **If "agent mode" meant something else, this is the wrong feature — say so.**

**What it does (Focus only; Classic is unchanged and still draws the stepper card):**
- Opens **by itself when a new agent job starts**; it never re-opens for later events of the same job, so closing it mid-run sticks. An **Agent** button appears in the Ask header after the first job and glows while one is running.
- Shows the **codebase root** and the task, the **file being worked on right now** (with elapsed time), a **file tree** with a status on every file (planned / writing / written / read / edited / created / fixed / failed; files only seen in a listing are hidden behind "show all"), and a short **log** of installs, runs, fixes and shell commands. **Open folder** reuses the existing `open_file_location` tool.
- **Placement:** docked beside the conversation at ≥ 1000 px (the stage steps aside; with the D.1 subagents dock also open it sits to its left and the stage clears both); an overlay drawer with the Focus scrim below 1000 px. Opening Activity closes it (same side); on a narrow screen opening Chats does too. Leaving Focus closes it.
- **Escape** closes it only as a drawer, or when focus is inside it — Escape in the composer (dismissing the `/` palette) does not close the docked panel.

**How it is wired (no new server route).** Both agents already print one `JARVIS_MEDIA\tdev_agent\t<json>` line per step. `app.js` hands each live event to `window.JarvisAgentPanel?.feed` (inside `try/catch`, so a panel bug cannot stop the chat card) and a reloaded conversation's saved steps to `restore`. New module `web/public/agent-panel.js` (+ `agent-panel.css`, scoped to `body.layout--focus`) holds a pure reducer and tree builder exposed as `JarvisAgentPanel._pure`.
**Backend, additive only:** `dev_agent`'s first event (`plan:start`) now also carries `project_dir`; `code_agent`'s successful `list_dir` event carries a `listing` (names only, capped at `LISTING_EVENT_CAP = 150`).

**Invariants worth keeping**
- **Paths and one-line outcomes only — never file contents.** A masked `.env` value (code_agent F.5) must not be reachable through the panel; the new test asserts `preview` text is never stored.
- **The `listing` is live-stream only.** `code_agent`'s `steps` go back to the outer model, and the first draft stored the listing in them, which would have added up to 150 lines of model context per `list_dir` round; it is removed from the stored dict right after `emit()` has printed it. **Correction (2026-10-05t):** this item originally said `code_agent` has no result-shaping entry. That was **wrong** — I had only searched `tool_result_shaping.py`. `code_agent.py` has its own `TOOL_RESULT_SPECS` (merged in by `tools.py`): it drops each step's `arguments` at medium/low verbosity and all `steps` at low; at high, `steps` are verbatim; and `listing` is not in that spec. The decision to drop the listing was still right (it would have reached the model at medium and high), but the stated reason was incomplete.
- A path outside the root, or one that escapes with `..`, is never drawn as a file.
- The panel lists nothing itself, so it adds no way to read the disk.

**Known limits (existing gaps, not new):** (1) ~~only `dev_agent` runs are saved as replay extras~~ — **fixed 2026-10-05t** (see below): `code_agent` is saved too, but **slimmed**, so a reloaded `code_agent` tree shows only the files it read or changed, not the folders it browsed (a note in the panel says so). (2) The panel shows **one job at a time** (the latest). (3) A `code_agent` tree only contains what it listed or touched — it is not a scan of the project.

**Files in the patch (10; +881 / −6):** new `web/public/agent-panel.js`, `web/public/agent-panel.css`, `tests/verify_agent_panel.js`; edited `web/public/index.html`, `web/public/app.js` (a feed hook, a restore hook, and `focus-agent-open` added to the class cleanup in `applyLayout`), `web/public/test-checklist-data.js` (watch notes on `dev_agent` and `code_agent`), `jarvis-cli/jarvis/actions/dev_agent.py`, `jarvis-cli/jarvis/actions/code_agent.py`, `REPO_MAP.md`, `AGENTS.md` (one command line).

**⚠ Base mismatch (resolved 2026-10-05t: `jarvis-main_95_.zip` already contains this patch — `agent-panel.js`, `verify_agent_panel.js` and both `app.js` hooks are present).** The patch is against **`jarvis-main_92_.zip`** (the repo the owner sent), but the docs describe later work against `_93_` / `_94_` (Channels P4–P11, Tool Manager L.45/L.46 and others). Those patches edit `app.js`, `index.html`, `REPO_MAP.md` and `AGENTS.md` too. The L.47 hunks are small and in different regions, but **it was never applied to an `_94_` tree** — expect to re-base if `git apply --check` complains.

**Verified:** `node --check` on `app.js`, `agent-panel.js`, `tests/verify_agent_panel.js`, `test-checklist-data.js`; `py_compile` on both Python files; `test-checklist-data.js` still parses as strict JSON; the patch dry-runs clean on a fresh extract of `_92_` and reproduces the working tree exactly.
**Not verified (owner said skip testing):** **nothing was run** — no Python test, no `verify_agent_panel.js`, no browser. `tests/verify_agent_panel.js` was written but not run at first — **run 2026-10-05u: passes (46/46 after the bug fix).** No live `dev_agent` / `code_agent` run; no Windows.

**Open.** (1) Is "agent mode" really `dev_agent` + `code_agent`? (2) Should the panel also open for sub-agents (D.1) or background jobs? (3) ~~Persist `code_agent` runs as replay extras~~ — done 2026-10-05t. (4) Let the panel show a file's diff or contents (it deliberately does not now)? (5) A history of several jobs instead of only the latest?

### L.48 Feature — dev_agent known-bugs batch from the first real agent-mode run (NEW, 2026-10-05x, owner request; **✅ BUG-1–4 FIXED IN PATCHES 2026-10-05x — `0001-Fix-BUG-1-markdown-style-leak-and-BUG-2-server-run-p.patch` and `0002-Fix-BUG-3-dev_agent-output_dir-and-BUG-4-reasoning-s.patch` against `jarvis-main_98_.zip`; BUG-5–8 OPEN**)

**Owner's words:** "start with bug 1 and 2", then "do bug 3 and 4", from `DEV_AGENT_KNOWN_BUGS.md` — the notes the owner wrote after the first real agent-mode run (conversation `13b360a90f8779b0`, "Fixing Missing Express Server File"; the task was a small node.js app that shows the current time; Gemini returned 503/429, so most agent turns fell back to Groq). From this batch on the owner wants **a git patch per change, the patch sent first, then the audit and this plan updated, and no tests run by the assistant.**

**BUG-1 — model-authored `<style>` restyles the whole page (✅ fixed; run).** `renderMarkdown()` ended in `DOMPurify.sanitize(html)`; DOMPurify 3's default config keeps a `<style>` that follows prose, so a reply with raw HTML (the generated clock page is full of `body{}` / `*{}` rules) restyled Jarvis until a reload. Reproduced in real Chromium (marked + DOMPurify 3.4.0): prose then `<style>`, a `<style>` inside a div, and an inline `style="position:fixed;…"` all survived the default config. The fix is a module-level `MD_SANITIZE_CONFIG` in `web/public/app.js` — `FORBID_TAGS: ["style","link","meta","base"]`, `FORBID_ATTR: ["style"]` — passed to the sanitizer; `link`/`meta`/`base` were already dropped by the defaults and are listed as a second lock. KaTeX output is unaffected because `restoreMath` runs after sanitizing. **Side effect to know:** any model HTML that relied on inline `style=""` now loses it, in the main chat and in every `JarvisMarkdown.renderInto` caller. `tests/verify_markdown_sanitize.js` reads the config out of `app.js` (so it tests the shipped code), asserts every case, asserts the page background is unchanged and real content (`<h1>`) is kept, and fails if the default config no longer leaks (otherwise the test proves nothing).

**BUG-2 — a web server can never pass the run phase (✅ fixed; run).** `_run_subprocess` used `subprocess.run(timeout=30)` and `returncode == 0`; a server never exits, so the timeout was a failure, `classify()` labelled it `unknown`, and the loop spent up to five attempts rewriting working files (job `101dc03eac06` passed only because the rewritten server exited immediately; job `46bc17c8eec9` rewrote `public/index.html` five times and gave up with `max_attempts`). New in `actions/dev_agent.py`: `_run_long_aware()` runs the command with `Popen`, own process group, output to temp files, and waits `LONG_RUNNING_GRACE` (8 s, capped by `RUN_TIMEOUT`). Exited 0 → ok; exited non-zero → failure with the real stderr; **still alive and not crashed → ok with `long_running: true`**, a `url` (first URL printed, else `http://localhost:<port>` from a "listening on port N" line), then the process tree is stopped (`taskkill /T /F` on Windows, `killpg` elsewhere). `dev_agent_errors.is_timeout()` recognises the harness's own `timed out after Ns` text (a real error that merely mentions a timeout, e.g. `ETIMEDOUT`, does not match) and `classify()` returns the new label `timeout`. The loop breaks on a bare timeout and returns `reason: "timeout"` instead of asking the writer model to fix it. The `done` event and result carry `long_running` and `url`. The UI says "started and kept running at <url>" instead of `exit None`. **Decision taken (owner may overrule):** the server is stopped after it is confirmed to start, because leaving a process running unattended is exactly what the daemons rule (the model may not create one) is there to prevent; "leave it running" would be a small, separate change. `_run_subprocess` is untouched and still used for installs.

**BUG-3 — `dev_agent` ignores the requested destination folder (✅ fixed; tests written, not run).** The schema took only `description`, `language_hint` and `project_name`, so the owner's `D:\MyDigitalVault\prjects\test` went into the description and was ignored; the app was built under `~/.jarvis/dev_agent_projects`, and Jarvis then improvised with `run_shell` / `make_dir` / `code_agent`. **Design:** an optional `output_dir` argument whose description tells the model to pass the user's destination there. The build still happens only inside the sandbox (the write/fix loop never gets write access elsewhere); a build that **passed** is then copied. `dev_agent_sandbox.validate_output_dir()` runs first, before any AI call is spent, and refuses: a non-absolute path, a drive/filesystem root, the home folder or any parent of it, anything inside `~/.jarvis` (or a folder that contains the projects root), a system folder (`/etc`, `/usr`, `/var`…, and on Windows `SystemRoot` / `ProgramFiles` / `ProgramFiles(x86)` / `ProgramData`), an existing file, and an existing **non-empty** folder — nothing is overwritten or merged. `deliver()` re-checks emptiness at copy time, skips `node_modules`, `.venv`, `venv`, `__pycache__`, `.git` (reported as `not_copied` so the model can tell the user to reinstall) and **never copies a symlink** (generated code runs before the copy and could plant one that points at a private file). A new `deliver` phase (start / ok / fail) is emitted between the run and `done`. A failed copy does **not** turn a working build into a failure: the result is `ok: true, delivered: false, delivery_error`, and the sandbox copy is always kept. Result fields when `output_dir` is given: `output_dir`, `delivered`, `not_copied`, `delivery_error`; with no `output_dir` the result and the event stream are exactly as before. `dev_agent` stays in `TOOL_CONFIRM_REQUIRED`, and `write_file` already writes anywhere under a confirmation, so a confirmed, validated destination does not widen what Jarvis can do — but this was **not** checked: whether the confirmation card displays `output_dir`. The tool-pack instruction now tells the model to pass `output_dir` and to report `delivered` / `delivery_error`. UI: a Deliver row in the step card (`app.js`) and a log line plus a "Copying" status in the Agent panel (`agent-panel.js`).

**BUG-4 — raw model reasoning in the "thinking" extra while thinking is off (✅ fixed; tests written, not run).** In the saved exchange the `thinking` extra had `level: "off"` and `requested: 0` yet carried 2,146 characters of Groq reasoning quoting internal instructions. `ai_client.ask()` saved the extra whenever the provider returned any reasoning. It now asks `reasoning.should_save_trace(level, text, save)`, which is true only when the level is not `off` (and the text is non-empty and `save` is on); the decision is a small pure function so it can be tested without the `ask()` fixture. **Kept on purpose:** the raw event log still stores the full reasoning (`raw_archive`'s `model_reply` — it is a debug archive, not UI). **No change needed:** the live thinking block is already hidden by the Thinking setting and the replayed block is already a collapsed `<details>`, so "collapse by default when on" already holds. **Not fixed:** with thinking **on**, the visible text can still quote internal instructions.

**Open items in the same file (not touched):** **BUG-5** too many cards stacked in one assistant bubble (resolved confirms collapse to one line, one progress card per job, thinking hidden by default); **BUG-6** the live path (`JARVIS_MEDIA\tdev_agent`) and the reload path (`renderThreadExtra`'s `devAgent` case) differ — start by diffing what each appends to the bubble; **BUG-7** mojibake in Groq replies (UTF-8 non-breaking hyphen shown as `â€‘`), decode site not found, start in the Groq adapter in `ai_providers.py` and check the SSE stream is decoded as UTF-8; **BUG-8** (context) provider failures pushed agent work onto a weaker model — consider a rule that agent-mode turns do not fall back to a model that cannot reliably read tool output.

**Files.** Patch 0001 (6 files, +367/−7): `jarvis-cli/jarvis/actions/dev_agent.py`, `jarvis-cli/jarvis/dev_agent_errors.py`, `web/public/app.js`, `web/public/agent-panel.js`, new `tests/test_dev_agent_long_running.py`, new `tests/verify_markdown_sanitize.js`. Patch 0002 (7 files, +470/−9): `jarvis-cli/jarvis/actions/dev_agent.py`, `jarvis-cli/jarvis/dev_agent_sandbox.py`, `jarvis-cli/jarvis/reasoning.py`, `jarvis-cli/jarvis/ai_client.py`, `web/public/app.js`, `web/public/agent-panel.js`, new `tests/test_dev_agent_output_dir.py`. **Apply 0001 first** — 0002 edits the same files.

**Verified (by me, in a sandbox, for BUG-1/2 only).** `test_dev_agent_long_running.py` 8/8 with real subprocesses (a server is detected and stopped within seconds, URL extraction, clean exit, crash, missing binary, the `timeout` label, the loop makes zero fix attempts for a running server and never fixes a bare timeout); `verify_markdown_sanitize.js` passes in real Chromium; the existing `test_dev_agent.py`, `test_dev_agent_errors.py`, `test_dev_agent_events.py`, `test_dev_agent_sandbox.py` (41 tests) and `verify_math_rendering.js` (24/24) still pass; `node --check` on both JS files.
**Not run (owner's instruction, BUG-3/4):** `tests/test_dev_agent_output_dir.py` — 20 tests written, never executed (validation rules; `deliver` copies, leaves dependency folders and never copies symlinks, refuses a folder that filled up; the loop rejects a bad path before any AI call, delivers only a passed build, survives a failed copy, behaves exactly as before with no `output_dir`; the schema keeps it optional; `should_save_trace` off / on / empty / `save=False`). Checks made: `py_compile`, `node --check`, `git apply --check` of both patches in order on a fresh `_98_`, and one import that printed the schema text (which is how a doubled-backslash example path in the description was found and replaced with `D:/Projects/clock` before delivery). **Not verified anywhere:** a real `node server.js` through the whole Jarvis flow, the Windows `taskkill` path, any browser (the Deliver row, the Agent-panel log line), the confirmation card, a live provider, the sanitizer against other places that render model HTML.
**Not done:** no Test Checklist entry, no `REPO_MAP.md` / `AGENTS.md` change (the new `output_dir` rules and the `deliver` phase belong in `REPO_MAP.md` — owed), build number not bumped.

**Spotted, not changed.** `jarvis-cli/ai_client.py` (package root) sits beside `jarvis-cli/jarvis/ai_client.py` and uses relative imports; `REPO_MAP.md` lists only the one in `jarvis/`. It looks like a stale copy — check whether anything imports it.

**Open.** (1) Should a finished server be left running (detached, with its URL) instead of stopped? (2) Should the confirmation card show `output_dir`, and should a destination that already holds files be allowed after an explicit confirm? (3) Should the model be told, in the tool result, to offer `npm install` when `not_copied` lists `node_modules`? (4) BUG-5 to BUG-8, in the owner's order.

## Revision 2026-09-26c (owner request — notification levels detailed, custom-skill/scheduler notify, custom UI tabs)

Doc-only revision, no codebase changes — the owner explicitly asked for the
plan to be updated without touching the codebase.

- **D.2.1 superseded.** The old three-level (`low`/`normal`/`high`) model
  wasn't detailed enough per the owner and is replaced with five explicit
  levels (Silent / Standard / Audible / Broadcast / Confirm), each mapped to
  a concrete delivery behavior instead of a vague immediate-vs-digested
  split. Levels 1, 2, and 5 were specified directly by the owner; levels 3
  and 4 ("you decide") are my proposed defaults — TTS readout and
  cross-channel DM broadcast respectively — tracked as open decisions
  **D-N1** and **D-N2**, not yet owner-confirmed the way D-I1–D-I10 are.
  See the rewritten §D.2.1 above, plus matching updates to K.2.7.1 (now
  split into K.2.7.1/1a/1b), the J.2 acceptance test rows, and the §J.3
  test-plan bullet.
- **New requirement: custom skills/actions can send notifications through
  the same D.2.1 pipeline**, at a level of their choosing (or a declared
  per-skill default) — tracked as new **K.2.7.1a**.
- **New requirement: scheduled reminders use the same five-level system**
  instead of a fixed generic notification — tracked as new **K.2.7.1b**.
  Composes with D.6 (fresh conversation per scheduled run) and the
  `needs_approval` gate D.5 confirmed already works.
- **New requirement: D.2.2, custom skill/action UI tabs.** Custom
  skills/actions should be able to register a full top-level web-UI tab

  custom panel content rather than a fixed built-in layout. Flagged one open

  panel content renders inline in the main page or inside a sandboxed
  `iframe`, given it would be the first place custom-skill markup/JS
  actually executes rather than being escaped as text (§5641's existing

- Nothing here was implemented, tested, or built — per the owner's explicit
  "do NOT add anything or edit any codebase, just the docs" instruction,
  this revision only records the requirements, the two proposed defaults
  (D-N1/D-N2), and the one open security question (D.2.2) for whoever picks
  this up next.

## Revision 2026-09-26i (five open owner decisions resolved: D-N1, D-N2, D.2.2's render mode, D-I10, K.2.9's invariant)

Doc-only revision, no codebase changes. Five previously-open owner
decisions were presented with purpose/options/upsides/downsides each, and
resolved:

- **D-N1 (level 3, "Persistent"):** re-surface on an interval, not just a
  non-auto-dismissing toast. Interval/cap not yet specified — flagged as a
  follow-up detail, not blocking.
- **D-N2 (level 4, "Broadcast"):** confirmed as the cross-channel DM — this
  was already the proposed default, now owner-confirmed.
- **D.2.2 (custom tab render mode):** support both inline and sandboxed
  `iframe`, tool author's choice via a `render:` field, with sandboxed as
  the documented/recommended default. New follow-up flagged: the
  message-passing API for a sandboxed tab to talk to the rest of Jarvis
  still needs its own design pass — "sandboxed" only means something if
  that API doesn't just hand back full access anyway.
- **D-I10 (`remember_sender` for non-owner senders):** carve out the
  exception (Option A), **with a new attached constraint** — it must not
  fire on irrelevant/one-off exchanges, since an over-eager rolodex would
  bloat input tokens on every future turn the same way D.5-#1's stale-memory
  bug did. A relevance gate is now required scope for this item, not yet
  designed.
- **K.2.9 (test-checklist invariant):** restate it rather than drop it — add
  a check that no tool's entry appears twice (inline and in
  `test-checklist-data.js`), instead of just removing the old
  custom-tool-only restriction with nothing replacing it.

Nothing here was implemented — these are decisions, not code. Each
decision's own section above now carries the resolution plus whatever new
follow-up work the decision itself introduced (the D-N1 interval, D.2.2's
message-passing API, D-I10's relevance gate).

snapshot (`jarvis-main_55_.zip`) — reading the real source, and running the
real tests, rather than taking either the report or this document's prior
status at face value.

(cross-turn compounding, not per-request/retry duplication) matches what's

the cross-turn declined-action check in `ai_client.py`) are present and

## Revision 2026-09-29 (H.1.6 fixed, H.1.7 added — `jarvis-h16-h17-daemon-running-and-console.patch`)

**H.1.6 — the panel never showing "running" — fixed.** The owner's triage put it in the backend; the cause is `daemons.pid_alive()` using `os.kill(pid, 0)`, which on Windows is not an existence check (signal 0 is `CTRL_C_EVENT`), so every pid read as dead. Now uses `OpenProcess` + `GetExitCodeProcess` on Windows; POSIX unchanged. 22 new checks incl. a real daemon on the host OS. **Owed: a real Windows run.** **H.1.7 — console Error/System/Output detector — fixed:** stamped stdout no longer System, INFO/DEBUG on stderr no longer an error, ERROR-level and tracebacks on stdout now errors, warnings no longer crashes, Node stacks grouped. 37 new checks.

Patch touches 6 files: `daemons.py`, `daemons.js`, two new tests, `AGENTS.md`, and `build_info.py` (build 40 → 41, per AGENTS.md). **If this is merged with another patch that also bumps the build, re-run `python build_tools/bump_build_version.py` afterwards or `test_build_info.py` will fail.** Applied with `patch -p1` to a fresh extraction of `jarvis-main_61_.zip`, result identical to the working tree, suites re-run there.

**Findings, recorded not fixed:** (1) same `os.kill(pid, 0)` bug in `sched_daemon`, `discord_gateway`, `doctor`; (2) `daemons.py` ignores `JARVIS_HOME` (`JARVIS_DIR = Path.home()/".jarvis"`), so daemon tests share one registry and race under `run_tests.py --jobs N` — `test_h12_daemon_fixes.py` and `test_h15_daemon_editor.py` fail intermittently in parallel (`test_h15` also on the untouched original tree); serially all pass; the new test isolates itself via `HOME`/`USERPROFILE` as AGENTS.md prescribes; (3) `run_supervisor()`'s fast-crash `last_error` still reports the `=== exited` banner rather than the process's real last line (found in H.1, still open); (4) `test_key_health.py` timing failures remain pre-existing.
