## Revision 2026-10-03 (L.25 Tool Manager built; tools and saved commands can be switched off; `jarvis-tool-manager.patch` against `jarvis-main_72_` — code + docs)

**Code and docs.** Owner instructions: build the Tool Manager's switch-off, saved-command and protected-tools parts; "by disabled I mean that the model cannot see that tool nor can he use it"; ship a patch against `jarvis-main_72_`; document it here and in the audit; "don't update the docs just yet" was lifted for these two files only (`AGENTS.md` and the rest are **not** amended beyond the rename edits listed under L.25).

- **What was built:** the whole of L.25 as scoped — the Tool Manager panel replacing Custom Tools, three per-tool safeguards (ask first, AI overview, **approval summary**), user-tool create/edit/import/on-off, and now an **"Available to Jarvis" switch for every tool and saved command**. Details, the files, the decisions and the test counts are in the **Built 2026-10-03** block under L.25; they are not repeated here.
- **The base repo did not have round 1.** `jarvis-main_72_.zip` is build 52 on a different line from the Tool Manager delivered earlier against `_70_` (no `tool-manager.js`, no `approval_summary`), and this plan and the audit still said L.25 was "documented only". The patch therefore carries **both rounds** (build 52 → 53, 27 files, +3,419/−438); the earlier work was merged onto `_72_` file by file with the `_70_` original as the common ancestor — only the generated `build_info.py` conflicted. The patch was applied to a **fresh unzip of `_72_`** and the full suite run there: **95 of 96 files**; the one failure is `test_key_health.py` (two timing assertions), identical on the unpatched tree.
- **Owner definition → implementation (Q-L25f).** "The model cannot see it and cannot use it" is built as *hidden from every model-facing surface* **and** *refused at the two choke points automatic callers use* (`execute_tool`, default-deny; the model's executor, before the cache and the confirm gate). The owner can still run it. Scheduled jobs count as automatic and fail clearly (Q-L25g, my reading). Protected tools: `search_tools`, `search_commands`, `get_tool_schema`, `load_skill` (Q-L25b, built from the code, unconfirmed).
- **Real defects found on the way, all fixed in the patch:** `update_command` by exact name could rewrite a switched-off command; **renaming a disabled command re-enabled it**; a deleted tool/command left its switch for the next one with that name; the editor's validator accepted files the loader silently drops (`TOOL_KEYWORDS` mismatch and two more); in the new editor (caught in the browser during the first round, before delivery) the file-name field stayed editable after a first save, so a retyped name could overwrite another tool file. Also, **by code reading, not by reproduction:** the old Custom Tools editor's Run flow used `JarvisUI.prompt`, which returns its default on Cancel, so cancelling the arguments dialog would still have run the tool; the new Run card has its own Run button. Each fix has a test except the old-editor Cancel behaviour, which no longer exists.
- **Cross-checks:** the protected set means the Tool Manager **cannot** switch off discovery tools globally, so L.28's "tools-off guests are still offered discovery tools that fail" and L.29's per-sender allowlist must keep using `JARVIS_ALLOWED_TOOLS` (per-process, per-sender) and not this switch — no conflict today, but do not merge the two mechanisms without revisiting the protected list. L.12's "unloading a tool removes its daemons/tabs/commands" is **not** done by the switch (open). L.18's Debug tool list and the Tool Manager both exist; Debug still lists a disabled tool unmarked and still runs it for the owner.
- **Not verified:** the real `server.js` (new routes only `node --check`ed; the browser pass used a stand-in server over the real CLI), a live model call, `script.bat`, a real restart, an MCP server's tools, a screen reader. **Not built:** tool-owned daemons/tabs/commands, a Test Checklist entry for the manager, palette verbs/CLI commands as switchable items (Q-L25e).
- **Owner decisions needed:** (1) confirm scheduled jobs should fail when they name a switched-off item (Q-L25g); (2) confirm or edit the four-tool protected list; (3) amend the `AGENTS.md` invariant — proposed wording is under L.25 Not verified; (4) whether a switched-off tool should take its daemons/tabs with it (L.12); (5) whether palette verbs and CLI commands should ever be switchable (Q-L25e); (6) whether Debug should mark disabled tools.
- **Also noted, not acted on:** `jarvis-cli/cli.py` is a 2,716-line dead copy (entry is `jarvis.cli:entry`, nothing imports it, its `RESERVED_NAMES` is stale) — worth deleting deliberately, not as a side effect.

- **L.27 — daemons now autostart (P1, fixed).** One call, `daemons.autostart_all()`, on the scheduler's **startup tick** (`scheduler.tick(startup=True)`), so the web server, `sched-daemon` and a Task Scheduler `sched-tick --startup` all get it; never on the 30 s tick. `autostart_all()` also now leaves a daemon alone whose supervisor is alive and records a failure on the daemon's status. ## Revision 2026-10-04f (`jarvis doctor` persona-file false FAIL fixed; template gets a UI example; code + docs; `jarvis-doctor-persona-files-and-ui-template.patch` and an optional `jarvis-doctor-pid-file-formats.OPTIONAL.patch` against `jarvis-main_80_.zip`)

**Code and docs.** Owner pasted a failing `jarvis doctor` run ("27 ok, 4 warnings, 1 failure") and asked for it to be fixed, for `actions/_template.py` to be updated "with everything and an example for ui things", and for **nothing daemon, front-end or conversation/console storage/logging related to be touched** (another agent is working there and the patches would conflict). Each line of the report was traced to its cause before anything was edited:

| doctor line | cause | what was done |
|---|---|---|
| `[FAIL] Action file starter_personas.py — __not_an_action__` and `13 loaded, 1 rejected` | **Code bug** in `doctor.check_tools()`. `starter_personas.py` is a legitimate persona-only file (`PERSONAS`, no tool trio). `tool_loader._validate` returns `valid=False, error="__not_an_action__"` for it *deliberately*, and `discover_actions` keeps that record only so the personas still reach `tools.py`. The doctor counted every `not valid` record as a rejection. | **Fixed (main patch).** Persona-only records are reported as an OK `Persona file …` line and counted separately; real rejections are unchanged. |
| `[warn] tesseract — not on PATH … can't work at all won't work` | **Machine state** (Tesseract not installed) plus a wording bug (the entry's `why` already said "can't work", the doctor appended "won't work"). | Wording fixed (main patch). Install with `winget install UB-Mannheim.TesseractOCR` and reopen the terminal. |
| `[warn] scheduler daemon — pid file is unreadable` | **Code bug in the doctor, not a bad file.** `sched_daemon._write_pid_file` writes JSON `{"pid": N, "started": …}`; `channels/discord_gateway._claim_pid_file` writes a bare integer; `doctor.check_daemons()` and `_pid_alive_from()` only did `int(text)`. A running scheduler therefore always read as "unreadable", and the suggested fix (delete the file) removes the live daemon's single-instance guard. `check_scheduler()` used the same reader, so an overdue job with a live scheduler was reported "nothing is ticking the scheduler". | **Fixed in a separate, optional patch** (daemon-adjacent, so kept out of the main one): one shared `_read_pid()` accepting both formats. Touches only `doctor.py` and a new test; not `sched_daemon.py`, `daemons.py` or the gateway. **Do not delete `sched_daemon.pid` while the daemon is running.** |
| `[warn] Jobs with errors — 2 jobs last ran with an error` | **Data on the owner's machine** (`last_error` on two scheduled jobs). The doctor is reporting correctly. | Not a code change. `jarvis sched-show <id>` for each, `jarvis sched-clear <id>` to remove. |

(3) A table of contents. (5) New section 9, "checking your file" (`jarvis doctor`, `tools-list`, `personas-list`, the Custom Tools Check button, and not `print()`-ing to stdout inside a handler, because `JARVIS_UI_REQUEST` lines travel on stdout). `_template.py` is never loaded by discovery (leading underscore), so the new tool does not exist at runtime; `tests/test_checklist_supplied.py` loads it directly.

## Revision 2026-10-04g (Windows test-run failures diagnosed and fixed; one real product bug in `daemons.py`; `jarvis-windows-test-failures.patch` against `jarvis-main_81_.zip` — code + docs)

**Code and docs.** Owner pasted a 104-file Windows run (`py run_tests.py`, 9 FAIL) and asked for the cause, a fix, a patch and updated docs. The patch is against `jarvis-main_81_.zip`, was checked with `git apply --check` on a fresh extract, and touches 9 files: `jarvis/daemons.py` (the only product code), `tests/run_tests.py`, five existing tests, one new test, and one paragraph of `AGENTS.md`. No invariant is touched (the model still may start/stop/inspect daemons but never create one).

- **Why the failure list was hard to read (runner fix).** `run_tests.py` showed the *last line* of stdout+stderr. A test that prints "42 passed, 2 failed" and then has a library write `[tools] Auto-discovered ...` to stderr therefore reported that notice as its "reason" — which is what `test_key_health` and `test_path_tools` showed. A failing file now reports its own `FAILED` lines, the final exception line and the `N passed` count (passing files show their count line). This is also why `test_l3_task_label`, `test_path_tools` and `test_l26_daemon_restart` could not be diagnosed from the pasted output (see below).
- **Real bug — `daemons.add()` / `daemons.edit()` on Windows (fixes `test_l27`; `test_l26` is the same cause).** Both split a command string with `shlex.split(cmd, posix=False)`, which keeps the quote characters inside the tokens. `"C:\\...\\python.exe" -c "..."` became an argv[0] that literally started with `"`, and `Popen` raised `[WinError 2]` — exactly the `last_error` in the L.27 failure. Any quoted path given to `daemon-add` or the daemon editor would hit it. New `daemons._split_command()` uses `CommandLineToArgvW` on Windows (what every Windows program's own argv is built from; the same approach `actions/code_agent._windows_argv_split` already used for `run_shell`), falls back to shlex(posix=False) with one surrounding quote pair stripped per token if the WinAPI call is unavailable, returns `[]` for an empty string (the raw API would return *this* executable's path), and is plain POSIX shlex elsewhere. New `tests/test_daemon_command_split.py` **11/11** (the Windows branches run on any OS through a `windows=` override; on Linux that exercises the fallback). It cannot run against the unpatched file (`_split_command` does not exist there).
- **Test bugs, not product bugs (fixed in the tests):**
  - `test_code_agent_budget_and_outcomes` — printed `→` on a cp1252 console (`UnicodeEncodeError` inside `check`), hiding a real failure. stdout/stderr are now reconfigured to UTF-8, and the two `python3 -c ...` commands use the running interpreter (`python3` is usually not on a Windows PATH).
  - `test_sched_daemon` — `check()` did `": " + detail` with an int detail (the `TypeError`), hiding the real failure: on Windows `os.kill(pid, SIGTERM)` is `TerminateProcess`, so the daemon exits with code 15, never runs its handler and leaves its pid file. The Windows branch now asserts only that the process is gone. **Product consequence, not fixed:** on Windows `sched_daemon.stop_running()` cannot shut the daemon down gracefully.
  - `test_run_shell_windows_args` — "non-Windows echo is never routed through cmd" never faked the platform, so on a Windows host it correctly routed through `cmd`. It now sets `sys.platform = "linux"` for that test.
  - `test_key_health` — compared `sleeps == [2.0]` exactly; the real value is `2 - elapsed` (1.9999...). It fails on Linux too and was listed in earlier revisions as "identical on the pristine tree". Now an approximate compare (±0.25 s).
  - `test_recent_dms` (14/15) — `newest first` depends on file mtime and two writes a few ms apart can tie on NTFS. The test now pins the mtimes. **Inferred from the code, not observed on Windows.**
- **`test_build_info`** — not a bug: the tree changed after build 56. Run `python build_tools/bump_build_version.py` from `jarvis-cli/` **after applying** (the patch does not bump it, as with earlier patches). The hash is over raw file bytes, so a CRLF checkout and an LF extract hash differently; the bump must run on the owner's machine.
- **Verified:** on Linux the full suite is **106 of 107** files; the one failure is `test_build_info`. The five edited tests and the new one pass, and the patch applies cleanly to a fresh `_81_` extract.
- **Not verified (no Windows here):** that the Windows fixes turn the owner's nine failures green; `CommandLineToArgvW` itself; `test_l26` and `test_l27` end to end.
- **Still unexplained:** `test_l3_task_label` and `test_path_tools` — the pasted run only showed an unrelated first/last output line, they pass on Linux, and nothing in either test was clearly Windows-specific. Re-run them with the patched runner (`py run_tests.py l3_task_label path_tools`) and the real `FAILED` line will print.
- **Sibling finding, not fixed:** `actions/dev_agent._shlex_split` still uses `shlex.split(command, posix=(sys.platform != "win32"))`, so a quoted `run_command` argument keeps its quotes on Windows — the same class of bug as `run_shell`'s old F.4 behaviour. Recorded; no change made.

## Revision 2026-10-05 (L.11 user-defined daemon categories built — code + docs; `jarvis-daemon-categories.patch` against `jarvis-main_79_.zip`)

**Built.** A daemon has a `categories` list (labels, up to 8 per daemon, 24 characters each, case-insensitive unique, first spelling wins). Empty = **Undefined**. `builtin` is untouched and still the lock; categories never unlock a built-in's argv/shell/stdin.
- **Backend:** new `jarvis/categories.py` (the shared name rules, per L.14.3); `daemons.py` (`categories` in `_EDITABLE`, strict on `add`/`edit` — refused with a reason, nothing written; lenient on load, so a hand-edited registry never fails to load; built-ins ship with defaults `scheduler: core`, `discord`/`instagram: chat`, `clipboard-watch`/`browser: desktop`, stored only as an override); `workspace_cli.py` (`--category NAME` repeatable on `daemon-add`/`daemon-edit`, replace-not-merge; `--clear-categories`; a bare `--category` is an error, never "clear"); `server.js` POST/PATCH forward `categories` through `daemonCategoryArgs()`, which **refuses names starting with `--`** (the CLI flag parser would read them as flags) and sends `[]` as `--clear-categories`.
- **Shared component (L.14.3):** `web/public/category-input.js/.css` — `JarvisCategories`: pure `normalizeName/normalizeList/vocabulary/suggest/canonical` plus the chip input (prefix suggestions most-used first, exact-spelling reuse, Enter/Tab accept, comma commits, Esc closes only the list, Backspace removes the last chip, 8-name cap). Python and JS rules are checked against one corpus by `tests/test_categories.py`.
- **Panel:** the kind select is now All / Built-in / a *Categories* group (one option per category in use, most-used first, ties alphabetical, then Undefined); Overview "By kind" → **"By category"**; chips on cards (one clipped row — a chip that doesn't fit is omitted, not wrapped); a Categories row in Details; a Categories field in the editor for custom daemons **and** built-ins. Saved `kindFilter: "custom"` migrates to `all`; a saved category that no longer exists falls back to `all`. `entrySignature` includes categories so edits re-render.

**Decisions made (change any and say so).**
1. **Undefined = any daemon with no category**, built-ins included if the owner clears theirs (the spec said "not built-in and uncategorised"; the wider rule avoids a cleared built-in being unreachable from any category chip).
2. The list's two **groups** keep the headers "Built-in" / "Custom" (they are the built-in-flag grouping and hold the add-one empty state). Only the *filter* lost "Custom". One-word change if the owner meant the headers too.
3. **Q5 honoured:** suggestions come only from daemons; the shared part is rules + widget. The acceptance line "…and commands" (L.11) is superseded.
4. CLI-typed names are **not** canonicalised against other daemons' spelling (the UI does that); filters are case-insensitive, so `Utility`/`utility` still land in one filter option.
5. Editing a category set sends the whole set; order is the display order.

**Tests.** New: `test_categories.py` 22 (rules + Python/JS parity incl. İ, ß, NEL, ZWSP, emoji), `test_l11_daemon_categories.py` 43 (registry, built-ins, lenient read, CLI, `daemonCategoryArgs` lifted from `server.js`), `verify_l11_daemon_categories.py` 48 in Chromium (3 clean repeats). `verify_daemons_panel.js` **127 → 160** (its harness now loads `category-input.js` first). Run by hand on the patched `_79_` tree: `test_workspace` 75, `test_h15` 19, `test_h12` 8, `test_h11` 13, `test_l27` 10, `test_slash_coverage` 545, `test_checklist_coverage` 6, `verify_l13` 19, `verify_daemons_console` 37. **The full suite was not run** (owner asked to stop testing).

**Not verified / owed.** The **real `server.js`** (only syntax-checked; the helper was lifted out and tested, the routes never ran); the owner's running app; Windows; applying on the **current tree** — the patch is against `_79_`, and the files it edits (`daemons.py`, `daemons.js`, `server.js`, `workspace_cli.py`, `index.html`, `AGENTS.md`, `REPO_MAP.md`) were touched by later revisions (e.g. 2026-10-04g's `daemons.py` fix), so expect to check hunks. `build_info.py` is bumped to build 56 in the patch but **must be re-bumped** (`python build_tools/bump_build_version.py` from `jarvis-cli/`) after merging; `test_build_info.py` was already stale on `_79_`. `tests/verify_panel_open_guard.js` fails with a missing module on the pristine `_79_` too (unrelated). **Still open:** L.14 command categories (should reuse `categories.py` / `category-input.js`), rename/merge/delete a category, L.12's "tools suggest categories", and a browser pass by the owner. `AGENTS.md` (new "Categories" section, test list) and `REPO_MAP.md` are in the patch.

## Revision 2026-10-05h (Channels: missing people, manual name, "Add a new person", Discord↔Instagram link — code + docs; `jarvis-channels-people-manage.patch` against `jarvis-main_87_.zip`)

**Code and docs.** Owner request, four items in the Channels panel (L.36): (1) people who were added on Discord "still don't show up"; (2) be able to change a person's **Name** by hand; (3) an **"add a new person"** button; (4) **link a person's Instagram to their Discord** by id, handle or name.

- **Root cause of (1).** The panel lists `people.json` records, and a record was only ever created by a *message*. Anyone added to `dm/reply/tool_allowlist` (Global lists, `channels-allow`, a hand-edit) who had not written yet had **no record**, so no row and no switches. Fixed at the source: `user_admin.list_view()` now reconciles on every read (`sync_listed` → `people.adopt_listed`) — every id/@handle named in a list or as `owner` gets a hand-added row (`"*"` creates nobody). Idempotent; never touches an existing record. **Limit:** per-scope overrides (`scopes.guild:…`) are not reconciled.
- **(2) Name.** Pencil next to the name in the panel; `jarvis channels-rename`. A name typed by the owner is **locked** (`name_locked`): `remember_sender` (the person telling Jarvis their own name) no longer overwrites it and tells the model it was kept. Clearing the name unlocks it.
- **(3) Add a new person.** "+ Add a new person" in the People header; `jarvis channels-add-person <platform> <id|@handle> [name]`. **Grants nothing** — it only creates the row. A numeric id makes a normal record; a handle the directory knows resolves to its id; otherwise a **placeholder** keyed by the handle (the usual Instagram case, since an IGSID only exists after the person writes). Adding someone already on file just selects them. A hand-added person who never wrote can be removed (`channels-remove-person`, also takes them off every list so the reconcile does not bring them back); anyone who has written is blocked, not deleted.
- **(4) Link.** A Discord and an Instagram record can be linked as one human (`linked`, stored on both sides, one partner each; linking again moves it). By id, @handle or **name** (a name must match exactly one person already on file; an id/@handle nobody has used creates a hand-added row). Panel: Profile tab → "Same person on …" with Open / Unlink; CLI `channels-link` / `channels-unlink`. **Identity only:** the model gets the shared name, a "same person as …" line and the other account's notes; **no permission is shared and `permissions.py` does not read it.** Linking to the owner's account does not make the other account the owner (the panel says so; the identity block still says "NOT your owner" and omits the "same person" line in that case).
- **Placeholder → real id.** On the first message from a handle-only person, `touch()` adopts the placeholder under the real id and **moves their `user_perms.json` entry with it** — a tool limit left under the handle would stop applying and widen access. `send_dm` skips handle-only people (nothing to address a DM to).
- **Files:** `channels/people.py`, `channels/user_admin.py`, `channels_cli.py` (+5 commands), `reserved_names.py`, `actions/channel_people.py`, `actions/send_dm.py`, `web/server.js` (+5 routes), `channels-panel.js`, `channels.css`, `index.html`, `slash-commands-data.js` (the five verbs under `channels`), `README.md`, `REPO_MAP.md`, `AGENTS.md` (one invariant), new `tests/test_channel_manual_people.py`, extended `tests/verify_channels_panel.js`.
- **Verified here:** `test_channel_manual_people.py` 79/79 (new), `test_user_admin` 97, `test_channels` 137, `test_channel_people` 24, `test_reserved_names` 12, `test_slash_coverage` 550, `test_checklist_coverage` 6, `verify_channels_panel.js` 49, `verify_slash_palette.js` 196; every `web/public/*.js` and `server.js` passes `node --check`. The full Python suite was started and **timed out in the sandbox, no result.**
- **Not verified:** **anything in a browser** (no Chromium/jsdom here — the new panel code, layout and CSS were never rendered or clicked), the real `server.js` routes (Express not installed; syntax-checked only), a live Discord/Instagram account, Windows, and the patch together with other pending `_87_` patches. Build number not bumped. No Test Checklist entry.
- **Decisions I took (owner may overrule):** a link shares identity, not permissions; the owner's typed name beats a guest's; adding a person grants nothing; Add person accepts a handle-only entry (placeholder) rather than requiring an id.
- **Open:** whether a link should ever carry permissions (not built, deliberately); editing a handle by hand; reconciling per-scope allow-lists.

## Revision 2026-10-05i (Channels: "+ Add a new person" opens its own panel — code + docs; `channels-add-person-panel.patch` against `jarvis-main_88_.zip`)

**Code and docs.** Owner request (L.36): *rework the add-person button in the Channels panel so it opens a whole new panel instead of that small thing.* Only the web UI changed — no server route, CLI verb, Python module or test file was touched.

- **What it is now.** `#btn-ch-add` opens `#channels-add-overlay` (`.debug-overlay.ch-add-overlay`, `z-index: 96`, one above the Channels overlay's 95), the same chrome as every other panel (header with close button, corners, footer). The Channels panel stays open underneath. The old inline `#ch-add` form and its `.ch-add*` CSS are removed.
- **Layout.** Left, a three-step form: **1 · Platform** (two radio cards, Discord / Instagram, arrow keys move between them), **2 · Who** (id or @handle, with a per-platform hint), **3 · Name** (optional). Right, **How they will appear** (a live preview card: avatar with hue and platform badge, name or handle, "Not seen yet" and "No reply" tags) and **What adding does** (grants nothing; the id fills in when they first write; a typed name is locked against the person's own "call me …"). Footer: Cancel and Add person.
- **Checks before the request.** The id is validated in the panel with the same rule `server.js` applies (`/^[A-Za-z0-9][A-Za-z0-9._-]{0,63}$/` after one leading `@` is stripped), so a typo or a name with spaces is caught without a round trip; the server's check is unchanged and still decides. If the platform/id already matches someone on file (by id or handle), a notice says adding will just open them — which is what the route already did (`existing`).
- **Behaviour.** Enter in either field adds; Escape closes **only** the add panel (`onKey` returns early while `state.adding`, so Channels stays open and nothing else reacts); Tab is trapped inside the panel; a click on the backdrop closes it **only if nothing has been typed**; on success the panel closes, the new person is selected on the People list (the existing `addPerson()` path), and focus returns to the button. Under 900 px the panel is full-screen like the other panels (a first version was not — see below).
- **Unchanged:** `POST /api/channels/people` with `{platform, ident, name}`, `jarvis channels-add-person`, "grants nothing", the placeholder-keyed record for a handle-only person, the locked name. Every string typed or shown still goes in with `textContent` (the only `innerHTML` in the file is still the fixed SVG icon strings). No new icon, no new dependency.
- **Files:** `web/public/index.html` (button no longer controls the inline form; the new overlay is placed before the Guides overlay), `web/public/channels.css` (`.ch-addp*` styles; the unused `.ch-add*` rules removed, the shared `.ch-name-input` / `.ch-link-input` rules kept), `web/public/channels-panel.js` (`renderAdd` rebuilt as the panel; `grabDom`, `onKey`, `ensureBuilt`, `addPerson` focus return; header comment). 3 files, 449-line patch.
- **Verified here:** the patch passes `git apply --check` on pristine copies of the three `_88_` files and reproduces the edited files byte for byte; `channels-panel.js` passes a syntax check; `node tests/verify_channels_panel.js` 49/49 (unchanged — pure helpers only). **In headless Chromium (Playwright) against a static server with the `/api/*` routes mocked:** the button opens the panel with focus in the id field; a name with a space shows the validation message; an id already on the list shows the duplicate notice; Escape closes only the add panel and leaves Channels open; Enter posts `{platform: "instagram", ident: "nour.ig", name: "Nour"}` and closes the panel; no page errors. Two screenshots (1400 px and 420 px wide) were looked at. **One bug found that way and fixed:** at phone width the panel was not full-screen, because `.ch-addp`'s own size beat the shared `.debug-panel` phone rule; a `max-width: 900px` rule now restores it.
- **Not verified:** the real `server.js` and a real `jarvis` process behind the form (the API was mocked); a live Discord/Instagram account; Firefox, Safari, a real phone; Windows; the full Python suite (not run — no Python file changed); the patch together with other pending `_88_` patches. The browser script was ad hoc and is **not** saved in the repo, so the new panel still has **no automated browser test**; `verify_channels_panel.js` does not cover it. No Test Checklist entry. Build number not bumped.
- **Decisions I took (owner may overrule):** the panel **stacks above** Channels rather than replacing it, so closing it lands back on the people list; it shows the live preview and the "what adding does" notes (not asked for — added to fill the larger panel and make "grants nothing" visible at the moment of adding); the id is checked client-side too; the backdrop does not discard typed text. `REPO_MAP.md`, `README.md` and `AGENTS.md` never described the inline form, so they were not changed.
- **Open:** whether the Channels panel's other small inline editors (the name pencil, the "Same person on …" link box) should become panels too — not requested, not done; the missing automated browser test for the new panel.

## Revision 2026-10-05l (Channels: P1 Conversation view, P2 Usage and P3 Test-as-this-person built — code + docs; `jarvis-channels-p1-p2-p3.patch` against `jarvis-main_89_.zip`)

**Code and docs.** Owner request: start the first batch of the Channels upgrade, **three features at a time** — **L.36-P1**, **P2**, **P3** (plan lines 11,492–11,494) — with one correction: *"Test as this person" does not save the conversation.* P4–P16 were **not** started. Baseline: plan `_56_` / audit `_41_`.

**What was built (16 files, +2,176/−37; new: `channels/usage.py`, `tests/test_channel_insights.py`, `tests/verify_l36_insights_ui.py`, `tests/_channels_fixture.py`).** Three tabs were added to the right of Permissions on every person; keys **3 / 4 / 5** open them. All three are **read-only**, load only when opened, never store a person's messages in the browser after the panel closes, and show every string as text, never markup.
- **P1 — Conversation.** What the person sent and how Jarvis answered, oldest first, grouped by day, their words on the left and Jarvis's on the right. A message the gate turned away shows **“Turned away”** with the stage and reason (`reply`, `dm_allowed`, …); a reply that failed to send shows its error. Newest 100 are shown, "Show older messages" raises it to a ceiling of 500; the full history stays in `jarvis channels-log`. *Attribution (the catch in the original entry):* `transcript.log_outbound` now takes an optional `to_user` and `base.handle_message` passes the sender, so a **new** reply in a group chat is tied to the person it answered. For lines written **before** this patch: a reply in a thread where **every** inbound line is a DM from that one person is attributed to them (marked `via: thread`); a reply in any other thread is attributed to **nobody**, and the tab says how many it left out ("N older replies in group chats aren't shown"). A thread that has only had one speaker so far is **not** assumed to be theirs, because someone else can join later. Rotated copies (`name.<stamp>.jsonl`) are read as part of their thread. A message over 4,000 characters is shortened in the view and says so.
- **P2 — Usage.** Over 7, 30 or 90 days: questions answered (and failed), tokens (total, average per answer, sent / written / extra thinking), provider requests, tool calls with the top tools, the providers that answered, messages sent / turned away / replied, a per-day bar chart, and their **share of that platform's tokens**. *The "unverified" question is answered:* nothing recorded who a request was for, so this is new plumbing — **`~/.jarvis/channels/usage.jsonl`**, one counts-only line per answered ask, written by `base.handle_message` from the ask's own ledger (`AskResult.usage_total`, the providers' real counts across every attempt, key and round). **It never contains a message, a reply, a tool's arguments or a tool's result**, and it is written even when `log_conversations` is off, for that reason. A message the gate refused costs nothing and writes nothing. A failed ask is counted as failed. The file rotates at 2 MB like the transcript and rotated copies are read; nothing is deleted.
- **P3 — Test.** Choose **Direct message** or **Group chat** (and, for a group, whether they **@mention** Jarvis) and see: the verdict (would answer / would ignore), the **gate step by step** (`✓` passed, `✗` the one that stopped it with its reason, `–` not reached), the **tools** they would get (everything / only the ticked list, shown with the helper tools Jarvis adds / none, with the reason — master switch off, not on the tool list, empty custom list, unreadable limits), and notes (below). **It is a dry run:** it builds an in-memory message and calls the real `permissions.decide` and `user_perms.resolve_tool_access`; it calls **no model, sends nothing, writes no transcript line, no usage line, no `people.json` touch, does not mark the cooldown clock and creates no conversation** — so it never appears in the person's Conversation or Usage. The result carries `saved: false, model_called: false` and the tab says so on screen. *Deviation from the plan's wording ("type a sample message"):* **there is no text box**, because no stage of the gate reads the text; offering one would imply the wording matters. If the owner wants one anyway it is a small addition, but it would not change any result.
- **One refactor, behaviour unchanged.** The per-message tool decision (gate says yes → per-person limits → `may_use_tools` / `tool_scope` / the log label) moved out of `base.handle_message` into **`user_perms.resolve_tool_access()`**, which `base` and the Test tab both call, so the dry run cannot drift from what a real message gets. It fails closed exactly as before (unreadable or failing limits → this message runs with tools off); the log lines and labels are the same strings.
- **CLI and routes.** `jarvis channels-conversation <platform> <id|@handle> [limit]`, `jarvis channels-usage <platform> <id|@handle> [days]`, `jarvis channels-user-test <platform> <id|@handle> dm | group [mentioned|unmentioned]` — JSON on stdout, exit 1 on an unknown or unregistered person, `@handle` resolved only against people on file; all three added to `reserved_names.py` and the slash registry. `server.js`: `GET /api/channels/people/:platform/:id/conversation?limit=`, `GET …/usage?days=`, `POST …/test` — argv arrays only, ids regex-validated, `limit` / `days` bare integers clamped to 1–500 / 1–90, `context` must be `dm` or `group`. The Test route is a POST so a stray prefetch or link preview cannot trigger it, though it changes nothing.
- **Invariants kept.** Registered people only (enforced in `user_admin`, not just the UI); `tool_safety.py`, confirmation prompts, `risk_review()`, `MAX_TOOL_ROUNDS` and `permissions.decide` untouched; no switch, allow-list or `user_perms.json` value can be written by any of the three; bot tokens never pass through the browser; guest data stays in `people.py`, never `memory.py`. `AGENTS.md` has a new invariant for the three views.

**Limits the Test tab states on screen (so it does not over-promise).** **Cooldown** is not simulated — it depends on when they last wrote, which only the running bot knows (shown whenever a cooldown is configured). **Server / channel filters** (`allowed_guilds`, `allowed_channels`) and **per-scope overrides** (`scopes`) are **not applied**, because the test names no particular server or channel; for a group test the tab says so. If a person is marked blocked but a `"*"` entry still lets them through, or `send_dm` is off for them, the tab says that too.

**Other limits and honest caveats.**
- **History starts when the ledger does.** Tokens, tool calls and "share of platform" count only from the first message answered after this patch is applied; before that the Usage tab says "tokens and tool calls haven't been recorded yet". The **message** counts (sent, turned away, replied) come from the transcript and cover the whole history.
- **Tool names come from the answering attempt only** (`AskResult.usage["tool_calls"]`); calls made on a provider attempt that then failed over are in the token total but not in the tool list.
- **Tokens, not money.** The repo has no price table and several keys are free tiers, so no dollar figure is shown anywhere.
- **Replies are only tied to a person from this patch on.** Older group-chat replies stay unattributed (see P1); nothing was rewritten or migrated.
- A **handle-only (placeholder) person** has no id yet, so they have no transcript or usage until their first message.
- Cached messages are dropped when the panel closes or Refresh is pressed; a person's tab data is fetched once per open and again on Refresh.

**Verified here (sandbox, before the final cosmetic edits noted below).** `python3 tests/test_channel_insights.py` **125/125** (new). It pins, among others: a DM and a group thread attributed correctly and **never leaking between people**, rotated files, torn lines, the 500 cap; one **counts-only** usage line per ask with the question and answer **provably absent from the file**; failed and refused asks; windows, per-day series, tool ranking, platform share, rotated ledgers; the stage list **forced against the real gate** (a denial at every stage of `decide()` must appear in `GATE_STAGES`, in order); and **`simulate` agreeing with what `handle_message` really hands the model** for five configurations plus unreadable limits. **The no-save requirement is a test:** the whole `~/.jarvis` tree is snapshotted (size and mtime of every file) around `simulate`, `conversation_view`, `usage_view` and all three CLI verbs, and must be identical afterwards; no model is called; the cooldown clock is untouched. Two deliberate breakages were checked to fail the suite: attributing a legacy group reply to anyone who spoke (5 failures) and a dry run that quietly marks the cooldown clock (1 failure). Existing related suites still pass on the patched tree: `test_channels` 137, `test_user_admin` 97, `test_channel_manual_people` 79, `test_channel_people` 24, `test_send_dm` 22, `test_reserved_names` 12, `test_slash_coverage` 550, plus `test_daemon_command_split`, `test_doctor_saved_commands` and `test_l41_prompt_no_commands`. `node tests/verify_channels_panel.js` **61/61** (was 49; 12 new checks on the day grouping, token formatting and bar model). **`python3 tests/verify_l36_insights_ui.py` — new, saved in the repo — 48/48 in headless Chromium**, driven by **real backend output** (`tests/_channels_fixture.py` seeds a throwaway HOME and calls the same functions the CLI calls): the five tabs, lazy loading, the **`<img onerror>` message shown as text with no element and no script**, no Markdown rendering, newest message in view, turned-away reasons, no refetch on revisit, error → Try again, range chips, the dry run's verdict / steps / tool chips, that the Test tab **only ever POSTs to its own `/test` route**, a slow reply for the previous person **not** overwriting the next one, keys 3 and 5, and no sideways overflow at 390 px. Screenshots at desktop and phone width were looked at. **The patch passes `git apply --check` on a fresh `jarvis-main_89_.zip` and reproduces the working tree byte for byte.** `web/server.js` passes a syntax check.
- **Bugs found by the new tests and fixed:** keyboard focus was lost whenever the Test controls redrew (now `renderDetail` restores focus by element id, which also keeps focus on the tabs); the Test tab's Tools card said "Answers only" even when the person would not be answered at all; the active tab could sit off-screen on a phone; the footer hint still said "1 2 tab".

**Not verified.**
- The **final cosmetic edits** — the footer hint (`1–5`), the "not answered, so no tools" wording, the verdict text colour and scrolling the active tab into view — were made **after** the last browser run and were **not re-run** (only a syntax check and `verify_channels_panel.js`). The Python suites were not re-run after the patch was cut, either, and no code in them changed since.
- The real **`server.js`** (Express is not installed here — the three routes were syntax-checked and exercised only through a mocked API), a **live Discord or Instagram account** (no real gateway ever wrote a `to_user` line or a usage line; the ledger was fed by `handle_message` with a fake model), **real token counts from a real provider**, Firefox / Safari / a real phone, Windows, the full Python suite, the patch together with other pending patches.
- Token counts shown by P2 are only as good as `AskResult.usage_total` for each provider; that was read, not checked against live provider responses.
- **Build number not bumped** — run `python build_tools/bump_build_version.py` from `jarvis-cli/` after applying. **No Test Checklist entry** (these are panel features, not tools).

**Decisions I took (owner may overrule).** No sample-message box on Test (see above); Test takes **DM / group + @mention** rather than text; the usage ledger is **separate** from `logs.py` and the transcript, and is written even when `log_conversations` is off, because it holds no text; **older** group replies are left unattributed rather than guessed; the ledger is capped by rotation only, not by age; "Show older" ceilings at 500; the three tabs load lazily; **Test** is a POST route although it changes nothing.

**Open.** Whether the owner wants a text box on Test anyway; whether Usage should also show a per-conversation breakdown; whether the ledger should have a retention limit; a Test Checklist entry for the panel; the older per-person and add-person panels still have **no browser test of their own** (P16's remaining part — the three new tabs now do); whether the Test tab should, later, let the owner pick a particular server or channel so the location filters can be applied. **P4–P16 are unchanged and still suggestions.**

**Docs updated with this revision:** this block, the three bullets above, `REPO_MAP.md` (files, state table, commands, tests), `AGENTS.md` (new invariant; the new browser verifier in the test list) and `README.md` (the three tabs and CLI verbs).

## Revision 2026-10-05l (Focus "more" menu fixed; people who DM Jarvis before being allowed now get a Channels row — code + docs; `jarvis-focus-menu-and-people-fixes.patch` against `jarvis-main_86_.zip`)

**Code and docs.** Owner report on the new UI: (1) the Instagram people in the Channels panel do not show up, and some Discord people do not either, **even though they have DMed Jarvis**; (2) in the new Focus mode, pressing the menu button to open "more" leaves nothing clickable, and pressing in a certain place makes the **Ask Jarvis** surface disappear. 6 files.

- **Cause of (1).** The panel lists `people.json` records, and `base.handle_message` only created one for a sender the gate let through. Someone who DMed Jarvis **before** being on an allow-list was turned away *before* a record was made, so the panel had no row to click to let them in — a chicken-and-egg. (Instagram senders are almost all in this group; some Discord people are too.) This is **separate from** the 2026-10-05h cause (people *added* to an allow-list without ever writing), which that revision fixed with `adopt_listed`.
- **Fix.** `channels/base.py`: a sender who **actually addressed** Jarvis (a DM, or an @mention / reply) is now registered with `people.touch` even when the gate refuses them. It creates / refreshes the record only: **grants nothing, answers nothing, does not ping the owner.** Unaddressed chatter in a busy server is still **not** recorded (`addressed_to_us`). A failure to register is logged, never raised. `instagram_gateway.py`: senders now also get a best-effort profile picture (`_fetch_profile_pic`, Graph `profile_pic`, separate from the username lookup so a missing field can never break the name lookup; `people.py` still re-checks the host against its image-CDN allow-list). Panel copy in `channels-panel.js` updated ("first time they DM or mention Jarvis"). **Not retroactive:** people whose earlier messages were never recorded appear after their next message.
- **Cause of (2).** Two things. The portaled "more" list (`.panel-menu__list`, `position: fixed`, `z-index: 70`) sat **below** the full-screen Ask overlay in Focus (it is the page there), so clicks landed on the overlay instead of the items; and the overlay's own click handler closes Ask for any click whose target is the overlay itself — which in Focus is every click on its margins. **Fix:** `style.css` raises the list to `z-index: 9000`; `app.js` makes the overlay-click close a no-op while `currentLayout === "focus"` (classic layout unchanged). The comment above the rule in `style.css` still says "below full-screen overlays (85+)" — it is now stale (the list sits above them); not corrected, since a delivered patch is not edited.
- **Tests.** New `tests/test_denied_sender_registered.py` (a refused DM is registered; no owner-ping state; unaddressed chatter is not). Passing in the sandbox: `test_user_admin` 97, `test_channels` 137, `test_channel_people` 24, `test_directory` 18, `test_recent_dms` 15, `test_send_dm` 22; `node --check` on `app.js` and `channels-panel.js`; the patch passes `patch --dry-run` on a pristine `_86_`. The full suite was not run.
- **Not verified:** **the Focus fix was never clicked in a browser** (no browser run for this patch); a live Discord / Instagram account; whether Meta returns `profile_pic` for this app's permissions; the patch on `_87_` / `_88_` — `base.py` and `people.py` were changed by the 2026-10-05h patch (placeholder adoption in `touch()`); the interaction is unchecked. Build number not bumped.
- **Relates to L.36-P14** (recent denied senders): this change makes P14's premise partly moot — an addressed sender is now "registered" — and it **reverses the assumption** recorded there that L.36 reads "registered" as "has passed the gate". Privacy: a stranger who DMs now has a handle, name and avatar URL in `people.json`.
- **Open:** whether strangers should appear in the main People list or a separate "not allowed yet" section (P14); an expiry for never-allowed records.
