## Revision 2026-10-05n (L.46 recorded — draft backups, daemon / persona / UI-element switches, tool-shipped web files, new template examples — documented only, nothing built)

**Doc-only.** Owner request, with the instruction *"add these in the docs, don't implement anything yet."* No code, test, patch or `REPO_MAP.md` / `AGENTS.md` / `README.md` change. Source read in the `_86_` tree; nothing run.

- **Written:** new section **L.46** (after L.45) with four parts — **L.46.1** server-side draft backups for unsaved tools (today: one `.bak` of the previous *saved* version on the server; unsaved text only in the browser's `localStorage` from L.45, plus an in-memory Undo copy); **L.46.2** Tool Manager rows and switches for **daemons, personas and UI elements** (today `disabled.json` covers tools and saved commands only; this is the known "tool-owned extras are not switched off with their tool" gap); **L.46.3** tools that ship their own **`tool.js` / `tool.html` / `tool.css`** in a declared folder, presented as a **button that opens the page** or a **Menu entry that opens a panel in a div** (builds on D.2.2's decided `render: inline | sandboxed` and declared-actions message API; the wire format is still unwritten); **L.46.4** **template examples**, with the **old UI-bridge (`ui`) template kept unchanged**.
- **Pointers added:** under **D.2.2** and **L.12**, and in the Part L list of the status audit.
- **Findings worth knowing:** custom tools are **flat `.py` files** today, so "tools in folders" is a loader and routes change, not just a manifest field; an **inline** `tool.js` would run in the owner's page with access to every `/api/*` route, so it is at least as powerful as the tool's Python — sandboxed should stay the default; **drafts could hold pasted secrets** on disk (Q-L46b); the **L.25 meaning of "off"** (the model can't see it) does not fit daemons, personas or UI, so L.46.2 proposes a per-kind meaning.
- **Opened Q-L46a–l.** Needed first: **Q-L46e / Q-L46f** (does "daemons, personas, UI elements" mean everything or only what a tool brought; what counts as a "UI element"), **Q-L46b** (secrets in drafts), **Q-L46h** (declaration shape). Suggested order (opinion): drafts, then persona / user-daemon switches, then folder tools with templates.
- **Not checked:** whether `tool_loader.py` would load or choke on subfolders; how Menu entries are registered; `_87_` / `_88_` changes; nothing run.

## Revision 2026-10-05o (Channels: P4 Quick setups and P5 Bulk edit built — code + docs; `jarvis-channels-p4-p5.patch` against `jarvis-main_91_.zip`)

**Code and docs.** Owner request: do the next Channels upgrade, **only P4 and P5**, **skip testing** (the owner tests it), cut the `.patch` against the supplied repo, present it, and only then update the audit and plan. P6–P16 were **not** started. Baseline: plan `_58_` (merged with `_57_`) / audit `_43_` (merged with `_42_`).

**What was built (13 files, +1,190/−14; new: `channels/presets.py`, `channels/preset_admin.py`).**
- **P4 — Quick setups.** A row of four buttons at the top of a person's **Permissions** tab: **No access** (not answered, no DMs, no tools), **Chat only** (DM + replies, no tools), **Chat + tell the owner** (DM + replies + tools limited to `notify_owner`, the one tool a guest is already steered to, L.28) and **Trusted** (DM + replies + every tool the platform allows; owner-only tools such as `send_dm` stay owner-only). **Clicking only previews:** each switch is listed as *will change / already / can't* with its before → after, plus any heads-up (for example the platform's master `allow_tools` switch being off). **Apply** is a second click; **Trusted** also needs a tick-box. After applying, the result stays on screen (what changed, what was refused) until dismissed.
- **P5 — Bulk edit.** **Select people…** above the list turns each card into a tick-box (All shown / None / Done; Esc leaves). **Edit selected…** replaces the person view with an editor for the ticked people: pick a **quick setup** (a per-person preview for the whole group, then Apply) or **one switch** (DMs, Replies, Tool use *off*, Jarvis may DM them, Blocked). The result is a **per-person list**; anyone who could not be changed is shown with the reason and the rest still apply. Anyone with an unsaved tool list open blocks the action until saved or discarded, so a bulk write cannot overwrite it.
- **One implementation.** `preset_admin.py` changes nothing except by calling `user_admin.set_flag` and `user_admin.set_tools` — the calls the single switches make — so a setup can only produce states the switches can produce, and every refusal they already make still happens. `server.js` shells out to the CLI as for every other Channels route.
- **One refactor, behaviour meant to be unchanged.** The two `dm / reply / tool` refusals (turning one **on** for a blocked person; turning one **off** for someone a `"*"` entry covers) moved from `set_flag` into `user_admin.list_flag_refusal()`, which `set_flag` and the preview both call, so a preview cannot promise what the switch would then refuse. `list_view()` now also returns the list of presets.
- **CLI and routes.** `jarvis channels-presets` (the list, JSON); `jarvis channels-preset <platform> <id|@handle> <setup> [preview]`; `jarvis channels-bulk flag <switch> <on|off> <platform:id> …` and `jarvis channels-bulk preset|preview <setup> <platform:id> …`. All three are in `reserved_names.py` and under the `channels` verb's `covers` in `slash-commands-data.js`. `server.js`: `GET /api/channels/presets`, `POST /api/channels/people/:platform/:id/preset` (`{preset, preview?}`), `POST /api/channels/bulk` (`{action: flag|preset|preview, …, people:[{platform,id}]}`) — argv arrays only, every value validated, 100 people at most, 60 s timeout on bulk.
- **Repo docs amended in the same patch:** `REPO_MAP.md` (the two modules, the three verbs, the panel row), `AGENTS.md` (a new invariant for quick setups and bulk edits) and `README.md` (the feature and the commands).

**Invariants kept.** Registered people only (enforced in `user_admin`, not just the UI); `permissions.decide`, `tool_safety.py`, confirmation prompts and `MAX_TOOL_ROUNDS` untouched; a setup that turns tools on writes the **tool list first and the `tool` switch second** and does **not** turn it on if the list failed (so a failure never means "every tool" by accident); a setup never touches **ownership, `send_dm`, blocking or the platform's `allow_tools`**; bot tokens never pass through the browser; guest data stays in `people.py` / `user_perms.json`, never `memory.py`. Every string from a person is shown as text, not markup.

**Decisions I took (owner may overrule).**
- **Presets are fixed in code**, not an owner-editable file (the plan left this open): a tool list is a permission, so adding one should be a reviewed change. The cost is that the owner cannot make a "Friends" preset without a code edit.
- **The four setups and their contents are mine** (the plan only gave "Chat only" and "Trusted" as examples). *Chat + tell the owner* assumes `notify_owner` is the right single tool for a limited guest.
- **A setup is refused for the owner's own account**: a custom tool list limits the owner inside chats too (L.36), so one click could lock the owner out of their own bot. The owner's switches remain on their own page.
- **A setup that turns tools off leaves any stored tool list alone** (it only switches `tool` off), the same as flipping the switch by hand.
- **Bulk edit may not set Owner** (one per platform), and **may switch Tool use off but not on** — turning it on without saying which tools is the broadest grant there is, so that goes through a setup. The server refuses both, not just the UI.
- **No per-person preview for a single switch** in bulk; the confirm text says refusals are listed afterwards. Previews exist for setups only.
- **Selection is not kept** when the panel closes. Bulk previews are thrown away when the ticked group changes, so an old preview can never describe a different set of people.
- **No before/after confirmation dialog beyond the preview itself** (the plan asked whether to show one): the preview *is* the before/after.

**Not run, not verified (owner's instruction: no testing).**
- **Nothing was executed.** Checks made: `py_compile` and `node --check` on every changed file; one import of `preset_admin`, `channels_cli` and `user_admin`; `git apply --check` on a fresh `_91_` and a byte comparison of the applied tree against the working tree. **No Python suite, no Node verifier, no browser, no CLI run, no real `server.js`, no live Discord / Instagram.**
- **No new tests were written.** Behaviour that most needs one: a preset or bulk write really leaves `user_perms.json` and the allow-lists in the expected state; every refusal path is returned per person; the tool-list-first ordering when the list write fails; the bulk preview matching what Apply does; `set_flag` behaving exactly as before after the refactor.
- **Run before relying on it:** `test_user_admin`, `test_channels`, `test_channel_insights`, `test_channel_manual_people`, `test_reserved_names`, `test_slash_coverage` and `node tests/verify_channels_panel.js` (the last because the panel's exported helpers gained `summaryText`; the existing checks were not changed). Then use the panel once on a throwaway person: preview, Apply, and a bulk run that includes the owner and a blocked person.
- **UI not seen by anyone:** layout of the new row, the select bar and the bulk editor at desktop and phone width, keyboard flow (Esc order: bulk editor → select mode → search → close), focus handling after a redraw, and the `.ch-card--pick` grid. The `channels-panel.js` footer still reads "1–5 tab" (unchanged).
- **Build number not bumped** (run `python build_tools/bump_build_version.py` from `jarvis-cli/` after applying). **No Test Checklist entry** (panel feature, as for P1–P3).
- **Not tried together with other pending patches** touching `index.html`, `channels-panel.js`, `server.js` or `channels_cli.py`.

**Open.**
- Should presets become owner-editable, and should the owner be able to name their own (for example "Friends")?
- Is `notify_owner` the right and only tool for *Chat + tell the owner*? Is *Trusted* wanted at all, given it is the broadest grant the system has?
- Should a setup also carry the per-person thinking switch (L.44) and the inbound-images grant (L.36-P8 / L.42) once those exist? Neither was touched.
- Should bulk **Tool use on** exist with a shared tool picker, instead of going through a setup?
- Should a setup be able to include `send_dm`? Today it never does.
- P15 (a change log of permission flips) matters more now: a single click can change many people and nothing records who or when. Still unbuilt.
- **P6–P16 are unchanged** and still suggestions; P9, P11, P13 and P14 still need an owner decision first.

**Docs updated with this revision:** this block, the P4 / P5 entries and the new Update line under L.36 above, `REPO_MAP.md`, `AGENTS.md` and `README.md` (in the patch).

## Revision 2026-10-05p (Markdown in the Channels conversation view and the Tool Manager's Ask Jarvis dock; the editor no longer looks reloaded while Jarvis edits — code + docs; `jarvis-markdown-and-live-editor.patch` against `jarvis-main_91_.zip`)

**Code and docs.** Owner request: (1) Markdown support for Jarvis in the Channels panel's conversations and in the new Ask Jarvis dock in the Tool Manager; (2) in the Tool Manager, every Jarvis edit made the code area reload, so the edit couldn't be watched live. Instructions: skip testing (the owner tests), say what to test, **present the patch first and only then update these two documents**. 8 files, front-end only, no server or CLI change.

- **Built:** one shared renderer, `window.JarvisMarkdown.renderInto` (`app.js`; marked + DOMPurify + KaTeX like the chat, **no images**, links in a new tab, an open code fence closed while streaming), styled by `.jv-md` (`style.css`). Used by `channels-panel.js` (only Jarvis's lines; a person's own text stays plain) and by the Ask Jarvis dock in `tool-manager.js` (Jarvis's notes only; the owner's text and errors stay plain). Details under L.45 and L.36.
- **The "reload" bug:** every streamed chunk called `setValue()`, which resets scroll and caret and repaints from scratch, then scrolled back to the end; on an edit the editor also showed only the new text so far, so the file visibly shrank and regrew. **Fix:** new `stream()` in `code-editor.js` (no reset, marks the line being written, follows it only when it leaves the view); the dock shows the arrived lines over the old file, old lines not yet reached dimmed (`overwriteView`); end-of-edit, Undo and restore keep the view; a provider that can't stream is typed in by lines over at most ~1.5 s; Stop and interruptions keep the new text and drop the old tail.
- **Not tried together with `jarvis-channels-p4-p5.patch`** (also against `_91_`, revision 2026-10-05o): both edit `channels-panel.js` and `channels.css`, in different places as far as I know, but I have not seen that patch — apply one, then `patch --dry-run` the other; if a hunk is rejected, it is the `messageNode()` body here that needs re-anchoring. Everything else in this patch is in files that patch's list does not name.
- **Files:** `web/public/app.js`, `channels-panel.js`, `channels.css`, `code-editor.js`, `code-editor.css`, `tool-manager.js`, `tool-manager.css`, `style.css`.
- **Checked:** `node --check` on the four changed scripts that were touched in logic (`app.js`, `channels-panel.js`, `code-editor.js`, `tool-manager.js`); `patch --dry-run` and a real apply on a pristine `_91_` extract, result identical to the working tree. **Nothing else was run** — no test, no browser, no model.
- **Not verified:** all of it in a real browser; live streaming through the real server; the dimmed-text view and the scroll-follow on a long file; Markdown tables / code blocks / math inside the narrow dock and the Channels bubbles; a non-streaming provider (typed-in reveal); Stop during the reveal. `verify_tool_manager_ui.py` may need a short wait after the mocked reply (see L.45). Build number not bumped; no Test Checklist entry.
- **Code comments say "L.45" for the Channels part as well** — the Channels part belongs to L.36; a delivered patch is not edited, so the comments stay as shipped.
- **Docs updated with this revision:** this block, the L.45 and L.36 updates, and the audit. **Not touched** (not in this doc set): `REPO_MAP.md` (new `window.JarvisMarkdown`, `stream()` on the editor, `.jv-md`), `AGENTS.md`, `README.md`.
- **Open:** see the end of the L.45 update — dimmed old text vs blank-then-type; Markdown for inbound messages; permanent tests for `overwriteView` and the renderer.

## Revision 2026-10-05q (Discord servers panel + tool calls in the Conversation view documented; bare-id `allowed_guilds` crash fixed — code + docs; `discord-servers-and-tool-calls.patch` (already in `jarvis-main_93_.zip`) and `jarvis-fix-bare-id-where-filters.patch` against `jarvis-main_93_.zip`)

**Code and docs.** Two parts. **(1)** This revision documents `discord-servers-and-tool-calls.patch` — it was in `jarvis-main_93_.zip` but had no entry in this document. **(2)** The owner ran `jarvis channels-servers` on an installed copy and got a traceback; that is fixed here and pinned by a test.

### Part 1 — what `discord-servers-and-tool-calls.patch` changed (12 files, +1,476/−17)

It delivers **L.36-P7** (per-server / per-channel overrides) and a second feature: **the tools Jarvis used are shown in the Channels Conversation view.**

**A. Discord servers: registry, names and switches**
- **New `channels/servers.py`** (pure of any Discord SDK; the gateway hands in ids and strings). Two separate jobs:
  1. **A registry** — `note_guild` / `note_channel` / `forget_channel` / `read`, stored in `~/.jarvis/channels/servers.json` as `{platform: {guild_id: {name, left, seen, channels: {id: {name, kind}}}}}`. **Names only — never a message, never a member list.** It is a cache: losing it costs the panel its labels and changes no behaviour. Bounded (500 servers, 1,000 channels per server); a re-announce of identical facts is not rewritten; every writer never raises.
  2. **Switches** — `set_switch(platform, kind, ident, switch, value)`, writing **only** into `scopes` of the platform block in `channels.json` (`"guild:<id>"` / `"channel:<id>"`, the override mechanism `permissions.resolve_scope()` already had).
- **The switches can only take access away** (same principle as `user_perms.py`): `enabled` off → `"enabled": false`, on → the key is **removed** (inherit); `tools` off → `"allow_tools": false`, on → inherit; `mention` on → `"require_mention": true`, off is **refused**. A scope `true` is never written, because it would override a switched-off platform and so GRANT access. Ids must be digits-only; kind / switch / value are validated before anything is written, and hand-written fields in a scope are preserved.
- **`allowed_guilds` / `allowed_channels` are deliberately not written by this module** — they are "empty = unrestricted", so removing the last entry would silently open every server. They are read and reported (a server outside them shows as not answering) and stay hand-edited.
- **`servers.view(platform)`** is the read model the panel and the CLI use: every known server (plus servers only the config mentions, shown unnamed) with its channels, the **effective** state using the same rules `decide()` does (channel override beats server override beats platform) and the reasons it is not answering (`Discord is switched off`, `switched off here`, `not in allowed_guilds`, `not in allowed_channels`), and `orphans` (config channels in no known server). It never carries the bot token. Instagram reports `supported: false` (its groups have thread ids, no servers).
- **`discord_gateway.py`** learns names for free: on `on_ready` it records every guild and its text channels; `on_guild_join` / `on_guild_update` / `on_guild_remove` (marks the server *left*) / `on_guild_channel_create` / `_update` / `_delete` keep the list current. All ride on the `guilds` intent already in use — no new or privileged intent, no message content.
- **Threads now route to their parent channel.** `discord_gateway._where()` reports a message in a Discord thread with the **parent** as its `channel_id` and the thread's own id as `thread_id` (`permissions.scope_keys` already had a `thread:` rung). Effect: `allowed_channels` and `channel:<id>` switches apply to a thread the way people expect — a thread inside an allowed channel is allowed, one outside is not. Everywhere else `thread_id == channel_id`, as before.
- **`IncomingMessage` gained `guild_name` and `channel_name`** (`permissions.py`) — display only, **no stage of `decide()` reads them** (the gate matches ids; any user with Manage Channels can rename a channel). `transcript.log_inbound` stores them on the line when known.
- **CLI:** `jarvis channels-servers [platform]` (JSON) and `jarvis channels-server-set <platform> guild|channel <id> <enabled|tools|mention> <on|off|inherit>` (exit 1 with `ok: false` on a refusal). Both are in `channels_cli.COMMANDS`, `reserved_names.py` and the slash-command data.
- **Web:** `GET /api/channels/servers?platform=` and `POST /api/channels/servers/:platform/:kind/:id` in `web/server.js` (digits-only id, kind / switch / value allow-lists, so `-x` never reaches the CLI's flag parser; nothing there touches the two allowed-lists). `channels-panel.js` adds a **Discord servers** section under the Discord platform block: a collapsible card per server (name, id, channel count, **Answering / Not answering / Left**), three switches per server, one **Answer here** switch per channel, notes about `allowed_guilds` / `allowed_channels` being set and about orphan channels, and a plain line that the switches only take access away. A locked switch states why (for example *the whole server is switched off — turn the server on first*, *Tools are off for all of Discord*). `channels.css` styles it.

**B. Tool calls in the Conversation view**
- **`base._ask_jarvis(..., tool_log=None)`** collects `{name, arguments}` for every tool the model calls, from the **same callback the stall watchdog already uses** — no new hook into `ai_client`. `handle_message` stamps the start of the ask (`_utc_stamp()`, same format `raw_archive` uses) and afterwards builds the records with **`_tool_calls_for_log`**: when the raw event log (`raw_archive`, L.38) has `tool_run` events for this conversation since the stamp, those are the source (name, arguments **and result**, plus approved / declined for a confirmation); otherwise the captured calls are used with no outcome rather than dropped. It never raises.
- **`transcript.py`:** `tool_call_record()` (pure, never raises), `clean_tool_calls()` (applied on write **and** on read, so an old or hand-edited line cannot hand the panel a wrong type or an unbounded string), `MAX_TOOL_CALLS = 25` per reply, arguments clipped to 300 characters and results to 500, and **secret-looking keys scrubbed** (`token`, `secret`, `password`, `api_key`, `authorization`, `cookie`, `credential`, `private_key`). `ok` is `null` when no result was captured. The record rides on the reply's **first** logged line (`tool_calls` on a `dir: "out"` line), so it is attributed to the same person; a long reply split into chunks carries it on the first chunk only. `read_person()` now also returns `guild_id` / `channel_id` / `guild_name` / `channel_name` on inbound entries and `tool_calls` on outbound ones. **Older lines still read fine.**
- **Only when `log_conversations` is on.** With it off, nothing is recorded (unlike `usage.py`, which records tool *names* and counts regardless). A person without tool access has no tool calls.
- **Web:** each reply that used tools gets a collapsible **“Used N tools — names”** row above it (a `×2` count for repeats, a red **“N failed”** tag, per-call `with …` / `result` / `error` lines, a notice when values were shortened and the full run is in the raw log); a **Hide tool calls / Show tool calls** button in the Conversation header (shown only when some entry has tool calls); and a `#channel · Server` label on group messages.

**C. Tests.** New `tests/test_channel_servers.py` (S1–S7: registry, switches checked against the **real** `permissions.decide()`, the read model, tool-call scrubbing / clipping / read-back, `handle_message` end to end, thread routing with fake discord objects, the CLI). **99 checks, all passing on `_93_`** before the fix below.

### Part 2 — the bug

**Symptom (owner's installed copy):**
```
jarvis channels-servers
  File ".../jarvis/channels/servers.py", line 309, in view
    allowed_g = _ids(cfg.get("allowed_guilds"))
  File ".../jarvis/channels/servers.py", line 296, in _ids
    return [str(v).strip() for v in (value or []) if str(v).strip()]
TypeError: 'int' object is not iterable
```
**Cause.** `channels.json` is documented as hand-editable, and `"allowed_guilds": 123456789012345678` — a bare number, no brackets — is the obvious thing to type (JSON has a number type; a Discord id is a number). `load_config()` normalized the four permission sets and `owner` (a bare string or int where a list belongs is "the single most common hand-edit mistake") but **never** normalized `allowed_guilds` / `allowed_channels`, so the raw int reached `servers._ids()`, which iterated it. **It is the same bug class as the `resolve_scope()` / `permissions.matches()` one recorded earlier, in a field that fix did not cover.** A bare string was worse: it would have been iterated character by character (`"123"` → `["1","2","3"]`).

**It was not only the panel.** `permissions.decide()` read the same two fields with `[str(g) for g in guilds]`, so a bare id there would have raised in the **gate itself** (`stage="error"`, the message denied) the first time someone wrote in a server — the confusing "the gate is broken" failure mode `resolve_scope`'s note describes. And a scope override carrying `"allowed_channels": <int>` skipped normalization too.

**Fix (three layers, one normalizer — `config.normalize_entries`, which already accepts a string, an int, a list, a set or `None`):**
1. `channels/config.py` — new `LOCATION_SETS = ("allowed_guilds", "allowed_channels")`; `load_config()` normalizes both to a list of clean id strings exactly as it does the allow-lists (the boundary fix).
2. `channels/permissions.py` — `resolve_scope()` normalizes `LOCATION_SETS` in a scope override too, and `decide()` runs both filters through `config.normalize_entries` (so a hand-built cfg, as tests and the Test tab use, cannot crash the gate either). Behaviour for well-formed lists is unchanged.
3. `channels/servers.py` — `_ids()` now delegates to `config.normalize_entries`.

**Semantics after the fix.** A bare id is a list of one (`allowed_guilds: 123` restricts to that server); `null`, `""` and a list of blanks are "unrestricted"; a string is one entry (it is **not** split on commas — write a list for several). Nothing the owner has to change in `channels.json`.

**Tests.** `tests/test_channel_servers.py` gains `test_bare_id_where_filters_do_not_crash` (+18 checks, **117 in the file**): the raw file is written with a bare int, a bare string, a list with a blank and a `None`, then `servers.view`, `load_config`, the gate (`decide` with a hand-built cfg: admits the matching place, still refuses another server at stage `where`) and a scope override are checked. **It fails on the unfixed code with the owner's exact `TypeError` (5 failures) and passes on the fix.**

**Verified here (sandbox, `jarvis-main_93_`):** `test_channel_servers` **117/117**, `test_channels` **137/137**, `test_channel_insights` **125/125**, `test_user_admin` **97/97**, `test_channel_people` 24/24, `test_channel_manual_people` 79/79, `test_directory` 18/18; the rest of `tests/` run in parallel, all green except two noted below; `py_compile` on the three changed modules.
- `tests/test_build_info.py` **fails on the untouched `_93_` as well** (stale `SOURCE_HASH`) — pre-existing; run `python build_tools/bump_build_version.py` from `jarvis-cli/` after applying (the build number is **not** bumped here).
- `tests/test_h15_daemon_editor.py` failed once under the parallel run and passes 19/19 alone, twice, and on the untouched tree — load flakiness, not this change.

**Not verified:** a live Discord gateway (the registry, the guild events and the thread routing were exercised with fake objects only); the real `server.js` routes and the **Discord servers** panel in a browser (no browser run was done here); the owner's installed copy — the traceback came from `...\Python314\site-packages\jarvis`, **an installed copy under `site-packages`, which only picks up the fix once it is reinstalled from the patched tree.**

**Docs updated with this revision:** this block, the L.36-P7 entry and an Update line under L.36 above, `REPO_MAP.md` (files, state table, commands, tests), `AGENTS.md` (new invariant: switches only take access away; never iterate a config list directly) and `README.md` (the Discord servers card, the tool-call rows, the two CLI verbs).

**Open.** Should the panel also let the owner edit `allowed_guilds` / `allowed_channels` (today: hand-edit only, on purpose)? Should a bare string with commas be split? Should the Test tab (L.36-P3) simulate the server / channel filters it currently states it cannot (see Revision 2026-10-05l)?

## Revision 2026-10-05r (Channels: L.36-P11 editable notes and "forget this person", plus an editable Name in Details — code + docs; `jarvis-channels-p11-notes-forget.patch` against `jarvis-main_94_.zip`)

**Code and docs.** The owner picked **L.36-P11** with "do this" and asked for the **Name** field in the Details list (the one that reads "— not told yet") to be editable too. **Owner's instruction: skip testing** — the owner will test by hand. Done here: `py_compile` on every changed Python file, `node --check` on every changed JS file, and `git apply --check` of the patch on a fresh extract of `jarvis-main_94_.zip` (clean). **No test was run and none was written.** 14 files, +688/−11.

### What it does

**1. Name, editable where it is shown.** The Details list's **Name** row now has a pencil (or, with no name, *Set a name*) that opens the existing name editor in place; **Save / Clear / Cancel**, Enter and Escape as before. It is the **same editor, the same route (`/api/channels/people/:platform/:id/name`) and the same `channels-rename`** as the pencil by the name at the top — no backend change. A name set this way is locked against the person's own `remember_sender`, exactly as before. (The top pencil already existed; the Details row was the missing control.)

**2. Notes — edit and delete.** Each line under **What Jarvis remembers** has an Edit and a Delete control. Delete asks first (inline, "Keep" / "Delete"). Edit retypes the line in place; an empty edit is refused (use Delete), a duplicate of another note is refused. Text goes through the same `_clean_text` / 160-character cap as a note a guest wrote. **A note is named by `people.note_id(text)` — the first 8 hex digits of a hash of its text — never by its position**, because the list is a six-entry ring buffer a guest can push to: a stale "note 3" could otherwise delete the wrong line. A note that has changed since the panel drew it is reported ("isn't there any more") and the panel re-reads. Notes saved on a **linked** account are not shown here (the panel shows the account's own notes) but are still shared with the model; the panel says to edit those on that account. *The owner cannot add a note from the panel (not asked; see Open).*

**3. Forget this person.** New **Forget** section on the Profile tab, for everyone except the owner and except a hand-added person who never wrote (that one keeps **Remove**). Clicking **Forget this person…** asks the server for a **preview** (same code as the real run, nothing written) and shows what will happen, then a **Forget** button. In this order, so a failure part-way leaves the person with *less* access and the record still there for a retry:
1. off the dm / reply / tool lists, under every spelling (id, handle, @handle);
2. their `user_perms.json` entry deleted (tool limits, DM setting);
3. **only if the tick-box is on:** the transcript files of every thread that is **only their DMs** (live file and rotated copies), the model-facing conversations those logs point at, and the `threads.json` mappings to them;
4. their handle → id entries in `directory.json` (so `@handle` stops resolving);
5. their `people.json` record, and the `linked` field on the other half of a link.

**Refuses** (and says why, in the preview, before offering a button): **the owner** (hand ownership over first); **anyone a `"*"` entry covers in any list** — deleting a custom tool limit for someone a wildcard still lets through would *widen* their access, the same reason a per-person switch cannot undo a wildcard; **anyone whose `user_perms.json` is unreadable** (limits we cannot see are never wiped). **Leaves alone, and says so in the dialog:** the usage ledger (`usage.jsonl`, counts only — no text), lines in **group** threads other people also wrote in (rewriting a shared file while a gateway appends to it, or deleting it, would hurt other people's history; the dialog says how many lines stay), the linked account on the other platform (only the link goes), and any scope-level allow-list a hand-edit put their id in (same limit as Block today).

**After a forget.** If they write again they are a **new person**: a fresh record, the owner is asked about them again, nothing is switched on. A **blocked** person who is forgotten loses the block *record*, but with no list entry (and no `"*"`) they are not answered anyway; to keep refusing someone permanently, block rather than forget.

### Interfaces
- **Python:** `people.note_id / list_notes / edit_note / delete_note / delete_record`; `user_perms.forget`; `directory.forget`; `transcript.history_summary / purge_person / forget_conv_ids` (+ `_history_split`, which uses the same "only sender, all DMs" test `person_records` uses); `user_admin.edit_note / delete_note / forget_refusal / forget_person(platform, id, purge_history, dry_run)`; `person_view` gained `note_items` (`[{id, text}]`) next to the unchanged `notes`.
- **CLI:** `jarvis channels-note <platform> <id|@handle> list | edit <note-id> <text …> | delete <note-id>`; `jarvis channels-forget <platform> <id|@handle> [--history] [--yes]` — **without `--yes` it only previews and exits 0 with `"preview": true`.** Both are in `channels_cli.COMMANDS`, `reserved_names.py` and the slash-command data (`channels` verb's `covers`).
- **Web:** `POST /api/channels/people/:platform/:id/note` (`{action: "edit"|"delete", note: <8-hex id>, text}`; id format, action allow-list, single-line ≤160, no leading `-`) and `POST …/forget` (`{history?: bool, confirm?: bool}`; only `confirm: true` passes `--yes`). Argv arrays only, as every route here.
- **Not reachable by the model.** No tool was added; `AGENTS.md` gets an invariant saying so.

### Decisions I made that you may want to change
- **Chat history is a tick-box, default OFF**, and covers only DM-only threads. (You said "do this" but the plan flagged "including whether the transcript is also purged" as your call; I chose the reversible default. Flip the default in `forgetSection()` — `history: false` in `openForget`.)
- **Forget refuses under a `"*"` entry** rather than proceeding with a warning (Block proceeds with a warning). Chosen because deleting limits there widens access.
- **No note-adding, no note locking.** A guest's `remember_sender` can still append, and once six exist the oldest (possibly one you edited) drops out.
- **The server rejects an edited note that starts with `-`** (same rule as names, so it can't be read as a CLI flag). A guest-written note that starts with `-` can be deleted but not re-saved as is.

### Checks for the owner (nothing here was run)
**Python (from the repo root):** `python3 tests/test_channel_manual_people.py`, `test_user_admin.py`, `test_channels.py`, `test_channel_insights.py`, `test_channel_people.py`, `test_channel_servers.py`, `test_denied_sender_registered.py`, `test_directory.py`, `test_send_dm.py`, `test_reserved_names.py`, `test_slash_coverage.py` (the two new verbs must be reserved and in the slash registry), `test_checklist_coverage.py`; then `python3 tests/run_tests.py --jobs 8`. **Node:** `node tests/verify_channels_panel.js`; `python3 tests/verify_l36_insights_ui.py` if Chromium is available. `test_build_info.py` was already stale on `_93_` (run `bump_build_version.py` from `jarvis-cli/`). **Manual:** see the list in the reply that delivered this patch (Name row, note edit / delete / stale note, forget preview, refusals, history tick-box, CLI preview vs `--yes`, forget then message again).

**Not verified:** anything in a browser; the real `server.js` routes; a live Discord / Instagram account; Windows; the full Python suite; whether an existing test pins the exact keys of `person_view` (a new `note_items` key could trip a strict-equality test); the `_93_ → _94_` differences beyond `git apply --check`. **No new automated tests** — the invariants (refusals, order, history split, note ids) are not pinned by a test yet; `AGENTS.md` says tests should pin them.

**Docs updated with this revision:** this block, the L.36-P11 entry and an Update line under L.36 above, and — inside the patch — `REPO_MAP.md` (two commands), `AGENTS.md` (new invariant), `README.md` (examples and table rows).

## Revision 2026-10-05u (Agent panel: bug hunt + fix — a failed step no longer erases an earlier success; docs corrected — code + docs; `jarvis-agent-panel-status-fix.patch`, applied on top of `jarvis-main_95_.zip` **plus** `jarvis-code-agent-replay.patch`)

**Owner's requests:** "do a quick bug hunt", then "yes fix everything". **Owner's order kept:** patch presented first, docs after.

**Bug hunt — what was actually run this time** (the earlier "skip testing" instruction was for the build; a bug hunt is a different job): `tests/test_code_agent_extras.py` **11/11**, `tests/verify_agent_panel.js` **37/37**, `tests/test_l38b_replay_from_log.py` **67**, `tests/test_conversation_persistence.py` **34**, `tests/test_dev_agent.py` (9), `tests/test_checklist_coverage.py` (6) — all passed on the `_95_` + replay-patch tree. **End-to-end check:** the real `code_agent` executor was run against a temp project with the model loop stubbed; its real events (read from the process's **stderr**, where `JARVIS_MEDIA` lines go) were fed to the panel's JS reducer and to `extras_from_runs`. Result: the real `list_dir` format parses into the right nested tree; live and restored trees both correct; `.env` shows as a path only; an outside-root write is never drawn; neither a marker string from a written file nor the `.env` value is in the saved copy. **Static checks:** every CSS variable the panel uses is defined; the element ids match; `JarvisHost.state()` and `toast()` exist; the Agent button sits inside a `focus-only` container so Classic never shows it.

**The bug found and fixed:** in `agent-panel.js`, any `failed` status overwrote whatever the file had before. If `edit_file` succeeded on a file and a later edit to it failed (typically "old_str not found") with no successful retry, the tree showed the file as `failed` although the first edit was on disk. A second path had the same effect: while a new edit was in flight the row flipped to `writing`, losing the earlier status. **Fix:** `setFile` now remembers the file's last settled status while a transient one (`writing` / `fixing`) is showing, and a failure on a file that was already `edited` / `created` / `written` / `fixed` leaves that status (the failure stays in the log; no stale failure note on the row). **Exception, on purpose:** a failed **fix** (`dev_agent`) still shows `failed`, because the file is still broken. A file that was never changed still shows `failed`, and recovers when later edited. Only the tree's status was wrong before; nothing was saved or sent wrongly.

**Tests added:** 9 checks in `tests/verify_agent_panel.js` (now **46/46**, run and passing) covering the second-edit case, the in-flight case, a recovered file, a never-changed file, and the failed-fix exception.

**Patch:** 2 files (`web/public/agent-panel.js`, `tests/verify_agent_panel.js`), +46 / −3. `patch --dry-run` clean in that order on a fresh `_95_` extract; applying it reproduces the working tree exactly.

**Not a bug, left as is:** after switching to a chat that has no agent run, the panel keeps showing the previous job, labelled "· other chat". The `[failed]` rows seen during the end-to-end run were from running the script twice on the same temp folder.

### Checks for the owner
**Run:** `node tests/verify_agent_panel.js` (expect 46), `python3 tests/test_code_agent_extras.py` (expect 11), then `python3 tests/run_tests.py --jobs 8`. **By hand, Focus:** have `code_agent` edit a file successfully, then make a second edit to the same file that cannot match (e.g. ask it to replace text that is no longer there) — the row must stay marked edited, with the failure in the log.

**Not verified:** a browser (the docked / drawer layout, the scrim, Escape alongside the existing Focus handler, the Activity and subagents-dock interplay); a live provider run; Windows; the full Python suite.

**Docs updated with this revision:** this block, and the "never executed" statements elsewhere in this file (the L.47 entry and Revisions 2026-10-05s and 2026-10-05t), which are no longer true.


## Revision 2026-10-05v (Ask Jarvis agent: "The reply was cut off before the file ended -- not applied." explained and fixed — code + docs; `custom_tools_agent_truncation.patch` against `jarvis-main_96_.zip`)

**Owner's report:** every time an agent is started to write a tool in the Tool Manager, the chat answers *"(The reply was cut off before the file ended -- not applied.)"* and nothing reaches the editor. **Owner's order kept:** patch presented first, docs after; no tests run by me (the owner runs them).

**Where the message comes from:** `custom_tools_agent.py` (the L.45 agent), not the web UI and not the model. It is shown when the model's reply opens the ```python fence and never closes it.

**Cause — found by reading the code, not reproduced against a provider.** Four things stacked: (1) the agent asked for **`AGENT_MAX_TOKENS = 8000`** output tokens, and for thinking models the hidden reasoning shares that budget (the same effect `GEMINI_DEFAULT_MAX_TOKENS` documents), so the room left for code is often a fraction of 8000; (2) `resolved["max_tokens"] = AGENT_MAX_TOKENS` **overwrote the provider's own `max_tokens`**, so raising it in the AI config did nothing for this feature; (3) the protocol is **whole file every turn**, plus `TOOL_KEYWORDS` and `TEST_CHECKLIST`, so each follow-up edit costs the full file again; (4) when the provider stopped on length, the agent **ignored `AIResult.cut`** (all five adapters already set it to `"length"`) and discarded everything written.

**Fix (`custom_tools_agent.py` only; no JS change):**
- **Continue instead of discard.** If a reply has an open fence **and** the provider reported `cut == "length"`, the agent makes up to **`MAX_CONTINUATIONS = 3`** more calls (the partial reply as an assistant turn, then "continue from the exact character where you stopped, output only the rest and the closing fence"). `_join_continuation` stitches the pieces: it drops a re-opened ```python fence and any repeated overlap of 8 or more characters at the seam. Streaming is unchanged — the browser appends deltas; the final `JARVIS_AGENT_DONE` is still authoritative.
- **Honour the config.** `_output_cap(provider)` = `max(provider max_tokens, 8000)`; 8000 is now a floor, not an override.
- **Say why when it still fails.** If the file is still open after the continuations, the note names the output limit, the `max_tokens` value and the provider, and says to raise it or ask for a smaller tool. A reply with no `cut` signal (the model simply forgot the fence) keeps the old generic message — that is the model misbehaving, not the budget.
- **Ask for less.** The system prompt now says: keep the file compact (short comments, no redundant helpers, at most two test steps per tool).
- Refactor: the per-call streaming setup moved into `_call_once`.

**Invariants kept.** The model still gets **no tools** (continuation calls pass `tools=None`), the module still writes nothing to disk, and Save/Validate are still the owner's. `tool_safety.py`, confirmation prompts and `MAX_TOOL_ROUNDS` are untouched.

**Decisions I took (owner may overrule).** (a) Continue **only** when the provider says it hit its length limit. (b) At most 3 continuations; a tool that needs more is too big for one file. (c) Cost, stated plainly: each continuation re-sends the system prompt, the file and the partial reply as **input**, so the worst case is 4 calls for one request. (d) No separate `agent_max_tokens` setting — the provider's `max_tokens` is reused.

**Tests added (written, NOT run):** 9 checks in `tests/test_custom_tools_agent.py` (29 → expected **38**): a length cut is continued into one complete file; the continuation call carries the partial reply then the ask; a re-opened fence and a repeated line are dropped at the seam; bounded at `MAX_CONTINUATIONS`; the give-up note names the output limit and the provider; a failing continuation still ends in exactly one DONE with nothing applied; and the cap is 8000 / 8000 / 32000 for a provider `max_tokens` of unset / 700 / 32000. The existing "cut-off reply is never applied" check should still pass unchanged (its fake gives no `cut`, so no continuation is attempted).

**Patch:** 2 files (`jarvis-cli/jarvis/custom_tools_agent.py`, `tests/test_custom_tools_agent.py`), +127 / −18. `git apply --check` clean on a fresh `jarvis-main_96_.zip` extract. Only `py_compile` was run.

### Checks for the owner
**Run:** `git apply custom_tools_agent_truncation.patch`, then `python3 tests/run_tests.py custom_tools_agent` (expect 38 passed, 0 failed), then the full suite. **By hand:** Tool Manager → Ask Jarvis → ask for a large tool (three or four sub-tools plus keywords and a checklist). It should finish in the editor. If the note still names the output limit, raise `max_tokens` on that provider (for example 16000, or the model's limit); on Gemini also set `"extra_params": {"thinkingConfig": {"thinkingBudget": 0}}` so thinking stops eating the budget.

**Not verified:** a real provider (fakes only) — in particular whether each provider honours a continuation prompt cleanly and a `max_tokens` above 8000; the continuation path through the real `web/server.js` stream; what the live editor shows at the seam (the browser may briefly display the repeated overlap until the DONE line replaces the buffer with the stitched file); Windows; the full Python suite.

**Known limits, left as they are.** (1) The seam trim removes any 8+ character overlap, so a legitimate repeat of that length exactly at a seam would be dropped — read the file before pressing Validate (already advised; Validate runs the file's top level). (2) The 150-second per-call timeout (`AGENT_TIMEOUT`) is unchanged: a slow provider can still time out on a very long file, and whether each adapter returns partial text on a timeout was not checked. (3) Whole-file replies remain the protocol; diff-style edits (Q-L45d) would cut the per-turn cost but were not built.

**Open:** **Q-L45f** — raise the 8000 floor or add a dedicated `agent_max_tokens` provider field? **Q-L45g** — allow partial/diff replies so editing a large file does not re-emit all of it?

**Docs updated with this revision:** this block, and a correction note at the end of L.45 (the "never applied" and "long files cost more tokens" statements).

P15 and P10 are self-contained, and P15 was flagged in Revision 2026-10-05o as mattering more once bulk edit exists.

**What was built (16 files, +851/−36; new: `channels/changelog.py`).**
- **P15 — change log.** `changelog.record()` appends one JSON line to `~/.jarvis/channels/changes.jsonl`: when, platform, kind, the person's id or handle, the new state, the old state where it is cheap, tool *names* (at most 30, plus a count), `via` (`panel` or `terminal`) and an optional `why`. **Written by the writers, not by callers:** `config.add_to_set` / `remove_from_set` (dm / reply / tool lists, including a `*` entry), `config.set_value` for **only** `owner` and `allow_tools`, `user_perms.set_tools` / `set_can_dm`, `people.set_follow`, plus `user_admin.set_handle` and `forget_person`. So a flip is recorded whether it came from the panel, a quick setup, a bulk edit or `jarvis channels-allow / -deny / -follow / -user …`. A line is written **only after the change was saved and only if something changed** (re-adding a listed person writes nothing). It **never raises** and never blocks a permission change. Rotated at 1 MB, never deleted.
- **`via`, and batch routes.** `server.js` sets `JARVIS_CHANGE_SOURCE=panel` for every `channels-*` command it runs, so a panel change reads "panel" and everything else reads "terminal". `changelog.reason()` tags every line a quick setup or bulk edit writes ("Quick setup: Chat only", "Bulk edit: Replies off"), so twenty lines from one click read as one action.
- **History tab (key `6`)** on each person: lines grouped by day with the time, a sentence, a panel/terminal tag and the batch reason. Lines that changed things for **everyone** (a `*` entry, the platform's tool switch) are shown on every person's tab, tagged "everyone". A person's earlier handles are followed, so a handle edit does not cut their history in two. "Show older changes" up to 500. The footer now reads "1–6 tab". Route `GET /api/channels/people/:platform/:id/history`; CLI `jarvis channels-history <platform> <id> [limit]`. Read-only; every string is shown as text.
- **P10 — edit a handle.** A pencil by **Handle** in Details (drawn only when the server says `handle_editable`), route `POST /api/channels/people/:platform/:id/handle`, CLI `jarvis channels-handle <platform> <id|@handle> <new-handle>`. **Refused for the owner and for anyone who has written** (the platform's own handle replaces an edit on their next message). The new handle must have no spaces, start with a letter or digit and **not be only digits** (that would read as an id). A handle already used by another record is refused **before** any list is touched.
- **How a handle edit keeps access from widening.** Order: (1) a handle-only placeholder's tool limits are copied to the new key; (2) the new handle is added to every list the old one was on; (3) the `people.json` record is moved (a placeholder is keyed by its handle) and a link partner is repointed; (4) the old handle is removed from those lists; (5) the old limits entry is dropped. A failure part-way leaves the old entries in place and is reported; running it again finishes it. **Only the old handle is removed from a list** — a real id entry stays. The old string is never left behind, so whoever really owns it cannot inherit the grant.
- **Also in the patch:** `reserved_names.py` and `slash-commands-data.js` (two new verbs), `preset_admin.py` (wraps apply / bulk in `changelog.reason`; the bulk-preset loop was re-indented into a `with`), `REPO_MAP.md`, `AGENTS.md` (two new invariants), `README.md`.

**Invariants kept.** `permissions.decide`, `tool_safety.py`, confirmation prompts and `MAX_TOOL_ROUNDS` untouched. The log holds no message, note, token or config value other than the `owner` id and the `allow_tools` flag. Guest data stays in `people.py` / `user_perms.json`, never `memory.py`. Bot tokens never pass through the browser.

**Decisions I took (owner may overrule).**
- **History is not backfilled.** Changes made before this patch were never recorded and are not guessed at; the tab says when tracking began.
- **"Forget this person" keeps that person's old log lines** and adds a "forgotten" line, so the log can still answer "what happened to X"; it does not hold their messages. Say so if you would rather a forget also purge their change lines.
- **Blocking writes a follow-status line as well as the list-removal lines** (two kinds of change, two kinds of line).
- **`via` records the route, not a login** — Jarvis has one owner and no accounts. A change Jarvis itself makes through a CLI path reads "terminal".
- **Everyone-lines show on every person's tab** rather than on a separate platform page.
- **Handle edit is limited to never-written, hand-added people** (the plan said only "must keep the placeholder→real-id move intact"). Editing a handle for someone who has written would be reverted by their next message, so it is refused instead of pretending to work.

**Not run, not verified (owner's instruction: no testing).**
- **Nothing was executed.** Checks made: `py_compile` on every changed Python file, `node --check` on `server.js`, `channels-panel.js` and `slash-commands-data.js`, `git apply --check` on a fresh `_97_`, and a byte comparison of the applied tree against the working tree. **No Python suite, no Node verifier, no browser, no CLI run, no real `server.js`, no live Discord / Instagram.**
- **No new tests were written.** Behaviour that most needs one: each writer logs exactly one line on a real change and none on a no-op; a failed save logs nothing; `reason()` tags every line of a quick setup and a bulk edit and nests correctly; `via` is `panel` only when `server.js` set the variable; a handle edit on a placeholder moves its limits and its list entries and leaves nothing under the old key; the owner, a person who has written, a taken handle and a digits-only handle are all refused with no list touched; a link partner is repointed; the log file rotates; a torn line is skipped.
- **Run before relying on it:** `test_channels`, `test_channel_insights`, `test_channel_manual_people`, `test_channel_people`, `test_user_admin`, `test_reserved_names`, `test_slash_coverage` and `node tests/verify_channels_panel.js`. `test_channel_insights` snapshots the whole `~/.jarvis` tree around the dry run: **a dry run that now writes a `changes.jsonl` line would fail it**, which is exactly the check wanted (the dry run should write nothing).
- **By hand, on a throwaway person:** (1) flip DMs / Replies / Tool use, set a tool list, toggle "Jarvis may DM them", block and unblock — History should show one correct "panel" line each; (2) `jarvis channels-allow discord reply <id>` in a terminal — a "terminal" line, and none when repeated; (3) a quick setup, then a bulk edit over 2–3 people — each line carries its batch reason; (4) add a handle-only person, put them on the reply list, correct the handle — the card re-selects, the list holds the new handle and not the old, tool limits survived, History keeps the earlier lines; (5) edit the owner's and a writer's handle — refused, no pencil; (6) a taken handle and a digits-only one — refused, lists unchanged; (7) History at phone width — six tabs scroll, footer reads "1–6 tab".
- **UI not seen by anyone:** the History rows, the handle editor, the six-tab bar at narrow widths, focus after the card re-keys.
- **Build number not bumped** (run `python build_tools/bump_build_version.py` from `jarvis-cli/`). **No Test Checklist entry** (panel feature, as for P1–P5).
- **Not tried together with other pending patches** touching `channels-panel.js`, `server.js`, `channels_cli.py`, `user_admin.py`, `people.py` or `config.py`.

**Known limits.** (1) A change made by editing `channels.json` by hand is not logged — the log hooks the code paths, not the file. (2) A line records the change, not the old tool list (only the new names and count). (3) Re-keying a placeholder uses the person's handle as their id until they write; the history follows the handle through the edit, but a later real id adoption (existing `_adopt_placeholder`) is not logged as a handle line. (4) `via` cannot tell the owner from Jarvis acting through the CLI.

**Open.**
- Should a forget also purge that person's change lines?
- Should the log have a retention limit (it rotates at 1 MB but nothing deletes the rotated files)?
- Should the old tool list be recorded, so a "limited to 3 tools" line can say what it replaced?
- Should there be a platform-wide History (all people, filterable) as well as the per-person tab?
- Should a handle edit also be allowed for someone who has written, if the owner first confirms the platform's handle really changed?
- Should P16 (a saved browser test) come next, now that the panel has six tabs and no automated browser coverage?
- **P6, P8, P9, P12, P13, P14 and P16 are unchanged** and still suggestions; P9, P13 and P14 still need an owner decision first.

**Docs updated with this revision:** this block, the P10 / P15 entries and the new Update line under L.36 above, `REPO_MAP.md`, `AGENTS.md` and `README.md` (in the patch).


## Revision 2026-10-05x (dev_agent known-bugs batch: BUG-1 to BUG-4 fixed — code + docs; `0001-Fix-BUG-1-markdown-style-leak-and-BUG-2-server-run-p.patch` and `0002-Fix-BUG-3-dev_agent-output_dir-and-BUG-4-reasoning-s.patch` against `jarvis-main_98_.zip`)

**What this revision is.** The owner's `DEV_AGENT_KNOWN_BUGS.md` (the first real agent-mode run) listed eight problems. This revision fixes the first four and records the other four as open. The full design, decisions and file lists are in **L.48** above; this block is the revision record.

**Fixed.**
- **BUG-1** — `renderMarkdown()` forbids `<style>`, `<link>`, `<meta>`, `<base>` and inline `style` (`MD_SANITIZE_CONFIG`), so a model reply can no longer restyle the whole page.
- **BUG-2** — a server that is still running after an 8 s grace window is a success (`long_running`, with its URL), not a timeout failure; a bare timeout is labelled `timeout` and never sent to the fix loop.
- **BUG-3** — `dev_agent` takes an optional `output_dir`; validated up front, the build stays in the sandbox and a passed build is copied there (new `deliver` phase; never overwrites; dependency folders and symlinks are not copied).
- **BUG-4** — the saved `thinking` extra needs thinking to have been on (`reasoning.should_save_trace`); the raw event log still keeps the full text.

**Decisions I took (owner may overrule).**
- A confirmed-running server is **stopped** after the start check rather than left running.
- `output_dir` must be **new or empty**; an existing non-empty folder is refused, not merged into.
- Delivery happens **only after a passed build**, and a failed copy leaves the build `ok: true` with `delivered: false`.
- `node_modules`, `.venv`, `venv`, `__pycache__`, `.git` and **all symlinks** are not copied.
- BUG-4 hides provider reasoning only when thinking is off; the raw archive keeps it.

**Process change from the owner.** From this batch on: one git patch per change (`git format-patch`), **the patch is presented before anything else**, then the audit and this plan are updated, and the assistant **does not run tests** — the owner runs them. BUG-1/2 were built before that instruction and were run; BUG-3/4 were not.

**Verified / not verified.** See L.48. In short: BUG-1/2 run and passing in a sandbox; BUG-3/4 compile-checked only, 20 tests written and never run; nothing verified in a browser, on Windows, or through a real `node server.js` run.

**Open.** BUG-5, BUG-6, BUG-7, BUG-8 (see L.48), plus the four questions at the end of L.48. The two owed follow-ups for this batch: `REPO_MAP.md` entry for `output_dir` / `deliver`, and the build-number bump.

**Docs updated with this revision:** this block, the new L.48 section above, and the 2026-10-05x Update line and L.48 section in the status audit.
